films.title: Nights of Cabiria
films.synopsis: In the role that won her the Best Actress award at Cannes, Giulietta Masina stars as Cabiria, a tough Roman streetwalker who, after a near-drowning by her pimp boyfriend, is swept off her feet by a square, but sympathetic, accountant... Federico Fellini’s showcase for his wife won the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film of its year. “A cinematic masterpiece... a deep, wrenching and eloquent filmgoing experience.”

films.title: The Macaluso Sisters
films.synopsis: 1985. The Macaluso sisters are five young, orphaned siblings who live in and work from a shabby rooftop apartment in Palermo, Sicily. One hot summer, a rare beach outing is planned on a day offwork. Near the end of a day of enchantment, reverie, and amorous trysts, a shocking catastrophe transpires. That single event will change the course of the relationships between the sisters for the rest of their lives. Best Film, Italian Golden Globes Best Film, Italian Film Critics 100% Fresh ROTTEN TOMATOES

films.title: Dear Diary
films.synopsis: STARTS JAN 7 Nanni Moretti picked up the Best Director prize at Cannes in 1994 with this deceptive doodle of a movie, a personal memoir that feels like a Roman counterpart to late 1970s Woody Allen; it’s very funny, self-reflexive and free-flowing. It falls into three parts: the filmmaker’s musing on cinema atop a Vespa, (including a pilgrimmage to the site of Pasolini’s murder), a trip to the Aeolian Islands to work on his new screenplay, and his search for health and wellness after breaking out in a nagging skin rash.

films.title: Il Boom
films.synopsis: Although Vittorio De Sica is best known for neo-realist tearjerkers like The Bicycle Thief, he was a dab hand at comedy, as this 1963 social satire aptly demonstrates. Alberto Sordi is the executive going to extreme lengths and racking up debt to keep his wife happy and their lifestyle on a par with their peers. “Packed with trenchant observation and mordant wit.” GLENN KENNY, NEW YORK TIMES (2017) “Among the most savage and surreal of Italian comedies.” BILGE EBERI, VILLAGE VOICE

films.title: The Inner Cage
films.synopsis: Toni Servillo (The Great Beauty; The King of Laughter) stars as Gaetano, Captain of the Guards in an old, crumbling Sardinian prison in this compassionate character drama. The prison is due to be shut down, but an administrative errror means that a handful of prisoners and skeleton staffremain while the paper work is sorted out. When the prisoners go on hunger strike, Gaetano negotiates with their de facto leader, a mobster named Carmine (Silvio Orlando) and they carve out an unorthodox arrangement...

films.title: The King of Laughter
films.synopsis: North American Premiere. Toni Servillo gives another astounding, complex performance as the famed Neapolitan comic actor and playwright Eduardo Scarpetta, whose showmanship was shadowed by equally ostentatious personal life, involving multiple wives, mistresses and children, most of whom wound up in his theatre company. “A feast of a film.... It’s a dazzling and technically brilliant feat, the work of an ambitious, experienced and passionate director.”

films.title: Death in Venice
films.synopsis: Dirk Bogarde plays the composer Gustave Aschenbach (loosely based on Mahler, whose 3rd and 5th Symphonies are woven through the soundtrack). He arrives in Venice to recuperate from illness. But the city is succumbing to a deadly cholera epidemic. Infatuated by a beautiful adolescent boy, Tadzio (Björn Andrésen), the artist is unable to tear himself away. Visconti’s film of Thomas Mann’s acclaimed autobiographical novella is an exquisite piece of cinema, langorous, lavish, steeped in longing and regret.

films.title: The Most Beautiful Boy in the World
films.synopsis: In 1971 at the world premiere of Death in Venice in London, Italian director Luchino Visconti proclaimed Björn Andrésen, the teen star of his latest film, “The most beautiful boy in the world.” This is the story of a boy who was thrust to international stardom for his iconic looks and lived a life of glamour and exploitation. 50 years later, Björn looks back. “Haunting... psychologically probing.” AO SCOTT, NEW YORK TIMES

films.title: The Predators
films.synopsis: A plan to exhume the body of Friedrich Nietzsche is one of several juicy plot motors in this confident and compelling black comedy about two very different Roman families, the working class Vismaras and the bourgeois Favone clan. The directorial debut of 28-year-old actor Pietro Castellitto (who also plays Federico, an assistant philosophy professor, and penned the screenplay), I predatori is a toothy ensemble comedy with plenty of laughs. “Relentlessly entertaining”

films.title: The Passionate Thief
films.synopsis: In Mario Monicelli’s evergreen 1960 comedy, struggling actress Tortorella (Anna Magnani) just wants to have a nice time on New Year’s Eve, but she is unwittingly dragged into a night of attempted thievery by her broke friend Umberto (Totò) and his partner-in-crime (Ben Gazzara). “Will make you smile like there is no tomorrow.” LA TIMES “Fun and frothy... Like a long night of champagne without the hangover.”

films.title: Caffè Italia
films.synopsis: Beginning on a high point with Italy beating West Germany to win the FIFA World Cup in 1982, this poignant and evocative 1985 documentary is a portrait of Italian immigrants to Montreal—their stories, and their parents’ stories, their thoughts about country, tradition, history and home. Among them is the young actor Toni Nardi, who features in some dramatic sketches prepared especially for the film. It’s a fascinating time capsule, but also an important piece of oral history in its own right.

films.title: The Hand of God
films.synopsis: Paolo Sorrentino—The Great Beauty; Il Divo; The Young Pope—returns with his most personal movie, the story of his coming in age in Naples in the 1980s. The title references the Catholic faith so deeply embedded in that culture, but also superstar Argentine footballer Diego Maradona, who used the phrase to justify a notorious goal against England in the World Cup, and who amazed everyone by signing for Napoli... and to a devastating family tragedy that befalls the teenage Sorrentino.

films.title: C’mon C’mon
films.synopsis: The latest from Mike Mills (20th Century Women; Beginners) is guaranteed to make you feel a little better about humanity. Joaquin Phoenix plays Johnny, a radio reporter working on a project in which he interviews youths about their aspirations and fears. Pressed into looking after his nine-year-old nephew Jesse (Woody Norman), Johnny is taken aback by the boy’s mixture of candour and mischief-making. Little by little they build trust and affection in beautifully written and often very funny scenes.

films.title: The Conductor
films.synopsis: STARTS FRI JAN 28 Marin Alsop first saw the legendary Leonard Bernstein when she was nine-years old. That’s when she found her vocation. Told that girls can’t do that, Marin struggled against enormous prejudices and institutional obstacles for decades to become one of the world’s most renowned classical music conductors. The film follows Marin’s improbable rise and her single-minded pursuit. “If conductor Marin Alsop’s done it, it’s probably because someone told her she couldn’t.”

films.title: Titane
films.synopsis: The love child of Jean Cocteau and David Cronenberg, this ugly duckling of a movie has more gasp-out-loud moments than anything we’ve seen in a long, long time. Alexia (Agathe Rousselle) has a steel plate in her head and a chip on her shoulder. She’s also a killer hand with a metal-tipped chopstick. Oh, and she’s carrying a baby which might very well be born with four wheels and a motor. The film’s dream logic is aggressive but deliriously, ecstatically demented. Did we mention it won the Palme d’Or?

films.title: Our Time Will Come
films.synopsis: Based on the true story of Fang Gu (Zhou Xun), a school teacher, and the legendary, JinJin “Blackie” Lau (Eddie Peng Yuyan), Ann Hui’s award-winning drama recounts the exploits of the Dongjiang during World War II. Tasked with fighting against the Japanese occupation of Hong Kong, this ragtag group of guerrillas recruits Gu, all against the wishes of her childhood sweetheart, Li Jinrong (Wallace Huo Chienhwa). “Beautifully mounted and emotionally engaging.” HOLLYWOOD REPORTER In Mandarin with Chinese, English subtitles.

films.title: A Simple Life
films.synopsis: Ann Hui’s lovely portrait of an elderly maid (Deanie Ip) retiring after 60 years of service is one of her most beloved and acclaimed movies. As the title suggests, this is a quiet, quotidien film, yet it speaks volumes about universal themes: aging, work, and personal relationships. Best Actress, Venice 2011; Best Director, Actor and Actress, Golden Horse Awards 2011

films.title: Keep Rolling (Ann Hui, Filmmaker)
films.synopsis: Recipient of Venice Film Festival’s 2020 Lifetime Achievement Award, Ann Hui’s 40-year artistic trajectory not only mirrors the roller-coaster ride that is Hong Kong cinema, but parallels the poignant yet resilient course of its history. Hui displays her storytelling genius not only with celluloid but in humourous, candid conversation. This documentary seamlessly weaves interviews and archival material into a Who’s Who of Asian cinema, and is catnip for cinephiles anywhere. In Cantonese, Mandarin with English subtitles. FEATURING Ann Hui, Hou Hsiao-hsien, Jia Zhangke, Tsui Hark, Andy Lau, Fruit Chan, Mark Lee, Sylvia Chang

films.title: Belfast
films.synopsis: Kenneth Branagh gets personal in this bittersweet black and white autobiographical drama, set in his hometown in Northern Ireland in 1969, at the advent of the Troubles. Buddy (Jude Hill) is nine when spiraling Catholic unrest upsets his previously cozy childhood and sends shockwaves through his tight-knit family: Ma and Pa (Caitríona Balfe and Jamie Dornan) and beloved grandparents (Judi Dench and Ciarán Hinds). For Buddy, it’s a rude awakening, but even hard times bring humour and vivid dreams of escape.

films.title: Tosca, From the Royal Opera House
films.synopsis: Jonathan Kent’s taut and intense production of Puccini’s tragic opera with Paul Brown’s historically charged designs wonderfully evokes the dangerous atmosphere of Rome in 1800, where love and evil come—thrillingly— face to face. Oksana Lyniv conducts. Elena Stikina (Floria Tosca); Freddie De Tommaso (Mario Cavaradossi); Alexey Markov (Baron Scarpia); Hubert Francis (Spoletta). Running time includes two 15 minute intermissions. Special ticket prices apply

films.title: Saint Jack
films.synopsis: Jack Flowers (Ben Gazzara) is an American pimp in Singapore, and, although his livelihood is unsavory, he is not morally bankrupt, and makes friends with auditor William (Denholm Elliott). Jack yearns for more than the smalltime, though—his ambition is to open an entire bordello. Meanwhile he gets the squeeze put on him by the local mob for his business dealings, and, to achieve his dream of luxury, he may need to assist in a sinister deal by the CIA to take some compromising photographs.

films.title: What’s Up Doc?
films.synopsis: After the acclaim which greeted The Last Picture Show, Bogdanovich proved his versatility with this colourful, contemporary screwball comedy inspired by Howard Hawks’ classic Bringing Up Baby. Ryan O’Neal stands in for Cary Grant, and Barbra Streisand for Katharine Hepburn. Instead of a paleontologist, it’s the story of an absent-minded musicologist whose impending marriage to Madeline Kahn is derailed by the force of nature that is Streisand’s disaster-prone Judy Maxwell.

films.title: The Last Picture Show
films.synopsis: Bogdanovich’s second film was a triumph, an adaptation of Larry McMurtry’s novel about a small Texas town at the dawn of the 1950s. Teenagers Duane and Sonny (Jeff Bridges and Timothy Bottoms) are best friends, but the soul of the film is Ben Johnson’s Sam the Lion, proprietor of the local movie house, and a father figure in the boy’s lives. Robert Surtees’ dusty monochrome cinematography evokes a great yearning for a lost golden age.

films.title: Poly Styrene: I Am a Cliche
films.synopsis: STARTS FRI FEB 4 Poly Styrene was the first woman of color in the UK to front a successful rock band. The death of this punk icon and X-Ray Spex frontwoman sends her daughter on a journey across the world and through her mother’s archives to reconcile their fraught relationship, featuring Oscar nominee Ruth Negga as the voice of Poly Styrene. Winner of 2 British Independent Film Awards including Best Documentary “This must-watch documentary tells a story often erased from rock history.” LEONIE COOPER, NME

films.title: Who We Are: A Chronicle of Racism in America
films.synopsis: The most important film about race since I Am Not Your Negro, Who We Are is an eloquent, passionate and revelatory reclamation of the history America sweeps under the carpet. This is the story of how white supremacy and slavery underpins the disUnited States, and, equally damning, a critique of how the tide for social justice has been betrayed by the rich and the powerful. Former ACLU Deputy Legal Director Jeffery Robinson’s argument is interwoven with archival footage, interviews, and his own story.

films.title: Music. Money. Madness - Jimi Hendrix: Experience Live in Maui
films.synopsis: This 2022 Grammy-nominated film chronicles the Jimi Hendrix Experience’s storied visit to Maui, and how the band became ensnared with the ill-fated “Rainbow Bridge” movie. Never-before-released original footage, and new interviews with key players such as Billy Cox and director Chuck Wein, form this fascinating account about one of the most controversial independent films ever made.

films.title: Striding Into the Wind
films.synopsis: STARTS FRI FEB 4 Slacker comedies may have fallen out of fashion in the US, but this debut feature from lauded short filmmaker Wei Shujun suggests the travails of young adulthood are not so very different even in China. Film school student Kun takes his sound recording skills from Beijing to Inner Mongolia in a beaten up Jeep Cherokee in this slow burning road comedy, which lands somewhere between Jia Zhangke and Jim Jarmusch. “Easily one of the best Chinese indie or arthouse films of the last few years.” EASTERN KICKS In Mandarin with simplified Chinese and English subtitles.

films.title: Cosmic Dawn
films.synopsis: There are cult movies, and then there are movies about cults. Cosmic Dawn could be both. Inspired by director Jefferson Moneo’s own childhood close encounter with UFOs and the revelations about nxivm right here in Vancouver, it’s a movie about a vulnerable young woman, Aurora (Camille Rowe) sucked into a cult led by the charismatic but probably bonkers Elyse (Antonia Zegers)... But for all the red flags, Cosmic Dawn does seem able to tap into some mysterious alternate reality...

films.title: Tribute to Sidney Poitier: A Raisin in the Sun
films.synopsis: The first film in our Landmarks series, curated by Nya Lewis, A Raisin in the Sun is the film version of the acclaimed 1959 play by Black writer Lorraine Hansberry. It is the story of tensions in a working class family in Chicago, 1930, as they await the arrival of a life insurance check after the passing of Lena’s husband, father to Walter (Sidney Poitier). Hansberry was the first African-American woman to write a play performed on Broadway. The New York Times said it “changed American theatre forever.”

films.title: The Power of the Dog
films.synopsis: In her strongest movie since The Piano, Jane Campion turns the machismo of the western film on its head. On the Burbanks’ Montana cattle ranch the boorish Phil (Benedict Cumberbatch) rules the roost over his mild mannered brother George (Jesse Plemons). When George finds himself a wife and heir in the form of Rose (Kirsten Dunst) and her effete son (Kodi Smit-McPhee), Phil is determined to make their life hell. But then he takes a shine to the boy... A stark, brooding tale destined to be a modern classic.

films.title: Tribute to Jean-Marc Vallée:
films.synopsis: The late Jean-Marc Vallée enjoyed working with some of Hollywood’s best and brightest on projects as diverse as Wild, Dallas Buyers Club, Sharp Objects and Big Little Lies. But his best film was his breakthrough feature, a coming out/coming of age movie, set in Montreal in the 60s, 70s and 80s, and a love story between a young gay man and his uncomprehending father. Considered one of the best Canadian films ever made, this movie has brio to spare, a terrific soundtrack, comic panache and compassion to spare.

films.title: The Flower of My Secret
films.synopsis: A pivotal film in Almodóvar’s development, maybe the first of his “mature” works, The Flower of My Secret dispenses with much of the decadent high camp gloss which had come to characterize the films of the early 90s (High Heels; Kika). Marisa Paredes plays novelist Leo, who writes romantic best-sellers under pen name Amanda Gris but wants to be taken seriously in her own right, and whose marriage is on the rocks. Smartly balancing melodrama and comedy, this is one of the director’s most under-rated movies.

films.title: Talk to Her
films.synopsis: A nurse (Javier Cámara) befriends a writer (Darío Grandinetti) at the hospital where they are both tending to women in a coma. Through an intricate series of flashbacks we learn about their relations with the women and what inspires their unflagging devotion. This sublime film also features a memorable dance work by Pina Bausch and an unforgettable and hilarious silent film, in which a man shrinks to a size small enough to crawl up a woman’s vagina... Winner, Academy Award: Best Original Screenplay

films.title: Bad Education
films.synopsis: While no two people can agree on Almodóvar’s best film, the semi-autobiographical Bad Education has to be part of the conversation. A filmmaker is forced to revisit memories of his childhood at a Catholic boarding school when an old friend turns up on his doorstep. This labyrinthine tale confronts and transcends traumatic revelations of abuse through the art of re-invention. “A poison-darted valentine to the movies, and to desire itself. This is a film you want to drink and devour.”

films.title: All About My Mother
films.synopsis: Cecilia Roth stars as Manuela. When her teenage son is killed in a traffic accident running after the autograph of his favourite actress, the grief-crazed Manuela quits Madrid to search Barcelona for her estranged husband, Lola. Instead, unconsciously, she falls to collecting emotional orphans... One of Almodóvar’s most beloved films, it is dedicated to “all actresses who have played actresses. To all women who act. To men who act and become women. To all the people who want to be mothers. To my mother.”

films.title: Volver
films.synopsis: Penélope Cruz’s put-upon cleaner, Raimunda, has enough aggravation in her life before she is visited by the ghost of her late mother. Despite several dark elements, Volver is one of Almodóvar’s warmest and most purely enjoyable films. The remarkable ensemble of actresses collectively won the Best Actress award at the Cannes Film Festival. “If the camaraderie of women forms a significant portion of Almodóvar’s aesthetic interests, then Volver is perhaps the most pleasurable expression of those aims.”

films.title: The Sleeping Negro
films.synopsis: “To be a Negro in this country and to be relatively conscious is to be in a state of rage almost all of the time.” Beginning with a quote from James Baldwin, Skinner Myers’ radical debut feature is an uncompromisingly confrontational movie, a portrait of a young Black man (played by Myers) on the verge of “making it”: marriage (to a white woman) and big money career (his fiancee’s brother is his boss). But it feels all wrong. Alienated and angry, he wavers between playing the game and tearing it all down.

films.title: Tie Me Up! Tie Me Down!
films.synopsis: In a variation on the themes of Law of Desire, Antonio Banderas is another obsessive fan with boundary issues. He kidnaps porn star and junkie Marina (Victoria Abril) and holds her captive until she falls in love. For the most part the film focusses on these confused lost souls. Despite the X rating slapped on it in the US, it’s probably best understood as a twisted marriage comedy, and surprisingly sympathetic to its trapped, all too fallible antagonists. They can’t help it if they’re also super hot.

films.title: Live Flesh
films.synopsis: Victor (Liberto Rabal) has a crush on junkie Elena (Francesca Neri). But when two cops happen across a heated argument, a gun goes off. One of the cops, David (Javier Bardem) winds up in a wheelchair, but married to Elena. Released from prison after 5 years Victor determines to get the girl and his revenge... Freely adapted from a Ruth Rendall novel, Live Flesh is another deliciously kinky thriller, Bunuelian in its fixation on eros, virility, and attendant anxieties. “Live Flesh has it all.”

films.title: Law of Desire
films.synopsis: A young, electrifying Antonio Banderas plays the psychotic gay super fan (Antonio) of homo-erotic film director Pablo (Eusebio Poncela) in this wonderfully over-wrought black comic melodrama, Almodóvar’s seventh feature. Pablo himself is pining for Juan, too straight to reciprocate, and also directing his trans sister Tina (Carmen Maura) on stage. There’s rampant sex and cocaine use, incest, jabs at the Catholic Church... It’s all Almodóvar’s movies in one, you might say. A statement of kinky intent.

films.title: Women on the Verge of a Nervous Breakdown + The Human Voice
films.synopsis: Almodóvar’s 1988 farce was his commercial breakthrough in North America, and his first film to be nominated for an Academy Award. His first muse, Carmen Maura stars as Pepe, who is summarily dumped by her married boyfriend, Ivan (Fernando Guillén). Over the course of two days as she frantically tries to connect

films.title: Breaking Bread
films.synopsis: Dr Nof Atamna-Ismaeel—the first Muslim Arab to win Israel’s MasterChef—is on a quest to make social change through food. And so, she founded the A-Sham Arabic Food Festival, where pairs of Arab and Jewish chefs collaborate on dishes like kishek (a Syrian yogurt soup), and qatayef (a dessert typically eaten during Ramadan). “This is a joyous film—with some mouth-watering looking food as a bonus. Hugely recommended.” GRAEME TUCKETT, STUFF

films.title: The Automat
films.synopsis: Want to know where Howard Schultz drew inspiration for his coffee chain? Even though it only operated in two cities, New York and Philadelphia, for a spell in the middle of Twentieth Century, the Automat was the most successful food franchise in the US. For a nickel, you could get a cup of coffee. For a couple more you could unlock a slice of pie. For many Americans, there was nothing more exciting, more modern, more American than this... Mel Brooks, Ruth Bader Ginsburg and Colin Powell concur. In English FEATURING Mel Brooks, Ruth Bader Ginsburg, Carl Reiner, Elliott Gould, Howard Schultz, Colin Powell

films.title: The Skin I Live In
films.synopsis: Reunited with Antonio Banderas for the first time since 1990, Almodóvar fashioned a creepy, kinky suspense movie about a brilliant but patently bonkers plastic surgeon who is dead set on creating an invulnerable synthetic skin. The guinea pig for this pet project is the mysterious Vera (Elena Anaya), who he holds captive in the bowels of his ridiculously luxurious mansion. “This film, by turns macabre, melodramatic, and gothic, makes the heart race and the skin crawl.” CARRIE RICKEY, PHILADELPHIA INQUIRER

films.title: Broken Embraces
films.synopsis: Diving back into the vein of film noir, this twisty psychodrama unspools the tale of filmmaker (Lluís Homar), who becomes besotted with his female star (Penélope Cruz), who happens to be the mistress of his friend Ernesto (José Luis Gómez)... “Broken Embraces is a voluptuary of a film, drunk on primary colors, caressing Penelope Cruz, using the devices of a Hitchcock to distract us with surfaces while the sinister uncoils beneath.”

films.title: Julieta
films.synopsis: Based on stories by Alice Munro, Julieta uses a familiar framework to house Almodóvar’s idiosyncratic style. The turning point in our heroine’s life was her daughter’s inexplicable disappearance long ago. Now in her 50s and still searching,, Julieta happens upon one of the girl’s childhood friends who may just offer a break in the case. She begins to write a letter to her estranged child, sifting through memories in hope of uncovering an explanation but finding only grief and guilt.

films.title: Pain and Glory
films.synopsis: In the performance of his career, Antonio Banderas plays a film director depressed by his mother’s death, suffering from the aftereffects of back surgery, and, basically, at the end of his tether. The chance to reunite

films.title: Sacco & Vanzetti
films.synopsis: The notorious 1927 murder trial of Italian immigrants Sacco and Vanzetti is the basis for this powerful and compelling drama by Giuliano Montaldo, here working in English with a predominantly Irish supporting cast. Gian Maria Volonte and Riccardo Cucciolla (the latter named Best Actor at Cannes) play the two men, a cobbler and a fishmonger, caught up in a violent crackdown on “subversives”. Ennio Morricone wrote the score, and Joan Baez contributes two songs. GUEST PRESENTER: Don Stewart (Macleod’s Books)

films.title: Fabian - Going to the Dogs
films.synopsis: Fabian is a cynical, idealistic aspiring writer in Berlin, 1931. By day he shills cigarettes. At night he explores the bohemian city with his wealthy Communist buddy Labude. A serendipitous encounter with a young actress, Cornelia, leaves him lovestruck and, briefly, hopeful. This epic melodrama, adapted from Erich Kästner’s autobiographical novel, begins with a combative salvo of modernist tricks and tropes, but eases into a resonant, edgy and regretful liebestraum.

films.title: Lunana: A Yak in the Classroom
films.synopsis: Ugyen dreams of leaving Bhutan and becoming a singer in Australia. First though, he has a year left on his teaching contract—and to his dismay he’s posted to Lunana, a mountain village hundreds of miles away from anything Ugyen considers “civilization”. With more yak dung than people and an altitude of nearly 5,000 metres, Lunana is a shock to the city slicker’s system. A visual balm, this is a heartfelt film about the unexpected ways life can change us. Academy Award Nominee: Best International Feature

films.title: Young Frankenstein
films.synopsis: Brain surgeon Dr Viktor Frankenstein (it’s pronounced “Fron-ken-shteen!”) is embarrassed by his grandfather’s legacy. Yet who can resist the temptation to play God when reanimation seems within his grasp? This is Mel Brooks’ best movie, and an all-time comedy classic. Inspired by the 1930s Universal Frankenstein films, it’s beautifully shot in black and white. But ultimately this is about the genius clowning of Gene Wilder and a superb supporting cast (look out for Gene Hackman as a blind hermit).

films.title: Blazing Saddles
films.synopsis: Mel Brooks’ 1974 parody of westerns is one of the most successful and influential comedies ever made. It’s also one of the funniest. Two things are of note: by bringing a Jewish perspective to America’s Manifest Destiny myth it highlights the racism on which the country is founded. Blackness, here, is a powderkeg. Secondly, its anything-goes approach to race ensures the movie could never be made today, and runs the risk of censure from all sides. Cleavon Little, Gene Wilder and Madeline Kahn star.

films.title: Drive My Car
films.synopsis: Kafuku is a theatre director, actor, and storyteller... yet even he withdraws when it comes to confronting his deepest sorrow. Mourning his wife, and the secrets that died with her, he accepts an invitation to mount a new production of Uncle Vanya, and surprises everyone by casting a troubled young movie star, his late wife’s lover, in the title role. Elaborating on a short story by Haruki Murakami, Asako I & II director Hamaguchi has crafted a piercing, sublime philosophical drama. 4 Oscar Nominations In Japanese, Korean, English, Cantonese, Mandarin, Tagalog, Indonesian, German, and Malaysian

films.title: Alice
films.synopsis: Krystin Ver Linden’s kick-ass first film—which injects a funky blaxploitation vibe into a slave plantation scenario —features a jaw-dropping twist worthy of M Night Shyamalan or Jordan Peele. But it comes just half an hour in. If you like to be surprised by movies, this could be your jam... Alice (Keke Palmer) works in the fields for Paul Bennet (Jonny Lee Miller), a cotton farmer who keeps his slaves in line with brutal cruelty. Paul takes a shine to Alice, not realizing that she is ready to run...

films.title: Great Freedom
films.synopsis: In post-war Germany, liberation by the Allies does not mean freedom for everyone. Hans (Franz Rogowski, from Undine and Transit) is imprisoned again and again under Paragraph 175, a law criminalizing homosexuality. Over the course of decades, he develops an unlikely yet tender bond with his cellmate Viktor, a convicted murderer, a junkie and an avowed homophobe. “An exquisite marriage of personal, political and sensual storytelling.”

films.title: Ascension
films.synopsis: Filmed across 51 locations in China, Jessica Kingdon’s remarkable Ascension takes the pulse of the “Chinese Dream”, particularly as it relates to work, production, and the economic divide. In other words: class. Influenced by Godfrey Reggio’s Koyaanisqatsi and the pioneering Berlin: Symphony of a City, Kingdon builds her argument not through voice over, but through observation and montage. Score by Dan Deacon “Mesmerizing” CARLOS AGUILAR, ROGEREBERT.COM Nominated for the Academy Award for Best Documentary

films.title: Writing With Fire
films.synopsis: Winner of Best Documentary award at Sundance, and now nominated for the Academy Award, Sushmit Ghosh and Rintu Thomas’s film follows three genuinely intrepid women journalists from the “untouchables” caste as they break news and confront the powerful for their paper, Khabar Lahariya (Waves of News). In a society built on patriarchy and caste prejudice everything is stacked against them, but from this they draw strength. “The most inspiring journalism movie—maybe ever.” JASON REZAIAN, WASHINGTON POST Nominated for the Academy Award for Best Documentary

films.title: Tzouhalem
films.synopsis: British Columbia is belatedly waking up to the histories that we were not taught in school about this land, its peoples, privileges and prejudices. You could certainly be forgiven for not knowing the story of Tzhouhalem, (Ts’uwxilum), but this documentary about the great warrior chief of the Cowichan tribes should change that, for this larger than life figure is the stuff of popular myth. There will be a Q+A session following the March 12 screening with filmmakers Leslie Bland and Harold Joe.

films.title: The Learning Tree
films.synopsis: A bittersweet and idyllic story about a year in the life of a 14-year-old Newt Winger, born into a poor Black family in Kansas, who learns about love, fear, racial injustice, and immorality. When Gordon Parks translated his autobiographical 1965 novel to the screen, he became the first Black man to direct for a major Hollywood studio. Parks also produced, wrote the screenplay, and composed the score. Part of the Landmarks: Black Atlantic Independent Film 1961-1969 series. “A very beautiful and moving film.” AUSTIN VASHAW, CINAPSE

films.title: Wildhood
films.synopsis: When Link (Phillip Lewitski) discovers that, contrary to his abusive dad’s claims, his Mi’kmaw mother may still be alive, he and his half-brother Travis (Avery Winters-Anthony) finally have purpose. On the road to Mi’kma’ki, they pick up Pasmay (Joshua Odjick), a gregarious drifter who represents Link’s best chance of locating his mom and finally accepting his Two-Spirit nature. Bretten Hannam crafts a compelling road movie in which both the journey and destination offer opportunities for self-discovery. In English and Mi’kmaq

films.title: Donkeyhead
films.synopsis: Agam Darshi makes an impressive feature film debut as writer-director (and lead) in this emotionally wrenching drama. Mona (Darshi) is a writer who has put her ambitions on hold to care for her dad in the suburban Regina home where they grew up. But to her siblings, Mona’s doing what she always does: refusing to accept reality. Donkeyhead reverberates with a nuanced take on generational stress points in immigrant families, bereavement, sibling rivalry and the hardships of living up to your own best self. There will be a Q+A session following the March 12 screening with filmmaker Agam Darshi, actor Balinder Johal, and producer Anand Ramayya. Moderated by Baljit Sangra (Because We Are Girls).

films.title: After Yang
films.synopsis: In his second feature (after Columbus), Kogonada has crafted an achingly tender philosophical treatise on emotional connection based on a short sci-fistory by Alexander Weinstein. When his young daughter’s beloved companion—an android named Yang—malfunctions, Jake (Colin Farrell) searches for a way to repair him. In the process, Jake discovers the life that has been passing in front of him, reconnecting with his wife (Jodie Turner-Smith) and daughter across a distance he didn’t know was there.

films.title: Întregalde
films.synopsis: A trio of friends make their annual pilgrimage into the mountains of Transylvania with food boxes for the impoverished peasants who eke out a living in these remote parts. But when they pick up an old man asking for a lift they are soon lost without a phone signal, and, worse, stuck in the mud as night falls... It sounds like the set up to a horror movie, but this engrossing, witty Romanian film keeps things poised nicely on the edge between suspense, satire and drama.

films.title: Apollo 101⁄2: A Space Age Childhood
films.synopsis: 4:00PM, 8:10PM 5:20PM, 7:10PM Apollo 10½: A Space Age Childhood tells the story of the first moon landing in the summer of 1969 from two interwoven perspectives—the astronaut and mission control view of the triumphant moment, and through the eyes of a kid growing up in Houston, Texas who has intergalactic dreams of his own. Taking inspiration from Boyhood director Richard Linklater’s own life, Apollo 10½ is a snapshot of America in the 1960s that is part coming of age, part societal commentary, and part out-of-this-world adventure.

films.title: Ahed’s Knee
films.synopsis: In this Cannes Jury Prize winner, a celebrated Israeli filmmaker is pushed into a spiral of rage when a government employee asks him to sign a form restricting what he can say at a Q&A following a screening of his latest film at a remote desert library. Nadav Lapid (Synonyms; The Kindergarten Teacher) wrote the film soon after the death of his mother. It offers a sharp critique of the censorship, hypocrisy, and violence instigated by Israel and repressive governments everywhere.

films.title: The Big Scary ‘S’ Word
films.synopsis: Featuring interviews with Bernie Sanders, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Cornel West, and Naomi Klein, Yael Bridge’s film explores the rich though often unacknowledged history of the American socialist movement. Socialism led to public schools and Medicare, after all. Activists and journalists explain how the 2008 financial crisis, the Wall Street bailout, the Occupy Movement, and the ascension of politicians like Sanders and AOC have pushed a new generation to embrace the language of socialism.

films.title: Atlantis
films.synopsis: Set in a devastated Ukraine in 2025, “a year after the war”, this 2019 Venice prize-winner is an astonishingly vivid vision of love among the ruins. Structured as a series of artfully composed tableaux, the film tells the story of Sergey, a former soldier suffering from PTSD. When the foundry where he has been working closes, he joins a volunteer outfit exhuming the battlefields—which is where he meets Katya, a former architect. Despite the bleak surroundings Vasyanovych finds unexpected shards of hope.

films.title: Uptight
films.synopsis: This month’s selection in Nya Lewis’s Landmarks series is a punchy political suspense thriller set against the violent years of the Civil Rights movement, directed by blacklistee Jules Dassin from a script by Ruby Dee and Julian Mayfield. We are in Cleveland, 1968, in the wake of the assassination of Dr King. A group of militants steal guns from a warehouse, but a guard is killed in the robbery and Tank (Mayfield), an alcoholic, snitches on the killer. For this, he becomes the prey of his former comrades. Part of the Landmarks: Black Atlantic Independent Film 1961-1969 series.

films.title: The Viewing Booth
films.synopsis: The Viewing Booth recounts a unique encounter between a filmmaker and a viewer—exploring the way meaning is attributed to non-fiction images. A young Jewish American woman, Maia Levy, is shown watching videos of life in the Occupied West Bank. An enthusiastic supporter of Israel, Maia processes and comments on these images in ways which may surprise and dismay the audience watching her... “One of the smartest documentaries I’ve seen in years” MARK GLASSMAN, POV

films.title: Dune
films.synopsis: Timothée Chalamet leads a remarkable cast in one of the most anticipated films of the year. Adapting Frank Herbert’s legendary novel for a true big-screen experience, Denis Villeneuve confirms his status as that rarest of artists, a visionary maker of blockbusters. Dune delivers a complete immersion into new, spectacular worlds. Nominated for 10 Academy Awards

films.title: The Conversation
films.synopsis: Gene Hackman is Harry Caul, ‘the best bugger on the West Coast’, a surveillance expert whose jealously guarded anonymity is threatened when he happens across what seems to be a murder plot. Francis Coppola’s existential thriller had the commercial good fortune to coincide with the public airing of the Watergate tapes, but the soul-searching here is intensely personal. Walter Murch created the brilliant, densely layered sound design.

films.title: Revolution of Our Times
films.synopsis: 2:00PM, 7:00PM This clandestine account of the massive Hong Kong democracy protests which brought a million citizens out onto the streets in 2019 is riveting viewing. Director Kiwi Chow was there in the midst of the epochal moment, and with the help of a wide array of interviewees (many of them masked or digitally camouflaged) presents a fascinating chronicle of how the movement sprang into being, evolved and organized itself in the face of brutal authoritarian repression.

films.title: Sundown
films.synopsis: Neil (Tim Roth), his sister Alice (Charlotte Gainsbourg) and her two teens are vacationing in Acapulco when they learn their mother has taken seriously ill back in the UK. They pack up in a frenzy - but at the airport Neil doesn’t have his passport, and the others leave without him. It’s a lie. He has no intention of going back. Instead he checks into another hotel, pulls out a deck chair, and starts working through a case of beer... A compellingly terse existential mystery from Michel Franco (New Order).

films.title: Rendez-Vous French Film Festival presents... Au revoir le bonheur
films.synopsis: Starbuck writer-director Ken Scott returns with a comedy about four grown brothers trying to put aside their differences to pay their final respects to their late father... but they are so very, very different. This one-offscreening is a partnership between VIFF and the Rendez-Vous French Film Festival, part of their Les Rendez-Vous du Printemps series. “A good time.” MANON DUMAIS, LE DEVOIR

films.title: Big Giant Wave
films.synopsis: The earth is music... Life is music... The heartbeat is a drumbeat. Produced by the late Jean-Marc Vallee, Big Giant Wave creates a cinematic tapestry of sight and sound, reminding us the essence of what it is to be human. Come. Sit. Surrender to the sensations and let us take you there. In French, English, Dari, and Spanish

films.title: Cow
films.synopsis: 2:30PM, 7:00PM The first documentary from Andrea Arnold (American Honey, Fish Tank) allows us to get to know a farm animal

films.title: Forgotten Warriors
films.synopsis: What does “Canada” mean to the Indigenous peoples of this land? In this mid-length 1997 documentary from Loretta Todd (Monkey Beach) we meet Indigenous men and women who volunteered to serve in the fight against Hitler during the second world war. For those who survived, their reward was often racism, exclusion, and even punishment, as Treaty land was parceled off for settler veterans. Todd’s poignant film features archival footage and the moving testimony of those who were there.

films.title: Islands + short film: Kalinga
films.synopsis: Still living with his aging parents, Joshua, a Filipino immigrant to Canada, prays every night for God to rid him of his shyness. The Almighty seemingly answers his petition when his beatific cousin Marisol arrives and slowly transforms Joshua’s house back into a home. As Joshua is lured from his shell, Martin Edralin fashions a disarmingly tender, deeply nuanced character study that achieves an exquisite balance of gentle humour and humane drama.

films.title: L’Inhumain
films.synopsis: We’re capping off National Canadian Film Day with a free preview of a new feature from Anishinaabé filmmaker Jason Brennan. Matthieu (Samian) is a successful neurosurgeon, with a beautiful wife and child, a sexy mistress, and a bad pill-popping habit. His life falling apart, he’s called North for his father’s funeral, and reluctantly agrees to return to the cabin where he grew up in order dispose of the ashes. There his fraught nerves and blackouts come face to face with his worst nightmare: Wendingo. In French, English, and Anishinaabemowin

films.title: Scarborough
films.synopsis: Adapted by Catherine Hernandez from her own acclaimed novel (inspired by her own experiences working in a neighbourhood literacy centre), this is the story of three children: Bing (Liam Diaz), a gifted Filipino boy struggling with his sexuality; Sylvie (Essence Fox), an Indigenous girl whose brother may be developmentally delayed; and Laura (Anna Claire Beitel), a blonde who is bounced between her parents and who can’t yet read. The mode here is social realism, but the emotional pay offis something else.

films.title: Stories We Tell
films.synopsis: Ten years on, Sarah Polley’s deeply personal essay film is widely considered to be among the best Canadian films of the past quarter century. Stories We Tell revolves around a few key questions: Who was my mother? Who is my father? Have I been told the truth? What is truth? Subjective questions, but such is the formal inventiveness of the film and its deft interplay of subjectivities that subjectivity itself is transcended.

films.title: Spring & Arnaud
films.synopsis: Influential photographer Arnaud Maggs, turning 85, embarks on a series of self-portraits that wryly depict his life’s work. Spring Hurlbut, at 60 is creating haunting works that evoke mortality while harboring the certainty that Arnaud’s time is limited. Together more than 25 years, each grapples with the nature of an artist’s creativity where the drive for invention and discovery resists life’s finite reality. Filmmaker Katherine Knight will attend screenings April 9 and 10.

films.title: Still Max
films.synopsis: Winner of the Audience Award at Hot Docs, this is a lovely film about mortality and art, the creative expression of the joy of living and the impermanence of things. Katherine Knight encounters Canadian artist Max Dean in Toronto, defiant in the face of prostate cancer, even as his partner is diagnosed with aggressive ovarian cancer. Taking inspiration from his disease, Dean takes a hard look at his own body, which is also, of course, our own. Filmmaker Q&A April 8 (with Max Dean), 9 and 10th.

films.title: Final Account
films.synopsis: Luke Holland’s film is an urgent portrait of the last living generation of everyday people to participate in Adolf Hitler’s Third Reich. Over a decade in the making, the film raises vital, timely questions about authority, conformity, complicity and guilt, national identity, and responsibility, as men and women ranging from former SS members to civilians reckon with their memories, perceptions and personal appraisals of their own roles in the greatest human crimes in history.

films.title: Between Two Worlds
films.synopsis: Juliette Binoche plays a reporter who goes undercover working as a cleaner on a ferry to understand the plight of the underclass during the economic downturn. But is her subterfuge another form of exploitation? Emmanuel Carrère’s film is Ken Loach—or Nomadland—with a French philosophical dimension. “Visually hypnotic, laugh-out-loud funny and emotionally devastating... I confess, I spent most of the second half sobbing.” CHARLOTTE O’SULLIVAN, EVENING STANDARD

films.title: Portrait of Jason
films.synopsis: Shirley Clarke’s 1967 documentary rounds out Nya Lewis’s programme Landmarks: Black Atlantic Independent Film 1961-69. Captured in the heat of the civil rights era and three years before Stonewall, Portrait... was shot in a single all-night session in Clarke’s apartment as a behindthe-scenes look at the life of a Black gay sex worker Jason Holliday. A turning point for queer representation on film, Holliday turns Clarke’s questioning on its head, delivering profound and fiercely courageous monologues.

films.title: Hit the Road
films.synopsis: 2:30PM, 7:45PM In his feature debut, Panah Panahi turns the road movie on its head. Hit the Road is the story of one family and their mysterious journey through rural Iran; along the way, there are laughs, moments of reverie, and plenty of opportunities for the cast to shine. The son of famed auteur Jafar Panahi, Panah shares his father’s subversiveness, and he has a similarly sharp camera eye; the wacky humour and the fantastical digressions, however, are his alone.

films.title: Koyaanisqatsi
films.synopsis: A quarter century before An Inconvenient Truth, filmmaker Godfrey Reggio set out to show the dichotomy between the natural world and the technological civilization that was paving over the planet. He did so in a film without words, using a stream of images that becomes a river, a flood, a tidal wave of beauty and disaster, each step synchronized to a mesmerizing original score by Philip Glass (his first), sounds and images tripping over into an altogether new language of time-lapse transcendentalism...

films.title: Earth Day: Going Circular
films.synopsis: Maybe the most optimistic climate emergency film we have seen, Going Circular suggests the paradigm shift that would save the planet is staring us in the face. 102-year-old inventor Dr James Lovelock, biomimicry biologist Janine Benyus, engineer and designer Arthur Huang, and financier John Fullerton are among the key thinkers who embrace the concept of circularity, an economic system based on the idea that nothing should go to waste—and which already exists throughout the natural world.

films.title: One Night Only: Huda’s Salon
films.synopsis: Inspired by real events from the 1980s, the latest from the Academy Award-nominated Hany Abu-Assad (Omar; Paradise Now) is a tense thriller depicting how Israeli security services compromise and blackmail Arab women into becoming double agents. From their perspective, Huda (Manal Awad) is ideally placed, running a hair salon in Bethlehem. Blackmailed, she in turn chooses vulnerable women who can be targeted; women like Reem (Maisa Abd Elhadi), whose jealous husband would never stand for scandal...

films.title: One Night Only: Justin Kurzel’s Nitram
films.synopsis: STARTS MAY 6 Caleb Landry Jones (Get Out) won the Best Actor award at Cannes last year for his performance as “Nitram”, a socially awkward, intellectually disabled young man living with his parents (Judy Davis and Anthony LaPaglia) in Australia. In a surprise turn of events, Nitram meets Helen, an eccentric, much older and very wealthy woman who takes a shine to him. The latest from the exciting Australian director Justin Kurzel is patient, discreet, compassionate and disturbing. Winner: 8 Australian Academy Awards

films.title: Enter the Void
films.synopsis: Venturing where angels fear to tread, virtuoso filmmaker Gaspar Noé creates a dazzling journey into the Tokyo night, a mind-bending exploration of the outer reaches of human experience inspired by the Tibetan Book of the Dead. This day-glo nocturne is told through the eyes of an American dope-dealer, Oscar, tripping on a powerful hallucinogen. That is, until Oscar is shot in a nightclub, when the film takes on the aspect of an out of body experience. “A capital M masterpiece.” MARK HARRIS, GEORGIA STRAIGHT

films.title: Je t’aime moi non plus
films.synopsis: Rough translation: “I love you, me neither,” the title of Serge Gainsbourg’s hit song—and also the name of his first film as writer-director, starring his wife Jane Birkin. She’s Johnny, a waitress in desert truck stop cafe. Enter Krass (Warhol star Joe Dallesandro), a haulage driver

films.title: Playground
films.synopsis: One of the most vivid and authentic films about childhood ever made, Laura Wandel’s first feature puts us in the shoes of seven-year-old Nora (Maya Vanderbeque) on her first day at a new school. She soon learns some hard truths: School is a battleground where dog eats dog and Darwin’s survival of the fittest theorem is enacted every time the bell rings. “A knockout, as flawlessly constructed as it is harrowing. A work of striking integrity and force.”

films.title: Jane by Charlotte
films.synopsis: Charlotte Gainsbourg’s film is a portrait of her mother, the English-born, Serge Gainsbourg-wed Jane Birkin, a singer, movie star and sex symbol in the sixties with films like Blow Up and Je t’aime, moi non plus (also showing at the VIFF Centre this week). It’s clear from the film both how much mother and daughter share—Charlotte too, is an actor and singer, and exudes a mixture of candour and diffidence which appears to be a Birkin characteristic - and that they’re not as close as they might like to be.

films.title: Happening
films.synopsis: Audrey Diwan’s Venice Film Festival top prize-winner is an unfalteringly empathetic portrait of Anne, a talented student whose academic career is derailed by an unwanted pregnancy. In seeking termination Anne is forced to venture into a shadowy backstreet world where help carries considerable risk. We are in France in the early 1960s, and abortion is illegal... And we are in 2022, and reproductive rights are being rolled back across the US. This immensely moving film dares us not to avert our eyes.

films.title: The Rose Maker
films.synopsis: Eve (Catherine Frot) has dedicated her life to growing roses. But her small independent farm faces bankruptcy. Her assistant has the smart idea to bring in three convicts serving social rehab to help out, and indeed, while they lack horticultural experience, the trio do bring other useful skills to the table... With its picturesque charms, gentle humanism and likable cast this sweetly aromatic sentimental comedy definitely grows on you.

films.title: The Family of the Forest
films.synopsis: Gérard and Catherine sacrificed family, friends and their homeland for a life of self-sufficiency deep in the boreal forest of Québec: building their own home, planting fruit and veg, rearing animals, foraging in the woods. Now, as their three sons become young adults, what will happen to this remarkable life they’ve given everything to create? Laura Rietveld’s exquisitely beautiful film ponders the hard work, the paradoxes and intangible rewards of going back to the land and living in harmony with nature.

films.title: Vortex
films.synopsis: 3:00PM, 6:00PM 3:00PM, 7:45PM 3:00PM, 6:00PM 4:30PM, 7:15PM 4:30PM, 7:15PM 4:30PM, 7:15PM 4:30PM, 7:15PM Reminiscent of Amour, Gaspar Noé’s superb film compels us to look at aspects of life we too often shy away from: declining cognitive powers, the strains and stresses it places on an elderly married couple, played by the Italian filmmaker Dario Argento and the French actress Françoise Lebrun (The Mother and the Whore), and on their only child (Alex Lutz). One of narrative cinema’s great experimentalists, Noé conveys the isolation of dementia by shooting the film in split-screen. It’s a master stroke.

films.title: Lux Aeterna
films.synopsis: In 2019 Gaspar Noé was commissioned to make a 15 minute commercial for Yves Saint-Laurent. Somehow, Noé being Noé, it turned into a 51-minute faux verite satire on moviemaking, with Beatrice Dalle and Charlotte Gainsbourg nominally playing themselves on the set of a postmodern witchcraft movie, “God’s Work”. Dalle is apparently the director, but behind her back the producer and DP are scheming to have her fired—leaving the star in a difficult position. Warning: Extended sequences of flashing lights.

films.title: Hello, Bookstore
films.synopsis: In the shadow of the pandemic, a small town rallies to protect a beloved local bookstore. A landmark in Lenox, Massachusetts, The Bookstore is a magical, beatnik gem thanks to its owner, Matt Tannenbaum, whose passion for stories runs deep. This intimate portrait of a literary treasure offers a journey through good times, hard times, and the stories hidden on the shelves. “Compelling and heartwarming. A drama worthy of Hollywood magic created by Frank Capra and Jimmy Stewart.”

films.title: Mau
films.synopsis: Bruce Mau believes we can change the world, and he’s certainly playing his part. From humble roots, he has become a talismanic designer, assigned projects that range from remapping Mecca to reimagining the country of Guatemala. A visionary, Mau is a pragmatist who dreams outside the box and inspires others to do the same. His conviction that radical transformation is within our grasp makes him an essential voice for our times. Also featured: Rem Koolhaus, Bjarke Ingels, Paola Antonelli.

films.title: Revue Starlight - The Movie
films.synopsis: Plunge into the world of the Stage Girls... Entertainers-in-training with a passion for song, dance, swordplay and Shakespeare. Imagine Japanese Idol, on acid.

films.title: The Addiction
films.synopsis: Lili Taylor, Christopher Walken, and director Abel Ferrara team up for this stylized triumph of 1990s indie horror that mashes up Godard, Bram Stoker, and East Coast hip-hop. As the “Disneyfication” of New York City takes root, a morbid grad student (Taylor) is bitten by a vampire seductress (Annabella Sciorra) and must navigate the shadows while tempering her growing addiction to blood. The Addiction sees Ferrara on his own terms and at his very best: raw, shocking, intelligent, and masterful.

films.title: Videodrome
films.synopsis: James Woods is Max Renn, a satellite broadcaster who stumbles across a signal broadcasting snuffcontent. He is repulsed and fascinated, and especially when he becomes involved withS&M advocate Nicki Brand (Debbie Harry). The deeper he goes down this rabbit hole, the more tenuous Max’s grasp of reality becomes. Videodrome explores the hypothesis, what if transgressive images really do pervert the viewer...? In our days of Q conspiracies and all-pervasive propaganda that idea is not so easily dismissed.

films.title: Dead Ringers
films.synopsis: Jeremy Irons gives two of the best performances of his career as identical twins Beverly and Elliott Mantle. Top gynecologists, they share everything... including the patients Elliott seduces, and eventually passes on to his brother. But when Beverly falls in love with one of them (Geneviève Bujold), this convenient if unethical arrangement begins to fall apart... Dead Ringers isn’t really a horror movie, but it’s a deeply disturbing and upsetting watch, without doubt one of Cronenberg’s strongest films.

films.title: Dual
films.synopsis: Diagnosed with a terminal illness, Sarah (Karen Gillan) employs some suspect technology to clone herself so that she isn’t missed. But after a miraculous recovery, she must challenge her other self to a duel in order to reclaim her old life and loved ones. Delighting in affectless deliveries and attention to absurd details, Riley Stearns (The Art of Self-Defense) ratchets up the stakes and the absurdity while maintaining a deadpan register in this stone-faced reminder that life is worth fighting for.

films.title: Resurrection
films.synopsis: Rebecca Hall gives a mesmerising performance as Margaret, an executive and single mother who psychologically unravels when a malevolent figure from her past (Tim Roth) returns to torment her. Recalling classic psychological thrillers like Repulsion and Possession, Andrew Semans’ tilt-a-whirl of terror keeps viewers disoriented for every gripping minute of its running time. As Margaret’s world grows increasingly nightmarish, Hall devastates us

films.title: We’re All Going to the World’s Fair
films.synopsis: In her attic bedroom, teenage Casey (Anna Cobb) ventures through the veritable looking glass by taking the “World’s Fair Challenge”, an online ritual/role-playing game purported to spark supernatural transformations in its players. But are the ensuing symptoms simply the fantasies of an alienated young woman who desperately wants to be part of something beyond her comprehension? Jane Schoenbrun’s film explores the genuine horrors lurking within virtual realms and their infinite rabbit holes.

films.title: The Fly
films.synopsis: Cronenberg’s tragi-comic parable about genetic mutation, this is also a love story, a film about fusion in which the connection between man and woman (Jeff Goldblum and Geena Davis) is more important than man and insect. The playful, quirky chemistry established between the stars (they married soon after) ensures that this gothic horror is heartbreaking as well as stomach churning, though the special effects by Chris Walas remain staggering even today.

films.title: Slash/Back
films.synopsis: 4:20PM, 8:30PM Sleepy Pangnirtung, Nunavut transforms into a chaotic battleground when Inuit teens confront alien invaders who’ve slithered into the skins of local policemen and wildlife. Drawing from Hollywood classics like The Thing and traditional Inuit stories of the shapeshifting Ijiraq, Nyla Innuksuk’s exuberant debut harnesses genre cinema’s allegorical power to revisit colonial histories and explore contemporary Indigeneity while also delivering enough suspense and spectacle to put many studio efforts to shame.

films.title: Flux Gourmet
films.synopsis: Peter Strickland (In Fabric; The Duke of Burgundy) returns with this drolly deranged and outrageously debauched tale of a “sonic catering” collective looking to refine their performance art while coping with their own disfunction and the machinations of their duplicitous benefactor. Serving up Strickland’s house specialties of alluring visuals, sensational textures, wicked absurdity, and unsettling sound design, this Gastronomic Guignol sees this singular director’s hallucinatory wavelengths cranked to 11.

films.title: Honeycomb
films.synopsis: When teenaged Willow stumbles across a decrepit cabin in the wilderness, she convinces four friends to abandon their lives in favour of creating a world of their own design. Instead, they succumb to age-old resentments and temptations and their commune distorts into something akin to a cult. Shot on Cortes Island by Avalon Fast and her young cast and crew, Honeycomb shifts from sardonic to dream-like to downright sinister. This DIY gem is an increasingly bad trip that proves to be one hell of a ride.

films.title: Piggy
films.synopsis: The victim of unrelenting bullying due to her weight, Sara (Laura Galán) is unexpectedly recast as an accomplice to a deranged kidnapper (Richard Holmes) who is targeting her abusive peers. Uncompromising and unflinching, Carlota Pereda’s troubling morality tale is the furthest thing from an easy watch. But, in boldly confronting social ills and calling on viewers to question their own capacity for cruelty, it possesses the courage of its convictions as it rattles you to the core.

films.title: Montana Story
films.synopsis: Cal (Owen Teague) is reunited with his alienated sister Erin (Haley Lu Richardson), still burning with anger and resentment even as their father lies dying in a coma at the broken down ranch where they grew up. Erin has her reasons, and the siblings circle each other cagily as they try to make the least bad choices in the face of an upcoming foreclosure. The latest from Deep End/What Maisie Knew team Scott McGehee and David Siegel is an absorbing, authentic family drama; subtle, understated and deeply felt.

films.title: Babysitter
films.synopsis: When a misogynist (Patrick Hivon) is suspended for accosting a television reporter and stuck at home with his exhausted wife (director Monia Chokri) and infant daughter, he cajoles his brother (Steve Laplante) into cowriting a memoir that will prove his newfound feminist credentials. But then a new babysitter (Nadia Terezkiewicz) blows into town and bewitches them all. Chokri pulls out the stylistic stops to create a freewheeling satire which has been aptly described as “screwball surrealism”.

films.title: Hatching
films.synopsis: When 12-year-old Tinja (Siiri Solalinna) nurtures an oversized egg until it hatches, an otherworldly changeling emerges, quickly becoming the lonely girl’s devoted companion and slowly morphing into her macabre doppelgänger. Director Hanna Bergholm demonstrates her panache with practical effects, innate understanding of which body horror buttons to push, and deftness

films.title: Jazz Fest: A New Orleans Story
films.synopsis: 4:00PM, 8:10PM 7000 musicians on 14 stages over 8 days... Jazz Fest, New Orleans takes some beating. This scintillating doc traces its first 50 years, its unique roots in the crucible of American music, the devastation wrought by Hurricane Katrina and incalculable highs from an incredible, eclectic array of performers (everyone from Irma Thomas to Katy Perry, Wynton Marsalis to Pitbull, Herbie Hancock to Earth, Wind & Fire).

films.title: A Chiara
films.synopsis: Calabria, Italy. A bomb goes offoutside Chiara’s home on the occasion of her sister’s 18th birthday; after this, she will never see the world the same way again. Her happy, loving home harbours dark secrets. Her father, it turns out, is part of the notorious ‘Ndrangheta mafia clan. How Chiara reacts to these revelations—and the way that various parties respond to her crisis—is the meat of this impressive, gripping film from Jonas Carpignano. “Enthralling... a touching, powerful film.” THE FILM STAGE In Italian and Calabrian dialect

films.title: La Traviata, from the Royal Opera House
films.synopsis: Richard Eyre’s stunning 1994 production of Verdi’s bestloved opera returns to the Royal Opera House for the umpteenth time... There is a reason it keeps coming back, this most sublime of operas is sumptuously furnished, balancing spectacle and emotion with rare delicacy. Pretty Yende plays Yvette, with Stephen Costello as Alfredo.

films.title: Unidentified
films.synopsis: 1:30PM, 6:20PM Two hotels have burned down, no small coincidence... Detective Florin Iespas (Bogdan Farcas) is convinced he can crack the case, and tries to persuade his boss to let him do just that while the assigned detective is away on leave. He’s turned down, but persists, fixating on the Roma security guard as his prime suspect. But Detective Iespas’s own motives are murkier than they first appear... A terse, tense thriller reminiscent of the twisted noir novels of Jim Thompson, from the director of Miracle. “A dark, propulsive thriller....”

films.title: The Thing (1982)
films.synopsis: BOGDAN GEORGE APETRI, ROMANIA/CZECH REPUBLIC/ LATVIA, 2021, 118 MIN. 4:00PM, 8:40PM In Miracle, Unidentified director Bogdan George Apetri returns to the same area in northern Romania. This time he tells the story of a novice nun, Cristina (Ioana Bugarin). In the film’s first half, she slips out of the convent to journey to the nearest city—for reasons which only gradually become clear. In the film’s second half, her steps are retraced by a police inspector (Emanuel Pârvu) who believes he knows the true story, but lacks the evidence to prove it... “Miracle lives up to its name, seamlessly blending narrative, style and technique with devastating results. Simple in scope, yet complex and precise in its execution, the result is a marvel befitting its title.”

films.title: Benediction
films.synopsis: Achingly intimate, visually sumptuous, and richly detailed, the latest from Terence Davies is a portrait of WWI poet Siegfried Sassoon. The subversive writer is played in old age by Peter Capaldi and in younger years by Jack Lowden; both give superb performances, and they’re matched by the rest of the ensemble cast. The real star, however, is Davies himself: with his musical treatment of images and his sublime articulation of emotion, he delivers a tour de force of filmmaking. “Achingly beautiful... a movie of acute sadness and intense pleasure.” JUSTIN CHANG, LA TIMES

films.title: The Passengers of the Night
films.synopsis: Elizabeth (Charlotte Gainsbourg) has given herself to her two children and her husband. But the marriage is over, and the kids are teenagers, on the cusp of making their own way. Now, in the middle of life, Elizabeth needs to do that too: to make a living, and, simply, to live. On a whim, she writes to the host of her favourite late night radio call-in (Emmanuelle Béart). Meanwhile, her teenage son becomes involved with a runaway girl, Talulah (Noée Abita), one of the radio show’s callers... “A panoramic, novelistic, decade-spanning portrait of a French family pulling together through troubled times. A love letter to the Paris of yesteryear. Gainsbourg is always a magnetic presence on screen, her hypersensitive emotional antennae forever twitching on the edge of tearful breakdown.” STEPHEN DALTON, THE FILM VERDICT

films.title: Blue Island
films.synopsis: “What does Hong Kong mean to you...?” That’s the question hanging over Chan Tze Woon’s memorable film. Blue Island takes a longer view on China’s authoritarian crackdown on the democracy movement. Chan draws parallels between today’s struggle and the arrival of refugees from mainland China 50 years ago fleeing the Cultural Revolution, while also looking at the impact of Tiananmen Square and the Umbrella protests as he explores the unique identity of the city and its people. In Cantonese, Mandarin, and English with English subtitles. Best International Documentary, Hot Docs 2022

films.title: Bitterbrush
films.synopsis: Even cowgirls get the blues... Hollyn and Colie have troubles like everybody else, but their job is unusual. For five (or is it six?) summers now, they have contracted to herd cattle across Idaho’s mountainous open range: just the two of them, their horses, their dogs, and landscapes that stretch for millennia.

films.title: Over the Edge
films.synopsis: When we asked Slash/Back filmmaker Nyla Innuksuk to nominate two movies which influenced her, we anticipated that she would come back with John Carpenter’s The Thing (screening Friday 24th), but her second choice came as a surprise – even if, in retrospect, it makes perfect sense. Over the Edge was never a commercial success, although it did get a second theatrical release in 1981 at the clamouring of fans who discovered the movie on HBO. The debut of Matt Dillon, this is a potent portrait of teen delinquents bored and ignored in a desolate Colorado “planned community,” a suburban tract designed to keep the middle class safe and secure – so long as they’re not kids. The more the adults crack down on them, the harder the teenagers kick back at them. Director Jonathan Kaplan was a graduate of Roger Corman exploitation movies (and before that, a student of Martin Scorsese) who would go on to make The Accused and some 40 episodes of ER. Screenwriter Tim Hunter would also carve out a long career directing in TV (including episodes of Twin Peaks) but not before directing another exceptionally dark and arresting teen movie, River’s Edge. Although the film was not a box office hit, it absolutely hit a nerve, and remains relevant to this day.

films.title: Run Woman Run
films.synopsis: Curated by Rylan Friday (Plains Cree & Saulteaux Ojibway, Cote First Nation), Finding Our Truth features work from First Nations and allied filmmakers, centering on Indigenous narratives with strong female leads, coupled with humour, determination, strength and resiliency. The films highlighted in this series challenge pervasive stereotypes by expressing the diversity of Indigenous experience—whether they are framed as historical or contemporary, speak to gender equality and sexuality, or are based in urban or rural settings, and all showcase Indigeneity in an equally authentic manner. In honour of National Indigenous Peoples Day, the screenings of Beans and Run Woman Run are free to Indigenous Peoples. When we asked Slash/Back filmmaker Nyla Innuksuk to nominate two movies which influenced her, we anticipated that she would come back with John Carpenter’s The Thing, but her second choice came as a surprise— even if, in retrospect, it makes perfect sense. The debut of Matt Dillon, Over the Edge is a potent portrait of teen delinquents bored and ignored in a desolate Colorado “planned community,” a suburban tract designed to keep the middle class safe and secure—so long as they’re not kids. The more the adults crack down on them, the harder the teenagers kick back at them. Filmed in Stewart, British Columbia, and legendary for the shocking creature fx created by Rob Bottin, the 1982 The Thing is now widely perceived as a classic in its own right, one of the scariest films ever made. National Indigenous Peoples Day

films.title: The Velvet Underground
films.synopsis: Todd Haynes and the Velvet Underground... This is a dream combo, and the movie does not disappoint. Haynes (I’m Not There) strips away the formal orthodoxies of the rock doc, recreating the alchemical experimentalism which ignited the New York art scene in the 60s, avant-garde music, film, poetry and pop art. “As a documentary, it’s wonderfully informative. It’s also a jagged and powerful work of art in its own right, one that turns archaeology into prophecy.” AO SCOTT, THE NEW YORK TIMES

films.title: Songs for Drella
films.synopsis: In 1990 former Velvet Underground bandmates Lou Reed and John Cale reunited to record a song cycle about their mentor Andy Warhol, who had died three years earlier. The cinematographer Ed Lachman—who had shot David Byrne’s True Stories and was much later DP on Todd Haynes’ Velvet Underground doc- was invited to film the record’s first live outing. The result is a hushed, barbed, deeply moving and often sublime concert film which—for various reasons—has gone virtually unseen for the best three decades.

films.title: Clara Sola
films.synopsis: As if a mythical being has graced the Costa Rican village, everyone is inexplicably drawn to Clara’s magnetic orbit, including her beloved mare, Yuca. Likewise, when Clara starts to rebel against her oppressive religious upbringing, her wrath reverberates with equal force. This deeply evocative, mesmerizing feature debut by Nathalie Álvarez Mesén has been drawing easy parallels to Brian de Palma’s Carrie, but also fuses coming-of-age elements with feminism, mysticism, and Gaianism for a visceral ride.

films.title: Lost Illusions
films.synopsis: Winner of 7 Cesar awards including Best Film, this adaptation of Balzac’s Illusions perdues is a lavish costume drama with a thoroughly modern bite, a tragi-comedy about a young romantic poet who arrives in Paris with his aristocratic mistress full of hope and conviction and discovers a world as corrupt and treacherous as any sinkhole of iniquity. “Sensational... if there’s any justice this movie will become a touchstone among the grasping, scheming denizens of the current media jungle.”

films.title: Drunken Birds
films.synopsis: When Willy (Jorge Antonio Guerrero), a Mexican cartel henchman, falls for Marlena (Yoshira Escárrega), his boss’ wife, the star-crossed lovers must separate and go to ground. Convinced that Marlena is secreted away in Montreal, Willy becomes a migrant worker at a Quebec farm. Employing an intricate narrative structure and visually arresting sequences, Ivan Grbovic examines how new beginnings often run afoul of cycles of exploitation. Impressionistic yet immediate, Drunken Birds is exhilarating cinema.

films.title: Prism Prize Recipients 2022: Canada’s Best Music Videos (Free Screening)
films.synopsis: Come enjoy the Best Canadian Music Videos of the year as determined by a jury of 120 film and music industry professionals for the annual Prism Prize. The top ten shortlist includes work by BADBADNOTGOOD, Chad VanGaalen, Debby Friday, Mustafa, and The Beaches. You haven’t really seen these videos until you’ve seen them on the big screen, with top of the line projection and sound, at the VIFF Centre.

films.title: Mean Streets
films.synopsis: This is where Martin Scorsese hit his stride. After a decade on the brink, the man who had once contemplated entering the priesthood made his breakthrough by bringing it all back home: Little Italy, NYC, 1973. Here we find Charlie Cappa (Harvey Keitel), diligently making his way in the mob, looking out for his fuckup cousin Johnny Boy (Robert De Niro), and secretly carrying on with Johnny’s epileptic sister, Teresa (Amy Robinson). At the same time, he’s telling it like it is to the Lord: “It’s all bullshit apart from the pain…” How deeply did Scorsese identify with Charlie? In his prayers, the actor’s voice is mixed in with the director’s to the point where they become one. Mean Streets is a pilgrim’s progress which ends in a vision of hell – appropriately, given this particular pilgrim’s shortcomings. But let’s not overlook the film’s exuberance, the dynamic, inventive camerawork (including the greatest drunk scene ever shot), the inspired use of rock, and the hilarious comic shtick between Keitel and a firecracker De Niro. In the push and pull between these two characters we find the first embodiments of the dynamic which agitates so much of Scorsese’s work between the intellectual and the animalistic, the repressed and the anarchic, the sacred and the profane. Raymond Chandler was right: Down these Mean Streets a man must go… Scorsese’s Taxi Driver is also screening in our Ragged Glory: Summer in the 70s series.

films.title: The Long Goodbye
films.synopsis: Leigh Brackett – who wrote many of Howard Hawks’ best movies, including The Big Sleep – adapted Chandler’s most ambitious novel for director Robert Altman, updating the story to contemporary (1973) Los Angeles. As played by Elliott Gould, brilliantly, Philip Marlowe emerges as a shambling anachronism, whose apologetic catchphrase, “It’s okay with me”, is the very opposite of what he means. It’s another movie – like Altman’s near contemporaraneous western, McCabe & Mrs Miller – in conversation with Hollywood of yore, reflecting a decidedly jaundiced view of the present. “A satire in melancholy,” Altman called it. Look for an uncredited cameo by Arnold Schwarzenegger as one of the hoods, and listen out for composer John Williams’ endless variations on the theme tune, it’s one of the most remarkable scores in his illustrious career. Robert Altman’s McCabe & Mrs Miller and Nashville also feature in Ragged Glory: Summer in the 70s. For more films in our Crime Scenes sidebar, look out for Chinatown, The Parallax View, Night Moves, The Late Show and Mikey and Nicky, Thursday nights through the summer.

films.title: Chinatown
films.synopsis: When Bogart played Philip Marlowe, the detective was a white knight, troubled but untainted by the corruption he encounters at every turn on the mean streets of Los Angeles. Jack Nicholson’s Jake Gittes is an altogether seedier proposition, a two-bit snoop whose cynicism may be his best quality. He spends most of Chinatown jumping to wrong conclusions about what crimes have been committed, by whom, and for what reasons. He’s in over his head, but even that’s beyond him. He keeps on going and only makes matters worse. Chinatown is one of those gold-plated classics, a masterpiece that was recognized as a cut above the rest immediately on its release in 1974 (rave reviews; 11 Academy Award nominations) and which has only grown in stature over the years. It doesn’t hurt that it’s also weirdly timeless, set in 1937 and evoking the private eye film noir genres associated with Raymond Chandler and Humphrey Bogart… it’s a classicist’s classic. And of course its reputation was bolstered by the estimation of Syd Field in his seminal film school tome “Screenplay”, first published in 1979, that this was the best written film of the decade. Recent scholarship has revealed a more complicated authorship: movies are made by alchemy, not men. But Chinatown still resonates with our time just as it did back in the mid-70s. John Huston – who plays rich landowner Noah Cross – had directed one of the first film noirs in Hollywood, The Maltese Falcon, back in 1941. He was still making great films in the 70s, including Fat City, also showing in our Ragged Glory: Summer in the 70s series.

films.title: A New Leaf
films.synopsis: It didn’t make the telecast, but the American Academy presented Elaine May with an honorary Oscar this year. It was long overdue. May was (and is) a trailblazer. She found fame in the 60s in her comedy partnership with Mike Nichols. He went to Hollywood and made The Graduate. She adapted a short story by Jack Ritchie about a wealthy, timid, socially maladroit botanist, Henrietta, who is wooed and won by an unscrupulous cad, Henry, a rich playboy who has run through his family funds and intent on finding a wife to keep him in the manner to which he is accustomed (he is brilliantly played by Walter Matthau here). Apparently to May’s surprise, Paramount wanted her to direct it and star, which she did – though the studio were less thrilled when she presented a near three-hour cut after going significantly over budget. May hated the studio’s much shorter version, and sued to have her name taken off it, but the judge sided with Paramount, declaring their 102-minute cut “hilarious”. Critics agreed. You will too. The film plays like a classic 1930s screwball marriage comedy – think Arsenic and Old Lace – but it’s particularly icy in its caustic depiction of romantic self-deception. As Richard Brody notes in The New Yorker, “having started out with the hatred, dependency, and surrender that it takes most couples years to achieve, Henry and Henrietta are no less suited than regular folks for marriage until death do them part—one way or another.” May went on to make two more films in the 70s: The Heartbreak Kid, starring her daughter Jeannie Berlin, who is dumped by Charles Grodin for Cybill Shepherd during their honeymoon, and Mikey and Nicky with John Cassavetes and Peter Falk. (Both are featured in Ragged Glory: Summer in the 70s.) In the 80s the notorious flop Ishtar marked an end of her directing career, though it has recently been reclaimed by critics. She has enjoyed a long and still successful career on Broadway.

films.title: The Heartbreak Kid
films.synopsis: Comedienne Elaine May became that rare thing, a female film director, with A New Leaf, a black comedy about Henry, a spoiled, broke playboy (Walter Matthau) desperately seeking a wealthy wife...
