B’Twixt Now and Sunrise is a vampire movie about a washed up writer (Val Kilmer—channelling Coppola?) sucked into a nightmare scenario... It’s schlocky, campy, but also a deeply personal film about the greatest loss Coppola experienced, the death of his son at age 22.

films.title: Kurt Vonnegut: Unstuck in Time
films.synopsis: As a high school student, Robert B Weide was such a Vonnegut fan his English teacher asked him to lecture on Slaughterhouse-Five. A few years later, after getting a film on the Marx Brothers on PBS, Weide told his favourite author he wanted his second film to be about him. To his surprise, Vonnegut agreed. Neither of them imagined that the doc would take decades to come together, that they would become close friends, and in fact Weide would only finish it 14 years after Vonnegut’s death. So it goes.

films.title: tick, tick... Boom!
films.synopsis: The musical Rent by Jonathan Larson was a game-changer in the history of Broadway, but the composer passed away the day of its first off-Broadway performance and never had the chance to enjoy his triumph. Prior to Rent, Larson’s first musical, the long-gestating Superbia, was never produced professionally. His second attempt, tick, tick... Boom! was an autobiographical account of that early failure—and this is what Hamilton composer Lin-Manuel Miranda brings to the screen in his own directorial debut.

films.title: In Balanchine’s Classroom
films.synopsis: “In mathematics, there was Newton; in psychology, there was Freud; and in American ballet, George Balanchine was a foundational genius...” New York Times. Connie Hochman’s film takes us back to the glory years of George Balanchine’s New York City Ballet through the remembrances of his former dancers and their quest to fulfill the vision of a genius. With rare archive footage of Balanchine at the height of his powers, this is a fascinating study of what we can learn from a genius of dance in remembrance.

films.title: The Feast
films.synopsis: In this impressively controlled and elegantly grisly eco horror, a British MP convenes a three-course banquet at his modernist home in the Welsh countryside to seal a deal for a local mine. The household is the epitome of privileged decadence, and the family are an obnoxious and dysfunctional bunch. Their guests aren’t much better. But it soon becomes clear that the taciturn and distracted Cadi (Annes Elwy), brought in to help serve the titular feast, will see they get their just desserts...

films.title: Hunt
films.synopsis: 3:15PM, 7:45PM 1983. An assassination attempt on South Korea’s President puts intense pressure on the Intelligence community. Was his agency incompetent, or is there a mole in the house? Park (Squid Game star Lee Jung-jae, making his directorial debut) isn’t sure, but his opposite number at a rival agency (Jung Woo-sung) is quick to point the finger. This stylish, triple twisty espionage thriller navigates a compelling course between John Le Carré realpolitik and Michael Mann-style action heroics. “Sleek and serious, burnished and brutal.” STEVE POND, THE WRAP

films.title: A Couple
films.synopsis: In his 90s, the great documentarian Fred Wiseman has made his first fiction film, a vignette based on the letters and diaries of Sophia Tolstoy, and her (off-screen) husband, Leo. It was the latter who penned the famous opening “All happy families are alike; each unhappy family is unhappy in its own way.” Leo talked a good game about love, equality, and spirituality, but Sophia (who bore him 13 children) had a uniqags, as Wiseman puckishly illustrates. “An expressive and moving portrait of a tempestuous marriage, one told with elan that feels rich in feeling.” LESLIE FELPERIN, HOLLYWOOD REPORTER

films.title: Let There Be Drums!
films.synopsis: The world’s greatest drummers reflect on the art of drumming and how it has shaped their lives. Features interviews with the late Taylor Hawkins from Foo Fighters, Stewart Copeland from The Police, Mickey Hart and Bill Kreutzmann from Grateful Dead, Chad Smith from Red Hot Chili Peppers, and the one and only Ringo Starr, among many others. “Captures the spirit of drums and the maniacs who have played them better than any other film.”

films.title: Bardo: False Chronicle of a Handful of Truths
films.synopsis: 1:00PM, 4:00PM, 7:00PM 2:00PM, 5:00PM, 7:50PM 5:00PM, 7:50PM 5:00PM, 7:50PM 3:00PM, 8:20PM Silverio is an esteemed Mexican documentary filmmaker going through an existential mid-life crisis. Returning to his homeland for a few days, he is visited by dreams, old friends, ghosts, and his own uneasy conscience... This is a portrait of the artist trying to reconcile his success with his politics, his ego with shame. A surreal black comedy in the vein of Fellini, Jodorowski and Malick, Bardo is a movie of astonishing imagery and raw soul-searching from the director of The Revenant and Birdman.

films.title: Salvatore: Shoemaker of Dreams
films.synopsis: 1:20PM, 3:30PM Salvatore Ferragamo opened his first shoe shop at the age of 12. Before he turned 20 Ferragamo had swapped Italy for the New World, stopping only when he reached Santa Barbara, the two reeler capital of the silent movie era. His shoes immediately found favour with the first film stars. When the industry moved to Hollywood he followed, and over the decades added the likes of Marilyn Monroe and Audrey Hepburn to his long list of clients. Directed by Luca Guadagnino (Call Me By Your Name). In Italian, English, and French

films.title: Neil Young: Harvest Time
films.synopsis: In 1971, aspiring filmmaker Bernard Shakey (aka Neil Young) set out to document the creation of a new record, a country rock album featuring "the Stray Gators", a group of esteemed session musicians, as well as the London Symphony Orchestra. That album—Harvest— went on to become the best selling l.p. of 1972 and is considered an all-time classic. Songs include Heart of Gold, Old Man, The Needle and the Damage Done, A Man Needs a Maid. Includes never-before-seen performance footage + Neil Young intro.

films.title: Radu Jude: Uppercase Print
films.synopsis: Mugur Calinescu, a Romanian teenager, wages a graffiti war on the regime of dictator Nicolae Ceausescu. Mobilising hundreds of informants, the secret police track him down, interrogate him and his family, and ensure that this upstart is crushed. Based on a play, itself based on Securitat case files, this docu-drama reconstructs Romania in the early 1980s, a police state which could brook no dissent. “A fierce and impassioned denunciation of evil.” PETER BRADSHAW, THE GUARDIAN

films.title: Radu Jude: The Happiest Girl in the World
films.synopsis: Radu Jude’s sly comic debut feature draws on his prior experience as a commercials director, a profession he pointedly satirizes here. The title is ironic of course: 18-year-old Delia (Andreea Bosneag) is a child of the post-Communist era and permanently at loggerheads

films.title: Radu Jude: Everybody in Our Family
films.synopsis: Jude’s second feature is another comedy of family dysfunction. Marius wants to take his 5-year-old daughter to the beach. But his ex-wife Otilia says she’s been sick, and it’s not a good idea. It’s an impasse that Marius cannot accept, and their dispute degenerates into a psychological meltdown. “A masterwork of black comedy and suspense... Tense to the point of exhaustion... Even when heartbreakingly honest and sad, it still manages to sustain a heightened sense of hilarity.” ERIC KOHN, INDIEWIRE

films.title: Benedetta
films.synopsis: Dutch filmmaker Paul Verhoeven (Basic Instinct; Robocop; Showgirls; Elle) has successfully straddled the triangle between Hollywood craftsman, art house auteur and exploitation provocateur. As the author of a serious biography of Jesus, he’s ideally placed to tackle the true story of Benedetta Carlini, a 17th century Italian nun revered as a mystic and persecuted for engaging in a lesbian affair

films.title: Radu Jude: Scarred Hearts
films.synopsis: During the summer of 1937, Emanuel, a young Jew in his early 20s, is committed to a sanatorium on the Black Sea coast for treatment of bone tuberculosis. The treatment consists of painful spine punctures that confine him to a body cast and to bed. Despite his incapacitation, his life is a-whirl with competing emotions, political turbulence and passion. “Fantastically detailed, intellectually furious drama.” RICHARD BRODY, THE NEW YORKER In Romanian with English subtitles. Special Jury Prize, Locarno 2016

films.title: Framing Agnes
films.synopsis: Exhuming transcripts from a 1950s study on transgender individuals, Chase Joynt (No Ordinary Man) and his collaborators employ re-enactments, reinvention, and personal reflections to examine the trans stories that are told and how—and by whom—they are authored. Joynt restages interrogations of several individuals who transitioned, while creating space for his performers to share their experiences. The resulting film is in constant dialogue with itself, serving as both a vital record and bold deconstruction.

films.title: The Grizzlie Truth
films.synopsis: Kathleen S. Jayme (Finding Big Country) is out to solve a true sports crime: who robbed us of the Vancouver Grizzlies? Revisiting the short history of those bad luck bears, Jayme’s documentary doubles as a testament to the enduring passion of true teal blue fans. It’s this passion that fuels a dogged odyssey that finds her connecting the dots and reconnecting with the Grizzlies heroes and villains, including former players like Shareef Abdur-Rahim and Mike Bibby, and the team’s architect, Stu Jackson.

films.title: Geographies of Solitude
films.synopsis: At times, it seems like Nova Scotia’s remote Sable Island manifested from a fable. Jacquelyn Mills fully immerses us in the natural wonders of a stunning ecosystem that’s home to wild horses, sparrows, invertebrates, and a devoted researcher. Employing innovative exposure and emulsion techniques and deriving a melodious soundscape from the natural world, Mills ensures that Sable isn’t so much captured on 16mm film as incorporated into the very fabric of a documentary. “One of the loveliest feature debuts in years.” DUSTIN CHANG, SCREEN ANARCHY In English Best Canadian Documentary, VIFF 2022; Best Canadian Feature Documentary Award, Hot Docs 2022

films.title: Tantura
films.synopsis: In 1998 Israeli graduate student Teddy Katz documented a massacre of Palestinian civilians in the village of Tantura during the 1948 war for Israel’s independence. Initially celebrated, he was stripped of his degrees and was publicly shamed. Decades later, incendiary new evidence emerges to corroborate Teddy’s initial findings, not just vindicating him, but raising profound questions about how Israelis—and all of us—deal with the darker chapters of history. “A complex, measured but thoroughly blood boiling documentary.” LOS ANGELES TIMES “A gripping, earth-shattering documentary.” ELLE In Hebrew, English, and Arabic

films.title: Nelly & Nadine
films.synopsis: Nadine falls in love with Nelly as she sings the aria Un del di, vedremo (One Fine Day, We’ll See) from Puccini’s Madame Butterfly. Snow is falling. It is Christmas Eve. And they are both prisoners in a German Concentration Camp, 1944. This exceptional film (it happens to be a documentary) casts a new light on the Holocaust as it gently unravels the intertwined histories of these two women: Nadine, daughter of a Chinese diplomat; and Nelly, an opera singer who worked with the French Resistance. In French, English, Spanish, and Swedish with English subtitles. Teddy Jury Award, Berlinale 2022

films.title: Délicieux
films.synopsis: 3:30PM, 8:15PM France, 1789. Popular unrest is broiling, the people are hungry for change. But for Manceron (Grégory Gadebois), personal chef to a gourmand duke, the breaking point comes when his patron rebukes him for serving a potato and truffle appetizer: peasant food. Exiled to a country inn, the chef tries to forget about cooking. That is, until Louise (Isabelle Carré) insists he take her as an apprentice... This fanciful tale of the genesis of the first restaurant in France is a feast for the eyes. Bon appetit!

films.title: The Big Hit
films.synopsis: 1:30PM, 6:30PM 4:00PM, 8:40PM Etienne, an often out of work but endearing actor, runs a theatre workshop in a prison, where he brings together an unlikely troupe of prisoners to stage Samuel Beckett’s famous play Waiting for Godot. When he is allowed to take the colourful band of convicts on a tour outside of prison, Etienne finally has the chance to thrive. Each date is a success and a unique relationship grows between them. But soon comes the final performance in Paris. Will their last night together be the biggest hit of them all?

films.title: Prayer for a Lost Mitten
films.synopsis: STARTS FRI DEC 24 This Hot Docs prize-winner is a beautiful, delicate documentary that starts out in the lost property office on Montreal’s transit system, but evolves into a meditation on what we cherish in objects, what we miss when we lose them, and whether, sometimes, some things assume a higher value in their absence. “Shot in velvety black and white with a looping jazz sax score, Lesage’s film [is] light, soft and wafting with poetic nostalgia.” STEPHANIE BUNBURY, THE AGE Best Canadian Feature, Hot Docs 2020 “Romantic. Gorgeous. Giving of all the feels.” SCREEN ANARCHY In French, English, Haitian Creole

films.title: The Lost Daughter
films.synopsis: 4:00PM, 8:45PM 1:00PM, 5:50PM Leda (Olivia Colman) is taking a solo vacation on a Greek island. She’s looking for peace and quiet —hopes for which evaporate when a noisy clan moves into the same taverna. When their little girl goes missing Leda finds her. But in the confusion the child’s beloved doll vanishes. Nina (Dakota Johnson), the girl’s mother, suspects the prickly Englishwoman may be responsible... Adapting a novella by Elena Ferrante, Maggie Gyllenhaal probes taboos around motherhood in this subtle psychological mystery.

films.title: Spencer
films.synopsis: Xmas with the in-laws, House of Windsor-style. Pablo Larraín’s doomy but defiant tribute to Diana is rigorously designed to put us inside the gilded cage, and indeed, inside the head of the woman on her perch, desperate to break free—perhaps the performance of the year, from Kristen Stewart, who embodies an icon, a princess, in revolt. “Spencer is more than the portrait of a woman in distress. If it’s a fable, it’s a political fable, an allegory of powerlessness, revolt and liberation.”

films.title: In the Heights
films.synopsis: Usnavi (Anthony Ramos) runs the local bodega, but plans to return to his native Dominica. But the news that someone from the hood bought a winning lottery ticket at his store has the whole block buzzing... Lin-Manuel Miranda’s brash, expansive, euphoric musical about the predominantly Dominican working class community of Washington Heights, NYC, is a fascinating counterpoint to West Side Story, a rhapsody in red, white and blue.

films.title: Children of the Sea
films.synopsis: In this environmental fable for all ages, three teenagers become entangled in the call of the sea as they hang out at the local aquarium. On a narrative level, the film is hard to describe. Visually, it’s simply one of the most staggering aesthetic achievements in recent animation. “It leaves you with the sense that the art form’s boundaries have been nudged a little wider as you watched.” ROBBIE COLIN, DAILY TELEGRAPH “Stunning... something to be celebrated.” PETER DEBRUGE, VARIETY

films.title: Weathering With You
films.synopsis: In Japan, this dazzling magical realist love story from the director of Your Name was the biggest homegrown hit that year and it’s easy to see why: its heart-stopping tale of teen love is bathed in spectacularly detailed but frequently fantastical animation. Tokyo looks so real you can practically smell it—and oh, those skies, full of clamour, portent, tempest and hope. Whatever else it may be, this is a stunning climate change movie. “Irresistibly romantic... awe-inspiringly gorgeous.”

films.title: Hope
films.synopsis: STARTS FRI DEC 24 In this Bergmanesque Scandinavian drama, Anja (Andrea Bræin Hovig) learns the worst: the doctors want to fast-track her for brain surgery. All the unresolved aspects of what has been, overtly, a productive life, flood in. She is far too young to die. Most acutely, there is the hole at the centre of her relationship with Tomas (Stellan Skarsgård), a significantly older man who may be too much in love with himself to truly love her. A hasty, belated marriage proposal does not assuage her doubts...

films.title: It’s a Wonderful Life
films.synopsis: Every time a bell rings, an angel gets its wings. You know you need to see this genuine Christmas classic as it was intended to be seen, on the big screen. Although the picture has become synonymous with homespun, small town values—values James Stewart personified and director Frank Capra obviously cherished—it achieves its profound emotional resonance precisely by stressing their limitation; its riven with anxiety and doubt.

films.title: The Shop Around the Corner
films.synopsis: A Christmas classic that doesn’t get the love it should, this bittersweet romantic comedy is one of the jewels of Hollywood’s Golden Age. James Stewart is the well meaning but starchy head clerk in an up-market Budapest boutique who somehow rubs his latest employee (Margaret Sullavan) up the wrong way. She has no idea he is the same man she is falling in love with as a pen pal... Effortlessly witty and sophisticated, with a deeply romantic heart that’s impossible to resist.

films.title: Dear Comrades!
films.synopsis: STARTS FRI DEC 24 A prize winner at the Venice Film Festival last year, and Russia’s entry for the Academy Award for Best International Feature, Dear Comrades! is Andrei Konchalovsky’s searing, indelible account of the brutal suppression of a strike in an industrial city in the summer of 1962. More than two dozen citizens were killed, 80 wounded, and all of it covered up by the Communist Party. Shot in black and white, this is a drama of intense focus, fire and fury,

films.title: Zola
films.synopsis: Inspired by a viral 148-tweet thread by A’Ziah Zola King, Janicza Bravo’s movie is full of fresh flourish and bravado; it’s a smart and snappy crime film, a nightmare scenario jacked into an exhilarating and defiant black comedy. Zola (Taylour Paige) is persuaded to take off with brand new bestie Stefani (Riley Keough) to make bank dancing in Sunshine State strip clubs but the road trip spirals out of control. “Whip-smart, funny, complicated, and just plain wild, Zola is 90 minutes of brilliance.”

films.title: Pinocchio
films.synopsis: A treat for young and old, we are delighted to showcase this new live action version of the classic tale of the wooden puppet who dreams of being a real boy. Director Matteo Garrone is well known to festival audiences for his acclaimed films Gomorrah, Dogman, and Tale of Tales, and he has outdone himself here with a movie that is darkly gripping, openly emotional, authentic and fantastical. Roberto Benigni (Life is Beautiful) stars as Geppetto.

films.title: Yi Yi (A One and a Two)
films.synopsis: Few films speak so profoundly to life as we know it as this intimate epic from the Taiwanese director Edward Yang. When an old woman falls into a coma, her family is encouraged to come speak to her each day. This they do, individually, and over the course of some months they discover much about themselves. “Yi Yi isn’t hard to put into words because it’s one of the best movies ever made, it’s one of the best movies ever made because it’s hard to put into words.”

films.title: Boogie Nights
films.synopsis: Being the rise and fall of a prodigiously-endowed performer on the seventies porno scene (Mark Wahlberg’s Dirk Diggler). Paul Thomas Anderson’s flamboyant 1997 calling card movie revels in the wild success of xxxcess, before crashing to earth with a bump. “Nearly a quarter of a century later, Boogie Nights stands as one of the finest and most endlessly rewatchable films of the ‘90s.” KYLE SMITH, NATIONAL REVIEW, 2020

films.title: Phantom Thread
films.synopsis: Paul Thomas Anderson’s beautifully tailored piece is a battle of the sexes comedy (and a black comedy at that) dressed up as a prestige picture. In what he declared would be his last film role, Daniel Day Lewis is Reynolds Woodcock, a renowned dressmaker and an obsessive perfectionist. Vicky Krieps is Alma, a waitress who becomes his latest muse, and who is determined to prove more than that, his match. “Devlishly funny and luxuriantly sensual.”

films.title: El Planeta
films.synopsis: Flat broke and facing eviction, Leonor (director Amalia Ulman) and her mother Maria (Ale Ulman) refuse to go down without a flight of fancy. Their power may’ve been cut, but lightbulb ideas still spark as these acid-tongued scroungers grift their way into getting one more taste of the finer things. A fleetly paced, winningly droll comedy of poor manners, El Planeta transports us through the looking glass into the stylish shared delusion that this mother and daughter have tailored for their circumstances.

films.title: The Velvet Queen
films.synopsis: Within the vast, mountainous region of the Tibetan plateau, Vincent Munier, a wildlife photographer, and Sylvain Tesson, a travel writer, are determined to find one of the region’s most elusive creatures: the snow leopard. As we are treated to glimpses of these stunning landscapes, the pair and director Marie Amiguet begin to consider man’s position within nature, mourning a time when “beasts, humans, and gods conducted a common conversation.”

films.title: Bad Axe
films.synopsis: David Siev’s intimate documentary chronicles the unforeseen impacts of the pandemic on his parents’ restaurant, Rachel’s, in Bad Axe, Michigan. With a population of just over 3000, 97% of them white, the margins are always going to be tight for an ethnic restaurant. When they are allowed to reopen, the mask mandate splits the community, and there’s a scary rise in racist abuse. The Sievs navigate this stressful time with anxiety, sometimes anger, anguish, and with love. Audience Award for Best Documentary, SXSW 2022

films.title: No Bears
films.synopsis: In this Venice prize-winner, dissident Iranian filmmaker Jafar Panahi plays himself (again), a prisoner in his own country, banned from making films but nevertheless doing just that, remotely. The film he’s overseeing concerns a couple trying to get hold of passports to flee to Europe. Meanwhile Panahi is renting a room in a village near the Turkish border and trying to keep a low profile. No Bears is bare bones simplicity on the surface, but ingeniously conceived so that it reveals multiple layers of meaning and depths of emotion as it develops.

films.title: The Super 8 Years
films.synopsis: The French writer and 2022 Nobel Prize laureate Annie Ernaux, whose novels and memoirs have earned her a devoted following, opens a treasure trove with this delicate journey into her family’s memory, chronicling the years 1972 - 1981, when her first books were published, her sons became teenagers, and her husband Philippe brought an 8mm film camera everywhere they went. Supplying her own introspective voiceover, Ernaux guides the viewer through fragments of a decade, diffuse and vivid in equal measure.

films.title: Marcel the Shell With Shoes On
films.synopsis: The most charming documentary of the year turns out to be a portrait of a rare mollusk adapting to environmental change, a comedy about separation and loneliness, a touching drama about caring and friendship, and many other things beside (most obviously, to be sure, an animated entertainment for all the family). First time feature filmmaker Dean Fleisher-Camp trains his camera on the eponymous Marcel (voiced by Jenny Slate), a plucky and intelligent young seashell caring for his nana. “Pack a hankie. But don’t miss this strange, special little film.” PETER DEBRUGE, VARIETY

films.title: Aftersun
films.synopsis: Calum (Paul Mescal) and Sophie (Frankie Corio), his 11-year-old daughter, are often mistaken for siblings. Away on a discount holiday in Turkey, they conduct themselves like impish kids playing hooky. It is a vacation she will never forget. In her debut feature, Scottish filmmaker Charlotte Wells demonstrates a gentle command of emotional complexities and astonishing prowess to conjure those fleeting moments of truth which never leave you. “Aftersun cuts you in two with such emotional intensity, such impressive dramatic force, that I could only sit and fight back the inevitable tears.” BARRY HERTZ, GLOBE AND MAIL

films.title: Everything Everywhere All at Once
films.synopsis: The second film from “the Daniels”, EEAaO is nothing if not upfront about its methodology. Marvel/Disney don’t own the multiverse: the Daniels take the concept of parallel worlds as license to reinvent what a comic book movie can be and subvert the fascistic underpinnings of the super hero genre. Michelle Yeoh is Evelyn, whose IRS audit is interrupted by the news that only she can save humanity from her daughter’s out-of-control alter ego. Is it overthe-top? You bet. Anarchic, absurd, and a game changer. “It’s absurd and wild and wonderful, and will probably make you cry.” ALISSA WILKINSON, VOX

films.title: RRR (Rise Roar Revolt)
films.synopsis: India, 1920. Two future real-life Indian revolutionaries, Bheem (Jr. NTR) and Raju (Ram Charan) collide in an exhilaratingly wild plot involving a girl kidnapped by the English. The pair may be at cross purposes but it’s impossible not to root for them both in an escalating series of death-defying set pieces. The astonishing RRR is the kind of blockbuster action film that reminds us cinema has thrilled audiences all over the world for more than a century; it’s the most fun we had at the movies last year. “RRR is about the movies: the thrill of watching stories told at larger-than-life levels, the joy of watching stars collide, the effort of rendering lavish mythologies at whatever the digital equivalent of 24 frames per second is, the sensation of seeing manufactured movement via gleefully conspicuous special effects bump up against genuine physical effort.” DAVID FEAR, ROLLING STONE

films.title: Trouble in Paradise
films.synopsis: Herbert Marshall and Miriam Hopkins play lovers and thieves attempting to fleece the chic owner of a French perfume company, played by Kay Francis. What ensues is a sort-of modern ménage à trois in the most elegant, innuendo indulgent film comedy of all time. For his pre-screening talk, Michael van den Bos discusses the “Lubitsch Touch” in the director’s approach to sex on screen and his suggestive visual flair, and an appreciation for the beguiling actresses Miriam Hopkins and Kay Francis. Intro 2pm; Film: 2.30

films.title: XINEMA Program 4: The Framing of Perception
films.synopsis: Join us for XINEMA’s fourth program, this time in the Vancity Theatre! Selected works will highlight BC-based emerging and established filmmakers and will be followed by reflective discussions between filmmakers and audience. Program 4: The Framing of Perception includes works by David Jeric Avelino, Kaila Bhullar, Ross Birdwise, Elysia Bourne, Sidney Gordon, Cam Kletke, Andrew Power, Amanda Thomson, and Kirk Tougas. Curated by Celina de Leon & Sidney Gordon

films.title: Adult Adoption
films.synopsis: 20-something Rosy is an anxiously independent young woman... she’s getting by... but she’s also an orphan, and when a coworker suggests she tries the brave new world of adult adoption she can’t shake the idea. Turns out finding a “parent” at this stage of life is every bit as fraught as finding a romantic partner... Ellie Moon, who plays Rosy and also wrote the good-natured screenplay, taps the wryly comical, icky, and poignant implications of deep-rooted insecurity and longing. “Knox’s feature debut, with a distinctive kindness at its core, is a complete triumph. Its gentleness gives way to a profound search for belonging, while realising maybe we’re all on this search together.” SCOTT WILSON, ONE ROOM WITH A VIEW

films.title: Turn Every Page: The Adventures of Robert Caro and Robert Gottlieb
films.synopsis: 12:30PM, 7:30PM What makes a great biography? Robert Caro (writer: The Power Broker and LBJ biographer) and Gottlieb (his editor for half a century) are better qualified than most to answer this question. Diligence, time, and le mot juste all come into play. Anyone interested in the work of a writer, in books, or who shares Caro’s fascination with the workings of power will find much to think about. “Turn Every Page is one step away from turning into a Herzogian monument to obsession or plunging into crazed psychodrama. Instead, it is merely a great profile, filled with wit, affection and detailed stories of how the books came to be.” BEN KENIGSBERG, NEW YORK TIMES

films.title: Black Orpheus
films.synopsis: 1960 Academy Award Winner and winner of the Palme d’Or at the 1959 Cannes Film Festival, Marcel Camus’s Black Orpheus retells the Greek myth of Orpheus and Eurydice against the madness of Carnival in Rio de Janeiro. With its magnificent color photography and lively soundtrack, this film brought the infectious bossa nova beat to the United States. Screening in 35mm Guest presenter, percussionist Sal Ferreras has been a fixture of Vancouver’s music scene for the past 40 years. Light snacks—chicken and cheese coxinhas supplied by Brazailliant Café and Catering—included with your ticket. “A riotous, rapturous explosion of sound and color, Black Orpheus is less about Orpheus’s doomed love for Eurydice than about Camus’s love for cinema at its most gestural and kinetic.” ANN HORNADAY, WASHINGTON POST

films.title: When You Finish Saving the World
films.synopsis: In this first feature written and directed by Jesse Eisenberg, Finn Wolfhard (Stranger Things) gives an impressive performance as Ziggy, a dimly angry teenage troubadour courting a politically conscious classmate, even as he despises his altruistic mom (Julianne Moore), Evelyn, who says and probably believes all the right things but alienates everyone IRL. For her part, Evelyn rechannels her energies into mentoring a handsome young man at the shelter where she works, without asking if he wants her help. “Braids the biodigital sweetness of Miranda July around the poison wit of Noah Baumbach.” B+ DAVID EHRLICH, INDIEWIRE

films.title: Ever Deadly
films.synopsis: Throat singing is such a thrilling, strange, unique form of expression, for the first five minutes of this film, the camera just watches a duet, in intense close-up, and the results are mesmerizing, funny, sexy and beautiful. In Tanya Tagaq, we are fortunate to have a radical innovator in this art-form, and this collaboration with Chelsea McMullan (My Prairie Home) brings rare insights into her background and family life in Nunavut while doubling as a record of an extraordinary live concert performance.

films.title: Part of the Pack
films.synopsis: The wolf has always been a haunting symbol of the wild: proud, defiant, to be respected—from a safe distance. This beautifully shot BC-made film looks at the complex and evolving relationship between wolf and human: how the call of the wild still pulls on us, and how wolves today are compelled to live alongside us. A few even become pets. One wolf, Takaya (named by the Songhees First Nation) became world famous after claiming a scattering of tiny islands off Vancouver Island as his territory.

films.title: Maryada Ramanna
films.synopsis: Yes, this is a rom-com about honour killing. But darn if the RRR director doesn't pull it off, bicycle narrator and all. Maryada Ramanna has oodles of charm, splendid slapstick, and a sublime romantic climax.

films.title: Eega
films.synopsis: Murdered by a sleazy entrepreneur, Nani is reincarnated as a housefly. An angry housefly. With vengeance on his mind... Rajamouli's revenge thriller is one of the weirdest movies you'll ever see.

films.title: All That Breathes
films.synopsis: The air in New Delhi is so polluted that birds are falling from the skies. Two Muslim brothers—former bodybuilders Nadeem and Saud—are determined to nurse the megacity’s ailing black kites back to health. As they strive to keep their wildlife rescue clinic afloat, political tensions loom over their neighbourhood as ominously as the smog. Shaunak Sen’s sophomore documentary serves as a powerful meditation on the climate crisis, New Delhi’s ecology, and the interconnectedness of All That Breathes. 100% Fresh ROTTEN TOMATOES In Hindi with English subtitles. Glass Onion 3 Ticket Pack

films.title: Glass Onion
films.synopsis: “Glass Onion adopts the sturdy structural underpinnings of the Agatha Christie-like whodunit, and presents them with an ingenious mix of postmodern irony and bona fide awe.” DAVID JENKINS, LITTLE WHITE LIES

films.title: Knives Out
films.synopsis: “An entertainment that’s as smart, witty, stylish and exhilarating as any movie lover could wish for.” JOE MORGENSTERN, WALL STREET JOURNAL

films.title: Looper
films.synopsis: “A scintillating neo-noir gem of existential quandaries and inescapable fatalism.” NICK SCHAGER, LESSONS OF DARKNESS

films.title: Star Wars: The Last Jedi
films.synopsis: “As a sensational Star Wars vehicle and a pensive reminder of ideals for any age, The Last Jedi holds its lightsaber high—a beacon for what these films can be, and what they can impart.” CORY WOODROOF, NASHVILLE SCENE

films.title: The Brothers Bloom
films.synopsis: “I tried to stuff everything that I love into that movie all at once… My love of Ricky Jay and con-man movies, and traveling, and the romance of all of that. And nobody saw it.” – Rian Johnson Adrien Brody and Mark Ruffalo are the eponymous siblings, orphans raised and returned by several dozen outraged foster parents over the years. Bloom (Brody) is the younger of the two, and from an early age his brother’s Stephen’s instrument in dizzyingly capricious confidence games. Now in his 30s, Bloom wants out – but Stephen persuades him to do the proverbial last score, baiting him with Penelope (Rachel Weisz), a lonely epileptic millionairess who collects hobbies the way some people collect stamps. Posing as antique dealing smugglers, the brothers draw her into a crazy escapade of half-untruths. But is Bloom in love with her, or just caught up in Stephen’s script? Flitting from New Jersey to Montenegro, Budapest and St Petersburg, tossing off allusions to Herman Melville and Dostoyevski with the same abandon Penelope shrugs off another mil, The Brothers Bloom has a giddy flamboyance and a go-for-broke quality which gives it wings.

films.title: Descendant
films.synopsis: One of the five best documentaries of 2022, per the National Board of Review, Margaret Brown’s film zeroes in on the people of Africaville, Alabama, and the descendants of the 110 slaves brought in on the last known slave ship to transport kidnapped Africans to America as human cargo, an illegal shipment undertaken as a bet by a local landowner, Timothy Meaher. Descendant doesn’t just relate the history of a 200-year-old crime, it also looks at what’s changed and how much hasn’t—in the interim. “Margaret Brown’s fascinating film deals not only with the rediscovery of the ship by a team of marine archaeologists, but also with its impact on a community that has rallied together and has finally managed to establish a key element of their collective history. And while the past has a tendency to be claimed and reshaped by those in power, the residents of Africatown, Alabama, are not about to let that happen again.” WENDY IDE, THE OBSERVER In English We hope you’ll agree, February is as good a time as any to celebrate Black film, Black film artists, Black thinkers and activists, and to highlight the legacy of slavery, white supremacy, colonization and capitalism that underpins our unjust society. Our BHM programming this year includes two series: Icons and Dispatches. Icons spotlights the accomplishments of American movie stars like Denzel Washington, Viola Davis, Samuel L Jackson, Angela Bassett, Chadwick Boseman and others, emulating and transcending the path beaten by Sidney Poitier 60 years ago. Dispatches turns from fantasy to reality, with a focus on documentaries, ideas, and social justice, including work by and about James Baldwin, Camille Billops, and two exceptional recent Canadian films, Dear Jackie and Our Dance of Revolution. In addition, we’re starting the month with week-long engagements for two of the most acclaimed movies of last year. Alice Diop’s Saint Omer, from France, is a profoundly rich and fascinating response to the real life trial of an African immigrant for filicide (a trial Diop attended). And Margaret Brown’s award-winning documentary Descendant is a deep dive into the case of the last known slave ship transporting kidnapped Africans to the USA, and what it signifies for the descendants of the slaves, and the slave-runners too. In these films, and others, we are reminded of how cinema can offer insight as well as spectacle, extend empathy and inspire change. 3 ticket pack for $33 for Icons and Dispatches only. See viff.org for full programme details.

films.title: Saint Omer
films.synopsis: In a court of law, young novelist Rama attends the trial of Laurence, a French-Sengalese woman accused of killing her 15 month old daughter. But as the trial continues, the words of the accused and witness testimonies shake Rama’s convictions. Diop’s superb film, her first dramatic work after a series of acclaimed documentaries, subtly, almost surreptitiously evokes complex ideas and emotions around motherhood, gender, and marginalized communities.

films.title: Skinamarink
films.synopsis: Kyle Edward Ball’s extraordinary experimental horror film is pregnant with intangible apprehension. Two siblings, aged 4 and 6, wake up alone (or are they?) in the middle of the night. Shot in low light, with sparse dialogue (“Daddy?” “Dad?”) and next to no close ups. Skinamarink casts a spell somewhere on the edge of suppressed memory and childhood nightmare. It’s a movie about emptiness, the darkness under the bed, the bumps in the night, the vulnerability of the innocent. Prepare to be creeped out. “Unnerving... Mesmerizing...Ingeniously evoking a child’s response to the inexplicable, Skinamarink sways on the border between dreaming and wakefulness, a movie as difficult to penetrate as it is to forget.” JEANNETTE CATSOULIS, NEW YORK TIMES

films.title: Carole King: Home Again - Live in Central Park 1973
films.synopsis: This brand new feature-length concert film presents the legendary Carole King’s triumphant May 26, 1973 homecoming concert on The Great Lawn of New York City’s Central Park before an estimated audience of 100,000. New interviews with King and producer Lou Adler set the scene, but this is primarly about the music. King moved easily between her Tapestry classics (performed solo with piano) and songs from her soon to be released 1973 album Fantasy performed with a stellar 11-piece band.

films.title: In the Heat of the Night
films.synopsis: Sidney Poitier was the most important Black screen actor of the 20th century, but if he had only made this one film it would have been enough. He’s a Philadelphia police detective pulled in as a murder suspect when changing trains in Mississippi. His duel with bigoted local cop Rod Steiger is magnetic.

films.title: The Bingo Long Traveling All-Stars & Motor Kings
films.synopsis: “Genial, slapdash, high-spirited and occasionally moving. For a comedy whose principal mission is to entertain, The Bingo Long Traveling All-Stars also manages to provoke a lot of more sober, subsidiary responses that, happily, never get in the way of the show.” VINCENT CANBY, NEW YORK TIMES

films.title: Baby Ruby
films.synopsis: Black Swan meets Rosemary’s Baby in Bess Wohl’s gripping and disturbing psychological thriller about an exhausted, stressed new mother (Noémie Merchant, Portrait of a Lady on Fire) falling apart. Social media queen Jo has a perfect life. Until Ruby comes along. “A tense, visceral psychological thriller that sets out to dismantle everything you think you know about being a mom. To say that Baby Ruby is intense would be an understatement.”

films.title: Dear Jackie (free screening)
films.synopsis: Dear Jackie is a cinematic letter to Jackie Robinson, the first African American player in Major League Baseball and a civil rights activist who broke the colour barrier when he joined the minor-league Montreal Royals in 1946. For a short time, the impossible seemed possible in a segregated North America. But did Montrealers use this historic moment to perpetuate a myth of a post-racial society? “Through these Black voices—expressed truthfully, articulately, with dignity and from the heart—Canadians can learn the true history of their country.” CHARLIE SMITH, GEORGIA STRAIGHT In English and French with English subtitles. Recontres internationales du documentaire de Montréal (RIDM), Magnus Isacsson Award

films.title: Purple Rain
films.synopsis: Dearly beloved, we are gathered here today to celebrate Prince Nelson Rogers. Purple Rain is everything you could want from a rock film, and more—it’s sexy, sassy, slick and it captures the young Prince in the raw, coming into his own.

films.title: Under the Cherry Moon
films.synopsis: A rare opportunity to catch Prince’s notorious directorial debut on the big screen, and in 35mm, where its luminous black and white photography (by Fassbinder/ Scorsese collaborator Michael Ballhaus) belongs.

films.title: One Fine Morning
films.synopsis: Sandra (Léa Seydoux), a single mother working to support her young daughter and her ailing father Georg (Pascal Greggory), navigates the labyrinthine system of care homes, with their financial and logistical burdens. Then, an encounter with an old friend, Clément (Melvil Poupaud), blossoms into a passionate affair. In this intimate, thoughtful exploration through the vagaries of love—romantic, filial, domestic—Mia Hansen-Løve delivers another poignant, personal film that resonates long after it ends.

films.title: To Kill a Tiger
films.synopsis: Ranjit is a rice farmer in Jharkand, India. When his 13-year-old daughter is raped by three men, local custom decrees that she marry one of the men to redeem her honour. Ranjit scandalizes the village by insisting that the perpetrators should be punished for their crime. To Kill a Tiger is an emotional wringer of a a movie, but in the words of the late Ravi Srinivasan, also rigorous, compassionate, and galvanizing. In Hindi and Nagpuri with English subtitles. Baahubali: The Beginning S.S. RAJAMOULI, INDIA, 2015, 159 MIN. Baahubali 2: The Conclusion S.S. RAJAMOULI, INDIA, 2017, 167 MIN. “A splashy, big-budget film with an infectious sense of momentum that wins you over any time key plot points are glossed over for the sake of establishing the next big confrontation. It’s loud, it’s gory, and there are musical numbers.” SIMON ABRAMS, ROGEREBERT.COM

films.title: “This Time It’s Personal” Films by Camille Billops & James Hatch (Programme 2)
films.synopsis: The second programme in our short selection of independent films by Camille Bishops and James Hatch includes what is probably their masterpiece, Finding Christa, a deeply personal film about Camille’s relationship with the daughter she gave up for adoption as a child. “Terrifically artful... A rich and haunting film.” NEW YORK TIMES Programme 2: Take Your Bags (1998, 11 min); Finding Christa (1991, 55 min)

films.title: The Conformist
films.synopsis: New 4K Restoration • Probably Bertolucci’s most perfect film, this adaptation of Alberto Moravia’s novel is one of the most visually dazzling movies ever made (DP Vittorio Storaro went on to shoot Apocalypse Now and most of Bertolucci’s subsequent epics). Jean-Louis Trintignant is the existential anti-hero, pressed into a political assassination by Mussolini’s security apparatus. “A great film, drunkenly beautiful and deeply disturbing.” DAVID THOMSON, LA WEEKLY

films.title: Vertigo
films.synopsis: Runner-up in the 2022 Sight & Sound poll of the Greatest Films of All Time (and #1 in 2012), this is Hitchcock’s most personal and revealing film, a movie about male neurosis, fetishism and power, with James Stewart as the private detective who becomes obsessed with the married woman (Kim Novak) he’s been hired to follow. Sunday, February 19 screening will be introduced by William Brown, Assistant Professor of Film, University of British Columbia.

films.title: Broker
films.synopsis: Working for the first time in South Korea, festival favourite Hirokazu Kore-eda (Shoplifters) has come up

films.title: Widows
films.synopsis: Viola Davis is immense in Steve McQueen’s gripping crime story. When her husband dies in a shootout with Chicago PD, Veronica inherits his $2 million debt to a local mobster, and a notebook with plans to rip off the vault of a local politico. She persuades the other bereaved wives to help her pull off the job. But in this world, it’s impossible to know who to trust. McQueen (12 Years a Slave) and co-screenwriter Gillian Flynn keep us guessing; it’s one of the most underrated movies of the last 10 years. “There may be no honor amongst thieves, but at least one thing is true: Viola Davis knows a thing or two about getting away with murder.” MARJORIE BAUMGARTEN, AUSTIN CHRONICLE

films.title: Our Dance of Revolution
films.synopsis: “To be Black and queer is to be a danger to the world. I think that’s beautiful...” So says Rodney, one of the community activists telling the story of how Toronto’s marginalized non-white gay and lesbians of the 1980s forged community, organized, demanded recognition and equity—and continue to fight the good fight to this day. It’s a people’s history of activism, education, creativity and friendship, told by the folks who lived it with lashings of laughter, affection, and even nostalgia.

films.title: Black Panther
films.synopsis: The most important movie Marvel Studios has made to date, this Black blockbuster is a triumph for Creed/ Fruitvale Station director Ryan Coogler and star Chadwick Boseman. After the death of his father, T’Challa returns home to the African nation of Wakanda to take his rightful place as king. When a powerful enemy suddenly reappears, T’Challa’s mettle as king—and as Black Panther—gets tested when he’s drawn into a conflict that puts the fate of Wakanda and the entire world at risk. “The most political movie ever produced by Marvel Studios, both in its very existence—it’s the most expensive movie to have ever starred an almost entirely black cast— and in the questions its story raises.”

films.title: XINEMA Programme 5: Earth as Womb
films.synopsis: Selected short experimental works highlight BCbased emerging and established filmmakers followed by reflective discussions between filmmakers and audience. Program 5: Earth as Womb Earth as Womb invokes the existential feeling you get when you remember you’re a living entity on a floating ball in space. Includes works by Khalil Alomar, Inanna Cusi, Ann Marie Fleming, MiruFiyu, Lisa G, Luciana Siebert, Evan Swain, Rafael Zen. Curated by Celina de Leon & Sidney Gordon

films.title: To Leslie
films.synopsis: Andrea Riseborough’s nomination for Best Actress surprised many... but no one who has actually seen To Leslie. Inspired by a true story (one of many, in fact) about a West Texas single mom who won the lottery, blew the money and winds up on the street, alcoholic, and scorned by (almost) all. Which is where To Leslie begins...

films.title: Cinema Sabaya
films.synopsis: 2:30PM, 7:00PM A group of 8 Palestinian and Jewish women attend a video workshop at a small town community centre. Their homework assignments offer revealing glimpses of very different living conditions and life experiences. Yet through their differences, they become friends. Inspired by writer-director Orit Fouks Rotem’s own experiences as a teacher, Cinema Sabaya celebrates the joy of sisterhood. $1 of your ticket purchase will go to support Vancouver Rape Relief & Women’s Shelter

films.title: Godland
films.synopsis: In the late 19th century, a Danish Lutheran priest is dispatched to a far corner of Iceland where a devout farmer has seen fit to build a church. The journey is arduous but spectacular. This first half of the film evokes the epic colonial odysseys of Herzog, Scorsese, and Lucrecia Martel... In the second half, our missionary is forced to contend not with the forboding landscapes, but a crippling crisis of faith, his attraction to the farmer’s daughter, and the suspicious locals. From the director of A White, White Day, this is a stark, bitterly funny, elemental fable.

films.title: The Fabelmans
films.synopsis: Steven Spielberg’s bittersweet movie memoir is a portrait of the artist as the product of his artsy mom (Michelle Williams), his techy dad (Paul Dano), and, ultimately, a broken home. Beginning with young Sam’s first big screen memory, Fabelmans tracks his obsession with moving pictures through his first Super-8 camera, early home movie epics and high school hijinks. But it’s a more poignant and intimate film than that makes it sound; there is pain here as well as play.

films.title: Chess Story
films.synopsis: 1:00PM, 8:50PM In a standoffhe can't win with a Nazi SS officer, Josef Bartok is condemned to solitary confinement until he gives up his secrets. Fate throws him a lifeline: a stolen book... to his dismay it's a book of chess games. Yet this book will be key to his escape... Freely adapted from Stefan Zweig's novella, and dominated by Oliver Musucci's multifaceted performance, Philipp Stölzl's gripping movie is a compelling psychological study of torture, defiance and the kind of mind games no one can hope to control.

films.title: Castle in the Sky
films.synopsis: An island in the sky? The story of a young boy who sees a girl floating down from the sky. He comes to her aid in her flight from sky pirates, the army and secret agents. An adventure story influenced by Treasure Island and Gulliver’s Travels, Castle in the Sky is dynamic, imaginative family entertainment with valuable lessons about technology and ignorance.

films.title: Grave of the Fireflies
films.synopsis: Set in Japan during WWII, the film focuses on Seita and his little sister Setsuko. After their mother is killed in an air raid, and with their father serving in the navy, they are forced to fight for survival in the devastated Japanese countryside. This harrowing drama is one of the most affecting animated films ever made. Roger Ebert described it “as an emotional experience so powerful that it forces a rethinking of animation,” adding: “It belongs on any list of the greatest war films ever made.”

films.title: Kiki’s Delivery Service
films.synopsis: In keeping with tradition, 13-year-old witch Kiki dusts off her broom and flies away from home for a year of independence and self-discovery in the big city. Her only companion is her beloved black cat, Jiji. “Astonishing in its visual splendor and delightfully entertaining.”

films.title: My Neighbor Totoro
films.synopsis: Two little girls and their father move into a beautiful old house in the countryside to be near their mother, who is seriously ill in hospital. Largely left to fend for themselves, Mei and her big sister Satsuki encounter a strange and beautiful world of forest sprites named ‘Totoros’. Miyazaki’s most beloved film is simply magical and magically simple.

films.title: Nausicaa of the Valley of the Wind
films.synopsis: Miyazaki’s first film as writer-director (based on his own successful manga) is an extradinarily rich fantasy film, an eco-allegory set in a feudal, toxic future and a spirited adventure movie. Led by the courageous Princess Nausicaa, the people of the Valley of the Wind are engaged in a perpetual conflict with powerful insects called “ohmu”, guardians of a poisonous (and spreading) jungle. Curiosity. Courage. Ecology. Culture. These are the hallmarks of the famed Japanese animation company Studio Ghibli. Later this year Hayao Miyazaki will unveil his first film in a decade, so there could be no more fitting time to revisit these enchanting fairy tales. Newcomers are invited to expect a fantastical cinema imbued with a sense of the sublime, featuring plucky heroines, fabulous contraptions, endearing mythical creatures, and a living, breathing world both familiar and unique. The first installment of our complete Ghibli retrospective focuses on the years 1984-1999. Matinee family friendly shows will feature the English-language version, all ages welcome. Evening screenings will play

films.title: Queens of the Qing Dynasty
films.synopsis: Recovering from a suicide attempt, a neurodiverse Cape Breton teen is drawn into the orbit of a genderqueer hospital volunteer who hails from Shanghai. Despite their disparate backgrounds, the pair operate on identical idiosyncratic frequencies. A heady mix of unvarnished-yet-eloquent dialogue, transportive electronic compositions, and visual flourishes, Ashley McKenzie’s second feature upholds her social realist principles while exploring a more expansive, sensorially rich brand of cinema. In English, Mandarin, and Russian

films.title: Riceboy Sleeps
films.synopsis: Raising her son Dong-hyun (Ethan Hwang) in Vancouver’s suburbs, So-young (Choi Seung-yoon), a South Korean immigrant, desperately wants to instill a sense of pride in the boy. Meanwhile, he just wants to fit in. Elegantly entwining social realism with fable-like sequences, Anthony Shim (Daughter, VIFF 2019) crafts an emotionally and sensorially rich film. Wedding the autobiographical and universal, he likewise achieves an exquisite balance between Dong-hyun and So-young’s perspectives.

films.title: Pandora and the Flying Dutchman
films.synopsis: Love doesn’t come easily in this surrealist romance from maverick filmmaker Albert Lewin. Ava Gardner is American singer in exile Pandora Reynolds, perhaps the most beautiful woman in the world, and certainly the most desired. She meets her match in James Mason’s dour Dutch sea captain, doomed forever to sail the high seas until he meets a woman ready to die for him. You have never really experienced colour until you have seen Jack Cardiff’s Technicolor cinematography, restored to eye-scorching glory here. This screening is copresented with Vancouver Opera, whose production of Wagner’s The Flyng Dutchman runs from April 29.

films.title: Tenzin
films.synopsis: In the first Tibetan language film to be made in Canada, Tenzin (Tenzin Kelsang) is a young man living in Toronto, struggling to come to terms with the death by self-immolation of his older brother, and navigating the exigencies of Western culture on one hand and the Buddhist beliefs of his community on the other. Made collaboratively with Ontario’s Tibetan community, Tenzin is a poignant character study with deft political and philosophical shadings and a striking score by Colin Stetson (Hereditary).

films.title: In Viaggio: The Travels of Pope Francis
films.synopsis: Master documentarian Gianfranco Rosi (Fire At Sea; Notturno) assembles a mixed progress report on the current pontiff, drawing largely from archives’ of Francis’s seemingly never-ending travels (he’s visited 53 countries in a decade), including last summer’s trip to Canada. Counterpoint is provided by Rosi’s own images of conflict, refugees and poverty in the Middle East, Lampedusa and elsewhere. The Pope is eloquent and empathetic speaker, revered by many, but it’s hard not to notice the disconnect. In Italian, Spanish, and English

films.title: Until Branches Bend
films.synopsis: Discovering a potentially invasive insect inside a peach, fruit packer Robin (Grace Glowicki) immediately reports it. When management refuses to take action, she goes public with her concerns and precipitates a widescale shutdown in her Okanagan town. Parallels and allegories abound as Sophie Jarvis’ psychological drama delves into the ills of this seemingly postcard-perfect community. This intimate whistleblowing drama ultimately grows apocalyptic in scale, all while preserving the human story at its core.

films.title: Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon
films.synopsis: A rich, romantic take on the wuxia, China's heroic swordsman genre from Taiwanese director Ang Lee pitting veterans Michelle Yeoh and Chow Yun Fat against the wilful aristocratic thief Zhang Ziyi. They clash over the Green Destiny, a priceless sword. Once it's taken flight the movie never touches the ground, spinning myriad exhilarating duels of the body and spirit. A feast for the senses, this remains a breathtaking spectacle more than 20 years after it crushed it at the North American box office. Mandarin

films.title: Enys Men
films.synopsis: 4:10PM, 8:20PM Mark Jenkin’s follow up to Bait speaks in a strange cinematic tongue, appropriate to its remote Cornish setting (“Enys Men” means Stone Island), but which will feel familiar to anyone who has spent time alone in a cottage by the sea. Here we find a woman monitoring the blooming of a rare flower. She is alone. And not. The past steadily creeps up on her seclusion. Folk horror-adjacent... Enys Men builds an eerie, ominous ode to island life from echoes, intimations, hallucinations and a dark bottomless pit. Only Yesterday Matinee family-friendly shows will feature the English-language version, all ages welcome. Evening screenings will play

films.title: My Neighbours the Yamadas
films.synopsis: Takashi Yamada and his wacky wife Matsuko navigate their way through the ups and downs of work, marriage, and family life with a sharp-tongued grandmother who lives with them, a teen son who wishes he had cooler parents, and a pesky daughter.

films.title: Ocean Waves
films.synopsis: Taku and his best friend Yutaka are headed back to school for what looks like another uneventful year. But they soon find their friendship tested by the arrival of Rikako, a beautiful new transfer student from Tokyo...

films.title: Only Yesterday
films.synopsis: A wistful, lyrical film about a young woman escaping the city and taking stock of her life at 27. Visiting relatives in the countryside, Taeko is enthusiastic about helping out on the farm, but she’s also preoccupied with memories of her childhood.

films.title: Porco Rosso
films.synopsis: Pigs will fly! This spirited adventure yarn features an anti-fascist flier (who happens to look like a pig) tracking sky pirates over the Adriatic in the 1930s. An exhilarating romp with a melancholy undertow—and amazing flying machines!

films.title: Whisper of the Heart
films.synopsis: A lovely change of pace from Studio Ghibli, this is a teenage first-love story, set in a realistically observed modern day Tokyo. Bookish schoolgirl Shizuku meets her soul mate with a little help from a portly cat. “A beautiful film.”

films.title: Pom Poko
films.synopsis: As their habitat is stripped and paved by the encroaching humans, good-natured but rather undisciplined shape-shifting raccoons embark on a campaign of disruption and distraction. Another charmer from the director of Kiki’s Delivery Service. Guest introduction on Thursday, March 23.

films.title: Metronom
films.synopsis: Bucharest, 1972. Ceausescu’s autocratic regime has a stranglehold on power, but Ana is 17, and in love. Sadly for her, boyfriend Sorin is about to emigrate to Germany. Emotional, Ana sneaks out to her friend Roxanna’s party

films.title: The Five Devils
films.synopsis: Vicky isn’t a devil, but she might be an eight-year-old witch. Certainly she has an extraordinary sense of smell. But there’s more than that. Unravelling the mysteries of her mother Joanne (Adèle Exarchopoulos), Vicky sniffs out visions from before her birth, when Joanne was set on a very different path... Hot French screenwriter Léa Mysius (who has worked with Claire Denis and Jacques Audiard) follows up her debut Ava with another strikingly original, ambitious, slippery movie about the nature of girlhood.

films.title: Smoking Causes Coughing
films.synopsis: After a bloody battle with a foam-rubber turtle nearly goes awry, the blue spandex-clad, smokin’ hot Tobacco Force are ordered to undergo a week of team morale-building. But their ill-timed lakeside retreat only opens the way for an Evil Emperor to annihilate the earth. Fondly riffing on memories of Mighty Morphin Power Rangers and Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, Deerskin director Quentin Dupieux concocts the surprisingly chill superhero sendup that the world so desperately needs right now.

films.title: Showing Up
films.synopsis: 2:00PM, 6:30PM 4:15PM, 8:45PM Lizzie (Michelle Williams) has a gallery show in a week. But like most of us, she is occupied by keeping a roof over her head. Her boss is her mom, so there’s that. And her landlady, Joanne (Hong Chau) is both a more successful artist, and infuriatingly unconcerned that her hot water isn’t working. Kelly Reichardt’s latest is a gently observant, wry, understated film about carving out a creative life without much reward or recognition.

films.title: Rodeo
films.synopsis: They call her “the witch”. Julia (the remarkable Julie Ledru) is a loner and a weirdo, even among the wild clan of motocross bikers she latches on to. But when it comes to scamming, she’s got that down to a fine art. Hard to argue when she brings in a string of high priced rides, corralled from internet innocents. She’s not really accepted, but tolerated. Then she ups the stakes, pitching an audacious heist. Lola Quavron’s art-house Fast & Furious drama is tough, authentic, and burns like gasoline.

films.title: Last Film Show
films.synopsis: Slumdog Millionaire meets Cinema Paradiso? There’s someting of The Fabelmans too in this semi-autobiographical story about a 9-year-old boy whose first trip to the movies proves life-changing. Samay—who knows little beyond rural Gujarat—has seen the light. He returns to the Galaxy day after day, trading his lunch for free movies, befriending the projectionist, even building his own projector. A passion project for Pan Nalin (Samsara) with hommages to Leone, Tarkovsky et al, this is luminous filmmaking.

films.title: Navalny
films.synopsis: As enthralling as any thriller, Canadian Daniel Roher’s Academy Award-winning documentary gives us the inside story as the outspoken Russian dissident recovers from a near fatal illness, and through extraordinary digital detective work with Bellingcat pieces together the evidence proving that Russian security forces attempted to assassinate him. “The attitude of Mr. Navalny and his colleagues is fearless, in a country governed by fear. Thrillers are rarely so inspiring.” JOHN ANDERSON, WALL STREET JOURNAL

films.title: Singin’ in the Rain
films.synopsis: The greatest movie musical ever made, Stanley Donen and Gene Kelly’s sublime Hollywood on Hollywood satire is dynamic, romantic, and very funny, with some of the most memorable dance numbers ever shot—including, of course, the legendary title number. Kelly is the stuntman who breaks into silent era Hollywood to become an action star. But the entire industry is upended with the invention of sound recording. A touchstone for Damien Chazelle’s Babylon, in Sight & Sound’s canonical poll it came in at #10.

films.title: La Bête Humaine
films.synopsis: A stationmaster with a pretty wife (Simone Simon) murders the wealthy businessman who is her sugar daddy. There is a witness, but train engineer Lanthier (Jean Gabin) prefers class solidarity to snitching, and anyway, the woman is awfully pretty... Updating and condensing Zola’s 1890s novel, Renoir makes vividly authentic use of the trains and railway depot at Le Havre and somehow makes us care deeply about a trio of characters who well and truly go off the rails. Remade by Fritz Lang as Human Desire. “Renoir aided by a magnificent cast gets right underneath the plot... he is a director who knows how to get the most out of the everyday life of his characters, the routine of their work—in this case the immediate surroundings of a great railway station— all the small incidents which do not advance the plot. As if a plot mattered at all except as a dramatised illustration of a character and a way of life.” GRAHAM GREENE, THE SPECTATOR

films.title: La Chienne
films.synopsis: A hen-pecked office clerk and Sunday painter, Legrand (Michel Simon) is seduced by Lulu (Janie Marese) at the behest of her pimp. He sets her up in a studio-apartment and worries about how to extricate himself from his wife while Lulu cashes in on his paintings... Is it a tragedy or a comedy, debate two puppets in the wonderfully bizarre prologue. In Renoir’s supremely diffident handling of his second sound film, it’s both. (Remade by Fritz Lang in 1945 as the noir classic Scarlet Street.) “La Chienne is a ferocious, bitterly ironic drama, a diabolical satire on bourgeois hypocrisy that replaces complicitous laughter with accusatory roars of derision.” RICHARD BRODY, THE NEW YORKER

films.title: Le Corbeau
films.synopsis: One of the most cynical mystery thrillers of a cynical era, this searing drama exposes a midsized town to the contagion of rumour and innuendo when poison pen letters expose the lies and hypocrisies of prominent citizens. Probably the most honest film to come out of Vichy France, it made for such uncomfortable viewing it was subsequently banned as a slur on the national character. Guilt and paranoia are pervasive here, everyone is susceptible to infection. Clouzot—the French Hitchcock— spares no one. “Unforgettable... Le Corbeau is a hellbrew that has lost not a fraction of its flavor, and it feels all to pertinent to the age of trolls.” ANTHONY LANE, THE NEW YORKER

films.title: Le Jour Se Lève
films.synopsis: Holed up in a room awaiting capture or death, Jean Gabin reflects on the circumstances which brought him to this fate. The doom-laden sense of existential alienation and austere, claustrophobic atmosphere clearly anticipated the mood and form of American film noir, just as Gabin’s rough-hewn romantic predates American counterparts like John Garfield and Humphrey Bogart as an iconic working class hero. “More than a beautiful film, it’s indispensible.” BERTRAND TAVERNIER (DIRECTOR, ROUND MIDNIGHT; COUP DE TORCHON) “The realism of Le Jour se Lève is as rigorous as that of a poem. It is all written in verse or at least in prose which is invisibly poetic... While at the same time it is never really possible in the film to dissociate technique from scenario, form from content, subject for style. And that is the mark of good cinema.” ANDRE BAZIN In French with Subtitles subtitles.

films.title: Bob le Flambeur
films.synopsis: Among the demimonde of Montmartre, Bob the gambler, he’s a living legend, a real class act. Whether it’s cards, horses or roulette, Bob will place his bets and never wavers, win or lose. He bets on people too. When his luck turns sour, Bob comes out of retirement for one last big score—an audacious heist from the casino at Deauville. Of all French filmmakers, Meville was the most overtly influenced by American film noir, but Bob in turn would influence heist films all the way up to Ocean’s Eleven.

films.title: Port of Shadows
films.synopsis: Gabin is an army deserter planning to hop a boat to South America in foggy Le Havre when he meets and falls in love with a trench-coated, 18-year-old Michelle Morgan, whose various entanglements with men (Michel Simon; Pierre Brasseur) are no less thorny. This is the template for the fatalistic “poetic realism” which became Carné’s stock in trade. Port of Shadows articulates a mood of despair so effectively, some claimed its success guaranteed France’s imminent defeat. Dark, mysterious and shrouded in sensuous fog that Gabin’s character says is part of the emotional weather he carries around with him… The dialogue by Jacques Prévert boasts glorious lines comparable to those in Children of Paradise. Nelly says: ‘Each time the sun rises we think something new will happen.’ Pessimistic, yet strangely sublime.” PETER BRADSHAW, THE GUARDIAN

films.title: Quai des Orfèvres
films.synopsis: After fighting off the advances of a lascivious movie producer and, she thinks, killing him, showgirl Jenny Lamour (Suzy Delair) decides to conceal the episode from her jealous husband (Bernard Blier), unaware that he planned to kill the man himself. Complications, as they say, ensue. This richly seasoned police thriller restored Clouzot’s good standing in France, although it’s populated with prostitutes, lesbians and pornographers. At least there’s Louis Jouvet’s police investigator to affect some sense of decency. “An urbane police procedural, a cracking whodunnit, a Golddiggers sex comedy, and a stealth backstage musical… Clouzot and his restless camera track lives that seem already to have been unfolding before we’re invited in to regard them. Paris bustles in his backgrounds, a riotous can-can one moment and a shadowed dreamscape the next.” ALAN SCHEURSTUHL, THE VILLAGE VOICE

films.title: Touchez Pas Au Grisbi
films.synopsis: In this rueful crime film about the difficulty of bowing out and letting go, a grey-haired Jean Gabin allows sentiment to trump business. Before it’s even begun, Max and his longtime partner Riton have pulled off a heist rich enough to retire on. But a rival gangster kidnaps Riton and wants to swap the man for the loot. The missing link between Le Jour se Lève and Jean-Pierre Melville’s long line of Gallic noir, it’s like a French ‘50s Goodfellas. Look for Lino Ventura and Jeanne Moreau in supporting roles. “Unbeatable as a gripping story of loyalty, betrayal and the price of friendship.” KENNETH TURAN, LOS ANGELES TIMES

films.title: Les Diaboliques
films.synopsis: Even today, nearly 70 years later, this classic suspense film will have you on the edge of your seat. Paul Meurisse is the tyrannical headmaster of a provincial boarding school. Abusive not only to the pupils in his charge, he’s also pushed both his wife (Vera Clouzot) and his lover (Simone Signoret) to breaking point. Finding common purpose, they drown him in the bath then dump the body in the swimming pool. So far so good. But when the body disappears they start to panic... Screening in a 35mm print.

films.title: Elevator to the Gallows
films.synopsis: 24-year-old Louis Malle came out of the gate with this cool noir about a perfect murder that goes horribly wrong. A man (Maurice Ronet) kills his boss in his office, only to get stuck in the lift... Meanwhile, his lover (Jeanne Moreau) is in the dark about all this and going frantic. It’s an ironic genre exercise but the textures are fresh: Henri Decae’s monochrome images of nocturnal Paris paired

films.title: Le Trou (The Hole)
films.synopsis: Becker spent a year in a German POW camp. This meticulous recreation of a true 1946 prison break is the best the genre ever produced: claustrophobic, intense, utterly authentic. Becker co-wrote it with one of the original prisoners, and cast it with non-professionals, including another of the cellmates. Without music or melodrama, the film builds formidable tension through its concentration of time and space, its sensitivity to sound, and the discreet accumulation of nuance. “A masterpiece... And I weigh my words carefully: the greatest French film of all time.” JEAN-PIERRE MELVILLE “Le Trou is an escape film under the microscope, analyzed down to its basic elemental foundation... it may be the perfect incarnation of that genre.” CHADWICK JENKINS, POP MATTERS

films.title: Rififi
films.synopsis: Relocated to Paris after being named as a Communist at the HUAC hearings, American Jules Dassin took on a sordid heist novel as an assignment and crafted this expert and justly famous thriller. Celebrated for the long, superbly choreographed, near-silent safe-breaking sequence, the film is more concerned with the fallout from the job as the plan falls apart. (The Asphalt Jungle must have been an influence here.) Dassin also appears as expert safecracker Cesar le Milanais (under the pseudonym Perlo Vita). “The best film noir I have ever seen.” FRANCOIS TRUFFAUT “The best of all heist movies.” ALAN SCHERSTUHL, VILLAGE VOICE In French with Subtitles subtitles.

films.title: Living
films.synopsis: Bill Nighy was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Actor for his deeply moving performance as a London civil servant who reassesses his life when he's given a terminal cancer diagnosis. Suddenly a petition for a new children's playground becomes a mission for him. Kazuo Ishiguru wrote the screenplay, based on Akira Kurosawa's classic Ikiru, itself inspired by a novella by Leo Tolstoy.

films.title: The Colour of Ink
films.synopsis: For Jason Logan, master inkmaker, pigmentation is a living element. He forages for raw hues of red, blue, and black, materials that he can scratch, pummel, and boil to make inks that might be unique, or might draw down on traditions that stretch back thousands of years. Who knew you can milk molluscs for a particular scarlet dye? In another vignette, an artist repurposes black ink preserved in an octopus fossil dating back 95-million years. This radiant, artisanal doc is a real eye-opener.

films.title: back home
films.synopsis: In 1999, 11-year-old Nisha Platzer lost her brother, Josh, to suicide. Twenty years later, her search for a specialized medical treatment inadvertently leads her to the door of Josh’s chosen family. An eloquent collage of candid interviews, lyrical visuals, evocative motifs, and hand-processed sequences, Platzer’s back home gently asserts that both grieving and healing are meant to be communal experiences. As it builds to a quietly staggering close, it instills a desire to connect with those you hold dear.

films.title: Rematriation
films.synopsis: From the front lines of the fight to preserve BC’s old growth forests, Rematriation is both an urgent wake-up call and an inspiring tribute to land defenders. Aggressive logging destroys more than 10,000 hectares of our province each year. Less than 3% of our virgin forests remains. At Fairy Creek, a coalition of First Nations and environmental activists refuse to stand down. Alexi Liotti’s passionate, respectful film gives these protesters a platform and amplifies their call to action. Filmmaker panel: Earth Day (Saturday, April 22)

films.title: Nam June Paik: Moon is the Oldest TV
films.synopsis: 1:00PM, 7:25PM Prodigious Korean pianist Nam June Paik was expected to pursue a prestigious career in classical music. An encounter with avant-garde composer John Cage changed everything. Paik embraced performance art as central to his compositional work, joined Fluxus, and then discovered television, the apparatus that inspire his most acclaimed and influential work. Amanda Kim’s doc—narrated by Steven Yuen—makes a strong case that Paik was a genius who anticipated the internet and transformed video art. In English, German, and Korean

films.title: Rome Open City
films.synopsis: As fascist rule finally crumbled, Italian cinema gave birth to Rome Open City and neorealism, a new form of filmmaking. Using black market film stock, the street locations of war-torn Rome and mostly non-professional actors, Roberto Rossellini tells the story of a Communist Resistance leader sheltered from the Gestapo by Pina (Anna Magnani) and a sympathetic priest. The movie’s authenticity and urgency took the world by storm and Magnani was recognized as one of the great actors of her era. Guest presenter: artist/curator/producer Hank Bull.

films.title: The Merry Widow introduced by Devan Scott
films.synopsis: Madame Sonia (Jeanette Macdonald), Marshovia’s richest widow, is set to leave for Paris in search of a suitor. Count Danilo (Maurice Chevalier) embarks on a mission to woo her (and her fortune) back. The Merry Widow sees Lubitsch come alive in this brazenly risqué precode adaptation of Franz Lehar’s 1905 operetta. Join us for one of cinema’s most unjustly forgotten, not to mention naughtiest, musicals.

films.title: Hilma
films.synopsis: Hilma af Klint was an abstract artist before there was abstract art... Not that she would describe her paintings that way: the C19th Swede believed her brush was directed by the spirits; she was mapping an invisible terrain. A feminist, a lesbian, and a spiritualist, she was decades ahead of her time. Lasse Hallström’s rich, fulsome biopic is always engaged with the work. Tora Hallström, the director’s daughter, is the exuberant, youthful Hilma; her mother Lena Olin plays the character in later years.

films.title: Little Richard: I Am Everything
films.synopsis: Tutti frutti, oh rootie! The world was not ready for the irresistible force that is Little Richard, the rock n roll icon who influenced everyone from Bowie to Prince, Mick Jagger to Harry Styles. This definitive doc doesn’t need to break the mould: its subject all ready did all that, and more. Little Richard wasn’t just unapologetically Black, he was flamboyantly, outrageously queer, even if his lyrics were straightened out for mass consumption in the 1950s. He was also, off and on, a born again Christian.

films.title: John and the Missus
films.synopsis: The late Gordon Pinsent wrote and directed, as well as stars in, this forgotten gem of Canadian filmmaking, based on his own novel. The year is 1962 and the setting is a pretty coastal town in Newfoundland, Cop Cove, named not for the police but for the copper which is the community’s livelihood. John has worked his entire life in the mine, and so has almost every other fella he knows. But the mine’s played out, and the authorities would have the townsfolk relocate. John though, he has his own ideas... Special Guest: Producer Peter O’Brian (John and the Missus; My American Cousin; The Grey Fox; Hollywood North)

films.title: River
films.synopsis: In the tradition of Koyaanisquatsi, Anthropocene, and Jennifer Peedom’s magesterial Mountain, River is a symphonic ode to nature, and a contemplation on how man has explored, coursed, traversed, harnessed, harvested, and come to rely on rivers over millennia. The imagery here is jaw-droppingly spectacular, not just eye-opening but mind’s eye-opening. The soundtrack, with music by Richard Tognetti performed by the Australian Chamber Orchestra, and by Jonny Greenwood and Radiohead, is out of this world.

films.title: Man With a Movie Camera
films.synopsis: Certainly among the most exhilarating movies ever made, no matter that it’s nearly a hundred years old now, Dziga Vertov’s whirligig portrait of modern life as experienced in Soviet cities (Moscow, Odessa and Kyiv) uses a battery of innovative photographic and editing techniques including fast and slow motion, superimposition, freeze frames, jump cuts to create a purely filmic, universal language. This was the only silent film to crack the top 10 in Sight & Sound’s poll of the Greatest Films Ever Made. Guest lecture on Sunday by Ernest Mathjis, Professor in Film and Media Studies, University of British Columbia.

films.title: The Night of the 12th
films.synopsis: Moll’s police procedural is a weighty, compelling whodunnit which builds up a devastating picture of widespread misogyny. A young woman is murdered on her way home from a late night party. For Captain Vives (Bastien Bouillon), it’s a tough first case. The crime scene provides scant clues, and the more he finds out about the sexually promiscuous victim, the wider the field of suspects. Based on a true crime book, The Night of the 12th is a modern classic on a par with Zodiac and Memories of Murder.

films.title: Twice Colonized
films.synopsis: Renowned Inuit lawyer Aaju Peter has led a lifelong fight for the rights of her people.
