When her son suddenly dies, Aaju embarks on a journey to reclaim her language and culture after a lifetime of whitewashing and forced assimilation. But is it possible to change the world and mend your own wounds at the same time? Lin Alluna’s candid portrait balances the public strength and inner turmoil of an inspiring, fearless woman who still bears the scars of a childhood torn between two cultures. In English, Danish, Kalaallisut, and Inuktitut

films.title: Cadejo Blanco
films.synopsis: A young woman infiltrates the underworld in order to find the truth behind her sister’s disappearance in this nail-biting thriller in the vein of Miss Bala. American writer-director Justin Lerner spent years in Guatemala working with street kids and marginalized youths, learning about gang culture, and developing the script in collaboration with his first time cast. This authenticity underscores a movie that grows in authority and conviction the deeper its resourceful heroine digs herself into mortal danger.

films.title: The Searchers
films.synopsis: Ranked #15 in the Sight & Sound Greatest Films poll, The Searchers explicitly confronts the latent racist pathology embedded in the mythology of the western. At the same time, this film about a racist is itself unwittingly racist, especially in its lazy scenes of comic relief. Stunningly shot, it is both John Ford’s most terrible and most beautiful work... framed, as so often, against, the majestic backdrop of Monument Valley (see the essay film The Taking). This is a seminal movie, and a problematic one. “The Searchers is perhaps the greatest Hollywood film that few people have seen.”

films.title: Close to Vermeer
films.synopsis: Go behind the scenes of the largest Vermeer exhibition ever mounted, now on view at the Rijksmuseum in Amsterdam. Capturing the imagination of the art world, the Rijksmuseum’s Vermeer retrospective is nothing short of an historic event. This fascinating doc is a unique opportunity to discover what goes on behind the scenes, from the latest techniques for determining what makes a Vermeer truly a Vermeer, to new discoveries while searching for the master’s paintings around the world.

films.title: Joyland
films.synopsis: Unemployed and emasculated in the shadow of his father and older brother, Haider accepts a job at a theatre as a backup dancer for Biba, a trans woman trying to succeed as an erotic dancer, hiding the truth from his family as he begins an affair with her. Joyland weaves a rich tapestry of complex characters, finding moments of intimacy and grace as it explores a patriarchal family bursting at the seams with sexual repression and buckling under cultural pressures and expectations of gender and tradition.

films.title: Passion
films.synopsis: 4:00PM, 8:45PM Previously unreleased in North America, the second film from Drive My Car director Ryûsuke Hamaguchi proves as captivating as his subsequent achievements. When Tomoya and Kaho announce their engagement, their friends’ reaction is seeded with doubt; Tomoya is well known for his womanizing ways, meanwhile his buddy Kenichiro is in love with Kaho... Hamaguchi drills into these midlife romantic triangulations with the kind of intense scrutiny you might find in a play by Edward Albee or Harold Pinter.

films.title: Blind Willow, Sleeping Woman
films.synopsis: SAT MAY 6, SUN MAY 7 MON MAY 8, TUE MAY 9 4:20PM, 9:00PM Based on short stories by Haruki Murakami (Drive My Car), this whimsical animated feature by Pierre Földes transports us to Tokyo, 2011, shortly after the earthquake. In shock, Kyoko spends five days glued to the news - then walks out on her husband, Komura. He takes leave from his job at the bank and sets off on a pilgrimage of sorts. Meanwhile his colleague, Katagiri, is visited by a giant frog who informs him they must work together to save Tokyo from a second devastating quake...

films.title: The Melt Goes On Forever: The Art and Times of David Hammons
films.synopsis: An astonishing documentary about the elusive and provocative African-American artist David Hammons, The Melt Goes On Forever chronicles the legendary artist’s incredible body of work, firmly rooted in the questioning of dominant culture and exposing racial injustice. Using archival footage, interviews with artists, curators, and critics, alongside animation, this film is a remarkable record of the work of an artist who constantly defies the establishment and remains subversive at every turn.

films.title: Róise & Frank
films.synopsis: 2:30PM, 6:30PM 12:00PM, 4:30PM Two years after Frank’s passing, Róise is still grieving her husband of 40 years when a stray dog takes a shine to her. Róise isn’t looking for a pet but this dog won’t take no for an answer: he follows her on her walks, makes himself at home, and it’s not long before he’s helping himself to a steak dinner. That was Frank’s favourite too. Indeed, Róise decides he’s been reincarnated. This Gaelic-language charmer just wants to make you feel a little better about the world. In Irish Gaelic

films.title: The Three Musketeers
films.synopsis: Richard Lester’s boisterous swashbuckler mixes action, slapstick comedy and bawdy romance to stirring effect. Michael York plays the impetuous country bumpkin who arrives in Paris and manages to offend Athos (Oliver Reed), Porthos (Frank Finlay) and Aramis (Richard Chamberlain) before dusk. Fortunately the three musketeers find common cause with this born swordsman when it comes to defending the Queen’s honour. Also starring the late Raquel Welch (1940-2023). Fifty years on, this remains the most entertaining adaptation of the Alexander Dumas classic. 4k Restoration. + Short Film: The Moviegoer (Ross Munro, 2022, 19 min) (Sunday matinee only)

films.title: Tokyo Story
films.synopsis: Ozu’s most celebrated film follows an aging couple as they come to the city and make the rounds of their now grown children. Busy with their own lives, the children have little time or patience for their parents, who are quickly packed off to hot springs in Osaka. Then the mother, Tomi, falls ill… Less playful and more somber than many of his films, Tokyo Story is typical of Ozu in its seeming simplicity, its reserve and deep compassion. It came in fourth in the latest iteration of Sight and Sound’s poll.

films.title: Squaring the Circle (The Story of Hipgnosis)
films.synopsis: Pink Floyd, Led Zeppelin, Wings, Peter Gabriel... these 1970s rock kings all turned to the design studio Hipgnosis to create iconic l.p. sleeves for albums like The Dark Side of the Moon and Band on the Run. A labour of love, this doc from Anton Corbijn (who has created art work for U2, Tom Waits and The Rolling Stones himself) is a must for fans of classic rock. Even if you are too young to have fetishized record sleeves, it’s fascinating to explore the creative alchemy between sound and vision.

films.title: Big Fight in Little Chinatown
films.synopsis: The issues that we know face Chinatown in Vancouver—high rents; gentrification; the exodus to the suburbs—are not unique. Karen Cho's acclaimed documentary places our story in the context of Chinatowns in New York, Montreal, Toronto and San Francisco. And in interviews with activists, business owners, academics and community members, Cho reminds us what is at stake in the form of cultural legacy, and that this is also a story of resilience and empowerment.

films.title: Scarlet
films.synopsis: Raised by her father in a small French village after WWI, Juliette (Juliette Jouan) is a dreamy young woman encouraged by a witch’s prophecy to expect deliverance on “scarlet sails”. When a handsome pilot (Louis Garrel) literally drops from the sky, Juliette is swept off her feet. Making his first French-language film, Martin Eden director Pietro Marcello has created a captivating, poetic fable humming with music, love and fantasy.

films.title: Trenque Lauquen
films.synopsis: “Farewell, farewell. I’m leaving, I’m leaving.” That’s the note Laura left, abandoning her research in the titular town. Her boyfriend Rafael and colleague Ezequiel take up the search, but the harder they look the more mysteries they find. From the company behind La Flor, Laura Citarella’s epic—which is split into two parts and 12 chapters - would surely have appealed to Jorge Luis Borges for the ease with which it slips between narratives, following diversions until we’re all happily lost in the woods. Screening with a 30 minute intermission

films.title: T.S. Eliot’s The Four Quartets
films.synopsis: TS Eliot wrote The Four Quartets in the shadow of WWII. The poem-suite is a searching examination of who and what we are, a meditation on human experience, time, and the divine. During the lockdown, Ralph Fiennes committed the work to memory and in 2021 he brought it to the theatre as a one-man show. Filmed by his sister, Sophie, this is a remarkably intimate, mesmerizing, and enthralling communion with one of the great works of twentieth century literature. “Fiennes brings the fire.” TEO BUGBEE, THE NEW YORK TIMES

films.title: White Balls on Walls
films.synopsis: When Sarah Vos started filming her documentary in 2019, 90% of Amsterdam’s Museum of Modern Art collection was signed by white men. The Stedelijk’s recently appointed director, Rein Wolfs, determines that redressing this imbalance must be his priority. But how does the quest for greater diversity impact curation? Are the artist’s gender and skin colour criteria for evaluating his/her art? Is the canon canceled? Voss’s film is a shrewd, ironic, objective temperature gauge on the highly politicized cultural battle over “Woke”. We will follow our first screening on June 7th with a panel discussion. In Dutch, English, German, and Sranantongo

films.title: Other People’s Children
films.synopsis: The luminous Virginie Efira (Madeleine Collins) stars in this affecting portrait of a teacher whose biological clock is ticking. Rachel falls in love with Ali (Roschdy Zem), but their relationship is complicated by his fouryear-old daughter Leila. The girl is a treasure. But she already has a mother... Rebecca Zlotowski explores the nuances of this dynamic with great sensitivity. It’s the kind of relationship drama the French do so well; when it’s over you know you’ve experienced something true.

films.title: Chile ‘76
films.synopsis: Actress Manuela Martelli (Machuca) makes an impressive debut as writer-director with this tense and compelling drama about a doctor’s wife (Aline Kuppenheim) who is drawn into sheltering a political agitator during the time of Chile’s dictatorship. Carmen is persuaded by her friend, Padre Sanchez (Hugo Medina), to help care for the wounded fugitive—a gesture of Christian charity rather than political solidarity. But it’s a big step, and it leads her down a dangerous path...

films.title: Daliland
films.synopsis: 5:10PM, 7:45PM This is James’s job: assistant to a renegade genius. We are in New York City in 1974. Dali (Ben Kingsley) winters at the St. Regis. Gala (Barbara Sukowa) handles the money and any boytoy she can get a hold of. Fair to say they have seen better days, but these superannuated septuagenarian surrealists still know how to command the scene. As for James (Christopher Birney), he’s simply dazzled. Mary Harron (American Psycho; I Shot Andy Warhol) paints a sympathetic cine-portrait of the artist as an old man, still crazy after all these years.

films.title: Beautiful City
films.synopsis: The second film from writer-director Asghar Farhadi (A Separation; The Salesman; A Hero) again finds a potent dramatic entry point to explore themes that relate to both politics and ethics. Recently released from a juvenile detention centre, Ala combines forces with Firoozeh (Taraneh Alidoosti) in order to plead the case for his friend/her brother, Akbar, who having turned 18 is now eligible for the death penalty for the killing of his girlfriend. Akbar’s fate lies in the hands of the victim’s father, who in Iran’s judicial system holds the power to grant clemency. But he remains furious, not only with Akbar, but with God himself.

films.title: Dancing in the Dust
films.synopsis: With films like A Separation, The Salesman, A Hero, and The Past, Asghar Farhadi has established himself as one of the leading writer-directors in world cinema. Here, for the first time, we present his first two feature films, Dancing in the Dust (2003) and Beautiful City (2004), both recently restored. Farhadi’s debut is a love story of sorts: young and impulsive, Nazar woos and weds Reyhane, but his family and friends are scandalized; her mother is said to be a sex worker. Regretfully, Nazar divorces. Determined to pay his ex wife the marriage and separation monies he owes, he begs a taciturn old snake hunter to teach him his lucrative — but risky — trade. The film’s second half – largely set in the desert – is a compelling stand-off between the aggressive, passionate youth and the unimpressed veteran, who’s seen it all before and knows full well that Nazar is in over his head. (For one thing, the kid is mortally afraid of snakes.) Still, there’s something about his convictions – confused as they may be – which touches the benumbed older man.

films.title: Howl’s Moving Castle
films.synopsis: Teenager Sophie is cursed by the Witch of Waste and finds herself trapped in the body of an old woman, and is unable to tell her mother or anyone else what has happened. She finds help of sorts with the wizard Howl, living as a servant in his astonishing walking castle. Tragic, enthralling, heartfelt, surreal, fantastic... it’s the kind of children’s film which puts most adult dramas to shame. Sunday matinee: English language dub. Monday evening: Japanese with English subtitles. In English, Japanese

films.title: Tales from Earthsea
films.synopsis: The Kingdom of Enlad is in ruins. As crops dwindle, mankind stands on the verge of total chaos. Lord Sparrowhawk, a powerful wizard, and Arren, a troubled young prince, search for the force behind this mysterious imbalance that threatens to destroy the land of Earthsea in a tale of redemption and self-discovery full of adventure and peril. Considered a disappointment in 2006, this free adaptation of Ursula K LeGuin is ripe for reassessment, offering a potent blend of myth, philosophy and dragons. Sunday matinee: English language version. Monday evening: Japanese with English subtitles. In English, Japanese S T U D I O G H I B L I F O R E V E R F A R H A D I X 2

films.title: Polarized
films.synopsis: Lisa (Holly Deveaux) and her folks have lost their farm to the bank. Not only that, her father is succumbing to cancer. Like others in their rural community, they are resentful of the Palestinian immigrants who are making a go of it with their new “urban farm” facility. After a racist outburst, Lisa is fired by her boss, Dalia (Maxine Denis). But the two young women patch up their differences. As they become friends, they realize that they have more in common than their conservative families imagine.

films.title: Making Time
films.synopsis: This is much more than a film about watchmakers. It’s about Time, how we measure it, what it means to us, how to treasure it and how to spend it. “A watchmaker is a God, creating an object that comes to life in our hands,” says someone. Maybe, but the extraordinary craftspeople in Liz Unna’s exquisite movie are all very human, their stories often bruising, full of sharp reversals, brushed

films.title: Fashion Reimagined
films.synopsis: We buy three times as many clothes as we did in 1980. And we wear them for half as long. Becky Hunter’s film is a portrait of UK designer Amy Powney (Creative Director, Mother of Pearl). Powney was raised by environmentalists living off the grid on a farm. She rebelled by developing a passion for clothes, and won the prestigious Vogue Young Designer of the Year Award. She decides to use the prize money to develop a genuinely sustainable clothes collection. As the film shows, that’s easier said than done.

films.title: Tramps!
films.synopsis: In London, as the 1970s slumped towards the 80s, queer kids who had had their fill of punk began to explore a more flamboyant look: Glam meets highwayman frills and laces, with plenty of slap. The New Romantics emerged from the club scene and birthed bands like Spandau Ballet. Meet the the perenially young people who created the “proto-drag” scene from nothing: jewelry designer Judy Blame, filmmaker John Maybury, choreographer Michael Clark, and style icons Princess Julia and Scarlett Cannon.

films.title: Smoke Signals
films.synopsis: Now considered a classic, Smoke Signals was a game changer for Indigenous Cinema, written, directed, and acted by Indigenous people from Turtle Island. It's a culturally significant film, where Indigenous people felt seen and were humanized in a way that wasn't done before. Victor (Adam Beach), a disgruntled young man, embarks on a journey to forgive his father. Arnold (Gary Farmer) volunteers to join Victor, together they seek clarity and acceptance. All together now: "Hey Victor!"

films.title: Blood Quantum
films.synopsis: An award-winning visionary who specialized in the horror genre, and now recently an ancestor, Jeff Barnaby created many waves for Indigenous Cinema. This apocalyptic film references the colonial laws regarding Indigenous status (Blood Quantum in America). A zombie outbreak has left rural Quebec looking like a butcher’s block and, amidst the blood splatter, a pattern has emerged: while the white population is being decimated, the Mi’gmaq people at the Red Crow reserve appear to be immune to the virus. In English and Mi’gmaq

films.title: Kímmapiiyipitssini: The Meaning of Empathy + panel discussion
films.synopsis: Follow filmmaker Elle-Máijá Tailfeathers as she creates an intimate portrait of her community and the impacts of the substance use and overdose epidemic. Witness the change brought by community members with substance-use disorder, first responders and medical professionals as they strive for harm reduction in the Kainai First Nation. Panel discussion to follow hosted by Story Money Impact. “A soaring portrait of tragedy and resilience, yes, but also a handbook for healing that those of us in the privileged classes could learn a lesson or two from.” LAUREN WISSOT, FILMMAKER MAGAZINE In English, Blackfoot with English subtitles. Free Event Free Event

films.title: Back to the Future + 80s Costume Contest + The Dimes in Concert Back to the Future
films.synopsis: Cinema is a time machine. We are in 2023. The lights go down. The film begins. And we are transported. To 1985... to 1955... and back... back to the future. A youthful Michael J Fox is small town teen Marty McFly, propelled to the Eisenhower era by his friend Doc Brown’s souped up DeLorean. For all its knowing Oedipal comedy and irresistible ingenuity, the film’s slick confidence in 80s modernity now looks quaint. The movie hasn’t changed. But the way we see it has.

films.title: Escape from New York
films.synopsis: Future past: from the perspective of 1981, John Carpenter imagines America in 1997. Crime so rampant Manhattan is a sealed-offopen air prison. When Air Force One crashes next to the World Trade Center the President is held hostage, and master criminal Snake Plissken (Kurt Russell, sporting an eye patch and a sneer) is selected to mount a 24-hour rescue mission. Or else. Escape... is a hugely enjoyable action movie, deeply cynical about the state of things, juiced by a gallery of quirky character actors.

films.title: Subtraction
films.synopsis: Farzaneh (Taraneh Alidoosti) is dismayed when she spots her husband on a city bus. She follows him and sees what looks awfully like evidence of an extra-marital affair. Jalal (Navid Mohammadzadeh) swears his innocence and can prove his whereabouts. To say more would be to risk spoiling this genuinely unpredictable mystery. What we can say is, the actors do exceptional work to ground Haghighi’s bold conceit in psychological truth. But above all it’s a wild ride that keeps you guessing right up to the end.

films.title: Ponyo
films.synopsis: Written by Miyazaki himself and influenced by The Little Mermaid, this is a wonderfully strange fable about a curious fish-girl who breaks away from her siblings and over-protective father and winds up stranded on the shore. There she’s rescued by a little boy, Sosuke, who names her Ponyo—to the anger of her father, who unleashes the fury of the ocean to get her back. “Miyazaki knows the secret language of children; he dives deep into the pool of childhood dreams and fears and, through his animagic, takes children down to where they can breathe, and feel, and be free.” RICHARD CORLISS, TIME Sunday matinee: English language dub. Monday & Sunday evening: Japanese

films.title: L’Immensità
films.synopsis: 4:00PM, 8:00PM Inspired by filmmaker Emanuele Crialese’s own transition, this is the story of Andrew (Vincenzo Amato), assigned female at birth, who yearns for another life, one at odds

films.title: Music for Black Pigeons
films.synopsis: Jazz greats Lee Konitz, Paul Motian, Bill Frisell and Joe Lovano are among the collaborators who jump to work with acclaimed Danish composer Jakob Bro over the course of this gently eccentric but charming, funny, philosophical music doc.

films.title: North of Normal
films.synopsis: Having spent her early years in a wilderness commune founded by her anti-establishment grandfather, Cea must shed her alternative upbringing and acclimatize to civilization when her mother, Michelle, desires even greater freedom. Adapting Cea Sunrise Person’s beloved memoir for the big screen, Carly Stone (The New Romantic) brings both compassion and energy to this tale of a young woman’s bid to come of age while living with a mother experiencing arrested development.

films.title: Once Upon a Time in Uganda
films.synopsis: For anyone who ever wanted to make a movie Isaac Nabwana should be a source of inspiration. A self-taught entrepren(-aut)eur, Nabwana swapped making bricks for making action films. His base is the village of Wakaliga, on the outskirts of Kampala, Uganda. His cast and crew are his friends and neighbours, and he’s made more than 40 films, with an average budget of just $200. Even then, it’s hard to turn a profit. Enter Alan Hofmanis, an American film festival programmer and Nabawana’s biggest fan... “The perfect representation of the enduring spirit of independent cinema, our love for movies, and how they bring the world together.” ETHAN ANDERTON, SLASHFILM

films.title: So Much Tenderness
films.synopsis: 2:30PM, 7:00PM Aurora (Noëlle Schönwald) decides to flee her native Colombia after the suspicious death of her husband. With the help of a Canadian couple (Deragh Campbell and director Kazik Radwanski), she makes her way to Toronto to start over—but the past is not so easily left behind. Lina Rodríguez (This Time Tomorrow) imparts a sense of lived experience rather than walking us through a connect-the-dots storybook. It’s a challenge for which curious audiences will be well rewarded.

films.title: Afire
films.synopsis: Christian Petzold (Transit; Phoenix) returns with this serio-comic portrait of a sulky writer struggling with his second novel at his friend’s summer cottage. Leon (Thomas Schubert) is stuck inside his head most of the time. So much so, he’s not really alive to what’s going on around him, except in as much as it effects him negatively. Leon is especially put out to find they’re going to be sharing the cottage with a stranger, Nadja (Paula Beer), who turns out to be lovely, which is even more annoying...

films.title: 2001: A Space Odyssey
films.synopsis: Based on Arthur C Clarke’s short story The Sentinel, 2001 redefined the sci-figenre. With its radical structure, scant dialogue and oblique narrative, this was the first movie to emulate the philosophical seriousness of writers like Clarke and Philip K Dick, and the first to see that special effects could become an integral component in the art form. Experienced on the big screen, it remains a spellbinding film, with a genuine sense of awe. 2001 came in at #6 in the 2022 Sight & Sound poll of critics and academics, but topped the list voted by film directors.

films.title: Final Cut
films.synopsis: 4:10PM, 8:45PM A decade after he won the Academy Award for Best Director for The Artist, Michel Hazanavicius returns with a post-modern comic romp about a moviemaker (Romain Duris) shooting a single-take zombie flick... infected by actual zombies. The opening-night selection of last year’s Cannes, this is a big budget remake of Shin’ichirô Ueda’s cult hit One Cut of the Dead. Featuring a hysterically unhinged turn by Berenice Bejo, Final Cut serves up bloodsoaked high farce par excellence.

films.title: From Up on Poppy Hill
films.synopsis: Set in Yokohama in 1963, this is a poignant teen love story, graceful, understated but full of feeling. Written by Hayao Miyazaki and directed by his son Goro, the movie tells the story of a lonely high school girl who becomes involved in the fight to save a delipidated boys’ club house. “A beautifully artful, wistfully nostalgic coming of age romance!” TWITCH “With its beautiful visuals and songs, Poppy Hill finds a deserving place among its Studio Ghibli peers.” VARIETY Sunday matinee: English language version. Monday evening: Japanese

films.title: The Secret World of Arrietty
films.synopsis: In this adaptation of Mary Norton’s The Borrowers, co-scripted by Hayao Miyazaki himself, Arrietty, a tiny teenager, lives with her parents in the recesses of a suburban home, unbeknown to the homeowner and housekeeper. Like others of her kind, Arrietty remains hidden from her human hosts, but occasionally ventures forth from beneath the floorboards to borrow sugar cubes and other supplies. A secret friendship forms when 12-yearold Shawn meets his tiny housemate, but their relationship could spell danger. Sunday matinee: English language version. Monday evening: Japanese with English subtitles. S T U D I O G H I B L I F O R E V E R !

films.title: Ghostbusters
films.synopsis: Curbed from their cushy university positions, a team of paranormal researchers go private and offer their services to the public. After all, NYC is swarming with supernatural specters in all shapes and sizes. Bill Murray’s smirky Peter Venkman cemented his shtick here, part Groucho Marx, part Elliott Gould. Ghostbusters runs amok with its Reaganite ideological underpinnings but the wisecracks keep on coming, and the goofy ghouls and cool gadgets are great fun.

films.title: E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial
films.synopsis: ET begins with a quick, smart sketch of a typical middle class California family household, much like the one in which Spielberg grew up. There are three kids, teenager Mike, ten-year-old Elliott (Henry Thomas) and threeyear-old Gertie (Drew Barrymore). Mom is loving but too distracted to notice there is an alien living in the closet. One of only a handful of live action children’s films to capture the imaginations of generations, ET has a luminous warmth; it’s a suburban symphony of emotion.

films.title: Passages
films.synopsis: 2:30PM, 6:30PM 4:10PM, 8:30PM Tomas (Franz Rogowski) is a gay filmmaker living in Paris with his partner Martin (Ben Whishaw). Mercurial and needy, Tomas sleeps with Agathe (Adèle Exarchopoulos) at his wrap party. Martin is prepared to let it slide, but Tomas is excited to explore this side of his sexuality, and convinces Agathe that he’s in love with her. The latest from writer-director Ira Sachs (Love Is Strange) is a piercing account of messy emotional lives, powered by a full throttle performance from Franz Rogowski (Great Freedom). “Sachs delivers an achingly beautiful film that’s sexy, sad and so very French.” STEPHEN A RUSSELL, TIME OUT

films.title: Amanda
films.synopsis: 1:30 PM, 8:10 PM Amanda's only friend is the family maid, Judy. This might be cause for concern at any age, but for a 24-year-old? She can't seem to find human connection—and her loneliness only makes her weirder, more defiant, even less social. Carolina Cavalli's quirky Italian comedy has been compared to the work of Noah Baumbach and Greta Gerwig, Yorgos Lanthimos and Wes Anderson, and if that suggests a filmmaker in control of aesthetics, angsty, and

films.title: The Beasts
films.synopsis: In this gripping, tense rural thriller about a French couple trying to make a new life by starting a farm and fixing abandoned homes in Galicia, Spain, director Rodrigo Sorogoyen presents the feral underbelly of country life where tensions between foreigners and locals, educated and uneducated, brutally come to the fore. Filled with powerful performances, especially by the brilliant Marina Foïs, who dominates the latter half of the film with her stubborn determination. “The latest from Spanish director Rodrigo Sorogoyen is a terrific psychological thriller and a brooding, muscular piece of filmmaking which makes the most of both the Galician backdrop and the imposing physicality of Menochet and, as his nemesis Xan, the remarkable Luis Zahera.” WENDY IDE, SCREEN DAILY In Spanish, French, and Galician

films.title: Kokomo City
films.synopsis: The Black trans woman sex worker movie you didn’t know you needed, D. Smith’s doc (she wrote, produced, directed, edited and photographed it) is an outrageously sexy, funny, candidly human and compassionate communiqué from the front lines of the struggle for equality. Smith, who knows of which she speaks, delivers four vital portraits from New York and Atlanta: Daniella, Dominique, Koko Da Doll and Liyah. These women have different styles and stories, but they’re each compelling and charismatic. “As a Black and trans filmmaker, Smith refreshingly creates the space for [her subjects] to be provocative, raw and daringly glamorous in her taboo-breaking work filmed in gleaming black-and-white and edited with a fiery spirit.” TOMRIS LAFFLY, HARPER’S BAZAAR

films.title: Lynch/Oz
films.synopsis: In Wild at Heart, David Lynch explicitly forged links between film noir and The Wizard of Oz. But Lynch’s obsession with Oz reveals itself in all his work, from his first short The Alphabet (1969) to Twin Peaks: The Return (2016). An impressive roster of filmmakers (Rodney Ascher, John Waters, Karyn Kusama, Justin Benson and Aaron Moorhead, and David Lowery), plus critic Amy Nicholson, offer their personal takes on this strange attraction and hint at something larger about how we process movies. “The way Philippe organizes the hundreds of clips provides more startling and exhilarating moments per minute than most movies about movies can muster... among the many things this picture captures is how the fanciful worlds of Oz and Lynch illuminate the pain and splendor of the world we have to inhabit once we leave the magic realm of cinema.” GLENN KENNY, ROGEREBERT.COM

films.title: They Live
films.synopsis: When a drifter, Nada (Roddy Piper), discovers a very special pair of sunglasses, it gives him a whole new perspective on life. See, these are a kind of x-ray specs. They reveal the true nature of the world we live in: the power elite is in fact an alien race, feeding offour apathy through the promotion of rampant consumerism. John Carpenter’s sci-fiallegory kicks ass—it’s the anti-80s movie to end them all. “A landmark work of political subversion in American filmmaking.” DOMINICK SUZANNE-MAYER, CONSEQUENCE OF SOUND

films.title: sex, lies and videotape
films.synopsis: Ann (Andie MacDowell) is oblivious to the affair going on between her husband John (Peter Gallagher) and her sister Cynthia (Laura San Giacomo). But when John’s college friend Graham (James Spader) visits, his peculiar hobby—taping women talking about their sexual experience—will change everything. The film is an astringent, well acted character comedy. It was the first breakout hit for Harvey Weinstein’s Miramax, paving the way for the crossover success of the independent film sector in the 1990s. “This is a sexy, nuanced, beautifully controlled examination of how a quartet of people are defined by their erotic impulses and inhibitions.”

films.title: A Compassionate Spy
films.synopsis: A fascinating companion piece to Oppenheimer, Steve James’s doc tells the story of Ted Hall, who was recruited out of Harvard while he was still a teenager to work on the Manhattan Project... And who confessed 50 years later to having shared secrets of the atomic bomb with the Soviet Union. Told largely through the testimony of Hall’s wife Joan, the film plays as a historical thriller and as a love story. We learn why he did what he did, how he got away with it, and just how high the stakes were. “Engrossing... first-rate.” PHIL HOAD, THE GUARDIAN

films.title: When Morning Comes
films.synopsis: Nine-year-old Jamal (a radiant Djamari Roberts) is getting bullied at school and his mum—a widow—decides she needs to get him out of Jamaica and educated in Canada,

films.title: Do the Right Thing
films.synopsis: It’s the hottest day of a long, hot summer, and tensions in Bed-Stuy, New York are ready to boil. But for pizza delivery boy Mookie (Spike Lee) it’s just another day spent crisscrossing the neighbourhood. From the bristling title sequence through to its combustible climax, the movie is incredibly dynamic and exuberant, its saturated colours and barbed comic exchanges creating a heightened realism that’s appropriate for the pent up racial tensions the film taps into. Lee’s second feature is his masterpiece. “Do the Right Thing still holds up a mirror to our society, and it makes us laugh and think, and challenges all of us to see ourselves in one another.” BARACK OBAMA “Do the Right Thing is Lee’s most complex, heartfelt and disturbing film.” STUART KLAWANS, THE NATION

films.title: Hairspray
films.synopsis: It wasn’t so much that John Waters sold out, but the “Pope of Trash” escaped the midnight circuit when the mainstream came to meet him halfway, which is more or less what transpired when he wrote and directed Hairspray. A tongue-in-cheek tribute to the subversive art of shaking your tail-feather in Waters’ native Baltimore, circa 1962, Hairspray stirs up an all-inclusive cocktail of satire, camp and rock n roll. “A wonderful parody of the teen-movie and the concerned-liberal school of film-making... In a way the era and its crazes are beyond parody, and it takes considerable skill to sustain the slight joke; but the kitsch is a delight, and Divine, who has a low and fascinating deadpan voice, is very funny as Tracy’s mother. ‘It’s the times, they’re a-changing,’ she opines, in response to startling developments. ‘Something’s blowing in the wind.’” HILARY MANTEL, THE SPECTATOR

films.title: Satan Wants You
films.synopsis: 4:45PM, 9:00PM Sleepy Victoria, BC, isn’t typically associated with devil worship and human sacrifice. But as this eye-opening documentary makes clear, our provincial capital was once the epicenter of what became known as the “satanic panic”, a disturbing social phenomenon that swept across North America through the 1980s.

Marcello Mastroianni plays Guido Anselmi, a director whose new project is collapsing around him, along with his life. One of the greatest films about film ever made, Federico Fellini’s 8½ (Otto e mezzo) turns one man’s artistic crisis into a grand epic of the cinema. An early working title for 8½ was The Beautiful Confusion, and Fellini’s masterpiece is exactly that: a shimmering dream, a circus, and a magic act. In 2022 8½ dropped down to #31 in the Sight & Sound poll of Greatest Films, but other filmmakers rate it more highly—it was #6 in the Director’s poll.

films.title: Blue Velvet
films.synopsis: It’s impossible to disagree with Brett Easton Ellis’s assessment that this is the key film of the 80s. Blue Velvet appeared to hark back to an earlier, more innocent era... a sleepy, safe midwestern town with white picket fences where everyone knows everyone else... But when young Jeffrey decides to play detective, what he finds is big city toxicity: drugs, corruption, violent sex. Like us, he’s sucked into the vortex. This provocative, brilliant, funny, erotic and upsetting movie still gets under your skin.

films.title: Golden Delicious
films.synopsis: This East Van movie is a fresh and engaging coming-ofage story about an Asian-Canadian teenager who is torn between his girlfriend’s dreams of their future and his father’s ambition, all the while struggling with finding himself and following his own desires. In his first feature, director Jason Karman vividly brings to life the joys and complications of a young man who suddenly discovers feelings for the boy next door.

films.title: Midnight Cowboy
films.synopsis: Jon Voight and Dustin Hoffman are two street hustlers on different ends of the innocence and experience spectrum who establish something more than a business partnership in the seedy world of late 60s New York City in John Schlesinger’s New Hollywood classic. From its Harry Nilsson theme song (Everybody’s Talkin’) to its Steinbeckian fade out, this is a movie that imprints itself on the heart.

films.title: Mulholland Dr.
films.synopsis: Brunette Rita (Laura Elena Harring) wanders Mulholland Drive, dazed and confused after an auto accident. She finds refuge with Betty (Naomi Watts), an aspiring blonde actress who has arrived from Deep River, Ontario with her innocence intact. The two work together to try to piece together Rita’s story... But nothing is quite what it seems in this rich, disturbing neo-noir from David Lynch, an enigmatic mystery which invites multiple interpretations. Released in 2001, Mulholland Dr was instantly hailed as a classic, and it’s the most recent film in Sight & Sound’s Top 10.

films.title: Scrapper
films.synopsis: Charlotte Regan’s offbeat Sundance prize-winner is jampacked with fun and flourish. Georgie (Lola Campbell) is a 12-year-old North Londoner, alone in the world since the death of her mum and fine with it, thanks mate. She’s more than capable, and has a nice little earner liberating bikes from their chains with the help of her loyal chum Ali (Alin Uzun). The last thing she wants or needs is the dad she’s never known. But here he is anyway: Jason (Harris Dickinson) back from Ibiza to prove he’s all grown up.

films.title: The Zen Diary
films.synopsis: 4:00PM, 8:15PM As a child, Tsutomu Mizukami (Kenji Sawada) was taught the art of cooking in a Zen temple. Now an old man and a respected author, he lives alone in a house in Nagano, grows his own produce and forages in the nearby woods. Over the course of a year he reflects on the seasons, the cycle of planting and harvesting, food prep and pickling, and, naturally, how all this relates to the cycle of a human life. Lovingly photographed, this is a film to reflect on and savour. Featuring Food Pop-Ups. Details at viff.org. In Japanese with Eng subtitles.

films.title: Desperate Souls, Dark City and the Legend of Midnight Cowboy
films.synopsis: Still the only X-rated movie to win the Academy Award for Best Picture, Midnight Cowboy stands as a remarkable turning point in the history of American film, a frank and empathetic portrait of the relationship of two hustlers on the streets of New York. Nancy Buirski’s documentary is much more than a footnote to a great film. It’s an ambitious exploration of the different social, cultural and personal forces which forged this classic, a film which takes the temperature of America in a period of upheaval.

films.title: A Taste of Honey
films.synopsis: A key work from the British realist “kitchen sink” movement, Shelagh Delaney’s groundbreakng play explores multiple layers of social oppression. A selfish, hard-drinking mother (Dora Bryan) and her pregnant daughter (Rita Tushingham) represent examples of how women of no means often must choose between independence and security. Host Melanie Friesen will introduce the film and lead a discussion with guest Jan Wade, an internationally acclaimed mixed-media artist and the first Black female Vancouver-based artist offered a solo exhibition at the VAG in its history.

films.title: Days of Being Wild
films.synopsis: Set in 1960, in the milieu Wong Kar-wai grew up in (an immigrant from Shanghai, his father was the manager of a nightclub), the swooningly romantic Days of Being Wild envelopes you in a half-remembered world suffused in sweltering heat, torrential rain and existential ennui. Louche, listless lothario Yuddy (Leslie Cheung) seduces Su Lizhen (Maggie Cheung) then moves on to a showgirl (Carina Lau), before fate plays her trump card. September 12 would have been Leslie Cheung’s birthday... 20 years after his passing we pay tribute to this groundbreaking star and exceptional talent. Cantonese

films.title: Happy Together
films.synopsis: Buenos Aires, the end of the world, 1997. Leslie Cheung and Tony Leung are lovers trying to hash out their onoffrelationship in an alien environment. Very much a film made in exile, Happy Together is shot in grainy monochrome and bluesy greens and reds. An improvised movie, it’s akin to flicking through a photo album, over-exposed snapshots of splintered relationships. This fragmentary, intuitive style carries a powerful emotional charge, and Wong won the Best Director prize at Cannes. Cantonese, Mandarin, and Spanish

films.title: Nick Cave & The Birthday Party: Mutiny in Heaven
films.synopsis: Before The Bad Seeds there was The Birthday Party, four Melbourne school kids burning with the white heat of punk with Nick Cave as frontman, a teenage Bukowski channeling poetry, literature, rockabilly and blues. Narrated by the original band, and featuring never-before-seen personal footage and jaw dropping concert clips, the film provides an electrifying front row seat to one of the legendary live acts of a wild era.

films.title: In the Footsteps of Beethoven’s Rebel Opera
films.synopsis: Kerry Candaele’s second Beethoven film explores the composer’s only opera, Fidelio, through the lens of Jorge Pena Hen, a Chilean composer and conductor who was arrested and killed in the Pinochet coup. Candaele meets Pena Hen’s granddaughter, who dedicates her art form—Butoh dance—to memorializing him, and sees echoes of the opera in her tale. With Beethoven’s stirring music and singing front and centre, history, politics, Love & Justice is an inspiring testament to the enduring power of creativity.

films.title: Patricio Guzman’s The First Year
films.synopsis: September 11 is the 50th anniversary of the CIA-backed coup which toppled Salvador Allende’s socialist government in Chile and plunged that country into the Pinochet dictatorship. To mark this important date, VIFF is proud to present the first film by one of the world’s most respected non-fiction filmmakers, Patricio Guzmán (Nostalgia for the Light; The Pearl Button; The Battle of Chile). The First Year is a fascinating, vivid record of the radical changes Allende made to redress inequality.

films.title: Metropolis Re:worked
films.synopsis: This year, the landmark sci-fifilm Metropolis, directed by Fritz Lang, will enter the public domain. To celebrate this occasion, experimental music duo Magazinist (Matthew Tomkinson & Andy Zuliani) will offer a live rescoring of the film. With a focus on unique hand-built instruments alongside synthesizers, vocal processing, and other post-industrial electronics, their original soundtrack supports the film’s monumental visuals with a fittingly expansive score. S P E C I A L E V E N T - L I V E S C O R E Get an Early Bird ticket at viff.org for $18 before Sept 22

films.title: Farewell My Concubine
films.synopsis: 12:20PM, 8:10PM It’s 30 years since Chen Kaige’s masterpiece won the Palme d’Or, and 20 years since the passing of Leslie Cheung. Beginning in 1924 and spanning nearly half a century, Farewell My Concubine chronicles the rise of two young stars of the Beijing Opera House, and their turbulent relationship—as well as momentous events in the turbultent history of China. In 2014, Farewell My Concubine topped Time Out Beijing’s list of the top 100 Mainland Chinese films. Restored 4K 170 minute version “Farewell My Concubine is a demonstration of how a great epic can function. I was generally familiar with the important moments in modern Chinese history, but this film helped me to feel and imagine what it was like to live in the country during those times. This is one of the year’s best films.” ROGER EBERT, CHICAGO SUN-TIMES

films.title: Pedro’s Shorts: Strange Way of Life + The Human Voice
films.synopsis: 3:20PM, 4:50PM, 6:15PM For many years Pedro Almodóvar toyed with invitations to make films in the United States. One such invitation was Brokeback Mountain, and Strange Way of Life, his latest half hour short film, certainly has echoes of Ang Lee’s movie. It’s a gay western, with Ethan Hawke and Pedro Pascal, and loaded with emotion. Alongside, we’re screening The Human Voice, his brilliant 2020 Jean Cocteau adaptation starring Tilda Swinton as a woman jilted by her lover. In an hour, these two films give us entire worlds.

films.title: Relax, I’m From the Future
films.synopsis: 1:30PM, 3:30PM Rhys Darby (Flight of the Concords; What We Do in the Shadows) is perfectly cast as Casper, a time traveller whose unprepossing demeanour makes it hard for anyone to take his claims seriously. However, queer Black punk Holly (Gabrielle Graham) becomes convinced he really does know what he’s talking about—and is more than happy to help him monetize this inside knowledge. Neither gives much thought to the repercussions of their activities. Luke Higginson’s goofy comedy will put a smile on your face.

films.title: Manufacturing the Threat
films.synopsis: 4:30PM, 8:00PM in 2013, the RCMP triumphantly announced the apprehension of two terrorists responsible for planting bombs near the BC Legislature. With Al Qaeda atrocities fresh in mind, it seemed like distant menaces were coming uncomfortably close to home. Mercifully the RCMP were on the case! Trouble was, none of this was true. Amy Miller’s doc explores the dubious waters of police entrapment, incitement and agent provocateurs, raising alarming questions about the accountability and oversight of our security agencies.

films.title: Pain Hustlers
films.synopsis: Emily Blunt shines in this Wolf of Wall Street-style black comedy tracing the true story of how oxycontine was sold as a non-addictive pain killer, first to doctors, and then to patients. Director David Yates sees the story as a cautionary tale about America’s other great addictions: money and success. Blunt plays Liza Drake, a down-on-her-luck single mom picked up as hot sales prospect by a struggling pharma start up. She repays their faith in spades— after all, who isn’t about to cash-in on a sure thing? “Entertaining... propulsive... spirited and convincing performances.” LOVIA GYARKY, HOLLYWOOD REPORTER

films.title: A Brighter Tomorrow
films.synopsis: 4:00PM, 8:30PM Veteran writer-director-star Nanni Moretti plays a grouchy filmmaker who’s shooting a period drama about the Italian Communist Party and who’s insensitive to everyone else. But Moretti is slyer than his alter ego, and A Brighter Tomorrow also serves as a breezy satire on the movie business, a touching reflection on long-term friends, a critique of ideological intractability and a playful exercise in self mockery... there’s even a musical busting to get out. It’s an old man’s film in the best sense, in fact. In Italian with Subtitles subtitles.

films.title: The Rocky Horror Picture Show
films.synopsis: The original and unrepeatable midnight movie cult classic, The Rocky Horror Picture Show is a phenomenon unto itself and truly needs no introduction. If you’re a Rocky virgin just know that you may never be the same again. And if you’re an old hand, well, why not seize this opportunity to experience the ultimate audience participation flick in the city’s most spacious and comfortable cinema—on Halloween!? Check out our live musical performance The Rocky Horror Music Show earlier in the evening, enjoy a drink from our licensed bar, and come dressed to kill.

films.title: The Mission
films.synopsis: 1:30PM, 7:45PM In 2018, American missionary John Chau (26) traveled illegally to one of the most hard-to-reach places on Earth— North Sentinel Island, in the Bay of Bengal—determined to convert one of the world’s most isolated populations. This misguided mission would quickly see him killed. Through animated reenactments, intriguing interviews, and archival footage, The Mission examines the troubling legacy of romanticized colonial-era exploration narratives, and the persistent dangers of religious fanaticism.

films.title: Humanist Vampire Seeking Consenting Suicidal Person
films.synopsis: Meet Sasha, the world’s most compassionate young vampire. Her family is at their wits end with her reluctance to embrace their lethal traditions, instead relying on somewhat ethically sourced blood bags to survive. Ariane Louis-Seize has certainly arrived with this utterly charming, quirky horror comedy about an empathetic vampire refusing to compromise her principles. Boasting a cast and crew of Quebec’s finest, everyone is pitch perfect, led by the uber cool Sara Montpetit (Falcon Lake).

films.title: M3GAN + Electra
films.synopsis: The other big doll movie this year, M3GAN is actually a Model 3 Generative Android, the creation of toy designer Allison Williams, who figures she’d make the perfect companion for the 8-year-old orphaned niece she’s just inherited (and more importantly, Cady can road test the Beta-model for her). A big hit back in January, this nifty update on Child’s Play taps into contemporary AI angst and generates as many laughs as scares with its wicked black comic sensibility.

films.title: Dolls
films.synopsis: An old, dark mansion... A terrible storm... Half a dozen strangers looking for shelter. Judy, her self-absorbed father, and evil stepmother are the first to arrive, and fortunately for them (they think) elderly couple Gabriel and Hilary Hartwicke are friendly and sympathetic. A trio of hitchhikers are next, and they too are offered beds for the night. But not everyone is as benign as they appear, not even Mr Punch, the toy the Hartwicke’s press on Judy when they learn she’s lost her teddy...

films.title: Subterranean
films.synopsis: The sport of caving takes a special kind of person: someone who isn’t afraid of the dark, who isn’t claustrophobic, or scared of bears or spiders, someone who enjoys venturing into terra incognita, crawling through tight spaces regardless of mud and water, who doesn’t entertain anxious thoughts about rock falls, floods or earthquakes... For the rest of us, Subterranean offers a far more comfortable portal into the thrilling sights—and real dangers—that cavers enjoy.

films.title: XINEMA 11: Attack of the DIY!
films.synopsis: XINEMA is an ongoing series that showcases emerging and established filmmakers within and around “Vancouver”, BC to strengthen and preserve the local experimental film scene. Attack of the DIY! is a threefilm spooktacular including a cockroach invasion, an inspiring severed-head haunting, and a bodacious bloody threesome. Follow the sun and discover life’s deepest low-budget lessons through the twisted missions of an insectuous gamer, gatekeeping god, and bloodthirsty femme-doms. Screening works by: Owen Ellis, Jo Gaffney and Schnüdlbug. Content consideration: Strobing effects and gore

films.title: Child’s Play
films.synopsis: “I’m Chucky. Wanna play?” After this summer of Barbie (and with 45 more Mattel movies in development, praise the lord) let’s take a moment to remember that not all dolls play nice. Take Chucky, for example. On the outside, he presents as an all-round “Good Guy”. On the inside lurks the soul of infamous serial killer Charles Lee Ray. When innocent young Andy unwraps him as a birthday gift, he has no comprehension of who he’ll be bedding down with that night.... “Scary, yet darkly funny, this thriller of the supernatural from the director of the terrific ‘Fright Night’ moves with the speed of a bullet train and with style to burn.” KEVIN THOMAS, LA TIMES

films.title: Bride of Chucky
films.synopsis: Jennifer Tilly has a lot of fun as bleached blonde trailer trash Tiffany, Chucky’s old chick when he was still just your average flesh-and-blood psychotic. Having studied Voodoo for Dummies, Tiffany reckons she can bring her rubber lover back to life. Unfortunately, things don’t exactly go to plan, and a revitalised but still pissed Chucky decides he has to cut Doll face down to size. Hong Kong director Ronny Yu and screenwriter Don Mancini approach their assignments with infectious absurdist glee.

films.title: Deep Red
films.synopsis: As a curtain raiser for our Halloweenie celebration of devious, deranged and devilish dolls, a deep dive to Turin, 1975, and Dario Argento’s seminal giallo. A clairvoyant has a premonition of her own murder, and her neighbour, pianist Marcus (David Hemmings), is the first on the scene. Argento takes the lurid stuff of pulp and applies a high formalistic gloss, an endlessly probing camera, prog rock Goblin score, and a disquieting fixation on gender to craft a sinister slasher masterpiece. This 4K restoration includes 26 minutes originally cut from the release.

films.title: Nyad
films.synopsis: Diana Nyad first attempted to swim from Cuba to Florida in 1978 when she was 28 years old; 110 miles in a shark cage. She failed. Doctors pulled her out 40 hours and 70 miles into her epic swim. Three decades later, as her 60th birthday looms, Diana (Annette Bening) decides it’s time to give it another go, this time without the cage, but

films.title: The Killer
films.synopsis: 5:45PM, 8:10PM The professional hit man remains irresistible: an independent contractor with a godlike determination over life and death, an ascetic with a bullet and—as represented by Michael Fassbender—a penchant for The Smiths. After an unfortunate turn of events he finds himself on the receiving end of a termination order, but he knows better than anyone that the best form of defense is attack. Teaming up with Seven screenwriter Andrew Kevin Walker, David Fincher slyly upends expectations in this lean thriller.

films.title: The Delinquents
films.synopsis: Rodrigo Moreno's film begins with one of the most original bank heists ever conceived. But that's only the opening gambit in what evolves into a languid, meandering character piece about two bank tellers who try to reinvent themselves and fall in love with the same woman. The vibe here is gently ironic but keenly curious, a film that—like its protagonists—seems open to a scenic detour in the spirit of exploration and discovery. "Deeply strange, utterly distinctive, beguiling and fantastical."

films.title: Dario Argento’s Opera
films.synopsis: A horror director, Marcus (Ian Charleson), has been invited to stage Verdi’s Macbeth, and his modernist tropes are driving his diva to distraction. So much so, she dies in a car accident. Enter the understudy, Betty (Cristina Marsillach). But her big break is not be so lucky: the opera may be cursed, and a killer has her in his sights... Argento is playing with notions of high art and low, here, riffing on Shakespeare, Verdi and Hitchcock, and pulling off his last hurrah, the final word on the giallo. 4K restoration by Severin Films “Opera is a violent aria of memory, bad luck, the artistic drive and the horror of the stare... a film of rare beauty, a celebration of love’s absence and the ferocious force of the gaze.” ED GONZALEZ, SLANT

films.title: The Stones and Brian Jones
films.synopsis: 5:20PM, 9:10PM Who started the Rolling Stones? Why, Brian Jones of course. But a band can’t have two leaders and when push came to shove, it was Brian who was left out in the cold, fired just a few weeks before his death at the age of 27. The latest from documentary legend Nick Broomfield (Marianne & Leonard: Words of Love; Kurt & Courtney) scores candid interviews with the (many) women in Jones’s life, and with Bill Wyman, among others, to relate the sad story of how maybe the most gifted of the group went off the rails. “Tremendously well-made, intensely watchable and, in the end, achingly sad.” PAT STACEY, THE IRISH INDEPENDENT

films.title: May December
films.synopsis: 3:30PM, 5:50PM, 8:10PM 3:50PM, 8:25PM 3:30PM, 5:50PM, 8:10PM 3:50PM, 8:25PM 3:50PM, 8:10PM Todd Haynes (Carol; Safe) is the master of the post-modern melodrama. Here a tabloid tale about a thirtysomething wife and mother who seduced a seventh grade student becomes a teasingly deceptive drama about identity, desire, and codependency. 20 years after the scandal, TV star Elizabeth (Natalie Portman) comes to visit Gracie (Julianne Moore) to prep for a movie. Gracie figures affording access will win her some sympathy. But Elizabeth’s presence stirs up turmoil in her marriage and beyond... “Haynes has done something spellbinding here: heady, grown-up and committed to a refreshing dose of moral ambiguity at a time in cinema where moral pandering sadly seems to be the default.” TOMRIS LAFFLY, THE WRAP

films.title: Red Rooms
films.synopsis: 6:30PM, 8:50PM In this unsettling, stylishly sinister drama from Pascal Plante, model and mathematician Kelly-Anne (Juliette Gariépy) becomes obsessed with the trial of Ludwig Chevalier (Maxwell McCabe-Lokos), a loner accused of the torture and murder of three teenage girls. Even more disturbingly, these atrocities were streamed online in the Dark Web’s “red rooms”. Kelly-Anne’s personal life and career unravel as she plunges deeper into the abyss. “Blending courtroom drama and claustrophobic techtinged nightmare, Red Rooms is a striking and austere examination of the true-crime industrial complex that benefits from its formality and disturbingly removed protagonist.” HANNAH STRONG, LITTLE WHITE LIES

films.title: The Tunnel to Summer, The Exit to Goodbyes
films.synopsis: Tomohisa Taguchi’s anime won the prestigioius Paul Grimault Award at the Annecy Animation Festival. It’s a beguiling teen romance with one foot in the real world and the other in the stars. Kaoru and Anzu are near neighbours and high school classmates. Chancing across a disused tunnel Kaoru realizes it holds extraordinary magic within, but its mysteries come at a cost: exploring for five minutes translates as hours in the outside world; hours become days and weeks. And yet the teens venture further... “Ravishingly beautiful.”

films.title: Rustin
films.synopsis: 4:10PM, 9:00PM Colman Domingo gives one of the indelible performances of 2023 as the (gay) Black civil rights activist Bayard Rustin in this stirring historical drama from director George C Wolfe and producers Michelle and Barack Obama. His sexuality kept Rustin out of the spotlight, but he was a trusted advisor to Martin Luther King and in 1963 it was Rustin who masterminded The March on Washington, a turning point in the history of social justice in the US. Domingo plays him with immense conviction and charisma. “A stirring performance... Domingo runs the gamut... you believe in his Rustin as a divider of boardrooms and builder of coalitions, with a searing gift for galvanizing protesters into action.” JUSTIN CHANG, LA TIMES

films.title: Cabin Music + Concert featuring James Carson
films.synopsis: In this unique event, VIFF teams up with our Seymour Street neighbours at the Vancouver Symphony Orchestra School of Music to present James Carson’s self-directed documentary, Cabin Music, at the VIFF Centre’s Vancity Theatre (1181 Seymour St), followed by a live piano concert at the VSO School of Music’s Pyatt Hall (843 Seymour St). James Carson has been labeled a “meditative… piano texturalist” (Time Out New York), who creates “trance-inducing… shimmering arpeggiated figures, played with such speed as to invoke Coltrane-esque ‘sheets of sound’” (Feast of Music). Cabin Music tells the story of this prodigious classical pianist who turned his back on the concert hall to travel and reflect, before returning to compose a new form of music in harmony with nature. The film is also the story of the off-grid cabin James built in the Canadian wilderness. The result is a shimmering zen movie about the nature of music and the music of nature. Film screening: 7:30PM

films.title: Carpet Cowboys
films.synopsis: 85 percent of carpets in the US come from the town of Dalton, Georgia, the Carpet Capital of the World. Turns out this hitherto overlooked industrial powerhouse is a gift to documentary filmakers Noah Collier and M Emily Mackenzie, populated by quirky eccentrics with entertainingly arcane business practices and who take a philosophical view of the American Dream. That dream turned sour for the doc’s de facto hero, Roderick James, a Scottish-born cowboy with an eye for style and a love for Country.

films.title: Charlotte’s Castle
films.synopsis: Spadina Gardens is a throwback to an earlier conception of downtown living: a mid-rise apartment complex built in the heart of Toronto in 1904, it offers rental tenants a suite of spacious rooms off a long corridor. Not surprisingly the building has attracted an eclectic array of tenants, many of them bohemian, creative types with a taste for character over mod cons. When an international developer becomes the new landlord they fear the worst... Director Jamie Kastner was there to film the fall out.

films.title: Rojek
films.synopsis: Canada’s submission for the Academy Awards this year is a fascinating and impactful introduction to the mindset of defeated ISIS prisoners. Many of these men and women remain unapologetic believers in the fundamentalist dogma of radical Islam; others claim to have been duped; some are wary of what they say for fear of reprisals. Interspersed with savage, lyrical images of war-torn Syria and Kurdistan, these testimonies reflect the rise and fall of the Caliphate from a perspective we have not heard before.

films.title: The Giacomettis
films.synopsis: The rugged Swiss mountain valley of Bregaglia has produced an entire dynasty of artists: the Giacomettis. Alberto Giacometti would become a talismanic artist with his revolutionary slender sculptures. Before him, his father was among the first wave of impressionist painters. And his siblings, likewise, devoted their lives to creativity and art. What is it about this valley that makes it the birthplace of so many artists? Director Susanna Fanzun traces the footsteps of an extraordinary family.

films.title: Beyond Utopia
films.synopsis: Without recourse to reconstructions, Madeleine Gavin’s gripping and eye-opening doc about the nightmare authoritarian state of North Korea shares footage shot clandestinely by the Underground Railroad over the course of the attempted rescue of the Roh family as they flee through China, Vietnam, and Laos for the safety of Thailand. If they’re caught, they face torture, incarceration and even execution.

films.title: Diving in a Drop
films.synopsis: Frédéric Swierczynski is one of the best cave divers in the world. Sébastien Devrient, director, is also a mountain guide. The two friends set off to dive alone, without assistance, in the highest lake in the world, on the slopes of the Ojos del Salado volcano in Argentina. This extreme sports doc is a fascinating snapshot of a couple of adventurers exploring a deeply inhospitable part of the world, weighed down with diving gear, freezing cold in the high desert, and desperately searching for water. Q&A with Filmmaker Sébastien Devrient, Sunday Dec 4

films.title: The Tunnel to Summer, The Exit of Goodbyes
films.synopsis: Tomohisa Taguchi’s anime won the prestigioius Paul Grimault Award at the Annecy Animation Festival. It’s a beguiling teen romance with one foot in the real world and the other in the stars. Kaoru and Anzu are near neighbours and high school classmates. Chancing across a disused tunnel Kaoru realizes it holds extraordinary magic within, but its mysteries come at a cost: exploring for five minutes translates as hours in the outside world; hours become days and weeks. And yet the teens venture further...

films.title: Arthur Erickson’s Dyde House
films.synopsis: Vancouver’s most celebrated architect, Arthur Erickson gave us the Museum of Anthropology, the SFU campus at Burnaby Mountain, and Robson Square, among many other gems. But Dyde House, in Alberta, has been overlooked. One of his earliest commissions, it’s a private home nestled among the aspen parklands, a hidden masterpiece that holds clues to Erickson’s philosophy, methods and future large scale projects. This 53-minute film artfully tells the story of an undiscovered piece of history.

films.title: s-yéwyáw: Awaken
films.synopsis: In this poignant collaborative project directed by Liz Marshall (Midian Farm), Ecko Aleck of the Nlaka’pamux Nation (Lytton, BC,) Alfonso Salinas of the shíshálh Nation (Sunshine Coast, BC,) and Charlene SanJenko of Splatsin of the Secwépemc Nation (Shuswap, BC,) are learning and documenting the traditional cultural teachings and legacies of their Elders, including the deep impacts of the Residential School system. Gently guided by their mentors, they seek to build a bridge that their children may cross.

films.title: The Three Musketeers: D’Artagnan
films.synopsis: 5:30PM, 8:00PM 3:30PM, 6:00PM, 8:20PM 12:00PM, 4:00PM, 6:15PM 3:45PM, 6:15PM, 8:45PM 3:45PM, 6:15PM, 8:45PM 3:45PM, 6:15PM, 8:45PM 6:15PM, 8:45PM The Dumas classic has been filmed many times, but this latest French production will stand the test of time. Martin Bourbolon’s movie trusts to the spine of one of the great adventure stories. Gauche country boy D’Artagnan (François Civil) arrives in Paris in 1625 to join the king’s musketeers. After just hours in the capital he’s lined up duels with Athos (Vincent Cassel), Porthos (Pio Marmai), and Aramis (Romain Duris). Meanwhile Cardinal Richelieu is plotting to push Louis XIII into war.

films.title: Close-Up
films.synopsis: In Abbas Kiarostami’s self-reflexive non-fiction narrative feature, Sabzian, an illiterate film buffwho passed himself off as the Iranian filmmaker Mohsen Makhmalbaf plays himself in reconstructions of his fraud… His trial is genuine documentary footage, and then Kiarostami films him meeting the real Mahkmalbaf for the first time, an encounter that may be real and scripted at the same time. Ranked at #17 in the Sight & Sound critics’ poll, CloseUp was voted 9th in the directors’ poll. “Explores the fraught relationships between truth and falsehood, film and ‘reality’, intention and action, and acknowledges, from start to finish, the role and responsibility of the director in his engagement with the people in his film.” GEOFF ANDREW, SIGHT & SOUND

films.title: The Disappearance of Shere Hite
films.synopsis: Published in 1976, The Hite Report became a non-fiction sensation... It’s still one of the best-selling books of all time. Its subject: the female orgasm. Its author: a former Playboy model. Shere Hite believed that the prevailing assumption that penile penetration was the key to the female climax was wrong, and based her research on thousands of anonymous questionnaires. Her conclusions were explosive and controversial, at least for half the population. But how and why did Hite fall from grace? “Extraordinary... An astonishing, beautifully made corrective to the cultural amnesia that has for decades surrounded Hite... A film that deserves to become one of the documentary events of the year.” JESSICA KIANG, VARIETY

films.title: Fallen Leaves
films.synopsis: Aki Kaurismäki is a genre unto himself. If you’ve seen Le Havre or The Other Side of Hope then you know, and if you haven’t, they’re charming, deadpan comedies about working class people, often melancholic or just alcoholic, but goodhearted and kind to dogs (there’s always a dog). In Fallen Leaves, Ansi meets Holappa, and these two lonely souls feel they are meant for each other, but Fate may have other ideas... Kaurismäki crafts a poignant and pertinent comedy which picked up the Jury Prize at Cannes.

films.title: My Animal
films.synopsis: An outcast hockey player, Heather (Bobbi Salvor Menuez) is a closeted lesbian living with her alcoholic mom—and she’s inherited a familial curse that transforms her into a bloodthirsty lycanthrope. Falling for figure skater Jonny (Amandla Stenberg), Heather invites further persecution from the prejudiced townsfolk. But there’s a full moon rising... Jacqueline Castel’s My Animal is a full-blooded creature feature that weds the classic werewolf mythos with its own sapphic sensibility. “Sensual queer horror story My Animal marks an impressive, confident feature debut for several key talents. First and foremost, debutante director Jacqueline Castel, already an experienced short film and music video helmer who has collaborated with David Lynch and John Carpenter, imbues this first-feature script by Jae Matthews with a woozy, dreamy, retro sensibility.” LESLIE FELPERIN, HOLLYWOOD REPORTER

films.title: Orlando, My Political Biography
films.synopsis: Taking inspiration from Virginia Woolf’s Orlando, French writer and theorist Paul B. Preciado uses the transgressive novel as a framework to investigate the very real contemporary struggles of trans and non-binary people, casting 26 Orlandos of multiple ages, identities, and nationalities. Exuberant, joyful and deeply thoughtful, this poetic cinematic essay is a thought-provoking, and deeply felt work of art. Special Jury Prize, Encounters, Berlin. “The first trans masterpiece.”

films.title: The Wind Rises
films.synopsis: Hayao Miyazaki grew up fascinated by airplanes— his father owned a factory that produced rudders for biplanes —as can be seen in the whimsical flying contraptions that pop up in his work so often. It makes sense, then, that the film he intended would be his swansong should be a inspired by the life of Jiro Horikoshi, a young man much like the filmmaker, who grew up to be a designer and engineer, and who is best known for the “Zero” fighter plane, a masterpiece of aerodynamics. “A breathtaking dream of flying... a rich treat for the eye and soul alike.” MARK KERMODE, THE OBSERVER

films.title: Immediate Family
films.synopsis: 3:40PM, 8:15PM Few rock docs are as fondly remembered as The Wrecking Crew, Danny Tedesco’s revelatory tribute to the 1960s session men. His belated follow up is dedicated to the crew’s 1970s counterparts. You may not know the names of Danny Kortchmar, Leland Sklar, Ross Kunkel, Waddy Watchel, or Steve Postell, but you know the stars who turned to these sidemen to embellish their recordings: Neil Young, Keith Richards, Carole King, Stevie Nicks, James Taylor, Phil Collins, David Crosby, to name but a few.

films.title: Society of the Snow
films.synopsis: 12:30PM, 7:30PM In 1972, a plane carrying 101 people—many of them belonging to a rugby team—crashed in the high Andes between Uruguay and Chile. It was winter. Spotter planes missed the wreck. There was no food. In order to live the survivors had to turn to the unthinkable... Previously filmed as Alive in 1993 (and an inspiration, probably, for Yellowjackets), this harrowing saga makes for extreme drama. JC Bayona stresses authenticity along with the spiritual dimension of this prolonged near-death experience.

films.title: Distant Voices, Still Lives
films.synopsis: Cinema lost a unique voice in October with the passing of Terence Davies. His first feature is an autobiographical work, harking back to Davies’ childhood in a working class Liverpool family. Although there are painful dramatic vignettes—Davies’ father lived in a state of seething fury— the film is structured as a chorale, around pub singalongs, popular showtunes and Hollywood musical numbers. It’s this music which affords the family pleasure, kinship, community, and a sense of spiritual comfort. “It will be remembered and treasured as one of the greatest of all English films.”

films.title: Rouge
films.synopsis: In this supernatural love story, Cantopop idol Anita Mui is the heartbroken ghost who returns to Hong Kong 50 years after committing suicide to find out why her lover (Leslie Cheung) has yet to join her in the afterlife. Rouge is a funny, sad story beautifully told. Kwan captures the changing face of this booming metropolis and ties it to a glamorous love story from a bygone era, contrasting the tragic passion of yesteryear with a comparatively pallid modern couple.

films.title: Smoke Sauna Sisterhood
films.synopsis: 12:00PM, 4:15PM Within the confines of a smoke sauna deep in an Estonian forest, groups of women gather to cleanse themselves in both body and soul, sharing in traditional sauna-based rituals, while also revealing their hurts and longings, joys and pains. In this Sundance-winning documentary, filmmaker Anna Hints boldly combines an intimate documentary approach with sensuous lyrical expressionism. Less an act of individual portraiture than a kind of collective diary, the film sees a hotbox become a place of healing. In Estonian, Seto, Võro with English subtitles. World Documentary Directing Award, Sundance 2023

films.title: The Tale of Tsar Saltan
films.synopsis: Driven from the court by her sisters’ scheming (you’ll be reminded of Cinderella), the young Tsarina is thrown into the sea in a cask with her infant son. The mother and her now magically-adult son land on a remote island where he falls in love with a Swan Princess in human form and longs for reunion with his estranged father. Chock-a-block with spectacular flights of fancy, and based on a Pushkin poem, this is gorgeous live action fantasy from “the Soviet Disney”. And just wait for the singing squirrel! + Animated short The Mountain of SGaana (Christopher Auchter, Canada, 2017) 10 min

films.title: BlackBerry
films.synopsis: A Canadian success story that turned into a fiasco provides the raw material for one of the standout comedies of the year... a Canadian success story, in fact. It’s 1996, and Mike Lazaridis (Jay Baruchel) and his business partner and best friend Douglas Fregin (director Matt Johnson) are on the edge of creating the world’s first Smartphone. Unfortunately their tech savvy is not matched by their business acumen, until seasoned executive Jim Balsillie (a knockout performance by Glenn Howerton) signs on... “A riotous, fiery kind of comedy whose subterfuge is so subtly stage-managed that you don’t see the cans of gas fuelling the flames higher and higher.” BARRY HERTZ, GLOBE AND MAIL

films.title: Bottoms
films.synopsis: “A movie about empowering women (the hot ones),” as the poster puts its. Canadian Emma Seligman’s second film (after Shiva Baby) is a raunchy high school comedy, and a hilarious parody of the same. Shiva star Rachel Sennott is PJ, a loser with one friend to her name, Josie (Ayo Edibiri). Sapphically-inclined, the pair are determined to lose their virginity to cheerleaders, and hit upon a plan to form a fight club, for girls, to make it happen. Surprisingly, this works. Bottoms punches up and kicks ass. “For most of its tight running time, Bottoms hovers on the cusp of greatness. Bottoms confirms that Seligman and Sennott are major new forces in American comedy.” ELISABETH VINCENTELLI, NEW YORK TIMES

films.title: Anatomy of a Fall
films.synopsis: When Samuel is found dead outside his alpine cabin it’s clear he fell from the attic. But did he jump, or was he pushed? The French authorities suspect the widow (Sandra Hüller, Toni Erdmann), a prickly German novelist, and the marriage was evidently strained. The other key witness is the couple’s ten-year-old son. But as the trial unfolds his faith in his mom is shaken. Justine Triet became only the third woman to win the the Palme d’Or at Cannes, for this complex, thoroughly engrossing courtroom drama. “Anatomy of a Fall is formidable stuff, and you should arrange to watch it at the cinema with your most captious friends.” ANTHONY LANE, NEW YORKER

films.title: Past Lives
films.synopsis: Two men and a woman between them sitting at a New York bar. She’s engaged in conversation with one man, the other seems excluded—this would be her husband. Thus Celine Song’s lovely Past Lives sets the stage for a subtle, intimate romantic drama probing deep emotional connection and the forces that pull us apart. “A confident entry in the canon of great romances— one that expands the emotional scope of what a love story can be.” SHIRLEY LI, THE ATLANTIC “A movie that liberates your tears and makes you fall in love with it. It is almost assuredly predestined to be the single best movie you see this year.” DAVID FEAR, ROLLING STONE

films.title: The King and the Mockingbird
films.synopsis: The legendary animator Paul Grimault (who had a profound and lasting influence on Studio Ghibli’s Hayao Miyazaki and Isao Takahata) and the surrealist writer Jacques Prévert (Les Enfants du Paradis) collaborated for the second time in 1948 on an adaptation of Hans Christian Andersen’s The Shepherdess and the Chimney Sweep. It took them more than 30 years to finish it to their satisfaction, but it’s a masterpiece, an impish political satire for adults and a delightful adventure film for kids. “The filmmaker who most influenced me was the French animator Paul Grimault.” HAYAO MIYAZAKI, STUDIO GHIBLI

films.title: Asteroid City
films.synopsis: Starry, layered, and fleet, Asteroid City is a lot. It probably needs a few viewings to unpack it. It’s a film of a live 1955 TV doc about the creation of a TV play about a bunch of teen science whizz kids convening in a crater in Nevada, and it’s shot in Wes Anderson’s patently ersatz comedic style. That it stands in stark formal relief from the sombre Oppenheimer should not let us overlook how it distills the spiritual malaise ushered in by the Atomic Age with exacting precision. “Filled with the assiduous visuals, mythic faces and charming curiosities that you expect from this singular filmmaker. It’s comic and often wry, but like some of his other films, it has the soul of a tragedy.” MANOHLA DARGIS, NEW YORK TIMES

films.title: Oppenheimer
films.synopsis: Christopher Nolan is contemporary cinema’s great engineer. He sets himself a formal challenge like a scientist testing a hypothesis. So it makes makes that he finds his most substantial subject in Robert Oppenheimer, a theoretical physicist compelled to apply theory to the very practical concern of constructing the ultimate weapon. This is a giant Rubik’s Cube of a movie. It will amass Oscar nominations across the board, and Cillian Murphy and Robert Downey Jr are front-runners in the actor categories. “A great achievement in formal and conceptual terms, and fully absorbing, but Nolan’s filmmaking is, crucially, in service to the history that it relates.” MANOHLA DARGIS, NEW YORK TIMES

films.title: Menus-Plaisirs Les Troisgros
films.synopsis: For several weeks in the spring of 2022 veteran documentarian Fred Wiseman bedded down in one of the most highly esteemed restaurants in France, La Maison Troisgros. A family-run restaurant for four generations, it’s maintained its three Michelin stars for more than half a century. “Menus-plaisirs” means “small pleasures” and Wieman’s rich, savoury film is full of them. At four hours, this is a magnificent and unforgettable sitting. “Both a food lover’s dream and an aspiring chef’s guidebook, uncovering the sophisticated alchemy that makes such places not only run flawlessly, but serve up groundbreaking dishes that are also locally sourced.” JORDAN MINTZER, HOLLYWOOD REPORTER In French with Eng subtitles. Best Non Fiction Film 2023, New York Film Critics

films.title: Maestro
films.synopsis: Bradley Cooper’s second film as director is a symphonic portrait of the composer/conductor Leonard Bernstein, with Cooper in the title role and Carey Mulligan as his wife, actress Felicia Montealegre.
