Longtime Erickson associate Wyn Bieleska joins writer-director Michele Smolkin and Boddy in conversation, before a screening of Smolkin’s 54-minute 2002 film Concrete Poetry, the most lyrical and complete assessment of Erickson’s ideas and accomplishments in any media. In French with English subtitles. Curator Trevor Boddy (FRAIC) will show clips from several films, then host a panel with longtime Erickson associate Wyn Bieleska and the writer-director Michele Smolkin (Concrete Poetry).

films.title: The Smell of Wet Concrete: Talk + The Groundstar Conspiracy screening
films.synopsis: In this evening’s talk, series curator Trevor Boddy discusses Arthur Erickson’s major public buildings, including Lethbridge University, the Bank of Canada, Robson Square, Waterfall Building, and most important of all, the entire original campus of Simon Fraser University—which really should have star billing in Lamont Johnson’s Cold War 1972 thriller, The Groundstar Conspiracy—shot in the university’s plazas, hallways, classrooms and Burnaby Mountain hillside. Essential viewing for any SFU alumnus! Special guest: Geoffrey Erickson, Arthur’s nephew.

films.title: Queer Futures
films.synopsis: The Queer Futures series centers joy and connection to radically imagine future visions of queer life. Four short films explore fat beauty and liberation, gender-affirming healthcare, nonbinary siblinghood in ballroom culture, and the anonymous connections of a decades-old LGBTQ hotline. Just as queer lives subvert normative expectations of behavior, identity, and expression, these directors expand the boundaries of nonfiction forms to present new ways of seeing the queer experience lived out loud.

films.title: A Page of Madness: Live Score by Anju Singh
films.synopsis: An asylum janitor tries to persuade his wife—an inmate —to escape with him, but she doesn't want to go. This Expressionist horror film was directed by former kabuki female impersonator Teinsosuke Kinugasa, co-written

films.title: Anhell69
films.synopsis: A requiem for futures long forgotten, Theo Montoyo's heartbreaking "trans film" is a portrait of his queer community in Medellin, Colombia. It's a non-fiction account of a fantasy movie Montoyo embarked on nearly ten years ago, a ghost story in more ways than one. This is a vividly cinematic piece, fusing personal pain and poetry, candid interviews and sex-hungry spirits. Think Apichatpong, Carax, Fassbinder.

films.title: There Will Be Blood
films.synopsis: Paul Thomas Anderson’s lacerating epic about the birth of the oil age: Daniel Day-Lewis is extraordinary as the prospector entirely consumed with his own enterprise, a Trumpian figure of naked self-assertion; Paul Dano the evangelist who may be his nemesis. The tense score by Radiohead guitarist Jonny Greenwood draws on the work of Arvo Part, Krzysztof Penderecki and Brahms. Certainly one of the movies of the millennium. “A force beyond categories.”

films.title: Creating Colour Pt 2: Lighting + Black Narcissus presented by Devan Scott
films.synopsis: The use of gels to control the hue of film lights has been a key tool in every cinematographer’s toolkit since the advent of color film stocks. We’ll use Jack Cardiff’s work in the Technicolor masterpiece Black Narcissus (“one of the most ravishing films ever made” - David Thomson) as the jumping-offpoint for a discussion about the ways in which he paints with light to create moods, emotional cues, and color rhythms. Additionally, we’ll cover how innovations in color film stock impacted these creative decisions as well as more recent developments in lighting technology. Talk 1pm • Black Narcissus (100 mins) 1:40pm

films.title: Blade Runner: The Final Cut
films.synopsis: Los Angeles, 2019. Harrison Ford is Deckard, a “blade runner” hired to “retire” four rogue replicants – organic robots so lifelike they don’t even know they’re not human. In the course of his pursuit, Deckard comes to question his own – ambiguous – humanity. Audiences in ‘82 didn’t really buy into Scott’s vision of the future: mega corporations towering over street level squalor, technology erasing the boundaries between man and machine. It’s become harder to dismiss. “Blade Runner was ahead of its time and as poignant as any sci-fifilm I know just because of its sense of fragile identity. It is a superb piece of future-making and a film noir that bleeds over into tragedy.” DAVID THOMSON, HAVE YOU SEEN...?

films.title: Wings of Desire
films.synopsis: Two angels patrol Berlin, paying tender witness to the thoughts, anxieties and dreams of the people they come across—and trying to instill hope in those who despair. One (Bruno Ganz) falls in love with a trapeze artist. He wants to live a normal life and feel the ground beneath his feet. Recently restored in 4K, Wim Wenders’ iconic film shifts elegantly between black and white (for the world as the angels perceive it) and colour (our reality)— the same strategy that Michael Powell applied to his celestial romance, A Matter of Life and Death. “Few films are so rich, so intriguing, or so ambitious.” GEOFF ANDREW, TIME OUT

films.title: Mishima: A Life in Four Chapters
films.synopsis: In his best and most audacious movie, Paul Schrader blows up the literary biopic to give us not only insights into radical nationalist writer Yukio Mishima’s life, but also into his work. Mishima himself refused to separate the two, eventually leading his own private army. By incorporating large swathes of his fiction, Schrader suggests the life was a work of art; the body itself a piece of theatre. Cinematographer John Bailey and production designer Eiko Ishioka devise bold aesthetics for each section, compounded in a mesmerizing Philip Glass score. “One of the most gorgeous and sophisticated portraits of an artist ever put on film.” MICHAEL SRAGOW, NEW YORKER

films.title: Creating Colour Pt 3: Production Design + Young Girls of Rochefort presented by Devan Scott
films.synopsis: The building blocks of a color palette begin with what’s in front of the camera: the set, the props, and the costumes. Our discussion of production design and art direction will cover all the ways in which filmmakers can control the look of the world of the film such as in Jacques Demy’s The Young Girls of Rochefort, in which he repainted large sections of the titular French city to bring alive his candy-colored Hollywood-inspired fantasia. Talk 1pm • The Young Girls of Rochefort (125 mins)

films.title: Tron: Legacy
films.synopsis: Filmed right here in Vancouver, the belated followup is ripe for reassessment after director Joseph Kosinski’s recent triumph with Top Gun: Maverick. While Steve Lisberger’s original Tron anticipated the cyber culture that was still in its infancy in the early 80s, Kosinski’s film reaps the benefits of advanced digital technology to create an astonishing aesthetic overload: a stunning use of colour and Daft Punk’s throbbing soundtrack combine to create a virtual world you want to get lost in. “State of the art.”

films.title: Hukkle
films.synopsis: An old man has hiccups sitting on a bench, a drunken youth snores on the carriage, a kind old lady picks lilies of the valley, women sew in the dressmaker’s shop, men play bowling in a pub, the bee keeper spins the honey, a mechanical harvester harvests the wheat, which in the mill will be made into flour, and then in grandma’s kitchen into dumplings - and throughout all this the policeman investigates a murder... “Luminous... If you’re attracted to pure, exquisitely photographed cinematic depictions of the world, you could almost lie down in Hukkle as if it were a meadow and soak in its sun-drenched atmosphere.”

films.title: Nope
films.synopsis: The third and most spectacular Jordan Peele joint is a whole lot of movie. Set largely on a western ranch in a dusty California valley, the film flips between cowboy iconography, sci-fiplotting and horror set pieces, all re-

films.title: Creating Colour Pt 5: Digital Colour Grading + Amelie film screening
films.synopsis: Digital color grading tools have vastly expanded the possibilities in how directors and cinematographers manipulate color palettes, and the look of films and video have changed rapidly as a result. In the final talk in this Film Studies series, Devan Scott looks at the early days of this technology with Amelie, in which Bruno Delbonnel and Jean-Pierre Jeunet pushed the possibilities of motion picture palettes to previously impossible extremes in their realization of a romanticized Paris. Talk 1pm • Amelie (123 mins) 1:40pm

films.title: The Tree of Life
films.synopsis: Malick’s meditation on life, death and the whole damn thing is the kind of movie we rarely see in North America: a work of art, without apologies or compromise. The Tree of Life is nakedly autobiographical. But there’s more to it than that. Malick wants to marry the personal with the universal, the micro and the macro, to evoke not only his own past, but the miracle of life itself. Astonishingly beautiful in passages, the film won the Palme d’Or at Cannes and remains one of the most revered of the 21st century. “Profound, idiosyncratic, complex, sincere and magical; a confirmation that cinema can aspire to art.” IAN NATHAN, EMPIRE

films.title: Amadeus (4K) 40th Anniversary
films.synopsis: 1:00PM, 8:30PM In which the celebrated court composer Salieri welcomes a much ballyhooed young prodigy to Vienna. To his dismay, Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart is an impudent, callow upstart. Worse, he’s a genius. The Czech emigree Milos Forman knew that art and artists are a disruptive force, too unruly for polite society. His film of Peter Shaffer’s play is full of energy, wit, and boundless music. It went on to win 8 Academy Awards, including Best Picture, Best Director, and Best Actor (F Murray Abraham). Theatrical cut, 4K restoration. “A ravishing feast for the senses.” MILTON SHULMAN, LONDON EVENING STANDARD

films.title: The Last Emperor
films.synopsis: Bertolucci—collaborating with the great cinematographer Vittorio Storaro (The Conformist; Apocalypse Now)—created one of the most sumptuous of all epics to chronicle the life of Puyi, born in 1906 and regent Emperor of China from the age of three, forced to abdicate after the Chinese Revolution of 1912. But this was only the first chapter in a tumultuous life... The film won 9 Academy Awards, including Best Picture, Director, Cinematography, Sound and Score (Ryuichi Sakamoto, Cong Su and David Byrne).

films.title: Creating Colour Pt 4: Filtration + Three Colours: Blue presented by Devan Scott
films.synopsis: Directly filtering the image that comes into a camera’s lens allows cinematographers to vastly alter how a scene looks and feels. We’ll analyze the radical ways Kieslowski’s closet collaborator, cinematographer Slawomir Idziak, uses his complex system of filters to editorialize images, express the emotional state of characters, and establish place in such films as Three Colours: Blue, The Double Life of Veronique, and A Short Film About Killing. Talk 1pm • Three Colours Blue (94 mins) 1:40pm

films.title: Sunset Boulevard
films.synopsis: Hollywood on Hollywood: the tale of a screenwriter, Joe Gillis (William Holden), who stumbles into the orbit of a now-forgotten movie star, Norma Desmond (Gloria Swanson), and realizes this silent film diva could be his meal ticket. Styled as a film noir, Sunset Boulevard is a vicious comedy about Hollywood’s delusions of grandeur. It’s equally cynical about modern (mid-century) show biz—such was Wilder’s way.

films.title: Lawrence of Arabia
films.synopsis: Some films demand the big screen and this magnificent desert epic from David Lean is certainly one of them (no matter that Netflix boss Ted Sarandos recently claimed his son enjoyed watching it on his phone). In the role that would define him, Peter O’Toole plays the charismatic, articulate, adventurous English cartographer who would unite the Arab tribes to fight the Turks during WWI—it’s a complicated portrait of a flawed and contradictory man, who unwitingly seeded chaos in his wake. “A miracle... The first film I saw that made me want to be a moviemaker.”

films.title: Roma
films.synopsis: Alfonso Cuaron’s thrillingly diverse career encompasses everything from Gravity to Harry Potter. Roma is his masterpiece. An evocation of middle-class household in Mexico City in 1970, this scintillating black and white film focuses on Cleo (Yalitza Aparicio), a live-in maid, who tends to the two children, and observes, discreetly, as her employers’ marriage falls apart. The use of AVX sound gives it a whole other dimension—enjoy a rare opportunity to enjoy this modern classic on the big screen. “One of the most beautiful films I’ve ever seen.”

films.title: Disaster! The 70s movie craze ... + Earthquake (50th Anniversary Screening) presented by David C Jones
films.synopsis: Back in the 1970s audiences couldn’t get enough of things breaking down: Planes (Airport, 1970); cruise liners (The Poseidon Adventure, 1972); condos (The Towering Inferno, 1974)... There was a thirst for mass destruction as veteran movie stars and ingenues struggled to make it to the end credits. In this lighthearted lecture, actor and comedian David C Jones is our guide to the heyday of the disaster movie. Following the talk, David will be back to introduce a special 50th Anniversary screening of Earthquake in its full Sensurround glory.

films.title: Chuck Chuck Baby
films.synopsis: AUG 18-SEP 2 ADD’L SCREENINGS LOC/VCT No wonder Helen’s depressed: she works in a chicken-packing plant, lives with her ex-husband and his much younger girlfriend, and she’s looking after his dying mum. That is, until an old school flame, Gwen, returns to town… Despite the downbeat set up, Janis Pugh’s emotionally raw, semi-autobiographical film proves to be an exuberant and exhilarating musical crowd-pleaser, not a million miles away from the likes of The Full Monty, Kinky Boots and Mamma Mia. Song credits include Neil Diamond, Janis Ian, The Imperials, and the Pogues.

films.title: His Three Daughters
films.synopsis: SEP 14-18 ADD’L SCREENINGS VCT/LOC Three sisters—Carrie Coon, Elizabeth Olson, and Natasha Lyonne—congregate to attend the final few days of their father’s life. They bring with them years of barely-repressed jealousy and resentment, as well as wildly different personalities. Azazel Jacobs’ finely honed melodrama mines the awkward, painful humour that anyone who’s been on a prolonged death-watch will recognize, as well as the fraught emotions. The unwinding, when it comes, will leave not a dry eye in the house.

films.title: Electric Lady Studios: A Jimi Hendrix Vision
films.synopsis: 1:30PM, 6:00PM OCT 12-19 ADD'L SCREENINGS 1968 and Jimi Hendrix is happening. When he’s not playing (and sometimes when he is), he’s enjoying the New York club scene, and in particular he’s digging The Generation on W8 in Greenwich Village, a spot that had hosted BB King, Sly and the Family Stone and Dave Van Ronk. But Hendrix’s close advisors Eddie Kramer and Jim Marron persuaded him he didn’t really need a club—he needed his own a recording studio. And so Electic Lady Studios was born, the first ever artist owned commercial recording facility.

films.title: Dahomey
films.synopsis: OCT 26-29 ADD'L SCREENINGS When a 68-minute doc about cultural artifacts wins the top prize at the Berlin Film Festival, you can be sure that it must be very special filmmaking. Mati Diop channels Godard and Chris Marker to bring current political discourse to life around the return of plundered art works to colonized nations (here, the Republic of Benin). Diop's most audacious conceit is to give the antiquities themselves a voice. But the film's finale, a student debate about the value of these treasures, is equally inspired. A masterpiece. In French, Fon, and English

films.title: Monkey on a Stick
films.synopsis: The Hare Krishna movement dates back to 1966, when A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada brought his version of Hindu scripture to the USA. Despite prescriptions against eating meat, engaging in sex or consuming drugs and alcohol, the movement became hugely popular in the West—

films.title: Physician, Heal Thyself
films.synopsis: OCT 12-22 ADD'L SCREENINGS VCT/LOC In Asher Penn’s Physician, Heal Thyself one of the world’s foremost experts on addiction, trauma and childhood development, Dr Gabor Maté, shares not only his theories, but also his personal story: his difficult early childhood in Hungary, immigrating to Canada, his experience as a journalist for The Ubyssey, and his early reputation as a contrarian—before his long years of therapeutic practice in and around Vancouver’s Downtown Eastside. Oct 11 7:45pm screening followed by Q&A with Gabor Maté

films.title: Wallace & Gromit: The Curse of the Were-Rabbit
films.synopsis: After starting a pest control business, the dynamic duo land a job from the alluring Lady Tottington (Helena Bonham Carter) to stop a giant rabbit from destroying the town’s crops. Both Wallace and the stuffy Victor (Ralph Fiennes) vie for the lady’s affections. If Wallace wants to please his pretty client, and best Victor, he needs to capture that pesky bunny. Hilarious slapstick hijinks from Aardman Animation. All Ages Welcome

films.title: Adrianne & the Castle
films.synopsis: “It’s a brave thing people do when they fall in love. It’s gonna hurt.” Alan St-George fell for Adrianne at first sight. Although he had to woo her, his ardour proved irresistible. They married. Bought a house. And under Adrianne’s influence, Alan—an artist who created a successful business making animal mascot costumes—transformed the place into a palace fit for a queen. His wife was his inspiration, the love of his life for her love of life. How then, to carry on, after her passing? 7 8 10 11 12 13 14 16 17 18 19 20 22 23 24 25 26 27 28 T H U S U N M O N T U E W E D F R I S A T Film Studies: Creating Colour Pt 4: Filtration + The Double films.title: Spellbound
films.synopsis: Miklos Rózsa composed the outstanding score for Hitchcock’s early stab at a psychoanalysis suspense movie, a rare example of the theremin used outside of the scifigenre, though even here the aim was to connote the “paranormal” for trauma and dream sequences designed by Salvador Dali. When Dr. Edwards (Gregory Peck) takes over Green Manors mental hospital, one of his staff, Constance Peterson (Ingrid Bergman) becomes suspicious of his true identity... The movie itself is best seen as one long, two-hour dream sequence. “Hitchcock embellishes it with characteristically brilliant twists, like the infinite variety of parallel lines which etch their way through Peck’s mind.”

films.title: Ru + Kim Thúy in Conversation
films.synopsis: Guest Curator at the Vancouver Writers Fest this year, Kim Thúy, will join us for this special screening of Ru, based on her Governor General's Award-winning novel. Ru is the story of the arduous journey of a wealthy family fleeing from Vietnam, before landing in Quebec and experiencing their first Canadian winter. Directed by Charles-Olivier Michaud, and produced by Thúy, the film is a sombre, stunningly beautiful examination of forced migration, isolation, and newfound belonging, told through the eyes of the daughter of the family, Nguyen An Tinh. Following the screening, Thúy will engage in an onstage discussion about this bold, penetrating work.

films.title: Oliver Hockenhull:
films.synopsis: As the title implies Hockenhull’s new essay film is an autobiographical rumination on memory, and a philosophical disquisition on the technology of photography, cinema, and AI. Starting with a trove of family photos, Hockenhull explores how images function as mental constructs and ideological stamps. This film engages

films.title: Nosferatu With Radiohead A Silents Synced Film
films.synopsis: FW Murnau, meet Thom Yorke. Radiohead’s mind-blowing “Kid A” (2000) and “Amnesiac” (2001) albums breathe new life into the first great vampire movie, an expressionist landmark memorable for Max Schreck’s tall, bald, rodent-like bloodsucker. Radiohead’s music may have emerged 80 years after the images, yet the combination proves weirdly effective. Throw out your organs!

films.title: The Etiquette of Dying, film + Ron Samworth concert
films.synopsis: "When does one begin dying?" That's the first question posed by this poetical but direct contemplation of our universal—yet often obscured—fate. A unique collaboration between guitarist Ron Samworth and filmmaker Melissa Hubert, The Etiquette of Dying came out of Ron's experience with cancer a few years ago, which inspired a suite, and which in turn inspired Hubert's 51-minute animated film. After the screening Ron will lead a 4 piece band and the artists will invite the audience to share their thoughts and questions.

films.title: Reprise A Page of Madness - Live Score by Anju Singh / The Nausea
films.synopsis: An asylum janitor tries to persuade his wife—an inmate—to escape with him, but she doesn’t want to go. This Expressionist horror film was directed by former kabuki female impersonator Teinsosuke Kinugasa, co-written with Nobel prize-winner Yasunari Kawabata, and performed by Kinugasa’s avant-garde experimental group. Performer, composer and sound artist Anju Singh will deepen the cathartic and reflective experience of the film using percussion, strings, synthesizers, electronics and world instruments to echo the irrational extremes, dissonances and nuances conjured by this unique cinematic masterpiece.

films.title: Vampyr
films.synopsis: This Halloween, experimental music duo Magazinist will perform a live score to 1932 classic Vampyr. Described by Guillermo del Toro as being “the closest you get to poetry in film,” Vampyr combines dreamlike cinematography

films.title: Santa Sangre
films.synopsis: Jodorowsky’s unforgettable third film (after El Topo and Holy Mountain—and years trying to get Dune made) is a cavalcade of burning images, a circus of strange... Mexican trapeze artist Concha discovers her husband the knife thrower in flagrante with the tattooed lady and pours acid on his assets. He responds by cutting off her arms. Crazed, she ropes in their perturbed son to, literally, fill her sleeves. Those offended by graphic depictions of all that is unholy, this is definitely not the movie for you. “A film in which the inner chambers of the soul are laid bare.... I am reminded by Alejandro Jodorowsky that true psychic horror is possible on the screen—horror, poetry, surrealism, psychological pain, and wicked humor, all at once.”

films.title: Burden of Dreams
films.synopsis: There are only two documentaries about filmmaking that can be considered essential viewing. One is Hearts of Darkness, about the making of Apocalypse Now. The other is Les Blank’s Burden of Dreams, which was shot only a year or two later, and which chronicles the equally tumultuous struggle to make Werner Herzog’s Fitzcarraldo. Both are portraits of the artist grappling against overwhelming odds in the maw of the jungle. War, pestilence, plane crashes and mutiny... all this and Klaus Kinski too. “Blank created an enduring record of hubris, exploitation and unrelenting misadventure in the pursuit of artistic greatness.” ZACHARY BARNES, THE WALL STREET JOURNAL In English, Spanish, and German

films.title: Fitzcarraldo
films.synopsis: Herzog’s grandest folly was almost his undoing, but became his greatest triumph. One of cinema’s least convincing Irishmen, Klaus Kinski plays Brian Sweeney Fitzgerald, who has a dream to bring opera to the Amazon. Not content to bring in a phonograph, he means to ship in an entire opera house, and invite Caruso down in person. But first he’ll need to portage a 350 ton steamship over a mountain... Not for the first time, Herzog steals fire from the gods to pull off an impossible movie. “One of the great visions of the cinema, and one of the great follies. One would not have been possible without the other.” ROGER EBERT In German, Spanish and Asháninka

films.title: Hammett
films.synopsis: A troubled collaboration between director Wim Wenders and producer Francis Coppola, Hammett has barely been seen. That’s a great shame because it’s a clever and visually beguiling neo-noir mystery. Frederic Forrest plays Dashiell Hammett, the Maltese Falcon author who once worked for Pinkerton’s Detective Agency. Visited by an old friend from the agency, Hammett agrees to help him track down a prostitute, Crytal Ling, and gets sucked into a plot every bit as complicated as one of his own stories... “A neo-noir classic, it looks like a series of Black Mask covers drawn by Edward Hopper, has a bluesy score by John Barry, dazzling sets by Dean Tavoularis (production designer on the Godfather trilogy) and is allusively cast (eg, Elisha Cook from The Maltese Falcon as a Bay Area cabbie). A stylish, entertaining movie.” PHILIP FRENCH, THE OBSERVER

films.title: The Double Life of Veronique
films.synopsis: Kieslowski’s international breakthrough remains one of his most beloved films, a ravishing, mysterious rumination on identity, love, and human intuition. Irène Jacob is incandescent as both Weronika, a Polish choir soprano, and her double, Véronique, a French music teacher. Though unknown to each other, the two women share an enigmatic, emotional bond, which Kieslowski details in gorgeous reflections, colors, and movements.

films.title: The Maltese Falcon
films.synopsis: More than anyone, Humphrey Bogart was the face of film noir. Most histories of the genre mark John Huston’s definitive adaptation of Dashiell Hammett’s hardboiled novel as the starting point, and Bogie’s portrait of private investigator Sam Spade encapsulates much of what makes noir so compelling: Spade is a callous cynic by experience, a louse whose dim estimate of human behaviour is his strongest professional attribute, and a closet romantic beneath it all. See also: Hammett, by Wim Wenders and produced by Francis Coppola, screening later today.

films.title: The Fall
films.synopsis: Shot over four years across 24 countries, and entirely self-financed by commercials director Tarsem, The Fall is such a mind- (and eye) boggling movie it’s hard to believe it actually exists. Indeed, it only got a token release in 2006 despite the support of David Fincher and Spike Jonze, and for many years the film has been impossible to see on the big screen. It’s a tall story about storytelling: in 1920s Los Angeles, a bedridden patient captives a young girl with a wondrous tale of heroes and villains. “What would’ve happened if Andrei Tarkovsky had made The Wizard of Oz.”

films.title: Eyes Wide Shut co-presented with Vancouver Opera
films.synopsis: Kubrick’s Christmas story is a droll, furtive dream of sex and infidelity, probably the weirdest film in Tom Cruise’s filmography. Loosely based on Arthur Schnitzler’s Traumnovelle, it’s a film about a Manhattan doctor whose complacent beliefs about his marriage to Alice (Nicole Kidman) are shaken when she admits to having fantasized about another man.

films.title: Between the Temples
films.synopsis: In Nathan Silver’s gentle screwball comedy, Ben (Jason Schwartzman), a cantor in a small, upstate New York community, is suffering from a crisis in faith after the recent passing of his wife. He’s living with both is mother, and his step-mother, in the basement. On top of it all he’s also lost his singing voice. A chance encounter in a bar

films.title: Good One
films.synopsis: This movie feels like a perfect short story. 17-year-old Sam (Lily Collias) gamely heads out on a camping weekend with her recently remarried dad (James LeGros) and his newly divorced buddy, Matt (Danny McCarthy). Matt’s son drops out of the trip before it’s started. You can’t blame him. His dad is a mess and Chris is wrapped up to tightly in his own idea of what a camping trip should be to pay attention to anybody else. In her debut feature, wrtier-director India Donaldson knocks this one out of the park. “Gorgeous and subtle... This is a small, delicate film, but its ripples linger.” STEPHANIE ZACHAREK, TIME

films.title: Ghostlight
films.synopsis: Here’s another gem that flew under the radar earlier this summer: Ghostlight won rave reviews (100% Fresh on Rotten Tomatoes) but barely scored a release in Canada. Dan (Keith Kupferer) is a construction worker struggling to keep it together after his teenage son’s death. Daughter Daisy (Keith’s daughter, Katherine), is also acting out. Dan gets suspended from work but doesn’t tell his family. Daisy begins to think he’s an having an affair. The truth is stranger: he’s rehearing a play...

films.title: Janet Planet
films.synopsis: “You know what’s funny? Every single moment of my life is hell.” So says Lacy (Zoe Zigler), 11-years-old and learning fast. Her mom (Julianne Nicholson) demurs. But she also gets it. Over the course of several months Lacy and Janet do what mothers and daughters do, interrupted from time to time by friends and admirers, few of whom meet Lacy’s standards. For her first film as writer-director, Pulitzer prize-winning playwright Annie Baker distills an 11-year-old’s summer to its essence. “Not just one of the great films of its year, but one of the finest first films in the annals of the medium.” CHARLES BRAMESCO, LITTLE WHITE LIES

films.title: Sullivan’s Travels
films.synopsis: Continuing his exploration of Hollywood’s fascination with itself, critic and historian Donald Brackett introduces one of the great satires of the Golden Age, Preston Sturges’ Sullivan’s Travels. Joel McCrea stars as an earnest would-be artistic filmmaker who disguises himself as a hobo to get to know the real America... Sturges was a genius, and this is probably his masterpiece.

films.title: The Day of the Locust
films.synopsis: In the midst of the Depression of the 1930s, Hollywood shines like a beacon to all the helpless people scattered across the city. In one crumbling apartment block, a blond bombshell (Karen Black) aspires to be an actress, an artist (William Atherton) looks for legitimacy, and a child actor performs a gross homage to Mae West. Cockfights and poverty prevail out of the glow of show business. Introverted accountant "Homer Simpson" (Donald Sutherland) watches as society collapses under greed and ambition.

films.title: The Bad and the Beautiful
films.synopsis: Cynical but not, Vincente Minnelli’s Tinsel Town melodrama is really a love letter to the dynamism of the Dream Factory, made just as the studio system was at its peak. Kirk Douglas is the epitome of the unscrupulous movie producer, a manipulative hustler who nevertheless has the drive to make good things happen.

films.title: What Price Hollywood? Curated and Presented by film critic/historian Donald Brackett
films.synopsis: The movie screen is a magic mirror in which we all like to see reflections of our better selves. Filmmakers are not immune to the attraction, and Hollywood has been mythologizing itself since before movies could talk. In our latest Film Studies series film critic and historian Donald Brackett gives us a whistle stop studio tour taking us from the Golden Age to the C21st, beginning with George Cukor’s seminal 1932 film, What Price Hollywood—the inspiration for A Star Is Born.

films.title: Babylon
films.synopsis: Damien Chazelle’s second Hollywood on Hollywood movie (after La La Land) follows Margot Robbie as a starlet on the make at the tail end of the silent film era in the late 1920s, and a couple of friends she makes along the way, Manny (Diego Calva), who becomes a studio executive, trumpet player Sidney (Jovan Adepo) and established heartthrob Jack (Brad Pitt). Hollywood has always had an inherently self-absorbed quality that continues to fascinate us, so perhaps it comes as no surprise that many film directors choose to explore their own artistic obsessions via the vehicle of Hollywood mythology itself, past and present. This series explores some of the movie industry's own reflections on itself as a dream factory, from one of the earliest examples, George Cukor's pre-code examination of the seductive pitfalls of an actress's hungry aspirations, to one of the latest, Damien Chazelle's mesmerizing trip through a director's looking glass world. Along the way, our guided tour makes memorable stops that ask us all what makes our never ending appetite for screen dreams so tantalizing. Could it be that in the end it's something as simple as the deft observation once made by songwriter Van Dyke Parks? "Movies are magic." No matter how weird and challenging our daily lives might be, we'll always have the welcome escape of a dark cinema, where we can sit with complete strangers and dream together with our eyes wide open. Scheduled across five successive Monday mornings, our latest Film Studies adult education series will feature short, 25-minute introductions by film historian and curator Donald Brackett, followed by the screening and a brief audience talkback. Introduction 10.30am with Film at 11am.

films.title: Come and See
films.synopsis: As Nazi forces encroach on his small village in present-day Belarus, teenage Flyora (Aleksei Kravchenko) eagerly joins the Soviet resistance. Rather than the adventure and glory he envisioned, what he finds is a waking nightmare of unimaginable carnage and cruelty—rendered with a feverish, otherworldly intensity by Klimov’s subjective camerawork and expressionistic sound design. Perhaps the most visceral, impossible-to-forget antiwar film ever made.

films.title: Meanwhile On Earth
films.synopsis: Franck is lost in space. Literally. Which leaves his sister Elsa (Megan Northan) struggling with grief and susceptible to making a deal when contacted by an alien voice offering to trade her brother for a few fresh human bodies. But is this all in her head? Jérémy Clapin’s arresting second feature, his first live action film after the inventive animation I Lost My Body, explores loss and disaffection, and the sci-fitrappings allow him to invest introspection

films.title: The Manchurian Candidate
films.synopsis: Gulf War hero Raymond Shaw (Liev Schreiber) is picked for the VP slot through the influence of his mother (Meryl Streep). Meanwhile comrades from Shaw’s former unit are having nightmares about the operation for which he was awarded the Medal of Honor. Major Marco (Denzel Washington) is determined to find the truth... This smart update on Richard Condon’s classic paranoia novel feels weirdly prescient in its anxieties around global corporate brainwashing, war profiteering, assassination and election fixing.

films.title: Winter Kills
films.synopsis: 4:00PM, 8:45PM Assembling one of the weirdest casts ever, and a heavy hitting crew too, first time director William Richert pulled off an inspired black comic adaptation of the ultimate conspiracy theory, based on a 1974 novel by Richard (Manchurian Candidate) Condon. It’s a lunatic riff on the Kennedy assassination(s), with Jeff Bridges trying to find out who really killed his brother, the President. If this isn’t RFK’s favourite movie, it probably should be. Screening here on a newly restored 35mm print, presented by Quentin Tarantino

films.title: Van Gogh: Poets & Lovers
films.synopsis: 200 years after its opening and a century after acquiring its first Van Gogh works, London’s National Gallery hosts the UK’s biggest ever Van Gogh exhibition. This film is a chance to reexamine and better understand this iconic artist, focussing on the artist’s years in the south of France, where he revolutionised his style. Van Gogh became consumed with a passion for storytelling in his art, turning the world around him into vibrant, idealised spaces and symbolic characters. Poets and lovers filled his imagination. Adult Ticket Series Pass Senior/ Student Pass VIFF+ Pass $18 $80 $75 $70

films.title: Megalopolis
films.synopsis: Francis Coppola's self-funded, self-styled new Roman epic—set in a futuristic city that looks a lot like New York —has garnered pans, raves and everything in-between. And it deserves them all. It's a crazily ambitious folly, a wildly audacious swing, unlike anything else you might have seen before. Megalopolis is a movie about the present moment—about a decadent Establishment on the verge of eating itself—that dares to imagine a brighter future. It's a film of ideas, and sentiment, satire and play. Go with it, see where it takes you.

films.title: The Chef & the Daruma
films.synopsis: For 36 years, Tojo’s has been a mainstay in the Vancouver food scene, beloved by critics, foodies, and a plethora of celebrities. A pioneer of Japanese cuisine in the West, chef Hidekazu Tojo helped bring sushi to the mainstream, and is known as the inventor of the California Roll. Shot in Vancouver, Vancouver Island, and Japan, The Chef & the Daruma is a mouth-watering film, taking us on a journey of immigration, identity, and reinvention.

films.title: Union
films.synopsis: The latest observational doc from Canadian filmmaker Brett Story (The Prison in 12 Landscapes; The Hottest August) follows the campaign of a group of Staten Island factory workers to become the first unionized Amazon workplace in the USA. They have no official backing, no experience, no budget (save for $120,000 raised on GoFundMe) and the company tries everything in its power to tip the scales against them, but they know their workmates and figure out several unconventional tactics of their own (free weed!). US Documentary Special Jury Award for the Art of Change (Sundance)

films.title: Inay (Mama)
films.synopsis: 4:30PM, 8:15PM From the 1990s, the Live-In Caregiver Program attracted thousands of Filipino women to Canada as migrant workers, enabling them to send money back home and gain permanent residency. Director Thea Loo and cinematographer Jeremiah Reyes, a married couple, explore the psychological impact on the children who were left behind by their mothers due to economic necessity. Deeply personal, Inay reveals the hidden pain behind the lives of women who sacrificed themselves to take care of Canada’s children and elderly. + Dear Watsonville (Sondra Lucille, USA, 2024, 18 mins)

films.title: Brandon Wint: Moving for Love
films.synopsis: Poet and filmmaker Brandon Wint presents two new shorts, Moving for Love and Backbone, alongside live jazz with collaborators Feven Kidane, Yoro Noukoussi, and Quincey Mayes, and poetry. In Moving For Love Brandon explores his family’s migration from the Caribbean to Canada in the 1970s. Backbone examines how cerebral palsy, the visible disability with which Brandon lives, complicates the notion and practical realities of health and self-care. Limited Early Bird tickets available. Book now! Live Concert + Film Screenings

films.title: Flow
films.synopsis: 4:30PM, 6:30PM 4:45PM, 6:45PM DEC 4-15 ADDITIONAL SCREENINGS Open to Youth

films.title: Food Bank Benefit Screening: Hundreds of Beavers
films.synopsis: The funniest, and certainly the furriest movie you will see this year, Hundreds of Beavers channels the zany slapstick shtick of Buster Keaton, Charlie Chaplin and Bugs Bunny through a videogame quest narrative to retell the eternal saga of Man vs Nature. Man, in this case, is an inebriate applejack distiller, Jean Kayak (Ryland Brickson Cole Tews) who takes up fur trapping to survive a harsh winter. As for nature, the critters—beavers, raccoons, horses, skunks—stand tall in mascot costumes and put up stout resistance. “One for the ages: a dam fine movie.” MATT ZOLLER SEITZ All proceeds from this screening go to the Vancouver Food Bank

films.title: Oh Canada
films.synopsis: Veteran filmmaker Paul Schrader refuses to go gentle into that good night. And the same goes for his protagonist here: Leonard Fife (Richard Gere) is an American-born documentary filmmaker who made his home in Canada. Nearing the end of his life, Fife has agreed to film a lengthy autobiographical interview in order to set the record straight, especially about the reasons for his self-imposed exile. His testimony is a confession of lies and betrayal, but can his memory be trusted? This is Schrader in soul-searching mode, his forte.

films.title: Counted Out
films.synopsis: The fundamental importance of mathematics in the C21, the way we think about it, and, crucially, the way we go about teaching it, doesn’t add up. That’s the thesis behind Vicki Abeles’ documentary, a film persuasive enough to have you questioning basic principles and rethinking the whole equation. Why are we dividing classes between “math kids” and the rest when data and algorithms run our world? Revolutionary teaching practices are opening up the subject to curious minds and breaking down deeply entrenched barriers to access.

films.title: Queens (Reinas)
films.synopsis: Amidst socio-economic turmoil in 1992 Lima, Perú, Elena (Jimena Lindo) wants to move her daughters Lucia (Abril Gjurinovic) and Aurora (Luana Vega) to the USA for a safer life, but needs her ex-husband “El Loco” Carlos (Gonzalo Molina) to sign their travel permits. Given a brief window to reconnect with his daughters, Carlos tries to earn his way back into their lives. Klaudia Reynicke’s sensitive third feature weaves a poignant tale of sisterhood, summer heartbreaks, and tender goodbyes.

films.title: Dada
films.synopsis: Fifteen-year-old Kai (talented newcomer Ciara Alexys) and her divorced dad Adam (James Gilbert) embark on a weekend getaway to a rustic cabin on Lake Huron... nestled next door to a massive nuclear power plant. On the way they start to play a family nonsense game. It seems innocent enough, and yet as the trip progresses, it slides into territory that is enigmatic but definitely disturbing... Actor-turned-writer-director Aaron Poole has fashioned a strange and artful debut full of questions and mysteries. Aaron Poole Q&A Friday and Saturday

films.title: La Cocina
films.synopsis: The Grill is a New York greasy spoon. Undocumented Mexican immigrant, Estella (Anna Diaz) is thrown in at the deep end on her first day working alongside chef Pedro (Raúl Briones), whose affair with one of the waitresses, Julia (Rooney Mara) is in crisis: she is due to have an abortion this PM. On top of which, last night’s reckoning is $800 short. The work is unremitting, tempers flare, the soda machine floods. It’s based on a 1957 play, but feels plugged right into the fault lines short circuiting the US right now. In English and Spanish

films.title: Obsessed with Light
films.synopsis: Loïe Fuller may not be a household name, but nearly a century after her death she’s still inspiring artists like Taylor Swift, Shakira, Bill T Jones and William Kentridge. A somewhat pudgy midwesterner, Fuller became world famous as an innovative dancer, combining fabric, lighting effects and movement in revolutionary ways. Modern dance, fashion and stage craft would all feel her impact. Rodin, Cocteau and Toulouse Lautrec were admirers. One of the loveliest and liveliest arts documentaries of the year.

films.title: Brandon Wint: Moving For Love – An Evening of Film, Poetry & Music
films.synopsis: Poet and filmmaker Brandon Wint presents two new short films, Moving for Love and Backbone, alongside a live jazz performance with collaborators Feven Kidane, Yoro Noukoussi, and Quincey Mayes, and a poetry reading. In Moving for Love Brandon explores for the first time the details of his family’s migration from the Caribbean to Canada in the early 1970s. Backbone is a vulnerable memoir exploring how cerebral palsy, the visible disability with which Brandon lives, complicates the notion and practical realities of health and self-care. 6:30pm Intros, live music and poetry • 7.30pm Intermission • 7.50pm Films and Q&A

films.title: A Tribute to Artie Shaw + Time Is All You've Got screening
films.synopsis: One of the most popular and intriguing big band leaders of the Swing era, Artie Shaw took jazz clarinet to a new level of artistry and celebrity. On occasion, Shaw would tour

films.title: Ernest Cole: Lost and Found
films.synopsis: Raoul Peck (I Am Not Your Negro) tells the story of South African photographer Ernest Cole, who captured some of the most vivid and compelling images of the apartheid regime in the 1960s. Pulling from a recently discovered archive of 60,000 unseen negatives, mostly from his exile to the US, and from Cole’s often poetic diaries and interviews as well as the reflections of friends and family, Peck delivers a rich, insightful and empathetic portrait of a Black artist ripe for rediscovery. “Rich and nuanced... a treasure.”

films.title: Alien
films.synopsis: The crew of the Nostromo is awakened when the ship’s computer, Mother, picks up a distress signal from an uninhabited planet... What they find they won’t soon forget. By far the scariest in the long-running Alien franchise, this was the anti-Star Wars: a dirty, dark and dangerous space movie, claustrophobic and prickling with anxiety. It also features one of the most stomach-churning jump-scares in film history. “In Space, no one can hear you scream,” ran the famous tagline. Cinema audiences heard plenty.

films.title: Playtime
films.synopsis: Jacques Tati was modernity’s clown; technology his banana skin. No filmmaker scrutinized the rapid architectural, scientific and sociological evolution of Gaullist France as quizzically as Tati in Jour de Fete, Mon Hulot’s Holidays, and Mon Oncle. By Playtime, Hulot’s world has been transformed, and he seemed more than ever an anachronism. Shot over three years, in 70mm, the film was a commercial disaster, but it’s now evident that this is Tati’s masterpiece, a city symphony for the modern man. “A feast of subtle sight gags, playful noise and, above all, visual wonders.” DAVE CALHOUN, TIME OUT

films.title: Moulin Rouge!
films.synopsis: Paris has never been gayer than in this headlong karaoke culture crash set in a poptastic 19th century Montmartre, where Ewan McGregor composes The Sound of Music and Toulose Lautrec (John Leguizamo) leads an acting troupe. Nicole Kidman is Satine, a consumptive courtesan who is the queen of the show at da eponymous club. Ba-dazzling stuff from Luhrmann, a filmmaker seemingly intent on reaching the Palace of Wisdom at supersonic speed. “A breathtaking baroque film that marries the best of theatre, opera and cinematic technique.” LIZ MOODY, EMPIRE MAGAZINE

films.title: Victor Noriega’s Kuyatet + Lino Brocka’s Manila in the Claws of Light
films.synopsis: To celebrate our spotlight on Filipino director Lino Brocka, we are pairing a screening of Manila in the Claws of Light

films.title: Lino Brocka: Bona
films.synopsis: Philippine superstar Nora Aunor plays against type as Bona, a schoolgirl infatuated with a hunky supporting actor (Phillip Salvador as the noxious Gardo) in this kicky rediscovered Lino Brocka classic.

films.title: Wallace & Gromit: Vengeance Most Fowl
films.synopsis: 4:30PM, 6:20PM 11:30AM, 1:30PM, 3:30PM, 5:30PM DEC 22 - JAN 2 ADDITIONAL SCREENINGS Aardman Animation’s handcrafted mix of dad jokes, slapstick, mock dramatics and understated emotion makes this return for the claymation odd couple a constant delight. The villainous Feathers McGraw is back to no good, commandeering Norbot the robot.

films.title: Challengers
films.synopsis: Luca Guadagnino (Queer; Call Me By Your Name) snaps back into gear with this sexy, fun screwball comedy masquerading as a sports film. Frenemies Mike Faist and Josh O’Connor compete for the favours of Zendaya, on and off the tennis court. “Challengers goes by in a flash. Its ending is an erotic thunderclap. By the time it’s over, you don’t know what smacked you, but it felt like love.” STEPHANIE ZACHEREK, TIME

films.title: Vermiglio
films.synopsis: 3:00PM, 7:30PM 6:00PM, 8:30PM 4:00PM, 8:30PM Delperro’s exquisitely photographed movie—Italy’s submission for the Academy Awards—recreates the austere and harsh lifestyle in an Alpine village at the tail end of WWII with revelatory care and compassion.

films.title: Behind the Masks
films.synopsis: In the early 20th century many traditional Indigenous masks ended up in Europe, in museums and art collections, and, as this entertaining doc reveals, in the hands of surrealist artists like Max Ernst, André Breton, and Joan Miró...

films.title: My National Gallery, London
films.synopsis: This is a lovely premise for a film. The Exhibition on Screen team look at the National Gallery in London through the eyes of the art lovers who pass through its doors, Each interviewee gets a few minutes to tell us about their favourite painting...

films.title: A New Kind of Wilderness
films.synopsis: 6:00PM, An idyllic life on a family farm in Norway becomes an impossible task when Nik's wife dies from cancer. This quietly affecting film follows his struggles to do right by his kids, himself, and his late wife's wishes.

films.title: Memories of Murder
films.synopsis: Parasite director Bong Joon-ho’s police procedural is the centrepiece of our retrospective and arguably his masterpiece. Certainly, among serial killer movies this one is on a par with Zodiac and The Silence of the Lambs, but more politically astute. “One of the greatest films of the last 15 years.” LUKE BALDOCK, THE HOLLYWOOD NEWS (2018)

films.title: Who by Fire
films.synopsis: Seventeen-year-old Jeff, an aspiring filmmaker, is invited by his friend Max and his family to stay in the isolated lodge belonging to Blake, an award-winning film director. As Jeff tries to navigate his awkward crush on his friend’s older sister, Aloicha, he witnesses the vicious, ego-driven, alcohol-fueled interactions between the renowned auteur and his former collaborator, Max’s screenwriter father, Albert. Surrounded by monumental mountains and shimmering lakes, the party veers between moments of elation and cruelty, unease and palpable danger. Acclaimed Quebecois director Philippe Lesage (The Demons; Genesis) returns with a tense, mesmerizing tour de force that’s both agonizing and cathartic. Parallel, painful generational stories play out both in the seemingly infinite wilderness and across the dinner table; the slow burn of mounting dread punctuated with electrifying, deeply unsettling moments of feral intensity.

films.title: The Holdovers
films.synopsis: Destined to become a seasonal staple, this bittersweet comedy reunites Sideways director and star Alexander Payne and Paul Giamatti in the portrait of a surly classics teacher forced to babysit five “orphans” at boarding school over the holidays.

films.title: Nobody’s Fool
films.synopsis: Paul Newman brings a seasoned, irascible charm to this wintery gem from director Robert Benton, based on Richard Russo’s novel.

films.title: Mother
films.synopsis: Dominated by a remarkable performance from veteran Kim Hye-Ja as a quack herbalist who will stop at nothing to clear her son of a murder charge, this is Bong’s most under-rated movie, a fascinating companion piece to Memories of Murder.

films.title: Barking Dogs Never Bite
films.synopsis: Bong’s first film is a genial black comedy involving the deaths—accidental and otherwise—of several dogs in a Seoul apartment complex. Saturday’s screening will be

films.title: I Saw the TV Glow
films.synopsis: Two misfits are sucked into the deranged world of a supernatural TV show. Trans filmmaker Jane Schoenbrun taps into something deeply disquieting in ways that reverberate long after viewing.

films.title: The Host
films.synopsis: Bong’s monster movie (inspired by a real-life pollution scandal and carrying a prophetic viral load of its own) is his most purely fun entertainment. It’s the most successful Korean movie ever made.

films.title: Snowpiercer
films.synopsis: In a future where a failed global-warming experiment kills offmost life on the planet, a class system evolves aboard the Snowpiercer, a bullet train that travels around the globe via a perpetual-motion engine. In English, Korean, Japanese, and French

films.title: Close Your Eyes
films.synopsis: Twenty years after the film he was directing fell apart when the leading man disappeared, Miguel (Manolo Solo) agrees to reopen the mystery for a TV show... He needs the money, and he’s ready for a reckoning. A late masterpiece from Victor Erice.

films.title: Parasite
films.synopsis: South Korean master filmmaker Bong Joon-ho delivers an unpredictable comic suspense thriller with his Palme d’Or and Academy Award-winning film, Parasite— which cracked the top 100 in Sight & Sound’s Greatest Films list in 2022. In Korean with Korean subtitles.

films.title: Okja
films.synopsis: Bong #6: his wackiest movie, centered on a genetically modified super pig the size of a hippo. Raised by a Korean peasant farmer, prize specimen Okja is called to New York to launch its new food product. But animal liberationists mean to disrupt the show.

films.title: Thelma
films.synopsis: We've seen geriatric vigilante movies before but June Squibb, who recently turned 95, is definitely pushing the envelope. Squibb is a delight as a still independent senior scammed into posting bail for her beloved slacker grandson. Comedy of the year.

films.title: All We Imagine as Light
films.synopsis: :30PM What Wong Kar-wai did for Hong Kong, Payal Kapadia does for Mumbai: the Cannes Grand Prix winner is a romantic heartbreaker about three nurses at different stages of life. It’s a future classic.

films.title: Bribe, Inc. + Q&A
films.synopsis: Exposing one of the most audacious and lucrative bribery schemes in modern history, Bribe, Inc is a disturbing chronicle of corruption, bureaucratic bungling and impunity. “Filled with the kind of cloak-and-dagger developments one associates with potboilers and airport novels – clandestine meetings, coded emails and secret-filled hard drives.”

films.title: I Am Nevenka
films.synopsis: Bollain’s film is based on the true story of a young city councillor who reported the mayor for sexual misconduct, and faced a barrage of sexist innuendo and criticism—but refused to back down.

films.title: Little Loves
films.synopsis: Teresa (María Vázquez) is compelled to change her holiday plans to help her proudly independent mother (Adriana Ozores), who has had a fall. Mother and daughter will spend a stifling summer disagreeing on everything —but finding each other again.

films.title: Rioja, Land of a Thousand Wines + Wine Tasting (Sunday)
films.synopsis: Directed by multiple Goya award winner José Luis Lopez-Linares, this lip-smacking tour of Spain’s best known wine region dives into the push and pull between tradition and innovation in an industry that is led by family dynasties.

films.title: Teacher Who Promised the Sea
films.synopsis: Based on a true story, Patricia Font’s drama excavates a dark period in Spanish history. Antoni Benaiges takes up a village teaching position in 1935. But his new-fangled ideas about learning outrage the local priest.

films.title: Come Home My Child
films.synopsis: Filmed over ten years, Come Home, My Child narrates the American Dream through the lens of three women and their bond with prison inmates in America. Grandma Yang, Taiwanese, experienced the tragic loss of her son and husband, and for two decades has been corresponding with long-term prisoners. Mrs. Zheng, Chinese, works relentlessly to file an appeal for her son, serving an 84 sentence. Barbara Hust, American, suffers from multiple sclerosis disease. She teaches piano to bring comfort to the prisoners and herself. In English and Mandarin with English and Chinese subtitles.

films.title: Granny Must Die
films.synopsis: An absurd comedy about the daily life of a three-generational Hakka household in Taipei. Huichiao, her grandmother Chunmei, Chunmei’s son Fusang, and daughter-in-law Lichun live together in a three-generational household in Taipei. The story begins on a stormy night when Huichiao quietly approaches and kills the sleeping Chunmei: “Granny, just die!” In Mandarin, Hakka, and Taiwanese with English and Chinese subtitles.

films.title: Picnic
films.synopsis: After a surprise visit from her friend Geum-sun, Eunsim is headed to her hometown with Geum-sun for the first time in 60 years. There, she catches up with Taeho who had feelings for her when they were teenagers. Her long-lost memories come to life one by one and they decide to go for a picnic—after all, it may be their last...

films.title: Stand Up Story
films.synopsis: This gentle Hong Kong comedy drama teases humour out of hardship with heartfelt performances from the leads, while steering away from sentimentality.” “Siu-hin Ng and Ben Suen star as a graduate hoping to become a stand-up comedian, and his father who has a mild intellectual disability. This gentle Hong Kong comedy drama teases humour out of hardship with heartfelt performances from the leads, while steering away from sentimentality.” EDMUND LEE, SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST In Cantonese with English and Chinese subtitles.

films.title: Based on a True Story — Full Metal Jacket
films.synopsis: In our latest Film Studies series, filmmaker and educator Patricia Gruben—founder of the Praxis Centre for Screenwriters—unpacks different approaches to writing for the screen, focussing here on adaptation from literary sources. Stanley Kubrick’s war film is based on two sourc—Gustav Hasford’s novella The Short-Timers, which reads like a tortured diary of his dehumanizing stint as a military correspondent in Vietnam, and Dispatches, a nonfiction account by Michael Herr of his own trauma as a war journalist.

films.title: Hao Are You?
films.synopsis: In this emotional documentary, director Dieu Hao Do explores the fragmentation of his family. The American War in Vietnam scattered them across three continents. Nearly 50 years after their escape, contact between the seven family members has all but broken down. Dieu Hao Do visits relatives in Vietnam, Hong Kong, California and Germany. It's a road trip into the history of Vietnam after the withdrawal of the Americans: emotional, sobering, insightful, sad and uplifting. In German, Vietnamese, and Cantonese

films.title: Adapting Shakespeare — Throne of Blood
films.synopsis: Shakespeare’s primal conflicts have expanded into a cultural spectrum ranging from faithful British transcriptions to American musicals and Bollywood gangster dramas. Shakespeare himself adapted earlier sources to the social and political concerns of his day. Kurosawa’s 1957 epic homage to Macbeth draws on the style of Noh drama in place of Shakespeare’s language-based drama, while alluding to the Buddhist doctrine of impermanence. For contrast we’ll view clips from Vishal Bhardwaj’s Haider, an adaptation of Hamlet set in occupied Kashmir, and consider other international versions. Talk at 2pm. Screening 2.30pm

films.title: Interior Monologue — The Hours
films.synopsis: Virginia Woolf’s Mrs. Dalloway (1925) was a milestone in the development of stream of consciousness narrative; difficult to translate into cinema for obvious reasons. Working with playwright David Hare on the screenplay for Michael Cunningham’s novel The Hours, Stephen Daldry approaches the subject by focusing not on Woolf’s novel itself but on its impact; cycling through the last days of the author Woolf (Nicole Kidman), a desperate, devoted reader in the 1950s (Julianne Moore) and a contemporary literary agent (Meryl Streep). Talk at 2pm. Screening 2.30pm

films.title: Universal Language
films.synopsis: 2:00PM, 7:30PM FEB 4-10 ADDITIONAL SCREENINGS In a wintery, Farsi-speaking city that’s equal measures Winnipeg and Tehran, schoolchildren are tormented by cash encased in ice, a tour guide shepherds visitors to bizarre attractions, and Matthew Rankin (the film’s director) returns after enduring soul-crushing bureaucratic life in Quebec. As these storylines become comically entangled, the concepts of space, time, and identity grow increasingly opaque. Visually inventive and wantonly absurd, Rankin’s poetic fable reminds us that Winnipeg is a wonderland.

films.title: Adaptation, Innovation & Evolution — Pride & Prejudice
films.synopsis: Filmmaker and educator Patricia Gruben— founder of the Praxis Centre for Screenwriters —unpacks different approaches to writing for the screen, focussing here on adaptation from literary sources. In this six week course, combining 30-minute talks, clips, screenings and group discussion, Patricia examines how Jane Austen, Shakespeare, Virginia Woolf et al have been translated to the screen by the likes of Atom Egoyan, Kubrick and Kurosawa. Week 1: Joe Wright’s 2005 version of Pride and Prejudice is a prime example of the spunky updated heroine who gets both her man and her independence.

films.title: Feven Kidane & Tiny Pyramids Play the music of Sun Ra + Space is the Place film
films.synopsis: To celebrate the music of Sun Ra, two of Vancouver’s strongest creative voices join forces for a one-night only performance, along with a rare screening of the revolutionary 1974 Afro-Futurist film Space is the Place, featuring Sun Ra. For this show, legendary local trumpeter Feven Kidane will be collaborating with Tiny Pyramids, a group of interstellar travellers who perform the music of Sun Ra, featuring Dan Gaucher on drums, Colin Cowan on bass, Mary Ancheta on keyboards, and Tom Wherrett on guitar.

films.title: Broken Social Scene: It’s All Gonna Break
films.synopsis: Cited by Pitchfork as “one of the most important artists of the last 25 years”, Broken Social Scene is an unusual band, in that it began as a duo and mutated into a loose collective with as many as 19 regular or semi-regular contributors over the years. Also unusual: cameraman Stephen Chung was right there with them right from the start, picking up live shows, studio sessions, parties, hangouts, just because... It’s All Gonna Break is a candid record of BSS’s genesis and evolution from the turn of the millennium. What a Scene this was!

films.title: LIZA: A Truly Terrific Absolutely True Story
films.synopsis: Life is a cabaret, old chum... Certainly Liza Minnelli’s life fits the bill. The daughter of Judy Garland and director Vincent Minnelli, she was born into Hollywood royalty: Money, divorce, addiction, breakdown, ego... These were here birthrights, along with oodles of talent and the mentors to guide her. Pizzazz personified, she’s won Oscars, Tonys, Emmys and Grammys, worked her way through four husbands and multiple love affairs, done her share of drinking, but comes across here as more of a mensch than a diva.

films.title: To Kill a Mockingbird
films.synopsis: This is the first in a new regular series in which we invite our VIFF+ Premium Members to nominate a favourite movie to share. This month, Margot Pratt has chosen Robert Mulligan’s beloved film adaptation of Harper Lee’s novel To Kill a Mockingbird, the tale of a white lawyer, Atticus Finch, defending an innocent black man accused of rape in a small southern town in the 1930s. Margot says,”It’s a timeless film that hasn’t seen a big screen in years. The story is told through the memories of a 9 or 10-year old girl. Perfectly written, cast, shot... Everything!”

films.title: The Inheritance
films.synopsis: The inheritance is a house in Philadelphia bequeathed to Julian by his grandmother. He asks his girlfriend Gwen to move in, and next thing he knows there’s an entire collective, The House of Ubutu, a commune that will be a safe space for Black folk. On the wall, prominently, there is a poster for Godard’s La Chinoise, and this is clearly a key inspiration for writer-director Ephraim Asili. It’s heady but playful, a call to arms that resonates loud and clear. Celebrating Black Futures is copresented with the Vancouver Art Gallery and curated by Kika Memeh

films.title: Paying For It
films.synopsis: Talk about a hall of mirrors! Sook-Yin Lee adapts the graphic novel of the same name by her ex-boyfriend, Canadian cartoonist Chester Brown, about the end of their relationship in the early naughts and Brown’s subsequent decision to start paying for sex. Dan Beirne (The Twentieth Century) plays Brown, and he’s joined by a cast that includes Emily Lê (Riceboy Sleeps) as Sook-yin stand-in “Sonny”. The tone here is affectionately comedic, matter of fact, and sex positive, not salacious or leering; it may even have you reconsidering your views on sex work.

films.title: Mother of George
films.synopsis: Adenike and Ayodele are a Nigerian couple living in Brooklyn. Following the joyous celebration of their wedding, complications arise from their inability to conceive a child—a problem that devastates their family, defies cultural expectations, and leads Adenike to make a shocking decision. Director Andrew Dosumnu captures the nuances of this unique and fascinating culture by creating a beautiful, vibrant, and moving portrait of a couple whose joys and struggles are at once intimate and universal.

films.title: Mongrels
films.synopsis: “If you can catch and eat one hundred airplanes, you can make a wish come true...” Taking her mother’s whimsical notion to heart, Hana is determined to bring about the family reunion that will restore her happiness. Meanwhile older brother Hajoon seeks connection from his new Canadian peers while risking the fury of their angry, alienated dad, Sonny (Jae-Hyun Kim). Like Riceboy Sleeps, Jerome Yoo’s debut feature is a beguiling, introspective film looking back on the Korean immigrant experience, here split across three chapters, each with a distinct visual aesthetic. In English, and Korean

films.title: Play It Loud! How Toronto Got Soul
films.synopsis: Born in Montego Bay, Jay Douglas came to Canada as a teenager in the 1960s and brought reggae with him. As lead singer for The Cougars, he spearheaded Caribbean soul, ska and funk on the Toronto Yonge Street scene. Despite a voice to die for, dapper looks and charisma to spare, Canada wasn’t quite ready for Jay. It wasn’t until 2006 and hip-hop’s discovery of Wayne McGhie’s Dirty Funk that The Cougars found belated fame and respect. Still going strong, Jay proves the perfect guide to this joyful reclamation of Canadian soul and funk history. Special guests (Friday only): Jay Douglas and producer Andrew Munger

films.title: Brief Encounter
films.synopsis: Celia Johnson and Trevor Howard meet by chance at a railway station. Both are married and neither will stoop to impropriety. Yet there is an immediate attraction and a series of stolen lunch dates develops into one of the cinema’s most affecting love affairs. It’s not so far from Wong Kar-wai’s In the Mood for Love, with Rachmaninoff’s Piano Concerto No 2 in place of Nat King Cole. Considered one of the greatest British films ever made, the movie consolidated director David Lean’s growing reputation. “Lean’s sad, buttoned-up account of unconsummated love is about all of us and our cautious natures.”

films.title: Luther: Never Too Much
films.synopsis: 12:00PM, 8:45PM The dazzling but all too short career of singer-songwriter Luther Vandross gets revelatory reappraisal in Dawn Porter’s moving biographical documentary. The trailblazing soul artist was a titanic musical force in the 1980s and 90s, arranging and producing songs for David Bowie, Dionne Warwick and Mariah Carey, to name just a few. Drawn from roughly four decades of interview and performance footage, Luther restores the rightful reputation of an artist who couldn’t be appreciated on his own terms in his era.

films.title: Doctor Zhivago
films.synopsis: This Valentine Day, wrap yourself in David Lean’s epic, all-star adaptation of Boris Pasternak’s love story, set against the tumult of the Russian Revolution. With Maurice Jarre’s haunting score, Omar Sharif as the soulful doctor/poet, and Julie Christie as his soul-mate, this is unapologetically a decadent’s take on the Revolution. Adjusted for inflation, it remains one of the ten biggest box office movies ever made. Restored DCP. “It’s impossible not to swoon.”

films.title: Intercepted
films.synopsis: Of all the films to come out of the Ukraine over the past few years, this one stands out for its rigour, its visual restraint and eloquence, and the sheer horror it imparts. Director Oksana Karpovych juxtaposes shots of broken buildings, bombed out roads and bridges, scarred landscapes, with a soundtrack consisting of intercepted messages from Russian soldiers to their loved ones. In these uncensored phone calls, the men casually confess to (in some cases, boast of) widespread looting, murder and torture. Q&A with director Oksana Karpovych

films.title: Buster Keaton’s Sherlock Jr. with R.E.M.’s Monster and New Adventures in Hi Fi
films.synopsis: It didn’t take long for cinema to become self-reflexive. Buster Keaton’s Sherlock Jr anticipates post-modernism by decades. Buster plays a projectionist who dreams himself onto (and into) the movie screen, where he finds himself in high slapstick peril. The formal mastery here is dazzling and more than a century after the film’s release, audiences will be in gales of laughter. Hopefully none of them will end up on screen. This screening comes with a jukebox score from those indie rock dreamers REM, and specifically tracks from the albums Monster and New Adventures in Hi Fi. No Dialogue,

films.title: Les Enfants du Paradis
films.synopsis: Widely acknowledged as the crowning glory of classical French cinema, this sumptuous melodrama defies the Occupation stringencies under which it was made. Set in the early 19th century Boulevard du Crime, where popular audiences for mime shows and carnival rubbed shoulders

films.title: James and the Giant Peach
films.synopsis: Join us on Family Day for a classic family matinee with fun activities! Arrive early for bug antennae building, face painting, and peachy snacks before our noon screening. Forced to live with his cruel aunts, James finds a new life aboard an enormous, enchanted peach. Together with a group of friendly and caring insects who welcome him

films.title: Cure
films.synopsis: A string of shocking, seemingly unmotivated murders— each committed by a different person yet bearing the same grisly hallmarks—leads Detective Kenichi Takabe (Koji Yakusho) into a labyrinthine investigation to discover what connects them. Cure is a tour de force of psychological tension and a hallucinatory journey into the darkest recesses of the human mind. This month’s VIFF Premium member selection is a spellbinding thriller from Kiyoshi Kurosawa.

films.title: Parthenope
films.synopsis: Great beautician Paolo Sorrentino (The Hand of God; The Young Pope) returns to the city of his birth with this languorous, love-struck chronicle of the life of a modern day siren, Parthenope (newcomer Celeste Della Porta). Born in the ocean across the from the city which inspired her name, Parthe grows up a student of anthropology and so beautiful she’s courted by movie scouts and billionaires alike. Yet she navigates her own way... Unapologetically stylish, sensuous and philosophical, this is a deeply, insolently Italian movie. In Italian, Neapolitan, and English

films.title: Nickel Boys
films.synopsis: Nominated for Best Picture and Best Adapted Screenplay, Nickel Boys is the most radical big budget movie this side of Megalopolis. Making his dramatic feature debut, director RaMell Ross (Hale County, This Morning, This Evening) opts for a subjective camera throughout, albeit from complementary viewpoints, to convey the experiences of persecution and resistance at a racist Florida reform school. Adapted from Colson Whitehead's Pulitzer winning novel, itself inspired by a notorious instution in Florida.

films.title: Chez Jolie Coiffure
films.synopsis: Recruited by a Lebanese maid agency, Sabine leaves Cameroon and embarks for Lebanon. After many years of servitude, she escapes to Belgium, but her arrival there is complicated by the fact that she enters illegally. She settles in Matonge, the African quarter, where she becomes the manager of the beauty salon Chez Jolie Coiffure. The patrons here, many of them undocumented immigrants, are not only be made to feel beautiful but can also escape the daily difficulties and harsh realities of their lives.

films.title: Bam Bam: The Sister Nancy Story
films.synopsis: Dancehall queen Sister Nancy effortlessly carries this bright and buoyant music doc. You may not know Nancy’s name but her signature tune, “Bam Bam” enjoys the status of the most sampled reggae song of them all. (Janelle Monae is just one of the many stars who testifies to the fact.) It pops up all over hip hop, in movies, TV, commercials. Not that Sister Nancy received residuals until relatively recently. But mostly we’re impressed with this indefatigable star’s ceaseless energy, her compelling stage presence and personal integrity.

films.title: Dilli Dark
films.synopsis: African outsider Michael Okeke left Nigeria six years ago to survive in the frequently disconnecting and overcrowded New Delhi, which he despises heartily. He dreams of true love and a better job but is pushed into only the 4 C-s: cell phone, cocaine, cash, and clients.

films.title: The Stand
films.synopsis: Chris Auchter’s terrific doc explores a 1985 dispute over clearcut logging on Haida Gwaii. On one side are loggers, their bosses, and the BC government; on the other is the Haida Nation, which wishes to protect its traditional lands from

films.title: Atlantics
films.synopsis: Along the Atlantic coast, a soon-to-be-inaugurated futuristic tower looms over a suburb of Dakar. Ada, 17, is in love with Souleiman, a young construction worker. But she has been promised to another man. One night, Souleiman and his co-workers leave the country by sea, in hope of a better future. Several days later, a fire ruins Ada’s wedding and a mysterious fever starts to spread. Little does Ada know that Souleiman has returned. In English, French, and Wolof

films.title: There’s Still Tomorrow
films.synopsis: 3:00PM, 9:15PM MAR 10–16 ADDITIONAL SCREENINGS A critical and box office sensation in Italy, There’s Still Tomorrow looks back to yesteryear. It’s styled to evoke the neo-realist cinema of the 1940s, which is when this is set. Shot in monochrome and focussing on the labours of a working class wife and mother (writer-director Paola Cortellesi), the film at first plays as black comedy. But when Delia’s teen daughter announces she’s to be engaged the film turns to a more subtle register. By the end, we’re pletely immersed in the bitter emotional truths of this powerful feminist melodrama.

films.title: Housewife of the Year
films.synopsis: 1:00PM, 7:30PM 4:30PM, 8:15PM File under “What were we thinking?”. For nearly three decades, between 1967 and 1995, the women of Ireland competed on TV for the honour of Housewife of the Year (grand prize: a stove). Cooking abilities, keeping an orderly household, personality and hobbies, these were some of the attributes by which they were judged. Looking back on it now, many contestants are bewildered by who they used to be, but those were the times, and they were often hard. Ciarin Cassidy’s lovely doc says plenty while keeping mum. “Heartbreak and humour are in huge supply—the surreal archive footage takes care of the rest. Not to be missed. Four stars.” CHRIS WASSER, SUNDAY INDEPENDENT

films.title: The Way, My Way
films.synopsis: In recent times, all manner of pilgrims have flocked to France and Spain to walk the 800 km Camino de Santiago. One such is Bill, a stroppy Australian filmmaker several decades beyond his prime, who’s determined to do the Camino with minimal prep, a dickey leg, and no firm idea why. Not a doc, but a serio-comic recreation of Bill Bennett’s memoir, The Way, My Way was shot with a small crew and with the actual pilgrims Bill had walked

films.title: Transcript of a Tragedy – The Sweet Hereafter
films.synopsis: Atom Egoyan’s most admired film is based on Russell Banks’s novel of the same name, which in turn is based on the transcript of an inquest into a fatal school bus crash. Banks fictionalized the deadpan testimony of the original source into contradictory first-person accounts by survivors and witnesses to the accident. Egoyan refined this device and added an element of myth to deconstruct the narrative, leaving us wondering not which account is truest, but which will serve best to heal the community. Talk at 2pm. Screening 2.30pm

films.title: Santosh
films.synopsis: The feature debut by British-Indian writer-director Sandhya Suri, Santosh is a murder mystery that’s also an investigation into India’s social stratification, sexism, and corruption. When a 15 year old girl goes missing in a rural community near Lucknow, Utter Pradesh, the police are typically uninterested: the girl’s father is Dalit and illiterate, there is minimal chance of exacting a significant bribe. But female trainee officer Santosh (Shahana Goswami) feels differently, and when the corpse shows up there’s a new level of scrutiny...

films.title: 7 Beats per Minute
films.synopsis: While attempting a world record freedive in the Bahamas in 2018, Jessea Lu lost consciousness and stopped breathing for four minutes, forcing her to confront parts of her life and past she had long buried. Years later, Jessea returns to the site of her near-death experience, ready to dive again and become reborn. An amateur freediver herself, filmmaker Yuqi Kang gives us sublime images of the ocean depths and fascinating insights on the nature of the sport, the compulsions and trauma that drive Jessea.

films.title: The Untouchables
films.synopsis: Chicago. Treasury agent Eliot Ness (Kevin Costner) enlists Irish beat cop Jimmy Malone (Sean Connery) to school him in “the Chicago Way” so he can catch notorious gangster Al Capone (Robert De Niro). With a screenplay by David Mamet and a magnificect cast De Palma enjoyed one of his biggest hits with this oppulent, larger than life rendering of the Capone story. Ennio Morricone’s score certainly doesn’t hurt either (track titles include “Machine Gun Lullaby” and “The Strength of the Righteous”.

films.title: Days of Heaven
films.synopsis: Is this the most beautiful film of the seventies? Bathed in the amber light of the magic hour on the wheat fields of Alberta (it’s supposed to be Texas), it has a radiant glow; you could mount any frame on your wall. As in Badlands, Malick tells a sensational story—here a love triangle— through the oblique perspective of a child, collateral damage in this tale. In place of melodrama, he gives us an overwhelming, pure sense of loss. “One of the most beautiful films ever made.” ROGER EBERT WINNER Best Director, Cannes 1979; Best Cinematography, Academy Awards 1979

films.title: The Good, the Bad and the Ugly (Definitive Cut)
films.synopsis: Introduced by filmmaker and Sergio Leone-aficionado Devan Scott, this is the nearest you will get to the definitive director’s cut of the Italian’s 1966 masterpiece. The third and the best of the so-called ‘Dollars’ trilogy amplifies Leone’s baroque style: crane shots, shock cuts and Morricone music all vying for attention as three rogues hunt buried gold in a series of triangular variations. Morricone’s eclectic and innovative score is also integral to the film’s impact; flippant and ironic, but with an undertow of nostalgia and regret. “The best directed movie of all time.”

films.title: The Great Silence
films.synopsis: Simply and starkly a great movie, one of the most unforgettable westerns ever made anywhere. A mute gunfighter, Silenzio (Jean Louis Trintignant) circles the vicious bounty hunter Loco (Klaus Kinski) in the snowy mountains of Utah, a prolonged duel which culminates in an unforgettable showdown. As usual, Morricone’s score takes all this to another level, the icing on the proverbial cake. “It’s anarchic and rigorous, sophisticated and goofy, heartfelt and cynical. The score, by Ennio Morricone, is as mellow as wine.” AO SCOTT, NEW YORK TIMES

films.title: Once Upon a Time in the West
