films.synopsis: Casting iconic blue eyed-boy Henry Fonda as the bad guy, Leone simultaneously pays homage to a fistful of westerns and subverts them. With story credits for Bernardo Bertolucci and Dario Argento, both young turks at the time, this is a foundation myth writ large, one of the most imposing Scope films ever made. It’s also a real slow burn: Leone lays it out and bides his time, yet it’s not a minute too long. Morricone composed the score before filming and the actors performed the scenes while listening to the music, which set the film’s stately tempo.

films.title: Ennio
films.synopsis: Cinema Paradiso director Giuseppe Tornatore proves the perfect filmmaker to craft this loving tribute to one of the all-time greats: composer Ennio Morricone (1928-2020). Tornatore knew Morricone as a regular collaborator and a friend, and the film is built around a series of interviews they recorded together six or seven years ago. An extraordinary roster of talents testify to Morricone’s genius, but it’s his personal warmth and sensitivity that speaks loudest. Even at 2.5 hours the film barely scratches the surface of an immense career that stretched beyond 400 credits.

films.title: A Fistful of Dollars
films.synopsis: Leone’s first spaghetti western imported a US TV star (Clint Eastwood, from Rawhide) and brought a brazen cynicism to a story lifted from Akira Kurosawa’s samurai classic Yojimbo (1961): a mercenary gunfighter plays rival clans against each other and stands back as the town destroys itself. The film’s most revolutionary aspect was the score by Ennio Morricone, a wild cacophony of male chanting, Spanish guitar, whistling and bells. “A Fistful of Dollars has a cult, comic-book intensity. It is the punk rock of westerns.” PETER BRADSHAW, THE GUARDIAN

films.title: Dawn of Impressionism
films.synopsis: Everyone’s favourite art movement was assembled from a ragtag rabble of rejects and outsiders. Last year, the Musee d’Orsay and the National Gallery of Art in Washington DC recreated the 1974 exhibition where the artists (Monet, Cezanne, Renioir, Degas, Morisot among them) defiantly pitched their tent in opposition to the Academy’s all powerful Salon. The latest Exhibition on Screen film contextualizses this landmark show with correspondence and journal entries from artists, dealers and critics, and looks also at the turbulent history of the period.

films.title: Bang the Drum! A Live Set from the Kevin Romain Trio + Beware of Mr. Baker Film Screening
films.synopsis: Our latest VIFF Live presentation combines a jazz set led by drummer Kevin Romain followed by one of the most notorious music docs ever made, Jay Bulger’s bruising encounter with “the world’s greatest drummer,” Ginger Baker, of the 60s supergroup Cream. Kevin Romain is a drummer, improviser, composer, educator, bandleader and curator. For this performance, Romain will be joined by longtime collaborators Cole Schmidt (guitar) and Olive Shakur (bass), playing repertoire from the Ginger Baker Trio, which saw the iconic drummer team up with jazz legends Bill Frisell and Charlie Haden in the mid 1990s.

films.title: Eat the Night
films.synopsis: Apolline finds connection, excitement, and escape in the fantasy world of Darknoon, where her avatar strides about confidently in a medieval thong, wields a huge sword and rides a giant wolf. It’s a passion she shares

films.title: The Wild Bunch
films.synopsis: The Mexico/Texas borderlands, 1913: Pike (William Holden) leads his gang of aging outlaws on a foray south for one last hurrah, but the jig is nearly up and in their hearts they all know it. The Wild Bunch revolutionized the presentation of violence on screen, but it is also Peckinpah’s masterpiece, one of the great movies of the last 60 years. Before the bullets fly the film exerts a rueful, tender melancholy as the frontier passes into history, and in their death-throes, desperadoes and renegades like Pike must accept that they are yesterday’s men. Sunday’s Pantheon screening will feature a 20 minute introduction and talkback.

films.title: Crocodile Eyes
films.synopsis: For her 8th feature, Ingrid Veninger set out to make a film comprising 100 “real moments”. Drawing on what used to be called home movies and interactions with her immediate family, Veninger draws us into the challenge of creating structure. A mom and a daughter, she reflects on the cycle of birth and death: there is footage of her giving birth, and of her father’s last breath. If that’s too real for you, watch out! This is a film about momentous and mundane minutes, about the seemingly insatiable impulse to record, and the gift of memories, shared.

films.title: Incandescence
films.synopsis: Filmed across the Okanagan before, during and after several devastating fires by veteran non-fiction filmmakers Nova Ami and Velcrow Ripper (Metamorphosis; ScaredSacred), Incandescence is a mesmerizing cinematic contemplation of the power of wildfires, and also a philosophical rumination on loss and regeneration. The film marries stunning nature imagery with a chorus of disparate voices, including fire fighters and evacuees. While much of it is chastening, Incandescence holds out a sliver of solace in its apprehension of fire’s elemental core. Filmmaker Q&A, Fri 11 “As visually striking as it is thought-provoking, offering a compelling blend of education, storytelling, and immersive filmmaking.” CHRIS JONES, OVERLY HONEST REVIEWS

films.title: Sweet Summer Pow Wow
films.synopsis: After the local hit The Great Salish Heist, writer-director Darrell Dennis proves his versatility with this charming love story about two young people who meet cute on BC’s Pow Wow circuit. Jinny (Tatyana Rose Baptiste) is 17, beautiful, and destined for law school—according to her mom, Cara, who is Chief of the Coyote Lake Tribe. What Jinny really wants to do is dance. Then there’s Riley (Joshua Odjick), from the rival White Bluff Indian Reserve. Chief Cara knows he’s trouble from the moment she lays eyes on him... Filmmaker Q&A (Fri 11)

films.title: The Decline of the American Empire
films.synopsis: Friends from the History Department at the University of Montreal come together for a dinner party. While the men prepare the meal, the women work out at the gym. In both groups, the conversation returns repeatedly to sex... The Decline of the American Empire is recognized as one of the greatest of all Canadian films. A acute and funny erotic comedy of manners, the movie diagnoses how throughout history decadence and solipsism have typically been a precursor to social collapse. Denys Arcand’s Academy Award-winning sequel, The Barbarian Invasions, also shows at VIFF Centre this week.

films.title: The Players
films.synopsis: Stefani Kimber gives a remarkable, affecting performance as Emily, a talented teenager who joins an experimental theatre group led by the charismatic Reinhardt (Eric Johnson). She’s inspired to challenge herself, endures physically and mentally demanding exercises, and proves she’s not a kid anymore. But this rite of passage comes

films.title: Field Sketches
films.synopsis: “Not until we are lost do we find ourselves.” Thoreau’s observation reverberates through Carl Bessai’s plaintive mid-life crisis film. Vincent Gale plays Peter, a Vancouver architect trying to set up his own company in line

films.title: Village Keeper
films.synopsis: After the tragic loss of her husband, single mother Beverly-Jean struggles to bridge the emotional gap between herself and her children. Desperate to shelter them from a surge in gun violence, she takes it upon herself to cleanse the blood from crime scenes in her Toronto neighbourhood—a transformative act that impels her to examine the hidden wounds in her family’s own past. Karen Chapman’s sensitive debut feature delves into intergenerational trauma and the beauty of rediscovering life’s little joys.

films.title: On Becoming a Guinea Fowl
films.synopsis: When Shula returns home to Zambia and finds her uncle’s dead body on the roadside by a brothel, the last thing she wants is to mourn him. But as her aunties shame her into helping with the funeral rites, she and her cousins Nsansa and Bupe must grapple with their family’s sanctification of a man who caused great harm in his lifetime. Writer-director Rungano Nyoni (I Am Not a Witch) earned a Best Director prize in Un Certain Regard for her powerful, darkly comedic, absurdist sophomore feature. On Becoming a Guinea Fowl is the latest presentation in our rolling African Cinema Now series curated by the Akojo Collective.

films.title: My American Cousin
films.synopsis: Sandy Wilcox (Margaret Langrick) longs for adventure and a modicum of respect. Neither is readily available to a 12-year-old growing up in rural Penticton in the late 1950s. Enter Butch in a screaming red Cadillac. He’s 16 going on James Dean, a California runaway and about the most exciting thing to hit town since rock-n-roll. Sandy Wilson’s first feature—40 years young—is a genuine Canadian coming-of-age classic, evoking a more innocent time while also capturing the adolescent’s restless desire for change. Sandy Wilson Q&A

films.title: ScaredSacred
films.synopsis: In the wake of 9/11, BC filmmaker Velcrow Ripper (Incandescence) embarked on a form of pilgrimage, visiting ground zero in Manhattan and other sites of disaster and human calamity around the globe — war-torn Cambodia and Bosnia, Bhopal in India, Palestine, Afghanistan... A sobering itinerary, to be sure. But the artist’s mission was to seek out hope; to turn fear on its head and connect with what is truly sacred. Twenty years on, the world remains a scary and a fragile place, but the lessons Ripper took, from the Dalai Lama and others, are all the more precious. This screening is in honour of producer Tracey Friesen, who passed away in January. Filmmaker Q&A

films.title: Are We Done Now?
films.synopsis: Down River director Ben Immanuel (formerly Ben Ratner) returns with his third feature, a wry, self-aware Covid comedy in which a socially distant Vancouver documentarian checks in with a stressed-out therapist (Corner Gas star Gabrielle Miller) and several of her patients over the course of the pandemic. Although the tone is predominantly comedic, this framework allows Immanuel to take the temperature of the times and dig into contemporary obsessions and concerns: race, gender, sexuality, and of course mental health. Filmmakers in attendance Free Screening Free Screening

films.title: Heart of Gold
films.synopsis: Texas, 1969. Michael infuriates girlfriend Mary-Bob by accepting the draft to serve in Vietnam. But after a violent incident at boot camp, he deserts and escapes over the border to British Columbia. Here he finds shelter with a group of Russian dissidents, the Doukhobors. Meanwhile Mary-Bob becomes a militant anti-war activist... An original screenplay by director Patricia Gruben (who recently led our Film Studies series on literary adaptation), Heart of Gold examines an entire epoch by dramatizing the ethical quandaries of two young people faced with choices that will define their lives.

films.title: Biboye Onanuga Plays Monk + Thelonious Monk: Straight, No Chaser
films.synopsis: Returning to the VIFF stage, Biboye Onanuga, presents: ‘The Music of Monk’. The Edmonton-based drummer is joined by an iconoclastic ensemble of Vancouver musicians Quincy Mayes (piano), Jodi Proznick (bass), and John Nicholson (tenor) for an evening of Monk tunes and arrangements before the 1988 documentary Thelonious Monk: Straight, No Chaser. “I had heard the music before. What the film gave me was an opportunity to see Thelonious Monk creating some of it, and, just as importantly, an opportunity to see how those who knew him loved him.”

films.title: Grand Tour
films.synopsis: 1918. When a British civil servant stationed in Burma gets cold feet about his upcoming wedding, he promptly hops on a boat to Singapore—just the first stop in an unforgettable Asian “grand tour”. More bemused than angry, his fiancée resolves to follow him. In black and white and colour, mixing fiction and documentary, the latest from Miguel Gomes (Tabu) is at once a magisterial continental travelogue, a probing examination of colonialism and a time-warping journey into the history of cinema itself. In Portuguese, Chinese, Thai, French, Burmese, Vietnamese, Filipino, and Japanese

films.title: Misericordia
films.synopsis: APR 2-7 ADDITIONAL SCREENINGS VC/LOC A twisted tale of seduction from Stranger By the Lake director Alain Giraudie. Returning to beautiful Saint-Martial for the funeral of his former boss, Jérémie (Félix Kysyl) arouses widow Martine (Catherine Frot), her son Vincent (Jean-Baptiste Durand), and other local characters— each in a different way. Edgy, eccentric, and unapologetically queer, Misericordia straddles the line between comedy and thriller. It’s a fresh, darkly amusing take on human desire.

films.title: The Teacher
films.synopsis: The first feature from Farah Nabulsi is a potent thriller about an English teacher, Basem (Saleh Bakri) charting a course of smart resistance to Israeli occupiers. (The background here is very similar to the picture painted in the Oscar-winning documentary No Other Land). In a horrifying turn of events, Basem witnesses the murder of a teenager by a settler. While the subsequent investigation rolls slowly towards a foregone conclusion, the teacher is caught up in a parallel kidnapping case... In Arabic, English, and Hebrew

films.title: The Encampments
films.synopsis: 4:20PM, 8:45PM Few documentaries are more timely than this fasttracked account of the Columbia student Gaza protests. At the centre of this story is student activist Mahmoud Kahlil, who hit the headlines just last month after he was detained by ICE and who is fighting a deportation order. Another prominent character in the film, Grant Miner, who is Jewish, was recently expelled by Columbia. At a time when the right to free speech is policed with such rigour, The Encampments provides an opportunity to hear what the protestors have to say.

films.title: The Hermit of Treig
films.synopsis: In this rather special film, Lizzie MacKenzie trains her camera on octogenarian Ken Smith, who has lived more than four decades off-the-grid on the shores of Loch Treig, in the Scottish Highlands. This cheerful hermit is a personable storyteller and you can sense the warm bond that is forged between the filmmaker and her unusual subject. “When a film-maker is clearly captivated by their subject, the film can compel viewers to fall in love as well.” PHUONG LE, THE GUARDIAN

films.title: Mambar Pierrette
films.synopsis: The third and final film of the spring session of African Cinema Now! is the first dramatic feature from Cameroonian non-fiction filmmaker Rosine Mbakam (Chez Jolie Coiffure). Mbakam presents a glimpse into the daily life of her cousin, Mambar Pierrette. A quiet but persistent journey through the city of Douala, Cameroon, invites us into the goings-on of Pierrette’s life. Moving through joy and disaster, we are able to quietly follow a film invested in the quotidian pleasures and worries of life as a woman. “An original filmmaker of exquisite sensibility; one of the foremost filmmakers of creative nonfiction working right now.” RICHARD BRODY, THE NEW YORKER In Bamileke, French, and Pidgin

films.title: Our Lady of the Nile
films.synopsis: Rwanda, 1973. Veronica and Virginia are inseparable friends at an elite Catholic boarding school, Our Lady of the Nile, but what binds them together is the very thing that separates them forever. Months before graduation, the students’ lives are rocked by the venomous atmosphere that clouds the country. What comes first, sisterhood or politics? Screening in our African Cinema Now series curated by the Akojo Collective “A heart-breaking look at the corruption of innocence.” ORLA SMITH, SEVENTH ROW

films.title: Shepherds
films.synopsis: Advertising man Mathyas (Félix-Antoine Duval) quits his job in Montreal with the romantic notion of becoming a shepherd in the French Alps. Of course the reality is less bucolic than he imagines: hunger, loneliness, wolves... And yet, and yet, , there is life on the Alps, and love too.... Based on a true story, Sophie Deraspe’s follow up to Antigone (2019) effectively plays spiritual uplift offagainst some 3000 sheep, one donkey, assorted hens, goats, and several valiant dogs. “Majesterial... as rejuvenating to watch as the effect of being in nature.” STEPHEN SAITO, THE MOVEABLE FEAST

films.title: Bob Trevino Likes It
films.synopsis: John Leguizamo has a peach of a role in this touching crowd-pleaser inspired by writer-director Traciey Laymon’s own experience. “Lily Trevino” (Barbie Ferreira) is a young woman in her 20s saddled with a toxic, narcissistic dad, Robert (French Stewart). After a fight, he cuts her out of his life. Then lonely Lily looks him up on Facebook and happens across Bob Trevino (Leguizamo), a gentle, genial contractor who happens to live nearby, and who turns out to be an altogether better dad... “A celebration of friendship, and the small acts of everyday kindness that have their own redemptive power.”

films.title: Janis Ian: Breaking Silence
films.synopsis: In the mid-60s, Janis Ian, a tiny teenage Jewish singer-songwriter from New Jersey, scores a controversial hit single called Society’s Child, about an interracial love relationship. The song launches her illustrious career but also ignites death threats, plunging her into an emotional tailspin—only to emerge from the ashes in the 1970s with an even bigger hit, At Seventeen. Janis overcomes embezzlement, record industry misogyny, and heartbreak to find love and produce an indelible body of searingly honest songs.

films.title: Secret Mall Apartment
films.synopsis: 2:30PM, 9:00PM In 2003, Michael Townsend and several of his friends created one of the most original guerilla art projects of the 21st century: they built and furnished a hidden 750 sq. foot apartment inside the Providence Mall in Rhode Island, remaining undetected for four years. Secret Mall Apartment strikes a balancing act between the absurdity of its story and surprisingly profound questions about gentrification, the nature of social art, and what truly makes a home.

films.title: Our Blue World: A Water Odyssey Earth Day
films.synopsis: Connecting ancient wisdom with practical 21st century solutions, Our Blue World is a spectacular and eye-opening film about our deepest and most precious resource. As anthropologist Wade Davis points out, every culture holds water sacred. Ecologist and philosopher Li An Phoa experienced an epiphany drinking water directly from the Rupert River in northern Quebec... She now campaigns to (re-)create drinkable rivers all over the world. The film takes us to the Mississippi, to Cambodia, Europe, Burundi, China and Peru. Join us Tuesday, April 22 (Earth Day) for a post-screening discussion with author and anthropologist Wade Davis, Paul O’Callaghan (BlueTech Research, producer, Our Blue World) and others.

films.title: The Lunchbox
films.synopsis: Aimed at film lovers 55+, our new Talking Pictures series offers audience-friendly festival films, refreshments, and an open invitation to chat about our shared experience of the movie. Our first presentation is a modern classic rom-com from India. Irfan Khan is the lonely office worker who is delighted and perplexed to receive an unexpected lunch every day—no matter that it was meant for someone else. A correspondence develops, and with it, feelings both parties had almost put behind them... “One thing that makes Lunchbox so strong is that a touch of melancholy hangs over its sweetness. Finally this is a film about the wheel of life, about what helps us cope

films.title: Scarface Introduced by Michael van den Bos
films.synopsis: Along with Warner Brothers’ Little Caesar and Public Enemy, the independently-produced Scarface was the most violent film of the era. All were big hits. Paul Muni stars as the low level gangster with ambitions for greater things. In his pre-screening talk, Michael gives an overview of the genre conventions established in the early gangster movies and examines director Howard Hawks’s stylish and symbolic-laced cinematic presentation, an outlier in his filmography as a whole. Intro 2pm; Film: 2.30 “Its seminal importance in the early gangster movie cycle outweighed only by its still exhilarating brilliance”

films.title: Zappostrophe + Frank Zappa’s 200 Motels
films.synopsis: A prodigious and prolific talent, Zappa (1940-1993) composed, recorded and produced more than 60 albums; music that brought to rock the complexity and sophistication of classical composition, drawing on jazz, blues, pop and music concrete, but leavened with a surreal and satiric wit. Enjoy an electrifying set of Zappa tunes resurrected and reimagined by the eclectic 8-piece band Zappostrophe, followed by a rare screening of Zappa’s cult movie 200 Motels, with Keith Moon and Ringo Starr. ”Zappostrophe dares to take on Zappa’s weird and wonderful world—recreating his tunes with jaw-dropping musicianship, and a wink to his irreverent humour.” CHEK TV Talking Pictures

films.title: Rose
films.synopsis: Veteran French actress Françoise Fabian (My Night at Maud’s; Belle de Jour; Out 1) enjoys a luminous late role in this touching first feature by singer, songwriter Aurélie Saada. Fabian’s Parisienne Rose — an Orthodox Jew — is widowed after a long and happy marriage. Initially she turns recluse in her grief, but this is a film about re-awakening; rediscovering your lust for life in old age. “A feature steeped in love.”

films.title: Marcella
films.synopsis: Marcella Hazan taught North Americans that there was more to Italian food than pizza and meatballs. She wrote what remains the definitive book on the subject (Essentials of Classic Italian Cooking) and her tomato sauce is second to nonna. A science teacher in Italy who had never cooked before her marriage, to Victor Hazan, a Sephardic Jew who brought her to New York, she made it her mission to revive the flavours and traditions she remembered from her youth. Italian cooking is simple, she insisted. But it isn’t easy. This is her story.

films.title: They Say I’m Different: Mary Ancheta plays Betty Davis (live music + film)
films.synopsis: If you don’t know the Betty Davis, prepare to be blown away. With her deep, raw, earthy voice, a knack for stringing together funky riffs, and her sexually super-charged lyrics, Davis shook and shocked American soul in the early 70s. As her husband Miles Davis said: “She was Madonna before Madonna, Prince before Prince.” In this VIFF Live event, keyboardist Mary Ancheta and her band channel Davis’ funkiest tunes, featuring Dawn Pemberton on vocals. The live music portion of the event will be followed by a rare screening of Phil Cox’s invaluable 2017 documentary.

films.title: Kryptic
films.synopsis: Kourtney Roy’s fascinating feminist (?) horror movie —shot in and around Hope, BC—feints toward creature-feature quirk, but its oddity morphs into something altogether stranger, slipping and sliding across fixed identities like a David Lynch movie, purposefully pitching us into a cosmic space beyond sat nav, where our coordinates have been scrambled. It gets murkier, muckier, yuckier... Roy does not hold back! Oozing psycho-sexual anxiety, Kryptic is awkward, erotic, scary and exciting, just like the real thing. Friday May 9, join us for KRYPTIC LIVE a one-time-only screening live scored by composer Cayne Mackenzie + Q&A with director Kourtney Roy

films.title: Sabbath Queen
films.synopsis: The dynastic heir of 38 generations of Orthodox rabbis, including the Chief Rabbis of Israel, Amichai Lau-Lavie is what you might call the black sheep of the family. Certainly his queer identity has led him down a different path: an activist with the Radical Faeries in New York City, he hit upon a provocative drag act alter ego—Rebbetzin Hadassah Gross—and cofounded a “God-optional” Jewish sect with Lab/Shul. Yet Amichai’s journey, filmed across 21 years, has more twists in store... “Enthralling. It is one of the best films I’ve seen this year.” HOLLYWOOD REPORTER In English, Hebrew, and Yiddish

films.title: One to One: John and Yoko
films.synopsis: Both a concert film (Madison Square Gardens, August 1972) and a time machine, dropping us into the dizzying political kaleidoscope of the early 1970s, Kevin Macdonald’s latest documentary is a rewarding addition to Lennon Studies, illuminating a fractious point in his career shortly after the Beatles bust up, and in the midst of his activist phase. Yoko Ono is an equal point of fascination here. Their idealism and commitment remains inspiring and the concert synthesizes much of what is best about their union.

films.title: The Penguin Lessons
films.synopsis: Steve Coogan nails a juicy role in the true story of an English teacher in 70s Argentina who reluctantly p-p-picked up a penguin. Full Monty director Peter Cattaneo deftly conveys the contrast between a country in turmoil and the gated tedium of life in a boarding school for the upper classes. Cynical English teacher Tom Michell rescues the penguin from an oil slicked beach, but his new friend is stickier than he looks. It’s an appealing mixture of pathos and comedy, and a timely parable of resistance.

films.title: Steel Magnolias
films.synopsis: Oh momma! In a Louisiana parish, Shelby Eatenton (Julia Roberts) is getting married and, soon enough, getting pregnant. But this great news comes with considerable risk, due to her type 1 diabetes. Shelby’s mother M’Lynn (Sally Field) is terrified of losing her. Fortunately they have an extensive support group ready to offer advice, hugs and wisecracks: Louisa, Truvy, Annelle, Clairee (Shirley MacLaine, Dolly Parton, Daryl Hannah, Olympia Dukakis).

films.title: Terms of Endearment
films.synopsis: Spanning three decades in the lives of Aurora Greenway (Shirley MacLaine) and her daughter Emma (Debra Winger), the film chronicles the ups and downs of their romantic liaisons (Emma makes the mistake of marrying someone called Flap; Aurora dates an astronaut named Garrett Breedlove) as well as their own love-hate dynamic. You’ll laugh, you’ll cry, you’ll give your mom an extra hug. Winner: 5 Academy Awards including Best Picture, Best Actress (Shirley MacLaine), Supporting Actor (Jack Nicholson), Best Director, and Adapted Screenplay.

films.title: Freaks
films.synopsis: Beautiful circus trapeze artiste Cleopatra likes to flirt with one of the sideshow attractions, Hans, a dwarf — much to the dismay of his fiancee, Frieda. When Cleopatra learns that Hans is a wealthy man, she decides to marry him. It’s a choice she will live to regret… “Give me something that will out-horror Frankenstein,” MGM production chief Irving Thalberg demanded of his leading genre stylist, Tod Browning (Dracula). But he was not ready for what Browning wrought. One of the most shocking films to come out of the studio system, Freaks was a financial failure in 1932, but became a cult favourite decades later, and is now widely regarded as a masterpiece. It was decades ahead of its time, and it still packs a punch. In the pre-screening presentation, Michael van den Bos examines why and how this freak of an MGM film was made, its horror elements, the controversy it generated and director Browning’s visual approach.

films.title: Gloria
films.synopsis: Gena Rowlands was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Actress for her portrait of gangster's moll Gloria Swenson: a tough, chain-smoking broad who's run with the mob all her life, but now finds herself running from it to protect her next door neighbour's orphaned six-yearold kid. And she hates kids. This one especially. It's a gift of a part and Rowlands eats it up. Winner of the Golden Lion at the Venice Film Festival, this is Cassavetes' most accessible and entertaining movie.

films.title: Balloon
films.synopsis: The two little sons of virile Tibetan shepherd Dargye mistake their parents’ condoms for balloons. Their mother, Drolkar, puts up with her husband’s robust sex drive. Drolkar’s sister, an enigmatic nun, visits while Dargye is looking for a ram to impregnate his flock of ewes. Balloon is fascinated with ideas of potency, pregnancy, and the possibilities for female autonomy in a patriarchal traditional Tibetan family. The dead, the reincarnated, and the living interweave while this family’s world slowly catches emotional fire.

films.title: The Sacred Arrow
films.synopsis: A fascinating departure from Pema Tseden’s usual style, this experiment in commercial ethnic cinema is a fullblown, gorgeously shot, widescreen modern fable with professional actors and a largely Chinese crew. Handsome Nyima and brooding Dradon are two ace archers from rival villages who vie in an annual contest for the ultimate prize, the Sacred Arrow. The Sacred Arrow offers something like a utopian vision of how Tibetan culture might thrive, revivifying the strength of its roots to face the future.

films.title: Tharlo
films.synopsis: In Pema Tseden’s most sublime film, Tharlo is a Tibetan shepherd with a phenomenal memory. Needing to wash his long, braided hair for his ID photo, Tharlo meets beautiful hairstylist Yangtso, who takes him out for a wild and disorienting night on the town. Highlighted by DP Lu Songye’s mesmerizing black-and-white long takes, this fable about the agonizing clash of two Tibetan cultures—traditional and contemporary, pastoral and urban—is a penetrating psychosexual study of masculinity in crisis, and a riveting exploration of social change.

films.title: Old Dog
films.synopsis: An elderly Tibetan shepherd lives with his son Gonbo and Gonbo’s wife, Rikso. They own an old Tibetan mastiff, a sheepdog whose breed has become a prized possession for Chinese buyers. Their own old dog is sold, recovered, resold, stolen, and recovered again, passing through the hands of a Chinese dealer, the local police, and Tibetan dog rustlers. In what may be Pema Tseden’s darkest film, crises of identity and masculinity collide as vultures circle overhead.

films.title: The Silent Holy Stones
films.synopsis: In Pema Tseden’s first feature, a very young Tibetan lama living in a monastery in Qinghai discovers the delights of binge-watching a Chinese TV serial, The Tansen Lama. He shuttles between watching the shows at home and in his monastery with his friend the Tulku (a seven-year-old living Buddha), and attends—and hilariously, interrupts—a live traditional Tibetan opera. The little monk starts to explore various parts of his identity, as he’s pulled by traditional and contemporary society, by folk opera and modern media, by a life apart from and one that flows through the secular world.

films.title: Jinpa
films.synopsis: Produced by Wong Kar-wai, Pema Tseden’s offbeat fable is part road movie, part Tibetan western. Two men named Jinpa meet on a mountain road in the Kekexili highlands near Tibet. One Jinpa, never without his sunglasses, is a truck driver (and Neapolitan song fancier), upset he has struck and killed a sheep. He picks up the other, brooding, Jinpa, who announces he is on a search for the killer of his father. Eventually the two men’s stories, dreams, and fates intertwine, as weighty moral questions of karma and compassion hang in the balance.

films.title: Snow Leopard
films.synopsis: The last film Pema Tseden finished before his death at age 53 is an enthralling, semi-mystical fable about the deep spiritual connection between a young Tibetan priest and a snow leopard. This rare animal has killed nine rams belonging to the monk’s brother, Jinpa, who threatens to kill it unless he receives compensation. Local officials and the police try to mediate, leading to a tense standoff, as tensions between state power, traditional ways of life, contemporary media, and migrating souls play out in ways both troubling and deeply moving.

films.title: The Search
films.synopsis: The Search is a road movie wrapped around three love stories. A director and crew are looking for local cast to star in their film version of the classic Tibetan opera Prince Drime Kundun. They encounter a woman who agrees to play the prince’ wife, Mande Zangmo, only if the crew helps her to find her ex-lover. Along the way, a businessman companion recounts his own sad love story. Shot in exquisite long takes, this brilliant film explores how stories can be told and how love can be articulated, in a culture whose traditions are under great stress.

films.title: Magic Farm
films.synopsis: For 85 years, Blue Note Records has been the gold standard for recorded jazz music all over the world,

films.title: Close-Knit
films.synopsis: A young girl, Tomo, unexpectedly finds herself living with her uncle and his transgender partner, a woman named Tetsu. The unconventional family arrangement serves as a backdrop for exploring the challenges and joys of living authentically. Taking a gentle approach to serious topics, the film does not sensationalize the struggles faced by transgender individuals or the complexities of non-traditional family structures. Instead, it promotes an atmosphere of warmth and acceptance, and makes for a thoughtful viewing experience. “One might find the tremendous emotional swells of Close-Knit so moving at times that one can barely hear the sound of fresh ground being broken in Japanese cinema.” RORY O’CONNOR, THE FILM STAGE

films.title: Hedwig and the Angry Inch + The Human Voice
films.synopsis: John Cameron Mitchell’s groundbreaking queer film unflinchingly explores themes of love, identity, and the struggle for acceptance through the lens of a rock musical. Hedwig (Mitchell) is a gender-queer punk rock singer from East Berlin who develops a relationship with a younger man, Tommy, becoming his mentor and musical collaborator, only to have Tommy steal her music and become a rock star. The film follows Hedwig and her backing band, the Angry Inch, as they shadow Tommy’s tour, while exploring Hedwig’s past through song and flashback.

films.title: Fire
films.synopsis: In the realm of Indian cinema, few films have dared tackle the intricacies of desire within the constraints of tradition quite like Deepa Mehta’s Fire. Two women, Sadiya and Radha, played with nuance and depth by Shabana Azmi and Nandita Das, find solace and love in spite of the oppressive patriarchal confines of their lives. The film’s presentation of their emotional and sexual awakening is both tender and tumultuous; the use of fire as a motif symbolizes both the destructive and transformative power of love. “Funny, poignant, and sensual, Fire is a beautiful, painful experience.” GUINEVERE TURNER, THE ADVOCATE

films.title: Moonlight + Strange Way of Life
films.synopsis: Three chapters in the life of Chiron, a young black man grappling with his identity and sexuality in a rough Miami neighborhood. The film beautifully captures the complexities of coming of age as Chiron navigates his childhood, adolescence, and adulthood, intertwined

films.title: Vulcanizadora
films.synopsis: Based on his screen personality in a string of edgy self-directed indie comedies (including Buzzard and Ape), you might want to keep Joel Potrykus at arm’s length. He’s one of those men for whom adolescence remains a high water mark. Here he is again, walking into the woods with his mournful sidekick (the ever arresting Joshe Burge) on a mission to unleash fireworks and fulfill a secret pact. (A secret to us, at any rate.) The movie is artfully paced, always intriguing, and packs a surprising punch. “Spasmodically funny, though hardly a comedy, Vulcanizadora is raw, moving and, briefly, horrifying.” JEANNETTE CATSOULIS, NEW YORK TIMES

films.title: The True Story of Tamara De Lempicka & The Art of Survival
films.synopsis: If Art Deco had a face, it was surely Tamara De Lempicka, giving us the side-eye at the wheel of a green Bugati in her famous self-portrait. Julie Rubio’s documentary traces her tumultuous life and times: born to a wealthy Jewish family in Poland, she married a Russian aristocrat who lost everything in the Revolution. They fled to Paris, where Tamara made a name for herself as an artist and as a hedonist. Rubio’s invaluable doc teases out the truths behind the myths, shedding light De Lempicka’s still underrated art.

films.title: Finding Dory
films.synopsis: Join us for VIFF Kids Club—our monthly family matinee series with film-inspired crafts and special concession snacks before the show! Doors open at 11 am for activities, with the film screening at 12 noon. By popular request: Finding Dory follows everyone’s favorite forgetful blue tang as she sets out to reunite with her family in this fun, heartfelt adventure. Alongside Nemo and Marlin and a few new friends, Dory dives back into the stunning underwater world we all love, discovering the true meaning of family along the way.

films.title: Karaoke
films.synopsis: Talking Pictures offers audience-friendly festival films, refreshments, and an open invitation to chat about our shared experience of the movie. Tickets $10 (2-for-$16). Meir (Sasson Gabay) is slumping towards retirement and no longer has any fight in him. When the new guy in the penthouse suite double parks in front of Meir’s car, well, it just sums up the kind of day/week/life he’s having. But Itsik (Lior Ashkenazi) apologizes profusely and insists Meir and his wife Tova (Rita Shukrun) come up for a glass of wine. Turns out Itsik isn’t just rich and successful, he’s also charming and gregarious. Under the bright wattage of his attentive smile, Meir and Tova start to feel better about themselves and imagine a new chapter is possible.

films.title: Nechako: It Will Be a Big River Again
films.synopsis: “Nechako” literally means “Big River”. But this artery for the Stellat’en First Nation in BC was drastically and dramatically diminished by the imposition of the Kenney Dam in the 1950s, which diverted 70% of the flow into an artificial reservoir. Back then the Stellat’en and their neighbours the Saik’uz weren’t even allowed to hire lawyers to fight their case. But their struggle for justice continues all these decades later. Stellat’en filmmaker Lyana Patrick communicates what’s at issue legally, but also environmentally, which is to say culturally and spiritually.

films.title: Fairy Creek
films.synopsis: Considered the largest act of civil disobedience in Canadian history, the Fairy Creek blockade led to more than 1200 arrests. What Jen Muranetz’s film gives us is the story from the front line from the activists’ point of view (often, from the treetops), a searing sense of anger at the costly RCMP response, and sadness that so much has already been lost. The film also acknowledges the complexity of the situation at Fairy Creek, where the Pacheedaht First Nation’s tribal council had an agreement with Teal Jones lumber corporation. “A necessary film for those believing they’re fighting the good fight to consider their actions and motivations.” RACHEL HO, POV MAGAZINE

films.title: The Wedding Banquet
films.synopsis: Co-written by James Schamus, this pleasing and lively update on Ang Lee’s 1993 gay closet comedy transplants the story to contemporary Seattle and the Korean-American community (actually it was shot in Vancouver) . Of course attitudes have changed in the intervening 30 years, so this is anything but a straight remake: Schamus and Ahn (Fire Island) shuffle the pack with ingenuity and and intention, adding a second queer couple and doubling complications. Laughs flow thick and fast and you can tell that Ahn really likes his characters.

films.title: On Swift Horses
films.synopsis: In this elegant queer melodrama, Muriel (Daisy Edgar-Jones) and her husband Lee (Will Poulter) are beginning a bright new life in California when he returns from the Korean War. But their newfound stability is upended by the arrival of Lee’s charismatic brother, Julius (Jacob Elordi), a wayward gambler with a secret past. A dangerous love triangle quickly forms. When Julius takes off in search of the young card cheat he’s fallen for, Muriel’s longing for something more propels her into a secret life of her own. “On Swift Horses presents a potent picture of the faultlines simmering below the American surface.” MARJORIE BAUMGARTEN, AUSTIN CHRONICLE

films.title: Love
films.synopsis: Dag Johan Haugerud has a lot on his mind. His “Oslo Trilogy” (Sex—which played at VIFF last year—and Dreams are coming soon) puts us all the couch to examine social and psychological attitudes towards romantic and physical attachment in our time. It’s an ambitious agenda, but also rich terrain for comedy, pathos, and philosophy—and that’s what he delivers in Love, which trains a quizzical eye on the trysts of a female doctor, Marianne, and her colleague, a gay male nurse, Tor.

films.title: Beautiful Evening, Beautiful Day
films.synopsis: 1957, Yugoslavia. A hero of the Resistance, Lavro (Dado Cosic) is now a filmmaker, and engaged in a more subtle war with the Communist regime’s draconian crackdown on dissidents and homosexuals. The government’s network of spies and informers is an amorphous enemy, and he and his friends are in constant danger of denunciation. Shot in black and white, Ivona Juka’s powerful drama reminds us how insidiously Orwellian propaganda tactics normalize repression, as brutality breeds fear and subservience. It’s a compelling history lesson, conveyed with passionate conviction.

films.title: Tornado
films.synopsis: Tornado begins in the middle then twists back around on itself. "Tornado" is also the name of the young heroine, fleeing for her life across the Scottish Highlands from a crew of bloodthirsty brigands led by Tim Roth. Add in that she is a featured player with a traveling circus, in which she and her father (Shōgun star Takehiro Hira) have a puppet-samurai act. John Mclean's second movie (after Slow West) is a heady brew, and the film doesn't let up for 91 swift and swirling minutes.

films.title: Two Women
films.synopsis: Violette (Laurence Leboeuf) and Florence (Karine Gonthier-Hyndman) are neighbours in a Montreal apartment complex. Both are married. Neither is getting the attention they crave from their respective spouses. Benoit (Felix Moati) is having an affair with a colleague (Juliette Gariépy). David (Mani Soleymanou) just isn't feeling it. Fortunately for our heroines, there are many more fish in the sea... Two Women just wants to show us a good time and score some points about women's sexuality along the way. This it effortlessly accomplishes.

films.title: Night on Earth
films.synopsis: Five cities. Five taxicabs. A multitude of strangers in the night. Jim Jarmusch assembled an extraordinary international cast of actors (including Gena Rowlands as a casting director taken for a ride by Winona Ryder) for this amusing quintet of tales of urban displacement and existential angst, spanning time zones, continents, and languages. Jarmusch’s lovingly askew view of humanity from the passenger seat makes for one of his most charming and beloved films. The movie comes with a big bonus: a score by Tom Waits.

films.title: Another Woman
films.synopsis: the philosophy department, no less) on sabbatical to write a book. She rents an apartment for this purpose, but finds that she can hear sessions from the psychologist’s office next door. In particular, she’s drawn to the reflections of Hope (Mia Farrow), a woman whose crisis has Marion reevaluating her own rigorously disciplined emotional life. What she discovers about herself is deeply unsettling. “Rowlands’ perfectly pitched approach to a demanding role is particularly stunning.” COLETTE MAUDE, TIME OUT

films.title: Lust, Caution
films.synopsis: Each month we showcase a movie selected by one of our VIFF+ Premium members. This month, Shanwen Yan chooses Ang Lee’s 2007 drama, his first film after Brokeback Mountain. Based on a short story by Eileen Change, it’s a classic spy thriller set in Hong Kong in 1938. Tang Wei stars as an idealistic drama student, Chia Chi, who is recruited to set up a Japanese official, Yee (Tony Leung) for assassination. The first ploy narrowly fails, but four years later in Japanese-occupied Shanghai a second opportunity presents itself. She seduces Yee, but their affair gets out of hand... In Mandarin, Japanese, English, Shanghainese, Hindi, and Cantonese

films.title: Super Happy Forever
films.synopsis: Kohei Igarashi’s mysterious and beguiling film follows Sano (Hiroshi Sano) as he returns to the seaside town where he met his wife Nagi (Nairu Yamamoto) five years ago. Nagi is now deceased, and it quickly becomes clear that the return to the town is part of Sano’s attempt to process his grief. In the last third, the filmmaker flips the script to show us Nagi’s meeting with Sano. “Thoroughly moving and decidedly delicate, the film is a major work of emotionally charged, poetic existentialism, and a beautiful tribute to the enigmatic experience of being in love.” MATTHEW JOSEPH JENNER, INTERNATIONAL CINEPHILE SOCIETY

films.title: Shall We Dance?
films.synopsis: Shohei (Koji Yakusho) seems to have it all: a high-paying job, a beautiful home and loving family. However, something is missing. One day on the train he spots a beautiful woman staring out a window and eventually decides to find her. His search propels him into the furtive world of... ballroom dancing. ‘’Dance is more than just the steps,’’ counsels a kindly teacher. ‘’Feel the music and dance for sheer joy.’’ And Shohei does just that, finding a new lease of life in tripping the light fantastic. Masayuki Suo’s delightful and charming film was a box office smash and won 14 Japanese Academy Awards including Best Film. “Funny and poignant, this is entertainment in it’s kindest and swishiest form.” IAN FREER, EMPIRE

films.title: The Other
films.synopsis: Filmed from 2017–2024, including post October 7th and during the subsequent war, The Other focuses on Israeli and Palestinian peace-builders, anti-occupation activists, artists, academics, ex-fighters, bereaved parents and many more living the reality on the ground. Joy Sela’s documentary is an inspiring testament to how human beings—even in the worst circumstances—can transcend difference to forge connection and understanding. In Hebrew and Arabic with English subtitles. FRI 20 JUN, 2:00PM FRI 13 JUN, 1:30PM

films.title: Chen Baker play J-Pop + Sumo Do, Sumo Don’t
films.synopsis: After selling out multiple venues across Vancouver, Jeffery’s Chen Baker band is back (and bigger than ever) to present a set of city pop and jazzy J-pop before the screening of the hilarious underdog comedy Sumo Do, Sumo Don’t (1992), winner of five Japanese Academy Awards and the inspiration for the recent Disney+ series of the same name. Featuring an ensemble seasoned gigging musicians and rising stars, the septet will be celebrating the music of Miki Matsubara, Taeko Ohnuki, Lamp, and more! “[A] fully entertaining, sometimes laugh out loud movie about sports underdogs who rise to success....”

films.title: Jesse Zubot in Concert + Inedia preview screening
films.synopsis: Acclaimed composer and violinist Jesse Zubot is one of the most in-demand film composers in BC, contributing scores to Bones of Crows, Indian Horse, Nechako, Monkey Beach, Inedia and many more. This afternoon, Zubot will perform solo using a violin, viola and miscellaneous electronics incorporating multiple sounds and techniques that relate to his work as a film composer. This will be followed by a preview screening of Liz Cairns’ mesmerizing Inedia, a dark, compelling film about a young woman who joins a cult-like community. “Riveting... anchored by a powerful performance from Amy Forsyth.” STEPHEN SAITO, MOVEABLE FEAST

films.title: Julian Borkowski: Blues for Brando + The Wild One
films.synopsis: The Julian Borkowski Quintet is honoured to be paying tribute to what might be the most impactful development in jazz history: the emergence of bebop. In playing the music of such jazz legends as Thelonious Monk, Bud Powell, Clifford Brown and Charlie Parker, this set will highlight the innovations and evolutions of the bebop style. With a sophisticated, heartfelt, and exuberant sound, the group features Julian Borkowski—trumpet, Tamas Balai—alto saxophone, Jimi James—piano, Arvind Ramdas—drums, and Kosma Busheikin—bass. After the movie, enjoy Marlon Brando in one of his iconic roles, as the motorcycle rebel in The Wild One (1954) “A sleazy good time.” DAVE KEHR, CHICAGO READER

films.title: The Exterminating Angel: Live Scored by Magazinist
films.synopsis: Experimental music duo Magazinist perform a live score alongside Luis BuÑuel’s surrealist masterpiece. In this allegory of class divisions, a group of bourgeois opera-goers are walled off from the outside world when their extravagant dinner party becomes an inescapable prison. For reasons no-one understands, and no matter how long the party grinds on, none of them can leave the room. Magazinist will accompany the film with a lavish sonic feast of their own, using everything from ceramics to stale bread, ice cubes, crystal singing glasses, resonant bowls, pepper grinders, and other sound objects both culinary and out-of-the-ordinary. “Buñuel’s ferociously brilliant The Exterminating Angel is one of his most provocative and unforgettable works. In it, we watch a trivial breach of etiquette transform into the destruction of civilization.” MARSHA KINDER, BLOOD CINEMA: THE RECONSTRUCTION OF NATIONAL IDENTITY IN SPAIN

films.title: Gondola
films.synopsis: Nina and Iva cross every half an hour, as one cable car traverses the valley left to right and the other crosses right to left. The two conductors look forward to this fleeting encounter in their repetitive routine, and the crossings become increasingly flirtatious and creative, an opportunity to surprise and impress. Veit Helmer’s whimsical Georgian comedy dispenses entirely with dialogue and you don’t miss it; the lovely rural setting and deadpan visual panache put us in the elevated heights of Amélie, Grand Budapest Hotel, or Mon Hulot’s Holiday. “With a tone reminiscent of Jean-Pierre Jeunet’s Amélie, this romantic, enchanting, funny and fanciful film will have you leaving the cinema uplifted.” CHAD ARMSTRONG, THE QUEER REVIEW

films.title: Stories of Our Lives
films.synopsis: The latest installment in our on-going African Cinema Now! series is subtitled Our Queer Lives and invites us to consider the aesthetics and framework by which queer African stories reach us. Stories of Our Lives (62 mins) documents personal stories of lovers, fighters and rebels and the community histories that characterize the queer experience in Kenya. This is preceded by the touching and resonant 38-minute Nigerian love story, Ìfé. “With an artful and intimate touch, director Jim Chuchu beautifully gives voice to the lives of gay and lesbian Kenyans in this omnibus film, shot in black-and-white.” CRAIG TAKEUCHI, GEORGIA STRAIGHT

films.title: Walking with Shadows
films.synopsis: Curators’ statement: “In a quiet and determined way, we are invited into the life of Ebele Njoko (Ozzy Agu) as it begins to fall apart. Through his familial encounters, we come to the realization that he has been outed. While this film speaks on the violence many Queer people in Nigeria undergo, we consider the importance of the time the film emerges and the important identities it affirms and supports through raising awareness and representing a marginalized group that is often ignored and poorly represented.” “There is a constant questioning of masculinity. In that context, the struggle to be true to his desires nudges the film towards becoming a Nigerian Moonlight.” ALLAN HUNTER, SCREEN DAILY

films.title: While You Weren’t Looking
films.synopsis: The changing landscape of South African politics and lifestyles is portrayed through a trio of artfully counter-pointed relationships. A successful Black real estate woman in Cape Town is cheating on her white wife, while their bohemian daughter is dating a gender non-confirming woman in the Khayalitsha township. Meanwhile an ageing gay man goes in a search of one of his former lovers, a former uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) operative who is now a political heavyweight. “An incisive look at different levels of privilege in South Africa’s queer community.” GRETHE KEMP, CITY PRESS (South Africa)

films.title: #Skoden
films.synopsis: Pernell Bad Arm was a man, and much more than the provocative meme (captioned #Skoden: Let's go then) which went viral about a decade ago. Damien Eagle Bear gives us a warm and respectful portrait of the man he knew.

films.title: Angela’s Shadow
films.synopsis: When a socialite visits her nanny’s remote reserve, she discovers her Cree ancestry and delves into her new-found spiritual traditions to save herself and her newborn baby from her husband’s psychotic and purity-obsessed racism.

films.title: Endless Cookie
films.synopsis: The less you know about Endless Cookie beforehand, the better you will be prepared. Seriously.

films.title: Ghosts of the Sea
films.synopsis: 2:30PM, 7:00PM Imagine an especially poetic true crime podcast about a sailor who built his own sailboat and lived on the high seas, but lost not one, but two wives along the way... Now imagine it told from the vantage point of his daughter: Ghosts of the Sea. “A haunting, artfully constructed documentary that unravels the myth of Tangvald’s romantic freedom, exposing a legacy of loss, suspicion and generational trauma.” PETER HOWELL, TORONTO STAR

films.title: Stealing Angel
films.synopsis: In this humane comedy from Marseille filmmaker Robert Guédiguian a trusted caregiver takes advantage of her clients, stealing to support her grandson’s piano lessons. When her theft is discovered the repercussions are surprising... “A beautiful fable, distilled in music and grace and light.”

films.title: In the Mood for Love
films.synopsis: 6:30PM, 8:45PM Wong Kar-wai’s most acclaimed and popular film is a love story about two neighbours (Tony Leung and Maggie Cheung) who are drawn together by the long absences of their respective spouses + a newly released short companion piece from 2001.

films.title: Children of Men
films.synopsis: 2027: 18 years since the last baby was born, disillusioned Englishman Theo (Clive Owen) becomes an unlikely champion of the human race when he is asked by his former lover (Julianne Moore) to escort a young pregnant woman out of the country.

films.title: The Gleaners and I
films.synopsis: This lovely essay film about the art of foraging is also a self portrait of the artist at 72. “Urgent, graceful, accessible and at times openly cheerful—it takes a big bite out of life.”

films.title: The Headless Woman
films.synopsis: The pictures tell the story—and you better not blink —when Veronica (the superb Maria Onetto) hits something on the road home. But what? She is too traumatized, or panic-stricken, to go back and look, and her fears are too terrible to acknowledge.

films.title: Zodiac
films.synopsis: David Fincher is the most exacting American filmmaker since Stanley Kubrick. It makes him the perfect director for this compelling procedural consumed by the unsolved mystery of the Zodiac killer. “Zodiac accepts and embraces irresolvability, which may be why it’s so hypnotically rewatchable.”

films.title: A Serious Man
films.synopsis: The Coen brothers’ best movie is a painfully funny existentialist comedy about a physics professor, Larry Gopnik (Michael Stuhlberg), benumbed but bewildered by his wife’s announcement that she wants a divorce. That’s only the start of his troubles. “As funny, heartbreaking, questioning, trying, exasperating and sincerely inquisitive a portrait of the human condition as you’ll find on screen.”

films.title: Once Upon a Time in Anatolia
films.synopsis: Neither a fairytale, nor a Leonesque shoot-em-up, Nuri Bilge Ceylan’s somber, melancholy masterpiece is both a ruminative comedy about mortality and a subtle, poignant murder mystery.

films.title: Paprika
films.synopsis: A device capable of transmitting dreams falls into the wrong hands in this dazzling anime meta-movie from visionary filmmaker Satoshi Kon. The imagery here is never less than overwhelming; it’s probably the greatest scifimovie of our times. “You wake from it as if from a dream: spooked, provoked and exhilarated.” DAVID ANSEN, NEWSWEEK

films.title: Certain Women
films.synopsis: Spare, incisive portraits of four Montana women (Laura Dern, Michelle Williams, Kristen Stewart and Lily Gladstone) brushing up against the everyday wears and tears of difficult men, their own circumstances, and the desire for something better. “A work of art produced by a director in full control of her material. It leaves you reeling.”

films.title: Margaret
films.synopsis: 17-year-old Lisa is rocked with guilt after a woman is killed in a traffic accident. But that’s only one thread in a teeming social tapestry this intense, passionate teen must negotiate as she comes of age in a time of contradiction and confusion. “Frayed-edges filmmaking at its finest.”

films.title: Shoplifters
films.synopsis: A Palme d’or winner in 2018, Shoplifters is both a hardedged and heartwarming drama about a makeshift family of impoverished urchins and orphans in contemporary Tokyo. “This wise and insightful film is delicate, poignant and unexpectedly powerful.” KENNETH TURAN, LA TIMES

films.title: Toni Erdmann
films.synopsis: This hilarious and acerbic comedy follows a retiree as he stages a series of outrageous pranks to disrupt his executive daughter’s latest business deal. “An immensely rich, deeply felt exploration of human relationships that draws you in and holds you fast for nearly three hours.” TIRDAD DERAKHSHANI, PHILADELPHA INQUIRER

films.title: Get Out
films.synopsis: Guess who’s coming to dinner? Daniel Kaluuya is the Black boyfriend justifiably anxious about meeting his white girlfriend’s folks for the first time. “Peele’s perfectly tuned cast and deft camera work unleash his uproarious humor along with his political fury.” RICHARD BRODY, NEW YORKER

films.title: Lady Bird
films.synopsis: Greta Gerwig’s first film as writer-director is a delightful, painful comedy about “Lady Bird” McPherson (Saoirse Ronan), a Sacramento teen on the point of swapping high school for college, and her hard-working mom, Marion (Laurie Metcalf). “Exceptionally well-written, full of wordplay and lively argument.... You will almost certainly love it.”

films.title: Melancholia
films.synopsis: Lars von Trier squares up to the end times with this grandly luxuriant but surprisingly punky sci-fi, set in an imposing country mansion house, where Justine (Kirsten Dunst) blows up what’s supposed to be the happiest day of her life.

films.title: Moonlight
films.synopsis: Moonlight is many things—a portrait of a young black man coming of age in Miami in the 1980s, a film about fathers and sons, about mentorship and about the scourge of drugs—but it is also one of the most piercing movie romances of the last decade. “The best film I’ve seen in a long time and the best take on black masculinity... ever.”

films.title: Once Upon a Time... In Hollywood
films.synopsis: A film of luxuriant and sinister beauty, Tarantino’s last movie to date is a rich and lovely immersion in the dying days of Old Hollywood, LA, 1969. “A tender, rapturous film, both joyous and melancholy, a reverie for a lost past and a door that opens to myriad imagined possibilities.” STEPHANIE ZACHAREK, TIME

films.title: Petite Maman
films.synopsis: This “small” film from the director of Portrait of a Lady on Fire speaks volumes. It’s a poetical modern fairy tale about an eight-year-old girl who meets a new friend her own age in the woods behind her late grandmother’s house.

films.title: Silence
films.synopsis: This sober, probing examination of faith, ego, cruelty and compassion is the most underrated film from the often under-valued latter half of Martin Scorsese’s brilliant career; a passion project, about Catholic missionaries in 17th Century Japan. “A film for the ages.” GLENN WHIPP, LA TIMES

films.title: Synecdoche, New York
films.synopsis: Charlie Kaufman wrote Being John Malkovich, Adaptation and Sunshine of the Spotless Mind—all great, all successful—then turned director with Synecdoche, which is a masterpiece and which basically went unseen. It’s overdue rediscovery. “It will open to confused audiences and live indefinitely.”

films.title: Holy Motors
films.synopsis: Carax’s film a dazzler, a requiem for cinema that somehow breathes new life and new hope into the form. Denis Lavant (Beau Travail) plays 11 roles and the accordion. Absurdist, surreal, poignant and unforgettable, this is truly one of a kind. “Thrillingly, defiantly alive.”

films.title: It’s Not Me
films.synopsis: “Where are you at, Leos Carax?” To this question, the French filmmaker assembles an unpredictable essay-film made in the spirit of the late Jean-Luc Godard— an endlessly inventive self-portrait of an artist reflecting on his place in cinema history.

films.title: Bonnie Northgraves Quintet: To Louis with Love + Jazz on a Summer’s Day
films.synopsis: Join us for To Louis with Love, a joyful celebration of the legendary Louis Armstrong by Bonnie Northgraves and her band, followed by Bert Stern’s legendary concert film Jazz on a Summer’s Day, featuring Monk, Gerry Mulligan, and of course Satchmo. “Gorgeous. Probably the best feature-length jazz concert movie ever made.” JONATHAN ROSENBAUM, CHICAGO READER

films.title: Oscar Peterson Centenary Tribute: Triology plays Peterson + The Silent Partner screening
films.synopsis: Celebrate Oscar Peterson’s centenary with an evening of Canadian jazz and film. Triology—Jodi Proznick (bass), Bill Coon (guitar) and Miles Black (piano)—pays tribute to the legendary Oscar Peterson, followed by cult thriller The Silent Partner. “An uncommonly clever and gripping suspense thriller.” GARY ARNOLD, WASHINGTON POST

films.title: Aug 25–Sep 10 Matt Grinke’s Happiest Jazz Quintet play Classic Disney Songs + The Jungle Book screening
films.synopsis: The Happiest Big Band on Earth was born through Matt Grinke’s love of jazz and Disney. Since then, the Happiest band has continued to morph and shift into many different sounds and sizes, and VIFF Centre is happy to welcome the Happiest Jazz Quintet back for a second show this year. The band’s hour-long set will be followed by a brief intermission, and then a chance to enjoy the grooviest of the studio’s 20th century animated classics, the original 1967 version of The Jungle Book, featuring songs like I Wanna Be Like You, The Bare Necessities and Trust In Me.

films.title: Women in Blues: LJ Mounteney + Big Mama Thornton: I Can’t Be Anyone But Me
films.synopsis: Canadian blues vocalist LJ Mounteney often draws comparisons to Bonnie Raitt and Susan Tedechi, and she delivers the goods with her rich, soulful voice and high-energy performances. For this special VIFF show paying tribute to the pioneering women of blues and rhythm & blues she’s joined by an all-star Vancouver lineup: Jerry Cook on sax, Tim Porter on guitar, Linda Kidder on bass and Allan Dionne on drums. After LJ’s set, enjoy the Canadian premiere of the definitive documentary about the legendary blues singer Willie Mae “Big Mama” Thornton.

films.title: Cory Weeds plays Sonny Rollins + Saxophone Colossus film
films.synopsis: Local sax legend Cory Weeds is joined by pianist Sharon Minemoto, bassist David Caballero and drummer Jesse Cahill to play music from Sonny Rollins’ 1957 Riverside Records release The Sound Of Sonny. Sonny’s performances and recordings were at a peak during 1957 as Down Beat magazine proclaimed him the Critics’ Poll winner under the category of ‘New Star’ of the tenor saxophone. After their hour-long set, enjoy Robert Mugge’s essential documentary portrait, Sonny Rollins: Saxophone Colossus (1986, 101 min).

films.title: Licorice Pizza
films.synopsis: The San Fernando Valley, 1973. This charming coming of age comedy about a gifted—or at least, self-confident—15 year old aspiring actor (Cooper Hoffman) courting a bright but directionless young woman of 25 (Alana Haim) has an odd, meandering dynamic but it’s a long player that keeps on giving. Taking place over a year or so, the movie is a celebration of chutzpah, entrepreneurship, and romance, but it’s also a critique of over-bearing, egocentric men, the pitfalls of the entertainment industry, and indeed the waterbed business.

films.title: The Master
films.synopsis: If Boogie Nights is the story of California in the 70s and early 80s, and There Will Be Blood takes us back to the beginning of the 20th Century, The Master is about America in the 1950s. WWII veteran Freddie (Joaquin Phoenix) falls under the spell of charismatic writer and self-styled scientist Lancaster Dodd (Philip Seymour Hoffman), who has created his own Church: “The Cause”. Can Freddie find salvation? Can Lancaster? “The Master demonstrates a remarkable lucidity and assurance.”

films.title: Souleymane’s Story
films.synopsis: Exhausted by the grueling grind of the Parisian gig economy and hopping between homeless shelters, Guinean immigrant Souleymane races against time to prepare for his asylum interview, struggling not to lose himself in his pursuit of freedom. A multiple-award winner at Cannes and the European Film Awards, Souleymane’s Story is a riveting social realist drama centered around a virtuosic, heartrending performance from newcomer Abou Sangare. An angry, tender film which is as gripping as any thriller.

films.title: Punch-Drunk Love
films.synopsis: Giddy and hysteric, surreal and expressionist, PunchDrunk Love throws together goofball comedian Adam Sandler and arthouse princess Emily Watson, an experimental percussive score, abstract chromatic interludes like something out of the 1960s avant-garde, novelty toilet plungers with unbreakable handles, 12,000 puddings, seven sisters and a mysterious harmonium (for good vibrations). “Poetry is perhaps the best way to think about Mr. Anderson’s suave, exuberant balance of free-form inspiration and formal control.” AO SCOTT, NEW YORK TIMES

films.title: Sweet Angel Baby
films.synopsis: Eliza (Michaela Kurimsky) has a secret life. After church on Sunday she ducks out into the woods, strips off, pulls on a ski mask, and strikes a series of erotic poses for her anonymous Instagram project. Then there’s her friendship with Toni (Elle-Máijá Tailfeathers), the only “out” lesbian in town, and consequently an object of suspicion in this coastal Newfoundland community. Melanie Oates’ movie casts a baleful eye on small town hypocrisies, honours difference but recognizes the courage required to connect authentically.

films.title: Portrait of a Lady on Fire
films.synopsis: In pre-Revolutionary France, Marianne (Noémie Merlant) is deposited on a Breton beach to take up a position as companion to the beautiful Héloïse (Adèle Haenel). But she has a secret mission: she has been commissioned to paint the young woman’s portrait for a fiancee she has never met, a portrait which Héloïse has refused to sit for. But as she studies her subject, Marianne finds herself falling in love with her. Céline Sciamma’s queer costume drama was voted 30th Greatest Film Ever Made in a 2022 poll. Sunday’s Pantheon screening will feature a 20 minute introduction.

films.title: Folktales
films.synopsis: AUG 18-22 ADDITIONAL SCREENINGS Pasvik Folk High School in Norway provides a very special gap year education. Located in the far north, near the Russian border, it teaches arctic survival skills (bushcraft and hunting) and dog sledding (mushing). Jesus Camp directors Heidi Ewing and Rachel Grady follow three teens across their ten-month enrollment. Nineteen-yearold Hege is getting over the death of her dad. Bjorn is “likeable but annoying,” in his own estimation, and finds it hard to keep friends. Romain, an 18-year-old from the Netherlands, is painfully insecure. But it’s astonishing what bonding with huskies can do...

films.title: Hard Eight
films.synopsis: Sydney (PTA’s preferred title for this, his first feature) is a debonair old school gambler, played by Philip Baker Hall. He’s also the first of Anderson’s ambiguous father figures, who seemingly at random takes a homeless man (John C Reilly) under his wing, mentoring him in the art of craps, and looking out for him when he becomes involved with a Reno waitress, Clementine (Gwyneth Paltrow). A neo-noir character piece set in motel rooms, cafes and casinos, Hard Eight was enough to get Film Comment magazine to nominate him the most promising young director of the year.

films.title: Inherent Vice
films.synopsis: Surely PTA’s most underrated movie, Inherent Vice is adapted by Thomas Pynchon’s 2009 novel, a stoner reflection on a Raymond Chandler story set in LA in 1970 (shades of The Long Goodbye and The Big Lebowski). Joaquin Phoenix is hippie private eye Doc Sportello, caught up in the tentacles of multiple conspiracies which may all be one. By now we know that PTA isn’t about the plot, except in so far as everyone concerned is losing it, but with its billionaire fascist developers and corrupt cops, this has plenty to say about the world today.

films.title: The Last Class
films.synopsis: News junkies will know Robert Reich as a regular TV pundit and a former US Secretary for Labor in the Clinton administration. But his true vocation has always been teaching. This doc follows Reich’s last year at Berkeley before his retirement at 71, sitting in on his massively popular classes as he winds up another chapter in a life of public service. He’s an inspiring speaker, committed to fostering critical thinking and empowering his students with a sense of social responsibility and optimism (difficult as that may be in these times). “It’s heartening to hear a major figure in American political history talking about the future as if it might actually happen.” MATT ZOLLER SEITZ, ROGEREBERT.COM

films.title: Monk in Pieces
films.synopsis: Meredith Monk may not be a household name but her fans include Philip Glass, David Byrne, and Bjork, to say nothing of the Dalai Lama. As a singer, she has a rare three octave range. But it’s what she does with it that’s really interesting: vocalizing sounds you’ve never heard before. Monk’s also a performance artist, choreographer and composer. And, of course, she’s a woman, still notable in the New York avant-garde scene of the 1960s and 70s. This playful and personable portrait is a perfect introduction to a singular artist.

films.title: It’s Never Over, Jeff Buckley
films.synopsis: David Bowie said that Grace, Jeff Buckley’s 1994 debut, was the best album he had ever heard. Buckley became famous for his cover of Leonard Cohen’s Hallelujah, but his musical inspirations stretched from Nina Simone, Judy Garland and Edith Piaf to Nusrat Ali Fateh Khan and Led Zeppelin. With a voice that could range across four octaves, he made you hear them too. With the cooperation of Buckley’s former band mates, his romantic partners and his mother, Oscar-nominated director Amy Berg (Deliver Us from Evil) gives us a rounded portrait of a transcendent talent.

films.title: Capernaum
films.synopsis: Nadine Labaki’s Oscar-nominated heart-tugger tells the story of a 12 year old boy who has grown up in the slums of Beirut, and who decides to sue his parents for bringing him into such a world. “An absolute heartbreaker.” PETER HOWELL, TORONTO STAR Aimed at film lovers 55+, Talking Pictures offers audience-friendly festival films, refreshments, and an open invitation to chat about our shared experience of the movie. “It’s a fairy tale and an opera, a potboiler and a news bulletin, a howl of protest and an anthem of resistance.” AO SCOTT, NEW YORK TIMES

films.title: Raging Bull
films.synopsis: In the throes of a near-fatal drug problem Martin Scorsese made what he believed could be his last movie. Its subject: the Bronx Bull, Jake La Motta, a graceless but indomitable boxer who never quits beating himself up. Punishing, painful and pitiless, with the ultimate Method performance from Robert De Niro at its core, it’s in many ways the culmination of the American psycho-realist tradition, but this is realism pushing through to spiritual redemption by way of Scorsese’s heightened subjective style. The Wed 2pm screening of Raging Bull is part of the Film Studies series, introduced by Prof Harry Killas.

films.title: Blue Horse Opera + The Big Gundown
films.synopsis: A visionary song cycle by acclaimed Canadian artist Rick Maddocks, Blue Horse Opera is a bold fusion of indie, folk, classical music, and dance, drawing inspiration from the climate emergency and the cinematic landscapes of spaghetti westerns. Maddocks performs this original song cycle accompanied by some of Vancouver’s finest musicians and flamenco dancers. After the song cycle enjoy one of the classic horse operas that inspired it: Sergio Sollima’s left wing spaghetti western, The Big Gundown (1967), starring Lee van Cleef and Thomas Milian, and featuring one of Ennio Morricone’s most expansive scores. Co-presented with Pi Theatre

films.title: Sex
films.synopsis: SEP 15, 18, 20 ADD'L SCREENINGS Two chimney sweeps living in Oslo, both happily partnered in heterosexual marriages, find their views on sexuality and gender challenged by a series of unexpected events. Both men confront heretofore unexplored aspects of their identities—which, as it turns out, are more fluid than they had previously thought. Playfully structured as a series of sharply scripted two-hander conversations, Sex is a dryly humorous and unexpectedly poignant exploration of normative societal expectations.

films.title: Riefenstahl
films.synopsis: It was Susan Sontag who coined the term “fascinating fascism,” writing about the German filmmaker and photographer Leni Riefenstahl in 1975. The Nazis’ favourite filmmaker spent decades after the war attempting to rehabilitate her reputation. She was an artist, she said, not a politician. Andres Veiel’s film puts the lie to that argument, drawing on Riefenstahl’s personal archives and the many interviews she gave over the decades. It’s a complex and sad story. Veiel gives Leni her due, but never lets her off the hook.

films.title: Kit Eakle’s Jaz’n’theViolin String Band + Louie Bluie film screening
films.synopsis: Louie Bluie, the stage name of Howard Armstrong, was one of many fiddle players who gave birth to the new sounds of jazz and blues at the beginning of the twentieth century. Kit Eakle’s ‘Jaz’N’theViolin’ gives his music context, playing the music of the often forgotten, larger than life black fiddlers and jazz violinists like Louie Bluie, Lonnie Johnson, and the Memphis Jugband, who pioneered this music. After the band’s set, there will be a brief intermission and then a screening of the documentary Louie Bluie, by Terry Zwigoff (Ghost World; Bad Santa).

films.title: George Garzone Live + Fire Music: The Story of Free Jazz film screening
films.synopsis: George Garzone is a giant of the contemporary saxophone, having performed with Jazz luminaries like Joe Lovano, Jack DeJohnette, Kenny Barron, & Ingrid Jensen. In short, he’s considered one of the true living masters of this instrument. He’ll be performing a very special set music at the VIFF Centre, in tandem with a screening of Fire Music, documenting the birth and growing pain of Free Jazz in the 1960s & 70s. This music is near and dear to George’s heart and he’s enslisted the Jerry Steinhilber Trio to help celebrate it.

films.title: First Cow
films.synopsis: Kelly Reichardt’s First Cow had the misfortune of a March 2020 theatrical release date. Co-written by her regular collaborator Jon Raymond, based on his novel The HalfLife, this is set, for the most part, in Oregon Territory in 1820. The eponymous beast is a lonely Jersey cow, the property of the richest man in town, but surreptitiously milked every night by a baker (John Magaro, from Köln 75) and his enterprising buddy, King-Lu (Orion Lee). The two men hope that biscuits will be their golden ticket... Kelly Reichardt’s latest, The Mastermind, is in the festival.

films.title: August Winds
films.synopsis: A poetic debut narrative feature by the director of Neon Bull and The Blue Trail. Shirley (Dandara de Morais), a gorgeous young woman, is in the countryside taking care of her aging grandmother when her diver boyfriend discovers a skull in the ocean. Then a corpse washes ashore... Youthful vitality and decay contrast throughout the film, evoking a sense of the confluence of time. Shot by the director himself, the stunning cinematography lends an optimistic beauty to the seemingly dark subject matter.

films.title: On the Beach At Night Alone
films.synopsis: Art imitates life in this quietly devastating masterpiece from Hong Sangsoo. Kim Minhee (The Handmaiden, Right Now, Wrong Then)—in the role that won her the Silver Bear for best actress in Berlin—plays Younghee, an actress reeling in the aftermath of an affair with a married film director. Younghee visits Hamburg then returns to Korea, but as she meets with friends increasingly startling confessions emerge. See Hong’s latest in VIFF: What Does That Nature Say To You.

films.title: The Glassworker
films.synopsis: This animated fable is the next best thing to a new Hayao Miyazaki Studio Ghibli production. It’s so clearly influenced by Miyazaki’s work you might think it was made by his personal apprentice. (In fact, Usman Riaz worshipped from afar: the film was made in Karachi, Pakistan.) It’s a labour of love about making art (glass blowing) in a world seemingly hell-bent on destruction. Vincent is mentored by his father, a committed pacifist, but falls in love with a young violinist, whose father is a colonel in the military. “Construed as a family drama, it is a humanist tale aimed at youth, addressing the harsh realities and uncertain future during a military conflict ... showcasing how art and creativity can provide solace and strength, even in the darkest times.” MARTIN KUDLAC, SCREEN ANARCHY

films.title: The Road to Patagonia
films.synopsis: A travelogue, an eco doc, an adventure movie and a love story, The Road to Patagonia has touch points for just about everyone. Our first person narrator and cameraman is Matty Hannon, an Australian ecologist. After living

films.title: Breathless
films.synopsis: In anticipation of Richard Linklater’s extremely cool Nouvelle Vague (VIFF’s opening gala), this is an opportune moment to revisit Godard’s iconic debut feature, a criminal romance about a petty criminal (Jean-Paul Belmondo) on the lam with American in Paris Jean Seberg. Breathless lives up to its name. It bursts with energy. It is radical for its bebop-style montage (including the pragmatic use of jumpcuts), its mixture of neo-realism, thriller elements and an almost anthropological fascination with its young lovers.

films.title: Clearcut (Tribute to Graham Greene)
films.synopsis: The late, great Graham Greene gives the performance of his career as Arthur, who is either a pissed-offwarrior on a rampage against a mill encroaching on his people’s land, or a trickster spirit manifesting to teach an ineffectual liberal lawyer (Ron Lea) a lesson about the need for action— unless he’s both? This intense, radical environmental, aboriginal rights drama from the Polish filmmaker Ryszard Bugajski (Closed Circuit; The Interrogation) has a growing cult reputation. 4K Restoration by Severin Films “A Canadian answer to Deliverance... Graham Greene is riveting.” New York Times

films.title: I Am Cuba
