Through cheeky reenactments, stylized animated sequences, and interviews with a diverse community of sex workers, Werhun delves deep into the topics of shame, stigma, risk, and reward, reconceptualizing the archetype of the Modern Whore. “Insightful, funny and creative.” FLICKERING MYTH Winner: Best Canadian Documentary, Vancouver Film Critics Circle

films.title: Love and Money
films.synopsis: Love and money make the world go round, but there’s more of the former on display in this winning exercise in DIY filmmaking from writer-director David Ray (Grand Unified Theory) and his puckish band of merry pranksters. This is a totally improvised jape, made in Vancouver “for less than the cost of a used Honda.” Andrew McNee plays Andrew, a musician whose lost his way, not to mention his friend Scott, who’s missing. Seeking him out involves strange encounters with friends and strangers, none of whom seems to know what’s going on (probably because there wasn’t a script). Opening night Q&A with cast and crew

films.title: Follies
films.synopsis: After 16 years of marriage and two children, François and Julie have lost their spark in the bedroom. In an effort to reconnect, they decide to open up their relationship and rediscover their sexuality — but polyamory isn’t as easy as they hoped. Juggling family life while searching for matches on a swingers’ app, the couple find themselves in a series of awkward foursomes, and trust issues begin to complicate their experiment. However, as their paths diverge, new pleasures begin to reawaken dormant feelings. The feature-length directorial debut of Eric K. Boulianne (who co-writes and stars alongside Catherine Chabot), Follies is a laugh-out-loud sex comedy and a relatable depiction of marriage that recognizes the distinctions between love, sex, and intimacy. Frank in its portrayals of BDSM and kink, Boulianne’s film never loses sight of communication as the key ingredient to a relationship. Full of cheeky cinematic references to marital classics such as Scenes From a Marriage and Eyes Wide Shut, this is a bawdy riot with a heart of gold.

films.title: Erupcja
films.synopsis: Bethany (Charli xcx) has persuaded bf Will (Will Madden) that Warsaw is more exciting than Paris. Will means to propose and Beth knows this, although Will does not know she knows. Warsaw may or may not be more exciting than Paris, but it is home to Beth’s friend Nel (Lena Góra), and Beth believes this may save her. Will doesn’t know about Nel either. Or the volcanos… Charli’s big screen debut (she shot it before The Moment) is a lo-fi gem. Think Before Sunrise, 2025: young people figuring out love, or failing to, over a transitory weekend of plans unravelling, last minute all-nighters, secrets coming out. On the surface it might seem small. But the earth moves.

films.title: Starwalker
films.synopsis: Welcome to the House of Borealis! For Star (Dillian Chiblow), this East Van drag house is the home they’ve been searching for, an alternate family that’s genuinely supportive and inspiring. At its centre is Mother (Stewart Adam McKensy), who’s seen it all, been it all, and somehow knits together a wayward group of orphans and runaways. Corey Payette’s musical blends drag spectacle, Indigenous storytelling, and soaring emotion in a film that celebrates chosen family and the liberating magic of performance.

films.title: Dead Lover
films.synopsis: A lonely, foul-smelling gravedigger (Grace Glowicki) meets the man of her dreams — a poet (Ben Petrie) who is infatuated with her putrid odour. When her lover perishes at sea, she attempts to resurrect him… to mixed results. Dead Lover is a campy, romantic horror with a DIY aesthetic that combines Lynchian terror, Looney Tunes zaniness, and the surreal eroticism of Kenneth Anger. Glowicki shines in her fluorescent, oddball second feature that zaps fresh life into Mary Shelley’s classic. Friday, April 17’s screening will be presented in Stink-o-Vision! Each audience member receives a scratch-and-sniff card that unleashes a bold bouquet of aromas — dandy cologne, hot dogs, ghost puke, and more — that enhance select scenes in the film. A suitably skewed take on sensory cinema! Apr 17: Intro by DIY curator, Sook-Yin Lee

films.title: Parsley Days
films.synopsis: Kate (Megan Dunlop), a bicycle-maintenance instructor, is ambivalent about her relationship with Ollie (Michael LeBlanc), a birth control educator. While he’s a great guy who is beloved by her friends, he’s also her first true love and she’s curious about what else might be possible. But when Kate discovers she’s pregnant, breaking up becomes all the more complicated. What should Kate do?! Laced with magical realism and buoyed by an infectious soundtrack, Andrea Dorfman’s acclaimed debut is a delight.

films.title: Sansho the Bailiff
films.synopsis: and children are kidnapped. She is sold into prostitution, the boy and girl become slaves in the estate of the tyrannical Sansho. It will be ten long years before the opportunity to escape presents itself. The first thing to say about Mizoguchi’s most acclaimed film is that it’s a gripping story, as you might expect of a tale that’s been passed down for centuries. And it is beautifully told: shocking and brutal in places, but also exquisitely photographed, deeply compassionate and full of feeling. Sunday’s Pantheon screening will feature a 15 minute introduction by a local film scholar and be followed by an audience talkback.

films.title: Vancouver Opera presents... Moulin Rouge!
films.synopsis: Paris has never been gayer than in this headlong karaoke culture crash set in a poptastic 19th century Montmartre, where Ewan McGregor composes The Sound of Music and Toulose Lautrec (John Leguizamo) leads an acting troupe. Nicole Kidman is Satine, a consumptive courtesan who is the queen of the show at da eponymous club. Ba-dazzling stuff from Luhrmann, a filmmaker seemingly intent on reaching the Palace of Wisdom at supersonic speed. “A breathtaking baroque film that marries the best of theatre, opera and cinematic technique.” LIZ MOODY, EMPIRE MAGAZINE

films.title: Chasing Ice
films.synopsis: This visually stunning film follows renowned National Geographic photographer James Balog on a harsh Arctic expedition where he captures a multi-year record of the world’s changing glaciers—undeniable evidence that our planet is in crisis. Winner: People’s Choice Award, Hot Docs 2012

films.title: Chasing Time: An Evening with James Balog
films.synopsis: Renowned environmental photographer James Balog joins us for this Earth Day event honouring the power of images. Following a screening of Chasing Time (40min), which documents the culmination of his decades-long Extreme Ice Survey project, James will discuss how his groundbreaking photographic studies of melting glaciers have offered the world the most compelling visual evidence of climate change imaginable. In turn, they've driven him to seed hope and inspire action toward a sustainable future. Premium Pick

films.title: How Deep Is Your Love
films.synopsis: Filmmaker Eleanor Mortimer tags along with a team of oceanographers and marine biologists as they survey the Clarion-Clipperton fracture, one of the most remote spots on Earth, a 12-day maritime journey from the nearest land, and two miles below the surface. This is home to any number of previously unknown species, it turns out. The scientists are here to discover, study, and catalogue an entire “new” world — but an ecosystem under threat from deep sea mining.

films.title: Do You Love Me
films.synopsis: Beirut is under bombardment. There is nothing new about this story. Lana Daher’s non-fiction film is a cultural-historical self-portrait, comprised entirely of film clips (many of them from dramatic features, but also from news reports, TV and home video) culled from the last 70 years. Through the eyes of citizens, filmmakers and artists, the film reconstructs a fragmented history in a country without a national archive, celebrating creative expression as both resistance, renewal and a way to preserve memory. It is a love letter to Beirut, marked by joy and intimacy, destruction and loss.

films.title: Everyone Is Lying to You for Money
films.synopsis: Since 2008, Bitcoin and cryptocurrency has often been touted as better than money: digital tokens of exchange that can pass from peer to peer without financial institutions taking out a big chunk of your profit. And speaking of profit… the returns have been dizzying. (But so have the falls.) Here, former OC star Ben McKenzie brushes off his economics qualifications and digs into the cryptocurrency conundrum. If Bitcoin is truly all about transparency, how come no one can explain how it works? Channelling his inner Michael Moore and playing the celeb card, McKenzie interviews industry leaders like Sam Bankman-Fried and Alex Mashinsky to get a handle on what is beginning to seem like the greatest pyramid scheme of them all… Funny, tragic, and entertaining, this is the wake-up call we need.

films.title: The Doll
films.synopsis: On Thursday mornings through May, cinematographer Devan Scott takes us on a journey through the history of lighting in cinema, tracing its development from the sunlit studios of early silent film through the three-point setups that defined classical Hollywood realism and film noir to modern techniques of motivated lighting. Today Devan will screen the Lubitsch sex comedy The Doll (1919) after a workshop of approx 50 mins. Talk at 11am, film at noon. “One of the five funniest pictures I’ve ever seen.”

films.title: The Music Room
films.synopsis: Cinematographer Devan Scott continues his journey through the history of lighting in cinema. This week, he credits Satyajit Ray’s director of photography Subrata Mitra for profound innovations that laid the foundation for ideas of motivated lighting that dominated the latter half of the twentieth century. Devan’s workshop (approx 50 min) will be followed by a screening of The Music Room (1958), for many critics, Ray’s finest film. “It is the kind of cinema that flows with the serenity and nobility of a big river.”

films.title: Black Bag
films.synopsis: In the last of his studies in the evolution of cinematography, Devan Scott brings us right up to date with a survey of the modern era of digital photography and LED lighting, focusing in particular on the radical work of Steven Soderbergh, who regularly serves as his own cinematographer under the pseudonym Peter Andrews. After the talk, we will watch Soderbergh’s ingenious 2025 thriller, Black Bag, starring Pierce Brosnan, Cate Blanchett, and Michael Fassbender.

films.title: The Grapes of Wrath
films.synopsis: On Thursday mornings through May, cinematographer Devan Scott takes us on a journey through the history of lighting in cinema. Today, he will be looking at the purposes of three-point lighting and its evolution throughout the studio era in the 1930s and 40s. As well, he will look at the influence of German Expressionism on Hollywood film noir, and the development of Hollywood’s continuity-based lighting techniques. After the talk, we will watch John Ford’s The Grapes of Wrath, photographed by Gregg Toland (Citizen Kane).

films.title: Cassidy Waring + Hearse Chasing
films.synopsis: 12:30PM, 5:00PM, 7:30PM 1:45PM, 4:00PM 3:00PM, 5:00PM, 7:00PM In the late 1990s, eight-year-old Sasha and her Hungarian immigrant family relocate to a new home on Vancouver Island. As they settle in, Jeremy, the oldest child, grows increasingly withdrawn. As his erratic behaviour escalates his family are gripped by a sense of powerlessness. Sophy Romvari’s captivating debut feature is richly detailed and deeply felt. One of the most acclaimed Canadian films in years, Blue Heron’s haunting heartache ensures an indelible viewing experience. Q&A Fri 8 May

films.title: The Last One for the Road
films.synopsis: Carlobianchi and Doriano are a pair of middle-aged drunks driving across Veneto, bar hopping and reminiscing about days past. Joined by Giulio, a young architecture student who tags along to hear their stories, the group slosh their way through the city on the seemingly endless search for that one final drink. Equal parts Aki Kaurismäki and Alice Rohrwacher, The Last One for the Road is a celebration of the spirit of drink and the kinds of stories told around a table of old friends and too much wine.

films.title: Lou Reed’s Metal Machine Music as realized by Aram Bajakian, Stefan Maier and Anju Singh + BERLIN film
films.synopsis: Aram Bajakian is a guitarist, composer and educator, who performed with the legendary Lou Reed during his 2011 and 2012 tours. On May 16 & 17, Aram will be interpreting the music of Lou Reed at the VIFF Centre, in two very different, and very special performances. The first of these is inspired by Reed’s much reviled 1975 album Metal Machine Music. After the gig, we will be screening Lou Reed in concert from 2006, performing his equally reviled Berlin album. “Celebratory... It’s a miracle Reed was able to turn one of the most hermetic albums of all time into a communal experience.”

films.title: Omaha
films.synopsis: 1:00PM, 5:15PM Nine-year-old Ella is gently woken at dawn by her dad (John Magaro, Köln 75). “Imagine what you would grab if there were a fire,” he says. She takes a framed picture of mom, some books, gets the dog in the car and her younger brother Charlie. They take off, heading she knows not where, or why, but sensing their lives will not the same again. Cole Webley’s road movie is really just a fragment of a story, yet it unfolds with such authentic lyricism it lands with a heartbreaking emotional wallop.

films.title: Suburban Fury
films.synopsis: In 1975 Sara Jane Moore attempted to kill the President of the United States. She failed, and spent the next 30 years in prison. Seattle filmmaker Robinson Devor (Police Beat; Zoo) interviews Moore about what led a suburban housewife down the path of radical politics, her relationship

films.title: Blue Road - The Edna O’Brien Story
films.synopsis: The late Irish novelist Edna O’Brien was not one of those writers who hide behind their typewriter. She was vivacious, sometimes vicious, outspoken, and lived life at full tilt. Her parties were legendary and her love affairs not for the faint of heart. Interviewed for the film at the age of 93, she was candid about her past and passionate about her work. Academy Award winner Jessie Buckley reads extracts from O’Brien’s journals, reflecting on fickle men and clueless critics.

films.title: The Christophers
films.synopsis: Ian McKellen is at his imperious best as a toxic, burned out artist whose new assistant (the equally striking Michaela Coel) has a secret agenda: to get her hands on his famously abandoned series, The Christophers, and complete the canvases for discovery when the old man finally expires. This two-hander brims with energy and erudition as it explores what makes an artist pick up a brush, and what makes a painting worth a second look. “Sparkling, funny, wise... it could have gone on forever and not been long enough.” ALISSA WILKINSON, NEW YORK TIMES

films.title: Chasing My Why: The Mammoth 200
films.synopsis: Trailrunner and filmmaker Jeff Pelletier sets out to run the inaugural Mammoth 200, a 215-mile ultramarathon through California’s Sierra Nevada. But beyond the distance, the race becomes a search for something else: an answer to why he keeps returning to events like this. As he documents the journey along the way, the answer is something that must be earned, over time. World Premiere with filmmaker Q&A

films.title: Fiume o Morte!
films.synopsis: The Croatian city of Rijeka rediscovers its own forgotten history in this delightfully unconventional hybrid documentary. In 1919, the decadent Italian poet, lothario, general, and proto-fascist Gabriele D’Annunzio takes great interest in the city known in Italian as Fiume — occupying it and proclaiming himself ruler. His short-lived regency causes an international uproar and local consternation before his ouster. In the present, director Igor Bezinović invites hundreds of locals to take part in a new documentary, turning the film into a citywide occasion of participation and collective storytelling. A shifting, protean film, Fiume o Morte! moves between absurdist re-enactments and documented record. From whimsical sight gags to a sobering examination of fascism, Bezinović plays with history, inviting the viewer to laugh at the seams between history and invention while recognizing D’Annunzio’s self-aggrandizing vision of rule as an absurd act of invention in itself. This is a charming tour de force of cinematic storytelling that brings a truly fascinating piece of forgotten history to life.

films.title: The Wizard of the Kremlin
films.synopsis: Paul Dano is a “modern day Rasputin” to Jude Law’s Vladimir Putin in this smart, insightful slice of political drama from Olivier Assayas (Carlos) and co-writer Emmanuel Carrère. Vadim Baranov is a bohemian and intellectual turned TV executive who is approached to help persuade a KGB counterespionage expert, Putin, to stand for PM in the dying days of Boris Yeltsin’s Presidency. Baranov becomes his close advisor and spin doctor as the fledgling democracy reverts to autocracy over the next two decades. “Essential viewing for understanding the highly sophisticated workings of a totalitarian propaganda state.” TRAVIS JEPPESEN, SIGHT AND SOUND

films.title: Clan of the Painted Lady +
films.synopsis: In this bravely personal documentary, Jennifer Chiu reaches into her family’s history to explore the Hakka—a people, a language, and a culture that have been obscured for far too long. Chiu explores Hakka history, particularly the nomadic drift from China to India, Mauritius, Jamaica, and her home country of Canada. She addresses family secrecy, the costs of assimilation, and more in this engrossing, congenial work full of candid conversation and sharp insights. Q&A with filmmaker Jennifer Chiu In English, Hakka, and Bengali

films.title: My Name Ain’t Suzie
films.synopsis: Leaving behind her fishing village, Shui-Mei is sent to Hong Kong to earn money as a prostitute. Set between the mid 1950s and 1980, My Name Ain’t Suzie is an ambitious and surprising feminist film to come from the Shaw Brothers studio in 1985. Director Angie Chen, making only her second feature, set out to make as accurate a portrait of the HK bargirl trade as possible, and even cast several of them in bit parts. She also hit paydirt with her two leads, Pat Ha and Anthony Wong (in his first film). Director Angie Chen will join us for a Q&A, May 27 “A film that fascinates on so many levels: as a work of a brilliant film auteur; as a sign of the shift in local cinema; as a feminist statement; as a cinematic image of Hong Kong in the past; as a critique of Orientalism and generalized representation of the Far East reproduced in Hollywood films.” MAJA KORBECKA, EASTERN KICKS

films.title: Steal This Story, Please!
films.synopsis: 1:30PM, 6:00PM Best known for Democracy Now! the progressive news show she has hosted for 30 years, Amy Goodman earned her stripes in the field, uncovering nefarious activities in East Timor in 1991. She was arrested for her reporting of the Dakota pipeline protests and detained and questioned by Canadian border agents when she came up to speak in Vancouver in 2009. Urgent, provocative and unexpectedly funny, Steal This Story, Please! is both a call to action and a celebration of resistance.

films.title: Amrum
films.synopsis: 1945. The war is all but lost, but this cannot yet be admitted in public, not even on the remote North Sea island of Amrum, where 12-year-old Hitler Youth Nanning (Jasper Billerbeck) lives with his pregnant mother (Laura Tonke), and her sister (Lisa Hagmeister). Considered an outsider by the islanders, Nanning sets himself a mission: to secure honey and bread to cheer up his mum. But these luxuries are in scant supply, he will have to enter into several trades to reach his goal… Based on the childhood experiences of cowriter Hark Bohm, Fatih Akin’s superb film is both a relatable coming of age story and a resonant reminder that the virus of fascism ultimately consumes itself. Akin (Head-On; The Edge of Heaven) immerses us in the stark beauty of the island, and rarely strays from the 12-year-old’s side as he gradually comes to the painful understanding that his parents are on the wrong side of history.

films.title: The Other Side of Hope
films.synopsis: The Finnish master of the droll and the deadpan, Aki Kaurismäki makes a characteristically heartening contribution concerning the European refugee crisis. Khaled, a Syrian, washes up on Finland’s glum shores and becomes an unlikely friend to a middle-aged Finnish shirt salesman in the midst of remaking his life. Compassionate and wryly funny by turns. Talking Pictures is a monthly matinee series catering to the 55+ community. Patrons are encouraged to stay and chat about the movie and enjoy coffee and cookies on the house. Tickets are only $10, or two for $16. “The guiding ethic of The Other Side of Hope is as much topical as it universal: that altruism is not especially brave or courageous, but just the basic principle governing relations between human beings.” JOHN SEMLEY, GLOBE AND MAIL In Finnish, English, and Arabic

films.title: Space Cadet
films.synopsis: Join us for VIFF Kids Club—our monthly family matinee series with film-inspired crafts and special snacks before the show! Activities begin at 11 am and the film screens at noon. Raised by her devoted robot guardian, Celeste grows up to become an astronaut, off on her first solo mission. Back on Earth, Robot finds comfort in their shared memories. Told without dialogue, this tender animated story blends gentle humour, and a rich musical score to explore connection and distance, childhood and growing up.

films.title: M
films.synopsis: Although Fritz Lang is more famous today for his silent sci-fiepic Metropolis, he considered M his masterpiece. A sophisticated and gripping suspense drama about the hunt for a child murderer, played with disturbing compassion by the great Peter Lorre. M was Lang’s first sound film, and it’s thrilling to experience how he embraced the creative possibilities of the medium. It’s also a very early police procedural, and his first psychological film. 95 years later, it still stands as one of the great films of the criminal mind. Sunday’s Pantheon screening will feature a 15 minute introduction by a local film scholar and be followed by an audience talkback. “A film from 1931 whose power and originality seem startling and fresh today—a film that has not dated.”

films.title: Smiles of a Summer Night
films.synopsis: Bergman’s belated international breakthrough came with his sixteenth feature, a sophisticated comedy of sexual manners inspired by Mozart, Shakespeare’s A Midsummer Night's Dream, and Renoir’s Rules of the Game.

films.title: Wild Strawberries
films.synopsis: One of Ingmar Bergman’s pinnacle works—and an excellent entry point into his extraordinary cinema—Wild Strawberries is an intensely moving, highly lyrical drama of affirmation and reconciliation.

films.title: Crisis
films.synopsis: A pantheon career begins here. Ingmar Bergman’s debut feature, made when he was 27, tells the melodramatic tale of a young woman torn between two mothers and between small-town security and big-city seductions.

films.title: The Magician
films.synopsis: Nothing is quite as it seems in Bergman’s mesmerizing, metaphysical The Magician, a semi-comic, high-gothic period piece that sets faith, art, and illusion on a collision course with science, rationality, and reality.

films.title: THE PASSION OF ANNA THROUGH A GLASS DARKLY
Fårö Document
films.synopsis: Bergman’s first documentary feature offers a fond look at his beloved Fårö, the remote Swedish island in the Baltic Sea where he made his home and shot several of his most notable works.

films.title: Fårö Document 1979
films.synopsis: Ten years after his original documentary about life on Fårö, the small Baltic island where he had put down roots, Ingmar Bergman visited again with the film’s subjects to see where fortune had taken them.

films.title: The Silence
films.synopsis: Bergman took great risks with this sexually frank, formally daring drama, one of his most controversial works.

films.title: All These Women
films.synopsis: Ingmar Bergman takes aim at critics in this romping farce, his first film in colour—and a decided change of pace after the uncompromisingly bleak "Faith" trilogy.

films.title: Winter Light
films.synopsis: The silence of God resounds with a deafening, despairing clarity in Bergman’s masterfully austere Winter Light, one of the director’s most anguished explorations of spiritual emptiness.

films.title: A Lesson in Love
films.synopsis: “The popular image of Bergman as a frigid intellectual can scarcely survive a viewing of A Lesson in Love,” esteemed British-Canadian film critic Robin Wood wrote of this warm, witty sex farce.

films.title: Surname Viet Given Name Nam
films.synopsis: One of the best known works by celebrated film artist and theorist Trinh T. Minh-ha, Surname Viet Given Name Nam explores questions of identity, popular memory, and culture through Vietnamese women’s resistance in Vietnam and the United States.

films.title: Forgetting Vietnam
films.synopsis: Drawing on ancient stories of Vietnam’s creation, this lyrical film essay from Trinh T. Minh-ha moves between Hi-8 footage shot in 1995 and digital footage filmed in 2012.

films.title: Montparnasse Bienvenue
films.synopsis: Léonor Serraille’s debut feature isn’t the first French film to follow a young woman lost in the city, flirting with madness after the end of a relationship. But it may well be the most surprising and most honest.

films.title: Wùlu
films.synopsis: Wùlu is an astonishingly assured, spine-tingling thriller; a sobering picture of a once-stable nation threatened by corruption; and also a universal tale of a young generation forced to do whatever it takes to get by and find its place in society.

films.title: Diamond Island
films.synopsis: Diamond Island is a stylized tour-de-force of sharp contrasts, pitting glorified shantytowns and dusty construction sites against glittering high-end nightclubs and the cool, neon ambience of Phnom Penh at night.

films.title: Heaven Will Wait
films.synopsis: Though it reaches the emotional heights of great drama, Heaven Can Wait has the granular detail of first-rate investigative journalism: its portrait of vulnerable young women and their helpless families is unforgettable.

films.title: Paris Prestige
films.synopsis: Offering an insider’s Paris-by-night portrait of a vibrant, quickly gentrifying urban neighborhood, the film is also a profound reflection on the struggles and disappointments of two generations of Algerian immigrants in France.

films.title: Speak Up
films.synopsis: Every year, hundreds of students from all over the department of Seine-Saint-Denis face off in Eloquentia, a contest to crown the best orator in this diverse, sprawling suburb of Paris.

films.title: Before Summer Ends
films.synopsis: Fledgling director Maryam Goormaghtigh’s bittersweet chronicle of a single summer in the life of three Iranian students in France is an utterly unique, beguiling mixture of documentary and fiction in the perennial form of a road movie.

films.title: Kiss Me!
films.synopsis: In this charming romantic comedy about the bumps along the way to true love, French comedian and singer Océanerosemarie plays a fun-loving osteopath.

films.title: Heart of a Dog
films.synopsis: Initially approached to make a film about her “philosophy of life,” visionary multimedia artist Laurie Anderson created a rich, dreamlike mediation on loss and love, primarily starring her beloved rat terrier, Lolabelle.

films.title: The Passion of Joan of Arc
films.synopsis: Dreyer’s transcendent late silent masterpiece is perennially cited as one of cinema’s supreme works.

films.title: Jeannette, the Childhood of Joan of Arc
films.synopsis: With Jeannette, French iconoclast Bruno Dumont (La vie de Jésus, L’Humanité) joins the roll call of illustrious auteurs who’ve rendered the life of Joan of Arc in film—albeit never, ever before like this!

films.title: Loyalties
films.synopsis: Anne Wheeler’s powerful 1986 drama (her first fiction feature) is a highlight of a distinguished filmmaking career devoted to bringing authentic, socially conscious Canadian stories—and particularly women’s stories—to the screen.

films.title: Werewolf
films.synopsis: One of the strongest Canadian debuts in recent memory, Ashley McKenzie’s prize-winning first feature is a sobering, documentary-esque account of two recovering junkies making an onerous go of it in New Waterford, Nova Scotia.

films.title: Je tu il elle
films.synopsis: New Restoration. The first feature by the late Belgian auteur Chantal Akerman is a provocative, acutely-personal meditation on the terrifying need for human contact, and a formative aesthetic precursor to her 1975 masterwork, Jeanne Dielman.

films.title: Bridge of Sleep
films.synopsis: Oktay Baraheni’s first feature, the social drama Bridge of Sleep, freely adapts Dostoevsky’s Crime and Punishment and transposes it to contemporary Iran.

films.title: Privacy
films.synopsis: The debut feature of veteran short-film and television director Ahmad Moazzami makes potent drama out of the perils faced by young people in today’s digital environment.

films.title: Where the Wild Things Are
films.synopsis: Let the wild rumpus start! Zeitgeist-bottling author Dave Eggers and American indie icon Spike Jonze proved to be a formidable writer-director duo with this artful adaptation of Maurice Sendak’s indelible children’s book.

films.title: From Up on Poppy Hill
films.synopsis: Co-scripted by anime master Miyazaki Hayao and directed by his son Miyazaki Gorō, this lovingly hand-drawn film from Studio Ghibli is a poignant, tender coming-of-age drama adapted from a 1980 manga.

films.title: 32 Pills: My Sister’s Suicide The Work
The Seventh Seal
films.synopsis: Bergman’s very modern meditation on our search for meaning, presented in the guise of a medieval morality play, is one of cinema’s most famous (and parodied) works.

films.title: The Devil's Eye
films.synopsis: An ironic, stylized, self-consciously theatrical comic fantasy, The Devil's Eye opens in Hell, where Satan decides to send legendary seducer Don Juan (Jarl Kulle) to modern-day Sweden to deflower a country parson’s virtuous daughter (Bibi Andersson).

films.title: Sawdust and Tinsel
films.synopsis: The circus serves as the arena for a savage dissection of male-female sexual relations in the dark, fantastical Sawdust and Tinsel, another standout among Bergman’s early works.

films.title: The Virgin Spring
films.synopsis: Bergman won the first of his three Foreign Language Film Oscars—and Sven Nykvist became Bergman’s regular cinematographer—with this powerful drama of faith and vengeance.

films.title: Brink of Life
films.synopsis: A pared-down chamber piece set in a hospital maternity ward, Brink of Life features three key Bergman actresses—Ingrid Thulin, Eva Dahlbeck, and Bibi Andersson—as three very different expectant mothers.

films.title: Secrets of Women
films.synopsis: Early evidence of Bergman’s skill at comedy is found in the anthology-like Secrets of Women, a project designed to showcase some of Sweden's best actresses.

films.title: Summer Interlude
films.synopsis: Bergman becomes Bergman with the lyrical Summer Interlude, his first major critical success and, arguably, first mature work.

films.title: The Touch
films.synopsis: Bergman’s first film in English is regarded as one of Bergman’s most straightforward and accessible; the director himself described it as, simply, “a love story”—although Christian symbolism and the Holocaust figure into the drama.

films.title: Port of Call
films.synopsis: Roberto Rossellini’s Italian neorealism and Marcel Carné’s French poetic realism are pronounced influences on Ingmar Bergman’s fifth feature, a moody, gritty drama set (and largely shot) on the Gothenburg docks.

films.title: Wander About Me
films.synopsis: Mehraveh Sharifinia garnered much praise and a few festival laurels for her commanding performance in Vancouver Film School alumnus Ghazaleh Soltani’s timely new film.

films.title: No Date, No Signature
films.synopsis: A prominent medical examiner believes he might be responsible for a child’s death in the gripping second feature of Iranian arthouse filmmaker Vahid Jalilvand.

films.title: Babe
films.synopsis: Produced and co-written by Aussie auteur George Miller, this family classic about a resourceful little porker hasn’t lost an ounce of its wit, charm, or relevance in the decades since its release.

films.title: Babe: Pig in the City
films.synopsis: Mad Max mastermind George Miller steered the Babe series into gloriously nutty, left-field territory with this ingenious sequel to the 1995 sleeper hit.

films.title: Ferrari
films.synopsis: In Ferrari, veteran Iranian filmmaker Alireza Davoudnejad returns to tell another compelling coming-of-age story, this time of a teenaged girl from the provinces who travels to Tehran in search of her favourite car.

films.title: Negar
films.synopsis: Director Rambod Javan, known for comedies, tries his hand at drama in this mystery-thriller with surreal and supernatural elements.

films.title: Persona
films.synopsis: Ingmar Bergman’s first film with actress Liv Ullmann is a certifiable masterpiece and a key work of modernist cinema.

films.title: The Rite
films.synopsis: The rarest film from Bergman’s most innovative period, The Rite screens here in a 35mm print.

films.title: The Shame
films.synopsis: “One of Bergman's greatest films” (Pauline Kael), The Shame is a devastating dystopian drama set in an unnamed country in the throes of civil war.

films.title: To Joy
films.synopsis: Bergman based this drama of creative life, domestic strife, and the consolations of art on the failure of his own second marriage.

films.title: Dreams
films.synopsis: Bergman’s fifteenth feature is an enjoyable work in a trademark mode: the insightful, well-acted “women’s picture.”

films.title: Out of the Past
films.synopsis: Film Noir 2018. Jacques Tourneur’s hallucinatory, haunting Out of the Past ranks with Double Indemnity, The Postman Always Rings Twice, and The Killers as one of noir’s seminal works.

films.title: Criss Cross
films.synopsis: Film Noir 2018. A moody, fatalistic urban nightmare, Criss Cross comes from noir stalwart and stylist Robert Siodmak, one of the key contributors to noir’s aesthetic.

films.title: Dead Reckoning
films.synopsis: Humphrey Bogart plays Rip Murdock, a war hero investigating the disappearance of an army buddy, in director John Cromwell’s complexly plotted and claustrophobic noir thriller.

films.title: In a Lonely Place
films.synopsis: Film Noir 2018. Hollywood maverick and auteurist favourite Nick Ray’s film is a masterfully directed, darkly haunting portrait of disaffection and distrust.

films.title: The Postman Always Rings Twice
films.synopsis: Hollywood’s first version of James M. Cain’s torrid novel ranks with Double Indemnity (also based on a Cain story) as one of the quintessential examples of amour fou turned murderous in the tangled, treacherous noir universe.

films.title: My Name Is Julia Ross
films.synopsis: B-movie stylist Joseph H. Lewis (Gun Crazy, The Big Combo) made his first foray into film noir with this tense, fast-paced thriller.

films.title: Strangers on a Train
films.synopsis: Hitchcock’s 1951 classic is a nifty, nasty noir thriller with a great hard-boiled pedigree: it’s based on a Patricia Highsmith novel, with a screenplay co-credited to Raymond Chandler.

films.title: Macao
films.synopsis: Mixed-up identities, shifting alliances, jealous dames, and murderous gangsters propel the plot of this steamy, ultra-stylish noir thriller, produced by Howard Hughes at RKO, with direction credited to master of exotica Josef von Sternberg.

films.title: Pushover
films.synopsis: Fred MacMurray revisits Double Indemnity and Kim Novak (Vertigo) has her first credited role in this first-rate, finely-acted noir suspense drama, ably directed by Richard Quine.

films.title: It Rains on Our Love
films.synopsis: The influence of American film noir and French poetic realism is apparent in Bergman's moody, symbol-laden second feature, an early example of a favourite Bergman subject: the couple under siege.

films.title: A Ship Bound for India
films.synopsis: Bergman’s third feature is a sordid melodrama that makes claustrophobic use of space and centres on a strange quartet of characters.

films.title: Torment
films.synopsis: Ingmar Bergman, launching his film career, was screenwriter and assistant director of Torment, a sordid tale of passion and murder directed by then-reigning Swedish master Alf Sjöberg.

films.title: My Uncle
films.synopsis: A marvellous satire in the spirit of Chaplin’s Modern Times, Jacques Tati’s comedy classic was originally shot in both French and English versions, each edited in slightly different ways.

films.title: The Illusionist
films.synopsis: French comic-book artist and animator Sylvain Chomet’s follow-up to the irresistible Triplets of Belleville, a worldwide sensation, is another triumph of glorious hand-drawn animation.

films.title: Israfil
films.synopsis: Ida Panahandeh’s assured follow-up to Nahid, her award-winning first feature (which screened in this series last year), confirms her talents and continues her attention to contemporary women’s concerns.

films.title: Pig
films.synopsis: The latest from writer-director Mani Haghighi (A Dragon Arrives!) is a flamboyant, farcical black comedy satirizing artistic ego, gender relations, government censorship, and social-media culture.

films.title: The Last Movie
films.synopsis: Dennis Hopper’s little-seen follow-up to the epochal hit Easy Rider is one of cinema’s legendary films maudits (cursed films).

films.title: Cold Water
films.synopsis: Now, re-released in a brilliant 4K restoration, Assayas’s little-seen gem is garnering the attention it so deserved 24 years ago.

films.title: Wanda
films.synopsis: Named Best Foreign Film at Venice in 1970, multi-hyphenate talent Barbara Loden’s first and only directed feature is now regarded as a ceiling-shattering masterpiece of American independent cinema.

films.title: Scenes from a Marriage
films.synopsis: Unfolding in episodic fashion and spanning the course of a decade, Scenes from a Marriage features Liv Ullmann, in one of her finest performances, as Marianne, a woman struggling to cope with the infidelity of her husband Johan.

films.title: Autumn Sonata
films.synopsis: Actress Ingrid Bergman’s only film for director Ingmar Bergman was this wrenching mother-daughter psychodrama, shot in painterly autumnal colour tones by cinematographer Sven Nykvist.

films.title: Saraband
films.synopsis: A searing work in the director’s minimalist, chamber-drama mode, Saraband has Liv Ullmann and Erland Josephson reprising their roles from 1974’s Scenes from a Marriage, Bergman’s shattering analysis of a failed relationship.

films.title: Suspiria
films.synopsis: The stuff of nightmares is elevated to a high art in Dario Argento’s gorgeous and gory magnum opus, an immutable classic of Euro Horror that has spawned countless imitators.

films.title: Deep Red
films.synopsis: After a brief hiatus from giallo fare, Dario Argento returned to—and some would say, damn-near perfected!—the stalk-and-slash thriller with Deep Red, his blood-bathed reworking of Antonioni’s modernist milestone Blow-Up.

films.title: The Porchlight Sessions
films.synopsis: This documentary follows the fascinating story of bluegrass—from its origins in the Appalachian Mountains as a merging of jazz and blues with country and folk music, to its place in modern-day pop culture.

films.title: NEW DOCUMENTARY Antonio Lopez 1970: Sex, Fashion & Disco
The Listeners
films.synopsis: An engrossing look behind the scenes at Headquarters, a 24/7 suicide prevention crisis centre in Lawrence, Kansas, where more than twenty thousand calls a year are answered by trained volunteers.

films.title: Seven Samurai
films.synopsis: This brilliant, kinetic movie, fair to say, invented the modern action film.

films.title: Mishima: A Life in Four Chapters
films.synopsis: George Lucas and Francis Coppola funded Paul Schrader’s (effectively) banned-in-Japan Mishima, a dazzling, distinctive dramatization of the life, death, and art of Yukio Mishima, the renowned Japanese writer.

films.title: Maborosi
films.synopsis: The 1995 debut feature of now-reigning Japanese master Hirokazu Kore-eda, whose Shoplifters won the Palme d’Or at Cannes in 2018, is nothing less than sublime.

films.title: The Flavour of Green Tea Over Rice
films.synopsis: This lively, lovely, touching movie, one of Ozu’s most humorous, dates from perhaps the peak period of the master director’s esteemed career.

films.title: Roads in February
films.synopsis: Montreal-based writer-director Katherine Jerkovic’s admirably understated debut, winner of Best Canadian First Feature Film at TIFF, heralds the arrival of a distinctive new voice in our national cinema.

films.title: Les Salopes, or the Naturally Wanton Pleasure of Skin
films.synopsis: Women’s sexual pleasure is the subject (not the object) of writer-director Renée Beaulieu’s fearless second feature—which originated, she says, from a wish to see more women, and more positive depictions of female sexuality, on movie screens.

films.title: The Fireflies Are Gone
films.synopsis: Pilote’s latest film, named Best Canadian Feature at TIFF in 2018, is his most accessible and engaging yet, aided by a standout turn from young lead Karelle Tremblay.

films.title: Loveless
films.synopsis: The search for a missing child is parlayed into a razor-sharp examination of domestic decay and bureaucratic ineptitude in Zvyagintsev’s bleak, barbed 2017 feature, his second to be nominated for the Best Foreign Language Film Oscar.

films.title: The Banishment
films.synopsis: Andrey Zvyagintsev’s highly anticipated follow-up to The Return, his much-exalted 2003 debut feature, was another meditative, masterfully controlled rumination on family misfortune in the register of Andrei Tarkovsky.

films.title: Elena
films.synopsis: Winner of a Special Jury Prize at Cannes, Andrey Zvyagintsev’s superb third feature, co-written by the Russian director, is a Dostoevskian moral thriller that dials back the abstract in favour of a more grounded, socially situated point of entry.

films.title: Columbus
films.synopsis: Columbus, the just-released new feature from acclaimed writer-director Hatef Alimardani, is an Iranian comedy for—and about—the Age of Trump.

films.title: Hendi and Hormoz
films.synopsis: The second feature of director Abbas Amini (Valderrama) won Best Film and Best Director honours at November’s CineIran Festival in Toronto.

films.title: Leviathan
films.synopsis: A political masterwork of staggering scale and consequence, Zvyagintsev’s epic, ambitious, Oscar-nominated fourth feature is a stunner!

films.title: El árbol de las fresas
films.synopsis: The debut feature of Simone Rapisarda Casanova is an ethnographic documentary uniquely—and responsibly—aware of its own epistemological limitations.

films.title: La creazione di significato
films.synopsis: Part treatise on the spectre of history, part portrait of a vanishing existence, Rapisarda Casanova’s universally acclaimed sophomore feature was the centrepiece of New Directors/New Films 2015.

films.title: Zanj Hegel la
films.synopsis: Zanj Hegel la is another beguiling experiment in inside-out ethnography from gifted, globetrotting director Simone Rapisarda Casanova.

films.title: Narcissister Organ Player
films.synopsis: Narcissister debuts as a movie director with this personal documentary/performance film hybrid, crafting a smart, sassy, and moving self-portrait of her provocative art and the role her eccentric mother and biracial family played in shaping it.

films.title: Rey
films.synopsis: The psychotropic sophomore feature of Chilean video artist and analogue alchemist Niles Atallah is one of the most extraordinarily elusive biopics in recent memory.

films.title: Sweet Sweetback’s Baadasssss Song
films.synopsis: “Rated X by an all-white jury,” declared posters for Melvin Van Peebles’s badass 1971 feature, a landmark of African-American independent filmmaking and a work that helped launch the transformative blaxploitation movement.

films.title: Ganja & Hess
films.synopsis: Resurrected from the dead in a dynamic new restoration, writer-director Bill Gunn’s long-neglected Ganja and Hess, a radical, inventive mix of vampire horror and blaxploitation, has been called nothing short of a masterpiece of ’70s American cinema.

films.title: The War at Home
films.synopsis: Glenn Silber and Barry Alexander Brown’s urgent, electric, Oscar-nominated record of civil unrest in America chronicles the fervent antiwar movement in Madison, Wisconsin in the 1960s and ‘70s.

films.title: I Am Cuba
films.synopsis: One of the most ravishing films ever made has been re-released in a lustrous new restoration. Prepare to be astounded!

films.title: Mommy
films.synopsis: Mommy, the debut film by artist Maggie Lee, is a poignant, intergenerational diaspora memoir chronicling her mother’s life after migrating from Taiwan to suburban New Jersey.

films.title: Under African Skies
films.synopsis: For the 25th anniversary of his landmark album Graceland, Paul Simon returns to South Africa for a historic reunion concert.

films.title: Waiting for Barcelona
films.synopsis: Filmed at street level, in expressive black-and-white, this is an authentic portrait of a person we cross paths with every day, but never really see.

films.title: The Great Buster
films.synopsis: Peter Bogdanovich celebrates Buster Keaton’s life and art in this entertaining and insightful new documentary.

films.title: The General
films.synopsis: Buster Keaton’s best film remains a marvel.

films.title: Steamboat Bill, Jr.
films.synopsis: Buster Keaton’s movie-making genius and comic derring-do were rarely on better display than in the sometimes-underrated Steamboat Bill, Jr., one of his finest achievements.

films.title: We Like You, Miss Yaya
films.synopsis: Popular actors Reza Attaran, Hamid Farokhnezhad, and Amin Hayai head this film that, playing with stereotypes and expectations, clearly has more interesting (and more absurdist) things in mind than the average mainstream comedy.

films.title: The Music of Strangers: Yo-Yo Ma and The Silk Road Ensemble
Jules and Jim
films.synopsis: François Truffaut’s much-loved third feature is a lyrical, nostalgia-suffused exploration of the impossibility of living à trois and, like much of his work, a fond hommage to cinema itself.

films.title: The 400 Blows
films.synopsis: A young Jean-Pierre Léaud makes his memorable debut as Antoine Doinel, a troubled 12-year-old in revolt against parents and school.

films.title: The Sower
films.synopsis: Debuting feature filmmaker Marine Francen’s alluring French historical drama, described by The Hollywood Reporter as “The Beguiled meets Black Narcissus,” won the prestigious New Directors competition at Spain’s San Sebastián festival.

films.title: Diamantino
films.synopsis: One of the wackiest, wonkiest, and most inspired debut features in recent memory, Gabriel Abrantes and Daniel Schmidt’s delightfully deranged satire of modern-day Europe won the Grand Prix at Cannes’ Critics’ Week, with good reason.

films.title: Carmine Street Guitars
films.synopsis: Spend a heavenly summer week hanging out at an artisanal guitar shop in Manhattan’s Greenwich Village in this charmer from director and pop-culture chronicler Ron Mann, one of Canada’s most dependable documentarians.

films.title: The Vampire Bat
films.synopsis: Vampirism is suspected when residents of a picturesque German village start showing up dead and drained of blood in this stylish, spooky horror thriller made by the unusually ambitious Poverty Row studio Majestic Pictures.

films.title: The Sin of Nora Moran
films.synopsis: A head-spinning highlight of our Poverty Row series, this lurid melodrama has a feverish, surprisingly complex narrative structure that allegedly influenced Citizen Kane!

films.title: False Faces
films.synopsis: An unscrupulous and unqualified plastic surgeon wreaks havoc in False Faces, a delirious mix of sophisticated comedy and grotesque horror.

films.title: Damaged Lives
films.synopsis: The first American movie made by Austrian émigré and future Poverty Row auteur Edgar G. Ulmer did long service on the exploitation circuit as something of a venereal-disease counterpart to Reefer Madness.

films.title: Mamba
films.synopsis: This fast-paced film, representative of Old Hollywood’s racist depictions of “the Dark Continent,” was uncommonly extravagant and ambitious for a Poverty Row production.

films.title: Strange Illusion
films.synopsis: Detour director Edgar G. Ulmer’s Freudian film noir is an hallucinatory version of Hamlet set partly in an L.A. asylum.

films.title: The Grey Fox
films.synopsis: National Canadian Film Day 2019. Borsos’s beautiful movie offers a charming evocation of place and an elegiac, film-smart take on the Old West and Old Westerns.

films.title: Museo
films.synopsis: Writer-director Alonso Ruizpalacios's sophomore feature Museo nabbed Berlin’s Silver Bear for Screenplay and was last year’s best-received Latin American film—at least, until Alfonso Cuarón’s Roma came along!

films.title: The Raft
films.synopsis: The top-prize winner at Copenhagen’s CPH:DOX in 2018, Marcus Lindeen’s utterly engrossing and insightful documentary recounts the baffling Acali Experiment of 1973.

films.title: A Little Princess
films.synopsis: A Little Princess, based on Frances Hodgson Burnett’s cherished novel, was Cuarón’s first Hollywood picture, and first foray into family entertainment.

films.title: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban
films.synopsis: Of the now ten(!) movies in the ever-expanding Potter-verse, Prisoner of Azkaban is wands down our favourite!

films.title: That Way Madness Lies
films.synopsis: Filmmaker Sandra Luckow’s brother Duanne was well into his forties before he started obsessively following conspiracy theories, fell victim to extortionate internet scams, and stormed the U.S.-Canada border intending to marry a woman he’d never met.

films.title: A Monthly Mental Health Film Series
Black Mother
films.synopsis: With his breathtaking new film, Allah hones his singular, sensorial aesthetic and trains his (many) cameras on the island nation of Jamaica, his mother’s birthplace.

films.title: Meeting Gorbachev
films.synopsis: In this cinematic superpower summit, German film titan Werner Herzog meets former Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev to discuss some of the most momentous events of the late twentieth century.

films.title: The Killing
films.synopsis: Stanley Kubrick’s assured third feature — the legendary director’s breakthrough work — is one of the classic hard-boiled caper films.

films.title: Purple Noon
films.synopsis: French veteran Réne Clément (Forbidden Games) directs this intoxicating cocktail of sunny Mediterranean hedonism and chilling noir suspense, adapted from Patricia Highsmith’s vicious 1955 novel.

films.title: High and Low
films.synopsis: High and Low: From Pulp to Poetry. High and Low is one of Kurosawa’s most impressively formal works, with marvellous deep-focus compositions, gripping set pieces, and ironic point-of-view interplay.

films.title: Point Blank
films.synopsis: John Boorman’s fabulous, fractured 1967 thriller is a key link between vintage Hollywood film noir and the paranoid conspiracy films of the 1970s.

films.title: The American Friend
films.synopsis: Wim Wenders’s audacious adaptation of Patricia Highsmith’s Ripley’s Game is, in our humble opinion, one of the great films of the 1970s — and perhaps the perfect meeting of contemporary German angst and anxious American noir.

films.title: Shoot the Piano Player
films.synopsis: Truffaut’s film, like Godard’s Breathless, epitomizes the nouvelle vague sensibility: playfully mixing genres, radically shifting moods, punch-drunk with jump-cuts, in-jokes, cinema references, and self-reflexive touches.

films.title: The Charmer
films.synopsis: Intimacy and immigration make uneasy bedfellows in Iran-born, Denmark-based director Milad Alami's assured feature debut, a potent psychological drama combining elements of the erotic thriller, the social-issue drama, and the Nordic film noir.

films.title: Reza
films.synopsis: A flirtatious architect muddles through the aftermath of his failed marriage—and writes a book about his tribal ancestors, ancient migrants to the historic city of Isfahan—in Alireza Motamedi’s quirky and affecting first feature.

films.title: Invasion
films.synopsis: The hallucinatory and high-concept third feature of Shahram Mokri experiments with genre, time, and long-take sequence shots as it sets a dystopian mystery-drama against a strange athletic contest played in a disease-ravaged society.

films.title: Dead Souls
films.synopsis: Wang Bing’s colossal oral-history documentary, eight hours and fifteen minutes in length, bears witness to the living memory of those who suffered, terribly, during a little-known chapter of China’s recent past.

films.title: Tap World
films.synopsis: A love of tap infuses every moment of this briskly paced, beautifully shot film, which demonstrates that American-style tap dancing has become a truly international form.

films.title: Children of Nature
films.synopsis: Geriatric rebels-without-a-cause take a final stab at freedom in this lyrical, affecting road movie, the work that put Iceland on the world cinema map.

films.title: Jar City
films.synopsis: Based on the bestseller by Icelandic crime novelist Arnaldur Indridason, Baltasar Kormákur’s Jar City announced the mini-boom of “Nordic noirs” that would gain huge international exposure with The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo.

films.title: As in Heaven
films.synopsis: Sophomore director Kristín Jóhannesdóttir equalled the visual and narrative daring of her debut Rainbow’s End with this stunning magic-realist fable.

films.title: When the Raven Flies
films.synopsis: Evoking memories of Kurosawa’s Yojimbo and Leone’s A Fistful of Dollars, this starkly violent and enormously entertaining riff on the spirit of the Icelandic sagas drew the vocal praise of none other than Ingmar Bergman.

films.title: Nói albinói
films.synopsis: Not only one of the best modern Icelandic films, Nói albinói is also one of the key world-cinema titles of the 2000s, and helped pave the way for the warm international receptions given to Kári’s Icelandic compatriots.

films.title: Golden Sands
films.synopsis: Suggesting an Icelandic version of a classic Ealing Studios comedy, director Ágúst Gudmundsson’s satire chronicles the tumult that results when a group of American soldiers mysteriously sets up camp near a small town in Iceland’s south.

films.title: The Icelandic Dream
films.synopsis: The domestic-hit debut feature of Reykjavik music video director Róbert I. Douglas is an acerbic portrait of an Icelandic hoser and an engaging parody of the Icelandic (and American) Dream.

films.title: Rams
films.synopsis: Winner of the Prix Un Certain Regard at Cannes, Grímur Hákonarson’s festival-circuit hit focuses on two sheep-farming brothers whose long-standing grudge has kept them from speaking to each other for 40 years, despite the fact they’re neighbours.

films.title: Chocolat
films.synopsis: Claire Denis’s evocative debut feature brought her to international attention when it premiered at Cannes in 1988.

films.title: 35 rhums
films.synopsis: After the intoxicating interiority of L’intrus, Denis fashioned a tender and profoundly moving father-daughter drama in tribute to Yasujirō Ozu, one of her formative cinematic influences.

films.title: L’intrus
films.synopsis: Perhaps French cinéaste Claire Denis’s most abstract and elusive film, L’intrus is a daring masterwork of formal invention—and irresolvable storytelling—that erases the already porous line between inner and outer life onscreen.

films.title: Bastards
films.synopsis: Claire Denis plumbs new depths of darkness in this polarizing 2013 neo-noir thriller, one of the French auteur’s most penetrating and, frankly, misanthropic movies.

films.title: Let the Sunshine In
films.synopsis: Delicately balancing humour and heartbreak, Denis’s singularly intelligent movie casts the ever-luminous Juliette Binoche as Isabelle, a Parisian artist and divorcée negotiating the emotional hazards of middle-aged dating.

films.title: White Material
films.synopsis: A towering masterpiece in modern cinema, the much-exalted White Material returned Denis to her conflicted West African roots to stage an incendiary study of postcolonial insurrection.

films.title: Whale Rider
films.synopsis: An arthouse smash in the early aughts, Whale Rider tells the poignant tale of a young Maori girl in a modern New Zealand coastal village and her battle to become her tribe’s future leader.

films.title: The Kid
films.synopsis: To ring in Charlie Chaplin’s 130th birthday this year, Film Club presents a special Father’s Day screening of Chaplin’s sublime feature-length debut, “a picture with a smile—and perhaps, a tear.”

films.title: Good Neighbours
films.synopsis: This heartbreaking and timely film asks, “What do I owe my neighbours?” and, inevitably, “Who will care for me when I am old?”

films.title: Ikarie XB 1
films.synopsis: This sleek, superior science-fiction film, one of the finest made in the former Eastern Bloc, anticipates, in mood, style, and seriousness of purpose, Kubrick’s 2001 and Tarkovsky’s Solaris.

films.title: Solaris
films.synopsis: A Spaced-Out July. A brilliant exploration of love, truth, and what it means to be human, Solaris is magnificently mounted in widescreen and colour.

films.title: 2001: A Space Odyssey
films.synopsis: Kubrick’s stately, soaring cosmic epic, a landmark of 1960s cinema, is now regularly cited as one of the truly great films.

films.title: Cold Sweat
films.synopsis: A prominent female athlete battles Iran’s patriarchy in writer-director Soheil Beiraghi’s hot-button second feature, which raised the ire of the country’s hard-liners.

films.title: Hat Trick
films.synopsis: In writer-director Ramtin Lavafipour’s Hat Trick, a taut psychological thriller set amongst the Iranian middle class, two quarrelling couples strike something with their car while driving home from a party.

films.title: First Man
films.synopsis: First Man nods to Apollo’s questionable politics and unconscionable financial costs, but also captures the magic and grandeur of this momentous human triumph.

films.title: For All Mankind
films.synopsis: The gold standard for NASA documentaries, this Oscar-nominated 1989 film is rich with the alien wonder of a trip to the moon.

films.title: Apollo 11
films.synopsis: A treasure trove of pristine, previously unseen 70mm footage, discovered in NASA’s vaults, is put to superb use in this immersive, wondrous, and surprisingly suspenseful record of the historic Apollo 11 mission to the moon.

films.title: Touch of Evil
films.synopsis: Orson Welles’s spectacularly seedy 1958 noir (screening here in its 1998 reconstruction) is one of the great director’s major masterpieces.

films.title: Les Diaboliques
films.synopsis: Clouzot’s sordid, morbid chiller is one of cinema’s most heart-stopping works – and a decided influence on Hitchcock’s Psycho a half-decade later!

films.title: Elevator to the Gallows
films.synopsis: “I was split between my tremendous admiration for Robert Bresson and the temptation to make a Hitchcock-like film,” said Louis Malle of his stylish first feature, a gripping Gallic noir adapted from a suspense novel by French writer Noël Calef.

films.title: Vertigo
films.synopsis: Hitchcock’s dreamlike chef d’oeuvre is the current reigning “best film of all time” — at least according to prominent film journal Sight & Sound’s most recent (2012) decennial poll of international critics!

films.title: Paris Is Burning
films.synopsis: Just in time for Pride, Jennie Livingston’s invaluable and eternally enthralling record of the Harlem drag ball scene of the 1980s sashays into The Cinematheque in a brilliant new restoration!

films.title: Suburban Birds
films.synopsis: A major noisemaker at Locarno and New Directors/New Films 2019, the beautiful, beguiling debut feature of Chinese filmmaker Qiu Sheng heralds the arrival of an exceptional new talent in Asian cinema.

films.title: Touki bouki
films.synopsis: Legendary Senegalese auteur Djibril Diop Mambéty’s first feature is a truly watershed work in African cinema.

films.title: This Gun for Hire
films.synopsis: Based on Graham Greene’s novel and set in San Francisco, this moody, morbid wartime thriller is one of the foundational films noir and features Alan Ladd in his breakthrough role.

films.title: The Hitch-Hiker
films.synopsis: Lupino’s first noir (and most celebrated directorial outing) was this nerve-racking tale of two buddies (Edmond O’Brien, Frank Lovejoy) whose fishing trip turns into a nightmare when they pick up a psychopathic hitchhiker (William Talman).

films.title: The Killers
films.synopsis: Directed by noir luminary Robert Siodmak (Criss Cross, Phantom Lady), The Killers is one of film noir’s defining works — a master class in the criminality, corruption, and cynicism of the noir universe.

films.title: Scarlet Street
films.synopsis: Fritz Lang’s cynical, sordid noir was originally banned in several U.S. jurisdictions as indecent and immoral!

films.title: Detour
films.synopsis: Available for decades only in substandard public domain copies, Edgar G. Ulmer's legendary no-budget noir, often cited as the greatest B-movie ever made, has received its first major restoration!

films.title: Mildred Pierce
films.synopsis: Joan Crawford gives an iconic (and Oscar-winning) performance in this top-notch mix of moody film noir and glossy “woman’s picture,” expertly directed by Michael Curtiz and based on the hardboiled novel by James M. Cain.

films.title: The Big Heat
films.synopsis: Film Noir 2019. Fritz Lang’s nihilistic 1950s noir raised screen violence to new heights — with, among other things, a notorious scene involving Lee Marvin as a psychopathic gangster, Gloria Grahame as a gun moll, and a pot full of scalding coffee!

films.title: The Bigamist
films.synopsis: Ida Lupino’s follow-up to her noir landmark The Hitch-Hiker was this haunting hybrid of noir and melodrama.

films.title: Too Late for Tears
films.synopsis: Sultry noir fixture Lizabeth Scott sizzles as femme-fatale housewife Jane Palmer in this long-unseen, recently restored thriller – “the best unknown American film noir of the classic era,” says Eddie Muller of the Film Noir Foundation.

films.title: Woman on the Run
films.synopsis: Love and the complications of marriage get surprisingly complex treatment in this almost-forgotten, recently restored B-movie, aided by a multi-layered central performance by the excellent Ann Sheridan.

films.title: Le Samouraï
films.synopsis: Jean-Pierre Melville: Master of French Noir. Existential, austere, and eternally cool, Jean-Pierre Melville’s neo-noir masterpiece is, for many, the defining Melville film.

films.title: Army of Shadows
films.synopsis: Melville’s most personal film is, perhaps by no coincidence, his most powerful too, a haunting meditation on wartime survival that effortlessly transposes his noir sensibilities from criminal underworld to military underground.

films.title: Bob le flambeur
films.synopsis: A pulpy paean to night-time Paris, this atmospheric work stars aging Roger Duchesne as the silver-haired, trench-coated title character, who resolves to end a long streak of bad luck by masterminding the heist of a lifetime.

films.title: Le cercle rouge
films.synopsis: Melville reunited with his Le Samouraï leading man Alain Delon for this inimitable and impossibly cool heist-movie classic, the French director’s penultimate film.

films.title: Le doulos
films.synopsis: Screen bruiser Jean-Paul Belmondo, in his second outing with Melville, is tough-guy Silien, a safe-cracker and could-be cop informant who’s lined up a robbery with a shady colleague just released from jail.

films.title: Léon Morin, Priest
films.synopsis: Melville’s intimate and intellectual film was the second in a trio of acclaimed WWII pictures that showcased the robust range of the French virtuoso, best known for his laconic neo-noirs.

films.title: Ponyo
films.synopsis: To be expected from Studio Ghibli, Ponyo is awash in pure, unbridled imagination and visual fancy — but it’s the tender love, humour, and devotion exhibited by Ponyo and Sosuke that form the emotional heart of the film.

films.title: Lu Over the Wall
films.synopsis: From the visionary mind of anime eccentric Masaaki Yuasa (Mind Game, The Night is Short, Walk on Girl) comes a fresh, frenetic, and wildly fun take on the Japanese mermaid (or ningyo) legend.

films.title: Genesis
films.synopsis: Quebecker Philippe Lesage’s  latest is a perceptive drama of first love, palpably full of adolescent longing and uncertainty.

films.title: Stalker
films.synopsis: Tarkovsky’s immersive, deeply mysterious masterpiece — screening here in its vivid 2017 restoration — is haunting and unforgettable.

films.title: Barbara Rubin and the Exploding NY Underground + Christmas on Earth
films.synopsis: Chuck Smith’s illuminating documentary on taboo-breaking filmmaker Barbara Rubin, a beacon in Manhattan's male-suffocated experimental scene of the 1960s, is followed by Rubin's still-shocking 1963 art-port masterpiece Christmas on Earth.

films.title: Mikey and Nicky
films.synopsis: "A neglected masterpiece of ’70s American cinema" (Alicia Fletcher, TIFF), Elaine May’s third feature as director is an emotionally harrowing crime drama featuring two superb central performances.

films.title: What You Gonna Do When the World’s on Fire?
films.synopsis: Italian-born, Texas-based filmmaker Roberto Minervini (The Other Side) takes the pulse of race relations in Trump’s America in this urgent and incendiary new documentary.

films.title: A Bigger Splash
films.synopsis: Jack Hazan’s radical 1974 docufiction hybrid offers an invaluable glimpse into the tortured production of David Hockney’s iconic 1972 painting Portrait of an Artist (Pool with Two Figures), and the personal crisis that surrounded it.

films.title: La Notte
films.synopsis: Winner of Berlin’s Golden Bear in 1961, Antonioni’s striking modernist film charts twenty-four hours in the deterioration of a troubled marriage.

films.title: Distant Voices, Still Lives
films.synopsis: Terence Davies’s poignant, poetic debut feature, a semi-autobiographical account of growing up in a working-class Catholic family in postwar Liverpool, was an international triumph and announced a remarkable new filmmaking talent.

films.title: The Wicker Man
films.synopsis: Robin Hardy’s heathen-horror masterpiece, screening here in its 40th anniversary "final cut," remains the bedrock of the folk horror subgenre.

films.title: Night of the Demon
films.synopsis: Leave it to RKO alum Jacques Tourneur, who made high-art horror out of B-movie fodder with Cat People and I Walked With a Zombie, to elevate this British quickie into a formative folk-horror classic!

films.title: Where is the Friend’s House?
films.synopsis: This sublime 1987 feature, the first in the so-called "Koker Trilogy," brought Abbas Kiarostami to international attention.

films.title: And Life Goes On
films.synopsis: Straddling boundaries between drama and documentary in the singular Kiarostami fashion, the extraordinary And Life Goes On was made in the aftermath of a 1990 earthquake that killed tens of thousands in northern Iran.

films.title: Through the Olive Trees
films.synopsis: Abbas Kiarostami’s hall-of-mirrors playfulness hits miraculous heights in the tour-de-force third film in his Koker triptych.

films.title: Close-Up
films.synopsis: Abbas Kiarostami’s most critically admired work explores (or erases) the line dividing truth and fiction, documentary and drama, with breathtaking originality.

films.title: Homework
films.synopsis: A small miracle of documentary filmmaking, Kiarostami’s Homework is an alternately playful and poignant portrait of childhood.

films.title: Taste of Cherry
films.synopsis: Abbas Kiarostami’s exquisite meditation on mortality was co-winner (with Imamura’s The Eel) of the 1997 Palme d’Or at Cannes.

films.title: A Wedding Suit
films.synopsis: “In this neorealist comedy about the nature of friendship and the importance of money, a woman orders a new suit for her son to wear to a wedding. The tailor’s apprentice and his two teenage friends covet the fetching ensemble, and hatch a plan to borrow it for the night just to see how it feels — a plan that of course goes comically (and suspensefully) awry as the clothing passes among the trio, threatened by mishap at every moment” (TIFF). (Ghazieh-e shekl-e aval, ghazieh-e shekl-e dou wom)

films.title: ABC Africa
films.synopsis: Abbas Kiarostami, celebrated for works about children, was invited by the UN to make a documentary about the plight of AIDS orphans in Uganda.

films.title: The Wind Will Carry Us
films.synopsis: Abbas Kiarostami planted another flag on cinema’s summit with this understated, enigmatic, seductively beautiful work, his follow-up to the Cannes-winning Taste of Cherry.

films.title: Five Dedicated to Ozu
films.synopsis: Abbas Kiarostami pays tribute to Yasujiro Ozu in this non-narrative experiment, made for the Ozu centenary, and informed by the tranquil, meditative cinema (and the still-life "pillow shots") of the Japanese master.

films.title: How to Train Your Dragon
films.synopsis: One of our favourite kids’ films of the decade, this smart, super funny, and humongously big-hearted CG adventure boasts the most affecting human-animal palship this side of Lilo & Stitch.

films.title: More Earth Will Fall
films.synopsis: This documentary, set in Rio de Janeiro, tells a universal story of enduring love between a family, and of strength and resilience in the face of great adversity.

films.title: Bedlam
films.synopsis: Filmmaker and practicing psychiatrist Ken Rosenberg’s new documentary follows several severely mentally-ill people over a five-year period, detailing their struggles and hard-won (sometimes heartbreakingly short-term) victories.

films.title: Somniloquies
films.synopsis: Working out of the Sensory Ethnography Lab at Harvard University, Véréna Paravel and Lucien Castaing-Taylor (Leviathan) enter a bizarre dreamworld of naked bodies and soliloquies in this 2017 film.

films.title: La Pointe Courte
films.synopsis: Agnès Varda’s graceful debut feature is little seen but hugely important: “certainly the first film of the French nouvelle vague” (Georges Sadoul).

films.title: The Gleaners and I: Two Years Later
films.synopsis: Two years after The Gleaners and I, Varda revisited (and expanded upon) the subject of modern-day gleaning in this insightful and characteristically introspective one-hour epilogue to the original film.

films.title: Daguerréotypes
films.synopsis: Although already a veteran of the nonfiction mode by the mid-1970s, Varda hadn't made a feature-length documentary until this affectionate snapshot of her bustling Paris neighbourhood.

films.title: Faces Places
films.synopsis: A bona fide hit and awards darling for (then) 89-year-old Varda, this Oscar-nominated road-documentary, co-directed with French street artist JR, was the runaway audience favourite at both TIFF and VIFF.

films.title: Kung-Fu Master!
films.synopsis: A troubling subject gets sensitive treatment in Agnès Varda’s bittersweet 1988 drama starring Jane Birkin.

films.title: Jane B. par Agnès V.
films.synopsis: Agnès Varda’s “documentary” is a marvellously playful, decidedly unconventional portrait of singer, actress, fashion icon, and Serge Gainsbourg companion Jane Birkin.

films.title: One Sings, the Other Doesn’t
films.synopsis: Agnès Varda drew a line in the political sand with this spritely feminist musical-cum-manifesto about women’s reproductive rights.

films.title: Agnès Varda: From Here to There
films.synopsis: This delightfully discursive five-part film journal chronicles Agnès Varda's travels and conversations with artists the world over.

films.title: The Tobacconist
films.synopsis: Iconic arthouse thesp Bruno Ganz portrays psychoanalytic sage Sigmund Freud in Austrian director Nikolaus Leytner’s stately, sensitively rendered coming-of-age drama.

films.title: Freedom Under Load
films.synopsis: Seasoned alpine-filmmaker Pavol Barabáš documents the oldest generation of porters operating in the High Tatras Mountains of northern Slovakia.

films.title: A Picture with Yuki
films.synopsis: A maelstrom of moral uncertainty and ethnic conflict permeates Bulgarian director Lachezar Avramov’s striking debut feature.

films.title: Kurier
films.synopsis: The latest from Polish genre-hitmaker Władysław Pasikowski is a white-knuckled espionage thriller inspired by a real-life war hero who couriered intel across enemy lines in WWII.

films.title: Hope Frozen
films.synopsis: A scandal swirls around a grief-stricken Bangkok family and their unorthodox decision to cryopreserve their deceased two-year-old daughter.

films.title: Prey
films.synopsis: This riveting story of deceit, corruption, and vindication follows a survivor of sexual abuse as he and his lawyer take on the Catholic Church in an Ontario court.

films.title: Cavebirds
films.synopsis: Intrigued by her father's return to rural Malaysia to launch an edible bird nest farm, a Montreal filmmaker discovers truths about home and heritage that help bridge the gap between them.

films.title: Certified Copy
films.synopsis: Kiarostami entered the new decade in peak form, staging a Rubik’s Cube romance in the Italian countryside that interrogates — in its subject, theme, and form — the very nature of authenticity itself.

films.title: 10 on Ten
films.synopsis: Kiarostami is in the driver’s seat (literally) in 10 on Ten, a sequel of sorts to 2002’s Ten, and a fascinating master class in the great director’s creative methods.

films.title: Sátántangó
films.synopsis: Hungarian master Béla Tarr’s mammoth, mesmerizing magnum opus has been given a stunning new restoration on the occasion of its 25 anniversary!

films.title: The Florida Project
films.synopsis: A magisterial work of bursting emotion and heartrending humanism, Sean Baker’s sixth feature feels like the crescendo of the indie stalwart's career to date.

films.title: Starlet
films.synopsis: Sean Baker’s remarkable fourth feature won its director stripes — and an armful of trophies — for its delicate handling of an intergenerational friendship between two searching women.

films.title: Foreign Correspondent
films.synopsis: Hitchcock’s taut espionage tale, a sibling to his chase thrillers Saboteur and North by Northwest, features some of the most spectacular set-piece sequences in the great director’s canon.

films.title: Holiday gifts for the film lover in your life.
films.synopsis: “The empowering fiction-feature debut from documentary director Arash Lahooti showcases an inspiring performance from Hadieh Tehrani as a woman struggling to prove her worth in a man’s world. Aban, an overworked contractor in her forties, is dead set on outbidding her male competitor Kazem to harvest, with her crew of seasonal female workers, the largest orange orchard in northern Iran. Tough as nails and proudly self-sufficient, she wins the tender by going so far as to put up her house as collateral. But she soon finds herself doing damage control when it feels like the entire operation is being sabotaged at every step of the way ... From a finely tuned script co-written with Jamileh Darolshafaie, Orange Days is an absorbing drama inspiring us to battle through life’s challenges without losing track of our loved ones or ourselves” (Dimitri Eipides, TIFF).

films.title: The Wizard of Oz
films.synopsis: Too seldom experienced on the big screen, MGM's enchanting adaptation of L. Frank Baum's beloved children’s novel is a cinematic gift to behold.

films.title: Day One
films.synopsis: Day One chronicles the ups and downs of a group of teens from the Middle East and Africa, and tacitly demonstrates what can be achieved when a community goes out of its way to welcome immigrants.

films.title: False Confessions
films.synopsis: Delving into the complex psychology behind false confessions, this documentary reveals how an interrogation system allows police to lie and manipulate in order to elicit an expected admission of guilt.

films.title: Toni Erdmann
films.synopsis: If there was a film this decade that rivalled the curveball humour, squirmy awkwardness, or blindsiding joys of German writer-director Maren Ade’s universally adored Toni Erdmann, we didn’t see it!

films.title: Under the Skin
films.synopsis: Kubrick, Roeg, and Hitchcock are antecedents to Jonathan Glazer’s enigmatic, deeply unsettling third feature, adapted from Michel Faber’s novel.

films.title: Western
films.synopsis: The first film in over a decade from German writer-director Valeska Grisebach caught many moviegoers off-guard with its understated intelligence, delicate formal sensibilities, and clear-eyed command of the genre it shares its name with.

films.title: Roma
films.synopsis: Fellini’s opulent portrait of Rome, his adopted city, gives free rein to his outlandish imagination.

films.title: High Life
films.synopsis: French auteur Claire Denis —“the world's greatest working filmmaker,” sayeth Moonlight director Barry Jenkins —brought her singular sensibilities to astral sci-fiwith her astonishing English- language debut. Denis’s cosmic stunner is set in the near future, with an end-of-life Earth in search of alternative energy sources. Cue Monte (Robert Pattinson), one of a cohort of death-row inmates offered absolution by hurling themselves across the galaxy in a spaceship bound for the nearest black hole. That mission is dire but clear; murkier are the fertility experiments conducted by the on-board doctor (Juliette Binoche), obsessed with sparking new life in the cosmos sans sex. Denis’s penchants for elliptical storytelling and transgression (including, here, an abundance of bodily fluids) are fully in evidence. Like genre touchstones 2001: A Space Odyssey and Solaris, Denis’s philosophical space opera is less off‑world exploration than inward rumination on relinquishes nothing of the philosophical and visual force, the difficulty and seductiveness, that have made Denis’s films among the most compelling of Advisory: High Life includes scenes of sexual violence.

films.title: Burning
films.synopsis: A year before his compatriot Boon Joon-ho’s Palme d’Or-winning Parasite, Korean master Lee Chang-dong offered his own incendiary and constantly surprising drama set against economic inequality and social disparity in South Korea.

films.title: Ethnic Notions
films.synopsis: Marlon Riggs first established his reputation as a radical filmmaker and uncompromising authorial voice with this Emmy-winning documentary. The film revisits 150 years of American history through the lens of anti-Black prejudice and racial discrimination.
